# Date picker

Enter a calendar date, or a range of dates, by typing it or choosing it on a calendar: a closing date, a start date, a reporting period.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For a date people set on a record: closing date, start date, contract end.
- For a period that narrows a list or a chart: applications in the last 30 days, a quarter for a report.
- When people need to see the weekday or the week around a date, such as booking around weekends.

## When not to use

- For a date people know by heart and never browse to, such as a date of birth. Use a Text input (text-input) with the hint dd/mm/yyyy.
- For booking or moving events in time. Use the Scheduler (scheduler).
- For a chart's fixed period options such as Daily or Weekly. Use a Segmented control (segmented-control).
- To show a date. Use Timestamp (timestamp).

## Structure

1. Label
2. Field: the date as dd/mm/yyyy (From and To for a range)
3. Calendar button ("Choose date")
4. Popover: preset periods (range, optional), month heading, previous and next month, grid starting on Monday
5. Footer: why some dates are unavailable (optional)
6. Hint or error under the field

## Guidelines

- Typing is the main path: the field accepts 12/03/2026, 12/3/26, 12 Mar 2026 and 2026-03-12, and rewrites the value as 12/03/2026 when people leave it, so they see how it was read.
- The calendar is the second path: the button at the end of the field, or Alt+↓ in the field. It opens on the value's month, otherwise today's.
- Values are ISO calendar dates ("2026-03-12"), never a Date at midnight UTC, so they match Timestamp and don't land on the day before west of London.
- Weeks start on Monday and month and weekday names are UK English.
- Say why dates are unavailable in the footer, such as "Closing dates must be on a weekday." Unavailable days are skipped by the arrow keys.
- A range shows two months side by side from 768px, one below. The first pick sets the start, the second the end; days between are filled as people point or move.
- Preset periods (Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month…) apply at once. In a filter they are stored by name, so a saved view still means "last 30 days" next month. In a filter bar use DateFilterPill, which reads as a sentence like other filter pills: Applied is in Last 30 days.
- Check the value when people leave the field and on submit; show the error under the field, never in a toast.

## Content

- The hint is the format: dd/mm/yyyy. Add a reason only when it helps: "The last day applications are accepted."
- Errors say what to do: "Enter the closing date as dd/mm/yyyy, such as 12/03/2026.", "Choose a date on or after 7 December 2026.", "The end date is before the start date. Change one of them."
- Preset names say the period: Last 7 days, This month, Last quarter.

## Accessibility

- The popover is a dialog named "Choose date". The grid's day buttons have full names: "Thursday 12 March 2026", with "Today" and "selected" added.
- The month heading is a polite live region, so changing month is read out.
- Focus moves to the selected day, or today, when the calendar opens, and back to the field when it closes.
- Today has a ring and the selected day a fill, and both are named, so neither relies on colour alone.
- Day cells are 32px, above the 24px minimum target.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Alt+↓ | Open the calendar from the field |
| Enter (in the field) | Read the typed date |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Previous or next day; same day in the previous or next week |
| Home / End | Start or end of the week |
| Page Up / Page Down | Previous or next month (Shift for the year) |
| Enter or Space | Choose the focused day |
| Esc | Close the calendar without changing the value; focus returns to the field |

## Examples

### closing-date

```tsx
import { DatePicker, fromIsoDate } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Closing date", description: "Type the date, or press Alt+↓ or the calendar button. Weekends and past dates can't be chosen, and the calendar says why.", order: 1 };

const today = new Date();
const iso = (d: Date) => `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0")}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, "0")}`;

export default function Example() {
	const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null);
	return (
		<div className="w-72">
			<DatePicker
				label="Closing date"
				value={value}
				onValueChange={setValue}
				min={iso(today)}
				isDateUnavailable={(d) => [0, 6].includes(fromIsoDate(d).getDay())}
				unavailableReason="Closing dates must be on a weekday."
				hint="The last day applications are accepted. dd/mm/yyyy"
				required
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### filter-pill

```tsx
import { DateFilterPill, type DateRangeValue, FilterBar, FilterPill, FilterSummary, dateFilterToValues, describeDateFilter } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "In a filter bar", description: "DateFilterPill sits beside FilterPill and reads as a sentence. Presets and calendar ranges apply at once; typed dates apply on Enter. The value is stored as URL-safe strings.", order: 3 };

const STAGES = [{ value: "screen", label: "Screen", count: 42 }, { value: "interview", label: "Interview", count: 18 }, { value: "offer", label: "Offer", count: 4 }];

export default function Example() {
	const [stages, setStages] = useState(["interview"]);
	const [applied, setApplied] = useState<DateRangeValue>({ preset: "last-30-days" });
	const [closing, setClosing] = useState<DateRangeValue>({});
	const d = describeDateFilter(applied);
	return (
		<div className="grid max-w-full gap-3">
			<FilterBar>
				<FilterPill field="Stage" options={STAGES} selected={stages} onChange={setStages} onRemove={() => setStages([])} />
				<DateFilterPill field="Applied" value={applied} onChange={setApplied} onRemove={() => setApplied({})} />
				<DateFilterPill field="Closing date" value={closing} onChange={setClosing} presets={[]} />
			</FilterBar>
			<FilterSummary shown={12} total={64} noun="candidates" onClear={() => { setStages([]); setApplied({}); setClosing({}); }} />
			<p className="text-sm text-ink-3">
				URL: <code className="tabular">?applied={dateFilterToValues(applied).join(",") || "—"}</code>
				{d && <> · Applied {d.operator} {d.spoken}</>}
			</p>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### range-presets

```tsx
import { DateRangePicker, type DateRangeValue, resolveDateRange, formatDateLong } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Range with presets", description: "Pick a preset or two dates. A preset is kept by name, so a saved view still means last 30 days next month.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRangeValue>({ preset: "last-30-days" });
	const { from, to } = resolveDateRange(value);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-80 gap-3">
			<DateRangePicker label="Applied" value={value} onValueChange={setValue} presets maxDays={366} />
			<p className="text-sm text-ink-2">
				{from && to ? <>Showing applications from {formatDateLong(from)} to {formatDateLong(to)}.</> : "Choose a period."}
			</p>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### states

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "States", description: "The error says what to do. Read-only keeps the date selectable and drops the calendar.", order: 4 };

const noop = () => {};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-72 gap-4">
			<DatePicker label="Start date" value={null} onValueChange={noop} required error="Enter a start date." />
			<DatePicker label="Contract end" value="2027-03-31" onValueChange={noop} readOnly />
			<DatePicker label="Probation review" value="2026-12-07" onValueChange={noop} disabled />
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Timestamp

# Combobox

Pick one or several values from a long list by typing a few letters, and add a missing one without leaving the form: a location, skills, an owner.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- One value from eight or more options, such as a location from 40 offices.
- Several values from eight or more options, such as skills from a long list (multiple).
- Options the server searches, such as people in a large company (filter={null} with onSearch).
- When a missing option can be created on the spot: Create "Leeds office".

## When not to use

- Up to seven options. Show them all as Radio buttons (radio) or Checkboxes (checkbox).
- Free values with no list, such as email addresses. Use Tag input (tag-input).
- Narrowing a list or a table. Use Filter pills (filter-bar).
- Running commands or jumping anywhere. Use the Command palette (command-palette).

## Structure

1. Label
2. Trigger: the value, or chosen values as tags then +N more
3. Popover: search field
4. Options, grouped (optional), with a check for chosen ones and secondary text
5. Status: searching, no match, or failed with Try again
6. Create "…" (optional)
7. Footer for several: count, limit and Clear

## Guidelines

- Matching ignores case and accents and looks at the label and the secondary text.
- With several values, chosen options are listed first when the list opens and keep their place while people tick, so rows don't jump.
- For server search, results replace the list in one go. "Searching…" shows only if the wait passes one second.
- If options fail to load, say so inside the list with Try again; the rest of the form keeps working.
- Offer Create only when nothing matches exactly. A name-only record is created and selected at once; anything more opens an overlay side panel and is selected when saved.
- Up to three chosen values show as tags in the trigger, then +N more. The footer states the count and any limit.
- A required combobox shows its error under the field on submit; the submit button is never disabled.

## Content

- The placeholder names the action and the thing: Choose a location. The search field says Search locations.
- No match names the text: No locations match "lee".
- Create repeats the text in quotes: Create "Leeds office".

## Accessibility

- The search field is a combobox controlling a listbox; options are named and the highlighted one is announced with aria-activedescendant.
- The trigger is named by the label and the value: "Location, Leeds" or "Skills, 3 selected".
- Result counts and the searching state are announced politely.
- Each tag's remove button is named "Remove Python" and has a 24px target.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space or ↓ (trigger) | Open the list |
| A letter (trigger) | Open the list with that letter in the search |
| ↑ ↓ | Move through options |
| Enter | Choose the option; with several values it ticks and the list stays open |
| Esc | Close without changing the value; focus returns to the trigger |
| Backspace (trigger) | Move to the last chosen tag; Backspace again removes it |

## Examples

### location

```tsx
import { Combobox, type ComboboxOption } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "One value, with Create", description: "Type a few letters. When an office isn't listed, Create adds it and selects it in one step.", order: 1 };

const START: ComboboxOption[] = [
	["Aberdeen", "Scotland"], ["Belfast", "Northern Ireland"], ["Birmingham", "England"], ["Bristol", "England"], ["Cardiff", "Wales"], ["Edinburgh", "Scotland"],
	["Glasgow", "Scotland"], ["Leeds", "England"], ["Liverpool", "England"], ["London", "England"], ["Manchester", "England"], ["Newcastle", "England"], ["Swansea", "Wales"],
].map(([label, description]) => ({ value: label.toLowerCase(), label, description, group: description }));

export default function Example() {
	const [options, setOptions] = useState(START);
	const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>("leeds");
	return (
		<div className="w-72">
			<Combobox
				label="Location"
				noun={{ one: "office", many: "offices" }}
				options={options}
				value={value}
				onValueChange={setValue}
				onCreate={(text) => {
					const made = { value: text.toLowerCase(), label: text, description: "New office" };
					setOptions((o) => [...o, made]);
					return made;
				}}
				required
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### server-search

```tsx
import { Combobox, type ComboboxOption, matchOption } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useCallback, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Server search and errors", description: "The app filters as people type. Nothing flickers for quick answers; a failure shows inside the list with Try again. Type \"fail\" to see it.", order: 3 };

const PEOPLE: ComboboxOption[] = ["Amara Okafor", "Ben Hughes", "Chloé Martin", "Dev Patel", "Eilidh Ross", "Femi Adeyemi", "Grace Lin", "Harry Evans", "Isla Byrne", "Jonas Weber"].map((n, i) => ({ value: `u${i}`, label: n, description: ["Talent", "Engineering", "Design", "Finance"][i % 4] }));

export default function Example() {
	const [options, setOptions] = useState<ComboboxOption[]>(PEOPLE);
	const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
	const [loadError, setLoadError] = useState<string>();
	const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null);
	const search = useCallback((text: string) => {
		setLoading(true);
		setLoadError(undefined);
		setTimeout(() => {
			setLoading(false);
			if (text.trim().toLowerCase() === "fail") return setLoadError("People didn't load. Check your connection.");
			setOptions(PEOPLE.filter((p) => matchOption(p, text)));
		}, 1400);
	}, []);
	return (
		<div className="w-72">
			<Combobox label="Hiring manager" noun={{ one: "person", many: "people" }} options={options} value={value} onValueChange={setValue} filter={null} onSearch={search} loading={loading} loadError={loadError} onRetry={() => search("")} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

### skills

```tsx
import { Combobox } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Several values", description: "Ticking keeps the list open. Up to three skills show in the field, then +N more; the footer counts them against the limit.", order: 2 };

const SKILLS = ["Airflow", "AWS", "Azure", "dbt", "Docker", "Excel", "Figma", "GCP", "Go", "Java", "Kotlin", "Kubernetes", "Looker", "Power BI", "Python", "R", "React", "Rust", "Scala", "Snowflake", "Spark", "SQL", "Tableau", "Terraform", "TypeScript"].map((s) => ({ value: s, label: s }));

export default function Example() {
	const [value, setValue] = useState<string[]>(["Python", "SQL", "dbt", "Airflow"]);
	return (
		<div className="w-80">
			<Combobox multiple label="Skills" noun={{ one: "skill", many: "skills" }} options={SKILLS} value={value} onValueChange={setValue} max={8} hint="Shown on the listing and used to match candidates." />
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Checkbox
- Radio
- Tag input
- Choosing a selection control
- Creating a record: dialog, single page or steps

# Tag input

Enter several short values that don't come from a list, typed or pasted, and see at once which are wrong: email addresses to invite, allowed domains, keywords.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For free values with no list to pick from: invite emails, allowed domains, search keywords.
- When people paste a list from a spreadsheet, an email client or another tool.

## When not to use

- When the values come from a list, such as skills or locations. Use Combobox (combobox) with multiple.
- For one value. Use a Text input (text-input).
- For labels on a record that people only read. Use Tag (tag).
- For many rows of values with several fields each. Use a Sheet grid (sheet-grid).

## Structure

1. Label
2. Field holding the tags, then the text input
3. Tag: text and remove button; an invalid tag adds an alert icon and its reason
4. Hint, or what just happened (added, already added, not added)
5. Count when there is a limit: 3 of 10
6. Error under the field

## Guidelines

- Enter, comma or leaving the field adds the typed text. Tab adds it only when there is text, so the field never traps focus.
- Pasted text is split on commas, semicolons, new lines and tabs, so a column from Excel or a list from Outlook works.
- A duplicate (ignoring case) isn't added again: the existing tag is highlighted and the hint line says it is already added.
- An invalid value stays as a marked tag with its reason; the error under the field counts them. Nothing is dropped without saying so.
- Values past the limit stay in the input, and the hint line says how many weren't added.
- Fix a value by pressing Enter on its tag, or double-clicking it: the text goes back into the input.

## Content

- The hint names the separators and the thing: Separate addresses with commas or new lines.
- Messages say what happened and what to do: "anna@acme.co.uk is already added.", "Not an email address.", "2 addresses aren't valid. Fix or remove them."

## Accessibility

- The tags are a list named by the field label. Each tag's name includes its reason when it isn't valid.
- Adding, removing and paste summaries ("12 added, 2 not valid") are announced politely.
- The field is one tab stop; arrow keys move between tags, so long lists don't flood the tab order.
- Error is shown with an icon and words as well as colour.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter or comma | Add the typed text |
| ← or Backspace at the start of the input | Move to the last tag |
| ← → | Move between tags; → from the last tag returns to the input |
| Backspace / Delete (on a tag) | Remove it; focus moves to the tag before or after |
| Enter (on a tag) | Put its text back in the input to fix it |
| Esc (on a tag) | Return to the input |

## Examples

### invite

```tsx
import { TagInput } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Invite by email", description: "Type or paste addresses. Duplicates are reported, invalid ones stay marked with the reason. Try pasting: ben@acme.co.uk; anna@acme.co.uk; chris@acme", order: 1 };

const isEmail = (v: string) => (/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(v) ? undefined : "Not an email address.");

export default function Example() {
	const [value, setValue] = useState<string[]>(["anna@acme.co.uk"]);
	return (
		<div className="w-96 max-w-full">
			<TagInput label="Email addresses" noun={{ one: "address", many: "addresses" }} value={value} onValueChange={setValue} validateValue={isEmail} max={10} name="invite" required />
		</div>
	);
}
```

### states

```tsx
import { TagInput } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "States", description: "Invalid values are counted under the field. Read-only tags stay focusable and readable.", order: 2 };

const noop = () => {};
const domain = (v: string) => (/^[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$/i.test(v) ? undefined : "Not a domain, such as acme.co.uk.");

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-96 max-w-full gap-4">
			<TagInput label="Allowed domains" noun={{ one: "domain", many: "domains" }} value={["acme.co.uk", "acme com", "acme.com"]} onValueChange={noop} validateValue={domain} />
			<TagInput label="Keywords" noun={{ one: "keyword", many: "keywords" }} value={["Data engineer", "Analytics", "Remote"]} onValueChange={noop} readOnly />
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Tag
- Combobox
- Text input
- Sheet grid
- Form validation

# Form validation

Tells people which fields need fixing and how, at the field and in a summary at the top on submit.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- On any form where a value can be wrong or missing: a new listing, a salary, a closing date.
- Field errors as soon as the person leaves a field with a wrong value.
- The summary strip when someone submits and one or more fields fail.

## When not to use

- For errors not tied to a field, such as a server failure. Use a banner above the form or the table error state.
- To confirm success on every field. Use a Toast for the completed action instead.
- Before the person has touched the field. Leave untouched fields neutral until submit.

## Structure

1. Error summary strip (on submit)
2. Count of problems
3. Go to first link
4. Field with red border
5. Inline error message

## Guidelines

- Check a field when the person leaves it. Recheck on each keystroke once it is in error, and clear the error when fixed.
- On submit, check the whole form. Show the red strip at the top: 2 fields need fixing before you can publish.
- The strip has a Go to first link that scrolls to and focuses the first field in error.
- The summary adds to inline errors; it never replaces them.
- Message sits directly under the field, replacing the hint, in 12px red text.
- Keep everything the person typed. Never clear a form on error.

## Content

- Say what to do, not what went wrong in system terms: Pick a date after today.
- For empty fields, instruct: Enter a job title. For wrong values, describe the limit: Enter at least £23,400.
- No please, sorry, oops, invalid or blaming words.
- Use the field label in the message so it reads as one thing, and use the same words in the summary.
- The summary counts problems in plain words: 2 fields need fixing before you can publish.

## Accessibility

- Each failed field has aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing at its message.
- Errors are in text, not only red. The border colour is a second cue.
- The strip uses role="alert" so it is announced at once; Go to first moves focus to the field.
- Messages suggest a fix whenever the system knows one.
- Red text and the red border meet 4.5:1 and 3:1 on white.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Leave a field and trigger its check |
| Enter on Go to first | Move focus to the first field in error |

## Examples

### summary

```tsx
import { Button, ErrorSummary, TextField } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
export const meta = {"title": "Validate on submit, then summarise", "description": "Press Publish. On submit, each field shows its own error and the summary at the top counts the problems and links to each field.", "order": 1};

export default function Example() {
	const [title, setTitle] = useState("");
	const [salary, setSalary] = useState("18000");
	const [sent, setSent] = useState(false);
	const errs = [
		!title.trim() && { field: "Job title", message: "Enter a job title.", href: "#fv-title" },
		Number(salary.replace(/\D/g, "")) < 23400 && { field: "Salary", message: "Enter at least £23,400.", href: "#fv-salary" },
	].filter(Boolean) as { field: string; message: string; href: string }[];
	const show = sent ? errs : [];
	return (
		<form className="grid w-96 gap-4" noValidate onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setSent(true); }}>
			<ErrorSummary errors={show} />
			<TextField id="fv-title" label="Job title" required error={show.find((e) => e.field === "Job title")?.message} value={title} onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)} />
			<TextField id="fv-salary" label="Salary" required hint="Per year, before tax." error={show.find((e) => e.field === "Salary")?.message} prefix="£" value={salary} onChange={(e) => setSalary(e.target.value)} inputMode="numeric" />
			<div><Button type="submit" variant="default">Publish listing</Button></div>
		</form>
	);
}
```

- Text input
- Button
- Checkbox
- Radio
- Sign in
- File drop

# Checkbox

Lets people choose any number of options, or confirm one setting that is applied when they save.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To pick any number of options from a list, including none.
- To select table rows for bulk actions, with a header checkbox that selects all.
- For a single setting in a form that is applied when the person saves: Show salary on listing.
- As a parent with an indeterminate dash when only some children are selected.

## When not to use

- For one choice out of several. Use Radio.
- For a setting that takes effect at once. Use Switch.
- To switch the view of other content. Use Segmented control.

## Structure

1. Box (15px)
2. Check or dash mark
3. Label
4. Hint (optional)
5. Group label (for sets)

## Guidelines

- Box is 15px, 4px radius. Checked and indeterminate fill with primary.
- The label is part of the click target. Clicking either toggles the box.
- List options vertically, one per line. Horizontal only for two short options with clear spacing.
- Indeterminate is visual only; clicking it selects all rows.
- Opt-in checkboxes start unticked.

## Content

- Write labels positively: Accept CVs by email, not Don't accept CVs by email.
- Keep labels short, sentence case, no end punctuation.
- Group labels say what to choose: Columns to show.

## Accessibility

- Use a native input type="checkbox" with a label element. Space toggles it.
- Parent checkboxes expose aria-checked="mixed" when partly selected.
- Wrap related checkboxes in a fieldset with a legend, or role="group" with aria-labelledby.
- The 15px box is below 24px, so the label is clickable and rows are 36px apart to meet target spacing.
- Unchecked border and checked fill need 3:1 against white.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Space | Toggle the focused checkbox |
| X | Select the focused table row (single-key shortcut, can be turned off) |
| Shift+J / Shift+K | Extend row selection down or up |

## Examples

### select-all

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Select all", description: "The parent shows indeterminate when only some rows are selected. Clicking it selects all; clicking again clears all.", order: 3 };

const roles = ["Junior Product Designer", "Graduate Data Analyst", "Junior QA Engineer"];

export default function Example() {
	const [sel, setSel] = useState<string[]>([roles[0]]);
	const all = sel.length === roles.length ? true : sel.length ? "indeterminate" : false;
	return (
		<div className="w-72 overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<label className="flex h-row cursor-pointer items-center gap-2.5 bg-surface-2 px-3 text-sm font-medium text-ink-2">
				<Checkbox checked={all} onCheckedChange={() => setSel(all === true ? [] : roles)} aria-label="Select all listings" />
				{sel.length ? `${sel.length} of ${roles.length} selected` : "Select all"}
			</label>
			{roles.map((r) => (
				<label key={r} className="flex h-row cursor-pointer items-center gap-2.5 border-t border-line px-3 hover:bg-surface-2">
					<Checkbox checked={sel.includes(r)} onCheckedChange={(v) => setSel((s) => (v ? [...s, r] : s.filter((x) => x !== r)))} />
					{r}
				</label>
			))}
		</div>
	);
}
```

### states

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "States", description: "Unchecked, checked, indeterminate (some children selected) and disabled. The box is 16px; its row is 24px so it is easy to hit.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="flex items-center gap-6">
			<Checkbox aria-label="Unchecked" />
			<Checkbox aria-label="Checked" defaultChecked />
			<Checkbox aria-label="Some selected" checked="indeterminate" />
			<Checkbox aria-label="Disabled" disabled />
			<Checkbox aria-label="Disabled and checked" disabled defaultChecked />
		</div>
	);
}
```

### with-label

```tsx
import { CheckboxField } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "With label and hint", description: "The label is clickable and part of the target. A hint explains the consequence, not the control.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid gap-3">
			<CheckboxField id="ex-salary" label="Show salary on listing" hint="Listings with a salary get about a third more applies." defaultChecked />
			<CheckboxField id="ex-email" label="Accept CVs by email" />
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Radio
- Switch
- Form validation

# Radio

Lets people choose exactly one option from a short, visible list in a form.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To pick one option from two to seven, when seeing all options helps the decision: Full time or Part time.
- When both choices need a visible explanation, which a single checkbox cannot give.
- Inside a form that is applied with a Save or Publish button.

## When not to use

- For eight or more options. Use a select or Dropdown menu.
- For several choices at once. Use Checkbox.
- To switch the view of data outside a form. Use Segmented control.
- For a single on/off setting. Use Checkbox or Switch.

## Structure

1. Group label (legend)
2. Radio circle (15px)
3. Option label
4. Option hint (optional)

## Guidelines

- Circle is 15px; selected shows a thick primary ring.
- Preselect the most likely or safest option. Never preselect a risky one.
- Add None when no choice is valid, since a radio group cannot be cleared.
- Stack options vertically. Inline is allowed for two short options, as in Full time / Part time.
- Order from most to least likely, or least to most risky.

## Content

- Labels short and parallel, ideally under three words.
- The legend asks or names the choice: Contract type.
- Avoid overlapping ranges in number options.

## Accessibility

- Native radios share a name, wrapped in fieldset and legend (or role="radiogroup" with a label).
- Tab enters the group on the selected option; arrow keys move and select.
- Labels are clickable so the target exceeds the 15px circle.
- Ring and border have 3:1 contrast against white.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move into the group, onto the selected option |
| Arrow keys | Move to and select the next or previous option |
| Space | Select the focused option if not selected |

## Examples

### group

```tsx
import { RadioField, RadioGroup } from "@twoux/ui";
export const meta = {"title": "Radio group", "description": "One choice from a short, visible list. Arrow keys move and select; Tab leaves the group.", "order": 1};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<fieldset className="grid gap-2">
			<legend className="mb-1 text-sm font-medium text-ink">Contract</legend>
			<RadioGroup defaultValue="full">
				<RadioField id="r-full" value="full" label="Full time" />
				<RadioField id="r-part" value="part" label="Part time" hint="Under 30 hours a week." />
				<RadioField id="r-fixed" value="fixed" label="Fixed term" />
				<RadioField id="r-zero" value="zero" label="Zero hours" disabled />
			</RadioGroup>
		</fieldset>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Checkbox
- Segmented control
- Form validation


---

# Switch

Turns one setting on or off with immediate effect, without a Save button.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For a setting that applies the moment it is flipped: Email me when someone applies.
- For preferences in popovers and panels: Wrap long text, Single-key shortcuts.
- When the label describes the on state clearly enough on its own.

## When not to use

- In a form that needs Save or Publish. Use Checkbox.
- When both states need explaining, such as cost differences. Use Radio.
- For more than two options. Use Radio or Segmented control.

## Structure

1. Track (28 x 16px)
2. Thumb
3. Label
4. Description (optional)

## Guidelines

- Track 28 x 16px, thumb 12px. On fills primary; off is grey.
- The change applies at once. Confirm it with a short toast when the effect is not visible on screen.
- Label to the left in settings rows, right of the switch in inline lists; keep one pattern per surface.
- If disabled, say why nearby.
- Movement of the thumb is the main cue; colour is the second.

## Content

- Label says what is on when the switch is on. Read it with on/off after it to test.
- The label never changes with the state.
- Lead with the key word, no question: Single-key shortcuts, not Do you want single-key shortcuts?

## Accessibility

- Use role="switch" (or a native checkbox) with aria-checked true/false.
- Space toggles; Enter may also toggle.
- Label tied with for/id so the label row is part of the target; the 28 x 16 track alone is under 24px high.
- Off track and on fill need 3:1 against the surface.
- Changing a switch must not move focus or open a new view.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Space | Toggle the focused switch |
| Enter | Also toggles (optional) |

## Examples

### settings

```tsx
import { SwitchField } from "@twoux/ui";
export const meta = {"title": "Settings that apply at once", "description": "A switch changes something immediately, so there is no Save button. The label says what is on.", "order": 1};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-96 gap-4 rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-4 shadow-card">
			<SwitchField id="sw-email" label="Email me when someone applies" hint="One email per applicant." defaultChecked />
			<SwitchField id="sw-keys" label="Single-key shortcuts" hint="Turn off if you use a screen reader or voice control." defaultChecked />
			<SwitchField id="sw-digest" label="Weekly summary" disabled />
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Checkbox
- Segmented control
- Keyboard shortcut hint


---

# Status badge

Shows the system state of a record, such as Live, Draft or Closed early, in one short word or phrase.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To show workflow or system state of a listing or candidate: Live, Expires in 3 days, Closed early, Draft.
- In table rows, where a word reads faster than an icon alone.
- Next to the object it describes, never floating on its own.

## When not to use

- For user-made categories such as Design or Graduate scheme. Use Tag.
- To start an action or change state. Use a Dropdown menu or Button; the badge is static.
- For counts on tabs or filters. Use a plain count next to the label.

## Structure

1. Bordered container (20px)
2. Status text
3. Dot or icon (optional)

## Guidelines

- 20px high, 4px radius, 12px medium text, 1px border in the tone colour on a tinted background.
- Five tones with fixed meaning: ok (green), warn (amber), bad (red), mute (grey), accent (primary, for Featured).
- Match the tone to the meaning, not to how much attention you want.
- Keep the same tone for the same status everywhere in the product.
- Do not truncate. If the text is long, rewrite it; badges cannot be focused to reveal the rest.

## Content

- One to three words, sentence case: Expires in 3 days, not EXPIRING SOON.
- Use plain words people use, not system codes.
- Prefer a specific state over a vague one: Closed early, not Inactive.

## Accessibility

- The text carries the meaning; colour only reinforces it.
- Text on the tinted background needs 4.5:1; the border 3:1 is not required because the text identifies it.
- Badges are not interactive: no tabindex, no tooltip that holds needed information.
- When a status changes live (for example after an agent run), announce it with a status message.

## Examples

### dot

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = {
	title: "With dot",
	description: "A leading dot helps scanning down a long column. The word stays.",
	order: 2,
};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
			<Badge variant="success" dot>Live</Badge>
			<Badge variant="warning" dot>Needs you</Badge>
			<Badge variant="destructive" dot>Failed</Badge>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### in-table

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = {
	title: "In a table",
	description: "One badge per row, in its own column, left aligned so the words line up.",
	order: 3,
};

const rows = [
	["Junior Product Designer", "success", "Live", "86"],
	["Graduate Data Analyst", "warning", "Expires in 3 days", "54"],
	["Marketing Assistant", "secondary", "Draft", "0"],
	["Customer Success Associate", "destructive", "Closed early", "19"],
] as const;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<table className="w-full max-w-xl border-collapse overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line-strong bg-surface text-left">
			<thead>
				<tr className="h-8 bg-surface-2 text-sm text-ink-2">
					<th className="px-3 font-medium">Role</th>
					<th className="px-3 font-medium">Status</th>
					<th className="px-3 text-right font-medium">Applies</th>
				</tr>
			</thead>
			<tbody>
				{rows.map(([role, variant, label, applies]) => (
					<tr key={role} className="h-row border-t border-line">
						<td className="px-3 font-medium">{role}</td>
						<td className="px-3"><Badge variant={variant}>{label}</Badge></td>
						<td className="tabular px-3 text-right">{applies}</td>
					</tr>
				))}
			</tbody>
		</table>
	);
}
```

### statuses

```tsx
import { Badge } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = {
	title: "Record status",
	description: "Always a word. Colour repeats the meaning but never carries it alone.",
	order: 1,
};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
			<Badge variant="success">Live</Badge>
			<Badge variant="warning">Expires in 3 days</Badge>
			<Badge variant="destructive">Closed early</Badge>
			<Badge variant="secondary">Draft</Badge>
			<Badge variant="default">Featured</Badge>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Tag
- Tooltip
- Tabs (underline)

# Tag

Labels a record with a category people chose, such as Design, Hybrid or Graduate scheme.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For descriptive categories that classify or group records: team, contract type, work mode.
- For user-defined values that people add and remove.
- When one record belongs to several categories.

## When not to use

- For system state such as Live or Closed. Use Status badge.
- As a button. Use Button or a selectable control.

## Structure

1. Container (22px, 4px corners)
2. Colour dot (optional)
3. Text
4. Remove button (optional)

## Guidelines

- 22px high, 4px corners, white with a 1px grey border, 12px text, so it reads quieter than a status badge. Not fully round: in TwoUX a pill means a filter you can remove.
- Add a colour dot only when the colour means something, such as the team.
- Removable tags put a small x after the text.
- Show up to three in a table cell; summarise the rest as +N so the row stays scannable.
- Never wrap a tag over two lines. Truncate with a tooltip showing the full text.

## Content

- One or two words, ideally under 20 characters.
- Sentence case unless a proper noun: Graduate scheme, not Graduate Scheme.
- Use the same wording everywhere so filters match.

## Accessibility

- Text contrast 4.5:1 on white; the dot is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- The remove button is a real button named Remove Design.
- Remove buttons need a 24px target or enough spacing from neighbours.
- Colour never carries the only meaning; the text names the category.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to a removable tag's remove button |
| Enter / Space | Remove the tag |

## Examples

### tags

```tsx
import { Tag, TagList } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Categories on a listing", description: "Tags are quieter than status badges and have 4px corners (pills mean filters). A dot only when the colour means something. In a table cell, three at most, then +N.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [tags, setTags] = useState(["Design", "Hybrid", "Graduate scheme"]);
	return (
		<div className="grid gap-4">
			<div className="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5">{tags.map((t, i) => <Tag key={t} color={i === 0 ? "var(--color-c1)" : undefined} onRemove={() => setTags((x) => x.filter((y) => y !== t))}>{t}</Tag>)}</div>
			<div className="flex items-center gap-3 text-base text-ink-2">In a table cell: <TagList tags={["Engineering", "Remote", "Senior", "Visa sponsorship", "Urgent"]} /></div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Status badge
- Avatar and avatar stack
- Tag input
- Combobox

# Tabs (underline)

Splits one record or page into sections such as Overview, Candidates and Activity, one visible at a time.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To split a record into separate sections people do not need side by side: Overview, Candidates, Activity.
- When each section is substantial and can have its own URL.
- With a count when the number helps people decide to open the tab: Candidates 42.

## When not to use

- To switch between views of the same data, such as All / Active. Use Segmented control.
- For steps in a flow. Use a stepper or separate pages.
- When people must compare content across sections. Show it on one page.
- For app navigation. Use the sidebar.

## Structure

1. Tab list with bottom rule
2. Tab label
3. Count (optional)
4. Active underline (2px primary)
5. Tab panel

## Guidelines

- Single row, 20px gap, 13px medium labels. Active tab gets primary text and a 2px primary underline: two cues, not one.
- Two to seven tabs. Order by use, most used first; the first tab is the default.
- No nested tabs and no disabled tabs; hide a tab that does not apply.
- If tabs overflow on narrow screens, the list scrolls sideways; it never wraps to a second row.
- Put shared headings and actions above the tab list, not inside one panel.

## Content

- One or two words, nouns, sentence case: Activity, not View all activity.
- Labels must not overlap in meaning.
- Counts need screen reader text: 42 candidates, not just 42.

## Accessibility

- role="tablist" with a label, role="tab" with aria-selected and aria-controls, role="tabpanel" labelled by its tab.
- Tab enters the list on the active tab; Left and Right arrows move between tabs; Home and End jump.
- Panels load instantly, so tabs activate on focus (automatic activation).
- The underline indicator has 3:1 against white.
- Tab hit area is the full label height (about 36px), above the 24px minimum.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Left / Right | Previous or next tab |
| Home / End | First or last tab |
| Tab | Move from the tab list into the panel |

## Examples

### underline

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@twoux/ui";
export const meta = {"title": "Sections of one record", "description": "Underline tabs split one page into sections. Counts help people decide where to go. Arrow keys switch tabs.", "order": 1};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<Tabs defaultValue="overview" className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<TabsList>
				<TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
				<TabsTrigger value="candidates" count={54}>Candidates</TabsTrigger>
				<TabsTrigger value="activity">Activity</TabsTrigger>
			</TabsList>
			<TabsContent value="overview" className="text-ink-2">Views, applies and the funnel for this listing.</TabsContent>
			<TabsContent value="candidates" className="text-ink-2">54 people applied. 16 are shortlisted.</TabsContent>
			<TabsContent value="activity" className="text-ink-2">Edited by Rahul S. 2 days ago.</TabsContent>
		</Tabs>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Segmented control
- Status badge

# Segmented control

Switches between two or three views or settings of the same content, such as All, Active and Backlog.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To switch how the same data is shown or filtered: All / Active / Backlog, Chart / Table.
- For a view setting that always has a value: Rows per page 25 / 50 / 100, Daily / Weekly.
- When there are two or three short options and room to show them.

## When not to use

- For separate sections of a record. Use Tabs.
- For more than three options. Use a Dropdown menu or select.
- For an on/off setting. Use Switch.
- For choices inside a form that is saved later. Use Radio.

## Structure

1. Group label (often visually hidden)
2. Track
3. Segment buttons
4. Selected segment (white, raised)

## Guidelines

- Track is grey with a 2px inset; segments are 24px high, 12px medium text; selected segment is white with a hairline shadow.
- The change applies immediately, like a switch.
- Equal weight for all segments; one is always selected.
- Deactivate at most one segment, and give the reason in a tooltip.

## Content

- One word per segment where possible.
- Sentence case, parallel words: All, Active, Backlog.
- Icon-only segments need alternative text naming the view.

## Accessibility

- TwoUX renders it as a group of toggle buttons: role="group" with aria-label, each button with aria-pressed.
- Every segment label stays the same when pressed; state comes from aria-pressed.
- Segments are 24px high, exactly the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum; do not make them smaller.
- The selected segment differs by fill and shadow, with 3:1 against the track.
- Visible focus ring on each segment.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to each segment |
| Enter / Space | Select the focused segment |

## Examples

### views

```tsx
import { Segment, SegmentedControl } from "@twoux/ui";
import { List, Rows3 } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
export const meta = {"title": "Views of the same data", "description": "Two or three options, one always selected. Switches how the same list is shown; it never navigates.", "order": 1};

export default function Example() {
	const [v, setV] = useState("active");
	const [d, setD] = useState("list");
	return (
		<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
			<SegmentedControl aria-label="Listings to show" value={v} onValueChange={setV}>
				<Segment value="all">All</Segment>
				<Segment value="active">Active</Segment>
				<Segment value="closed">Closed</Segment>
			</SegmentedControl>
			<SegmentedControl aria-label="Layout" size="sm" value={d} onValueChange={setD}>
				<Segment value="list" aria-label="List"><List /></Segment>
				<Segment value="board" aria-label="Board"><Rows3 /></Segment>
			</SegmentedControl>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Tabs (underline)
- Radio
- Switch

# Dropdown menu

Opens a short list of actions or options from a button, with optional groups and one level of submenus.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To group related actions behind one button: Export, row actions, Add context.
- For about 5 to 15 commands, ordered by how often they are used.
- For settings with a current value, shown on the right and changed in a one-level submenu: Writing style Concise.

## When not to use

- For one or two actions. Show them as Buttons.
- When people must search or pick from a long list of values. Use a select or combobox.
- For the main action in a view. Use a primary Button.
- For rich content or forms. Use a popover or dialog.

## Structure

1. Trigger button with chevron
2. Menu panel
3. Group label (optional)
4. Menu item: icon, label, shortcut or current value
5. Separator
6. Submenu caret
7. Destructive item (last)

## Guidelines

- Panel 200px minimum, 10px radius, 4px padding, shadow. Items 30px high, 6px radius, hover in grey.
- Group with uppercase group labels and separators; put destructive items last, in red, after a separator.
- At most one level of submenu. Submenus open on hover, focus or Right arrow, and flip to the side with room.
- Icons on items: none by default. Add them only when every item in a group has a well-known icon from the icon meaning table, and then on all items in that group; never on one item alone. The label always stays, and the icon is 14px and muted.
- Show each item's shortcut on the right.
- Disable items that do not apply rather than hide them, so people can still find them.
- Keep the list under about 12 items.

## Content

- Action items start with a verb; navigation items are nouns.
- Sentence case, one line, no articles: Duplicate listing.
- Front-load the key word so the list scans: Export CSV, Export PDF.
- Ellipsis for items that open more input: Extend to a date…

## Accessibility

- Trigger has aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. Enter, Space or Down opens and focuses the first item.
- role="menu" with menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio; checked items use aria-checked.
- Up and Down move, Right opens a submenu, Left closes it, Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- Items are 30px high, above the 24px target minimum.
- Focus returns to the trigger on close, so the person is not lost.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter / Space / Down | Open the menu and focus the first item |
| Up / Down | Move between items |
| Right | Open a submenu |
| Left | Close a submenu |
| Home / End | First or last item |
| Type a letter | Jump to the next item starting with it |
| Esc | Close and return focus to the trigger |

## Examples

### actions

```tsx
import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuTrigger, Kbd } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Copy, ExternalLink, MoreHorizontal, Pencil, Trash2, UserRound } from "lucide-react";
export const meta = {"title": "Actions on a record", "description": "Shortcuts on the right, destructive last and separated. Submenus open on the side with room. Arrow keys and typeahead work.", "order": 1};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<DropdownMenu>
			<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
				<Button variant="outline" aria-label="Actions for Junior Product Designer" size="icon"><MoreHorizontal /></Button>
			</DropdownMenuTrigger>
			<DropdownMenuContent align="start">
				<DropdownMenuLabel>Listing</DropdownMenuLabel>
				<DropdownMenuItem><Pencil />Edit<DropdownMenuShortcut><Kbd>E</Kbd></DropdownMenuShortcut></DropdownMenuItem>
				<DropdownMenuItem><Copy />Duplicate<DropdownMenuShortcut><Kbd>D</Kbd></DropdownMenuShortcut></DropdownMenuItem>
				<DropdownMenuSub>
					<DropdownMenuSubTrigger><UserRound />Change owner</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
					<DropdownMenuSubContent>
						<DropdownMenuItem>Grace L.</DropdownMenuItem>
						<DropdownMenuItem>Rahul S.</DropdownMenuItem>
						<DropdownMenuItem>Jess M.</DropdownMenuItem>
					</DropdownMenuSubContent>
				</DropdownMenuSub>
				<DropdownMenuItem><ExternalLink />View public page</DropdownMenuItem>
				<DropdownMenuSeparator />
				<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive"><Trash2 />Delete listing</DropdownMenuItem>
			</DropdownMenuContent>
		</DropdownMenu>
	);
}
```

### options

```tsx
import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuTrigger } from "@twoux/ui";
import { ChevronDown } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
export const meta = {"title": "Options with a check", "description": "Radio items for one choice, checkbox items for several. The menu stays a menu: it does not replace a form.", "order": 2};

export default function Example() {
	const [sort, setSort] = useState("posted");
	const [cols, setCols] = useState({ salary: true, owner: false });
	return (
		<DropdownMenu>
			<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">Display<ChevronDown /></Button></DropdownMenuTrigger>
			<DropdownMenuContent align="start">
				<DropdownMenuLabel>Sort by</DropdownMenuLabel>
				<DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={sort} onValueChange={setSort}>
					<DropdownMenuRadioItem value="posted">Posted date</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
					<DropdownMenuRadioItem value="applies">Applies</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
				</DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
				<DropdownMenuSeparator />
				<DropdownMenuLabel>Columns</DropdownMenuLabel>
				<DropdownMenuCheckboxItem checked={cols.salary} onCheckedChange={(v) => setCols({ ...cols, salary: v })}>Salary</DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
				<DropdownMenuCheckboxItem checked={cols.owner} onCheckedChange={(v) => setCols({ ...cols, owner: v })}>Owner</DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
			</DropdownMenuContent>
		</DropdownMenu>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Button
- Popover rules
- Keyboard shortcut hint

# Tooltip

Shows a short, non-essential label or hint on hover or focus, such as an icon button's name and its shortcut.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To name an icon-only button: More, Add to Interviewing.
- To show the shortcut for a control: Search listings /.
- To show the full text of a truncated value, or the exact date behind a relative date.
- To give a short reason why a control is disabled.

## When not to use

- For anything needed to finish the task, such as format rules. Use hint text under the field.
- For links, buttons or more than a sentence. Use a popover.
- On labelled buttons, repeating the label.
- On status badges or other non-interactive elements.

## Structure

1. Dark container (6px radius)
2. Text
3. Shortcut hint (optional)

## Guidelines

- Dark ink background, white 12px medium text, 5 x 8px padding, 6px radius.
- Appears after a short delay (about 500ms) on hover or keyboard focus, so it does not flicker.
- Stays while the pointer is over the trigger or the tooltip, until Esc or blur.
- Placed so it never covers the thing it describes, and flips to stay on screen.
- One line; never truncated.

## Content

- A few words, no full stop: Search listings.
- For icon buttons, name the action in one or two words.
- Use the same words as the accessible name.

## Accessibility

- role="tooltip", referenced by the trigger's aria-describedby. Focus stays on the trigger.
- Esc dismisses it without moving focus; the pointer can move onto it; it does not time out.
- A tooltip does not give an icon button its name; the button also needs aria-label.
- Only on focusable triggers, so keyboard users see it too.
- Shortcuts in tooltips are hidden from assistive technology; list them in the shortcut sheet as well.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab to trigger | Show the tooltip |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### icon-buttons

```tsx
import { Button, Kbd, Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Bell, Pencil, X } from "lucide-react";

export const meta = { title: "Name an icon button", description: "Hover or Tab to a button. The tooltip repeats the accessible name and its shortcut. It never holds information found nowhere else.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
			<Tooltip>
				<TooltipTrigger asChild><Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Edit listing"><Pencil /></Button></TooltipTrigger>
				<TooltipContent>Edit listing <Kbd>E</Kbd></TooltipContent>
			</Tooltip>
			<Tooltip>
				<TooltipTrigger asChild><Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Inbox"><Bell /></Button></TooltipTrigger>
				<TooltipContent>Inbox</TooltipContent>
			</Tooltip>
			<Tooltip>
				<TooltipTrigger asChild><Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Close details"><X /></Button></TooltipTrigger>
				<TooltipContent side="bottom">Close details <Kbd>Esc</Kbd></TooltipContent>
			</Tooltip>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Button
- Keyboard shortcut hint
- Popover rules


---

# Keyboard shortcut hint

Prints the key or keys that run an action, on its button, menu item or tooltip, so people learn shortcuts by using the product.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- On buttons and menu items whose action has a shortcut: Try again R, Edit E.
- In tooltips of icon-only buttons.
- In the command palette, the ? shortcut sheet and footers that list navigation keys.

## When not to use

- For shortcuts that do not work in the current context. Leave the hint out.
- As the only way to reach an action. Every shortcut duplicates a visible control.
- Inside body text as decoration. Use plain text such as press Esc.

## Structure

1. Key cap (18px, mono 10.5px)
2. Further key caps for chords or sequences

## Guidelines

- Key cap is 18px high, 4px radius, 2px bottom border, grey surface. On buttons it shrinks to 16px and sits after the label.
- On primary buttons the cap is translucent white so it keeps contrast on primary.
- Chords show keys side by side (⌘ K); sequences show them in order (G then L).
- Render ⌘ on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere.
- Reserve shortcuts for frequent actions; keep them to one or two keys and never override copy, paste or undo.

## Content

- Use symbols for modifiers and capitals for letters: ⌘, ⇧, ↵, Esc, E.
- Use mnemonic keys: E for Edit, C for Create, F for Filter.
- The same action keeps the same key everywhere.

## Accessibility

- Single-key shortcuts (J, K, X, E, /) can be turned off in the shortcut sheet; ⌘ shortcuts stay on.
- Shortcuts avoid keys used by screen readers, such as Caps Lock and Insert combinations.
- The hint is visual. The full list is in the ? sheet so assistive technology users can find it.
- Every action also works by Tab and Enter.
- Key cap text has at least 4.5:1 contrast on its background.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘K | Open the command palette |
| ? | Open the shortcut sheet |
| G then L | Go to listings |
| J / K | Next or previous row |
| C | New listing |
| E | Edit |

## Examples

### keys

```tsx
import { Kbd } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = {
	title: "Keys",
	description: "One Kbd per key. Use symbols for modifiers: ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ↵.",
	order: 1,
};

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<dl className="grid grid-cols-[auto_1fr] items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-2">
			<dd className="flex gap-0.5"><Kbd>⌘</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd></dd><dt className="text-ink-2">Search or run a command</dt>
			<dd className="flex gap-0.5"><Kbd>J</Kbd><Kbd>K</Kbd></dd><dt className="text-ink-2">Next and previous row</dt>
			<dd className="flex gap-0.5"><Kbd>⇧</Kbd><Kbd>H</Kbd></dd><dt className="text-ink-2">Snooze</dt>
			<dd className="flex gap-0.5"><Kbd>Esc</Kbd></dd><dt className="text-ink-2">Close</dt>
		</dl>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Button
- Dropdown menu
- Tooltip
- Switch

# Avatar and avatar stack

Shows who owns or is linked to a record, as a photo or initials, and several people as an overlapping stack with +N.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To show the owner of a listing or the recruiter on a candidate, next to their name or in a table cell.
- A stack when several people relate to one record and space is short.

## When not to use

- When each person must be clearly identified. List names in full.
- For a single person in a stack. Use one avatar.
- For teams or categories. Use Tag.

## Structure

1. Circle (22px)
2. Photo or initials
3. Stack: overlapping avatars with 2px white ring
4. +N overflow count

## Guidelines

- 22px circle, 10px semibold white initials on a colour assigned per person; photo when one exists.
- Stack shows up to three, overlapping by 6px with a 2px white ring, then +N in small grey text.
- +N reveals the hidden names on hover or focus.
- Each person keeps the same colour everywhere.

## Content

- Initials stand in when there is no photo, and are hidden from screen readers when the name is shown.
- The +N count says how many people are hidden, not the total.
- Tooltips on avatars show the full name, matching the alt text.

## Accessibility

- Standalone avatars have alt text with the person's name; next to a visible name they are decorative (empty alt).
- A stack has a label (for example Candidates) and screen reader text for +N: 3 more candidates.
- White initials need 4.5:1 on the assigned colour; pick colours that pass.
- If the avatar opens a tooltip or popover it must be focusable.
- Interactive avatars are 22px, so keep 24px spacing from other targets.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab to +N | Focus the overflow count and show hidden names |

## Examples

### people

```tsx
import { AvatarStack, PersonAvatar } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Owners and interviewers", description: "Initials on a colour fixed per person (white text at 5.8:1 or more). A stack shows three, then +N, which names the rest on hover or focus.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid gap-4">
			<div className="flex items-center gap-3">
				<PersonAvatar name="Priya Shah" size="lg" /><PersonAvatar name="Tom Becker" /><PersonAvatar name="Amara Okafor" size="sm" />
				<span className="text-base text-ink-2">Priya Shah owns this listing</span>
			</div>
			<div className="flex items-center gap-3">
				<AvatarStack label="Interviewers" people={[{ name: "Priya Shah" }, { name: "Tom Becker" }, { name: "Amara Okafor" }, { name: "Liam Walsh" }, { name: "Sofia Romano" }]} />
				<span className="text-base text-ink-2">5 interviewers</span>
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Tag
- Tooltip
- Status badge
- Provider logo

# Popover rules

Shared behaviour for every floating layer (menus, filters, snooze, selectors): one open at a time and never cut off.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For short supporting content or a small set of controls tied to a trigger: filter values, snooze times, column choices.
- When the person must stay in context and the page behind stays usable.

## When not to use

- For long reading or a multi-step task. Use a dialog or side panel.
- For a one-line label. Use Tooltip.
- Inside another popover. Open a submenu (one level) or a dialog instead.
- For required fields that would be lost on outside click. Use a dialog.

## Structure

1. Trigger (aria-expanded)
2. Floating panel (10px radius, shadow)
3. Header (when dismissible)
4. Body
5. Footer actions (optional)

## Guidelines

- Only one popover is open at a time; opening a menu, filter, snooze or selector closes any other.
- Popovers open on a user action, never on page load.
- Placement flips and shifts to stay inside the panel and the screen, 8px from the edge. Nothing is ever cut off.
- Open 4 to 6px from the trigger, aligned to its start edge.
- Close on outside click, Esc, or when focus leaves; return focus to the trigger.
- Only the body scrolls, never sideways.

## Content

- Header in sentence case, one short line, when the popover can be dismissed.
- No help articles or Learn more links inside; keep help at page level.
- Footer buttons follow Button wording: Cancel and Apply.

## Accessibility

- Triggers set aria-expanded (and aria-haspopup for menus). Enter or Space opens.
- Give the panel a role (menu or dialog) and a label.
- Esc closes and focus returns to the trigger.
- The popover must not hide the focused element.
- At 320px width it fits without sideways scrolling.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter / Space | Open or close from the trigger |
| Esc | Close and return focus to the trigger |
| Tab | Move through controls inside; leaving closes it |

## Examples

### one-at-a-time

```tsx
import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger, FilterBar, FilterPill } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "One at a time, never cut off", description: "Open the Status filter, then the menu: the first closes. Each opens 4px from its trigger, flips and shifts to stay 8px inside the screen, and Esc returns focus to the trigger.", order: 1 };

const OPTIONS = ["Open", "Closing soon", "Draft", "Closed"].map((v) => ({ value: v, label: v }));

export default function Example() {
	const [status, setStatus] = useState<string[]>([]);
	return (
		<div className="flex w-full items-center justify-between gap-3">
			<FilterBar><FilterPill field="Status" options={OPTIONS} selected={status} onChange={setStatus} /></FilterBar>
			<DropdownMenu>
				<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline" size="sm">Actions</Button></DropdownMenuTrigger>
				<DropdownMenuContent align="end"><DropdownMenuItem>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem><DropdownMenuItem>Archive</DropdownMenuItem></DropdownMenuContent>
			</DropdownMenu>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Dropdown menu
- Tooltip
- Button

# Sign in

Provider buttons first, then email. Single sign-on is found from the email domain, and an email link means no password to remember.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- The first screen of an account: sign in and create account in one flow.
- Letting people choose how they sign in: a provider, single sign-on or an email link.

## When not to use

- Asking for anything beyond how to sign in. Setup questions belong in Onboarding step (onboarding-step).
- Gating content that people could read first. Show it before asking them to sign in.

## Structure

1. Provider buttons (logo and "Continue with" name)
2. Divider ("or")
3. Work email field
4. Continue button (becomes "Continue with SSO" for SSO domains)
5. Error under the field

## Guidelines

- Put provider buttons first, then email. One primary action: the email button.
- Find single sign-on from the email domain. Say "twoux.example signs in with single sign-on" and change the button to Continue with SSO.
- Use an email link so there is no password to remember or retype.
- Put errors under the field and say what to do, for example "This email uses Google to sign in. Continue with Google instead."
- Do not reveal which part was wrong, or whether an account exists, unless the product already shows that elsewhere. Use the same message either way.
- Set autocomplete on every field (email, current-password, one-time-code) so browsers and password managers can fill them.
- Validate on press, not on every keystroke, and keep the email people typed after an error.

## Content

- Button: "Continue with Google", "Continue with email", "Continue with SSO".
- Field error: "Enter your work email, for example sam@company.com."
- Do not write "Wrong password" or "No account found". Write what to try next.

## Accessibility

- The email field has a visible label and the right type and autocomplete values (SC 1.3.5, 3.3.2).
- The error is linked to the field with aria-invalid and the field description, and is announced when it appears (SC 3.3.1, 4.1.3).
- Signing in never depends on remembering or transcribing a password alone: providers and email links are alternatives (SC 3.3.8).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through the provider buttons, the email field and the primary button |
| Enter | In the email field, submit the form |
| Space or Enter | Press the focused provider button |

## Examples

### error

```tsx
import { SignInOptions } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Say what to do next", description: "The error sits under the field and names the way in. It does not say which part was wrong.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-sm">
			<SignInOptions
				providers={["google"]}
				error="This email signs in with Google. Continue with Google instead."
				onProvider={() => {}}
				onEmail={() => {}}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### sign-in

```tsx
import { SignInOptions, toast, type ProviderId } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Providers, then email", description: "Providers first. An email on a single sign-on domain changes the button to Continue with SSO. Try sam@twoux.example.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [busy, setBusy] = useState<ProviderId | "email" | "sso" | undefined>();
	const run = (what: ProviderId | "email" | "sso", message: string) => {
		setBusy(what);
		setTimeout(() => { setBusy(undefined); toast.success(message); }, 900);
	};
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-4">
			<h1 className="text-xl font-semibold text-ink">Sign in to TwoUX</h1>
			<SignInOptions
				providers={["google", "microsoft"]}
				ssoDomains={["twoux.example"]}
				busy={busy}
				onProvider={(p) => run(p, "Opened the sign-in window")}
				onEmail={(email) => run("email", `Sign-in link sent to ${email}. Check your inbox.`)}
				onSso={(domain) => run("sso", `Continuing with ${domain}`)}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Provider logo
- Onboarding step
- Text input
- Form validation
- Error messages

# File drop

Drop a file or choose one. Accepted types and the size limit show before choosing, and a preview replaces the icon once a file is picked.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A single file the product needs, such as a logo, an avatar or a CSV.
- Where dragging a file in is a shortcut, not the only way.

## When not to use

- Attaching files to a message. Use the Message composer (message-composer).
- Importing many files with progress. Use a list with a status per file.

## Structure

1. Label
2. Drop area (icon or preview, "Drop a file here", accepted types and limit)
3. Remove and Replace or Upload buttons
4. Hidden native file input
5. Error under the area

## Guidelines

- Show accepted types and the size limit before anyone chooses a file.
- Let people choose with a button as well as drop. Drag and drop is never the only way.
- Errors name the file's size or type and say what to choose, for example "That file is 14.2 MB. Choose one up to 10 MB."
- The preview replaces the icon, with Remove and Replace beside it.
- Use a visible label, and a native file input that is hidden visually but still labelled and focusable by the Upload button.

## Content

- Hint: "PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB".
- Wrong type: "That file type isn't supported. Choose PNG or JPEG."

## Accessibility

- The visible label is attached to the real input, which keeps its accessible name and value (SC 3.3.2, 4.1.2).
- The error is linked to the field with aria-invalid and announced when it appears (SC 3.3.1, 4.1.3).
- The drag state is not conveyed by colour alone: the text changes to "Drop to upload" (SC 1.4.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the Upload button |
| Enter or Space | Open the system file chooser |
| Tab, then Enter | Remove or replace the chosen file |

## Examples

### logo

```tsx
import { FileDrop } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Upload a logo", description: "Types and limit show first. Drop a PNG or JPEG, or press Upload. Try a file over 10 MB or a PDF to see the error.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [url, setUrl] = useState<string>();
	useEffect(() => () => { if (url) URL.revokeObjectURL(url); }, [url]);
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-md">
			<FileDrop
				id="company-logo"
				label="Company logo"
				accept="image/png,image/jpeg"
				hint="PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB"
				maxBytes={10e6}
				preview={url}
				onFile={(f) => setUrl(URL.createObjectURL(f))}
				onRemove={() => setUrl(undefined)}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### server-error

```tsx
import { FileDrop } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "An error from the server", description: "The message names what is wrong with the file and what to choose instead.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-md">
			<FileDrop
				id="hiring-csv"
				label="Candidates file"
				accept="text/csv"
				hint="CSV, up to 5 MB"
				error="Row 14 has no email address. Add one and choose the file again."
				onFile={() => {}}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Form validation
- Text input
- Message composer
- Provider logo

# Connector picker

Search and connect outside services. Each row says what connecting lets the product do, and a dialog explains the access before anything is shared.

Kind: component · Group: Actions and inputs · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Connecting several outside services, from onboarding or from Settings.
- Showing what is connected and what needs attention in one place.

## When not to use

- Setting what an agent may do with a tool. Use Agent permissions (agent-permissions).
- Reviewing one tool in depth. Use the detail card in Connected tools (connected-tools).

## Structure

1. Search (with the number of services)
2. Connected group
3. All services group
4. Row (logo, name, what it lets the product do, Connect, Reconnect or Manage)
5. Connect dialog (access in plain words, who it is shared with, OAuth or API key, Cancel)

## Guidelines

- Add search with the count of services, and put Connected first.
- Say what connecting lets the product do, in plain words, before connecting: "Read and send email".
- Say who the connection is shared with, for example "Only you" or "Everyone in TwoUX".
- OAuth opens the provider in a new window. Say so on the button ("Continue to Slack") and bring people back with a status message.
- Test an API key before saving it, store it encrypted and never show it again. Say all three beside the field.
- When a connection expires, show Needs attention with the reason and a Reconnect button, never colour alone.
- Disconnecting lives in Settings and asks what stops working before it does.

## Content

- "Read your calendar to find free times. Cannot change events."
- "Slack needs you to sign in again. Reconnect to resume the daily summary."

## Accessibility

- Rows are a list under group headings; the group names are real headings (SC 1.3.1).
- Buttons repeat the service name for assistive technology: "Connect Slack" (SC 2.4.6, 4.1.2).
- The dialog traps focus, returns it to the button and announces success with role="status" (APG dialog, SC 4.1.3).
- Status is carried by words (Connected, Needs attention) as well as colour (SC 1.4.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through the search, then each row's button |
| Enter or Space | Connect, Reconnect or Manage |
| Esc | Close the dialog without connecting |

## Examples

### api-key

```tsx
import { Button, ConnectDialog, type Connector } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Connect with an API key", description: "The key is tested before it is saved. Try any text to see the error, or \"nw-live-key\" to connect.", order: 2 };

const XERO: Connector = { id: "xero", provider: "xero", can: ["Read invoices and payments", "Cannot create or change anything"] };

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
	return (
		<>
			<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Connect Xero</Button>
			<ConnectDialog
				connector={XERO}
				open={open}
				onOpenChange={setOpen}
				method="apikey"
				scope="Only you"
				onTestKey={async (key) => { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 700)); return key === "nw-live-key" ? undefined : "Xero did not accept that key. Check you copied all of it from Settings, API keys."; }}
				onDone={() => {}}
			/>
		</>
	);
}
```

### connect-oauth

```tsx
import { ConnectDialog, ConnectorPicker, toast, type Connector } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Search, connect, reconnect", description: "Connected first, then everything else. Slack shows Needs attention with Reconnect. Connecting asks first, in plain words.", order: 1 };

const START: Connector[] = [
	{ id: "gmail", provider: "gmail", can: ["Read and send email as you", "Find threads about a candidate"], connected: true },
	{ id: "slack", provider: "slack", can: ["Post summaries to channels you pick", "Read messages in those channels"], connected: true, problem: "Your Slack sign-in expired. Reconnect to resume the daily summary." },
	{ id: "calendar", provider: "google-calendar", can: ["Read free and busy times", "Create interview events"] },
	{ id: "drive", provider: "google-drive", can: ["Read files you choose", "Never change or delete files"] },
	{ id: "notion", provider: "notion", can: ["Read pages you share with it", "Add notes to a database"] },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [list, setList] = useState(START);
	const [open, setOpen] = useState<Connector | null>(null);
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<ConnectorPicker connectors={list} onConnect={setOpen} onManage={() => toast("Manage opens Settings, Connections")} />
			<ConnectDialog
				connector={open}
				open={!!open}
				onOpenChange={(o) => !o && setOpen(null)}
				scope="Everyone in TwoUX"
				onAuthorise={() => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1000))}
				onDone={() => open && setList((l) => l.map((c) => (c.id === open.id ? { ...c, connected: true, problem: undefined } : c)))}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Connected tools
- Agent permissions
- Provider logo
- Empty state
- Confirmation dialog
