# Code block

Shows code, commands, IDs or log output exactly as written, so people can read and copy it. Inline Code marks a token inside a sentence.

Kind: component · Group: Content · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To let people copy a command, token, API key name or snippet exactly.
- To show a change as a diff, with added and removed lines.
- To show tool or agent output, such as a run log, using the small size.
- Inline Code for a prop, token or file name inside a sentence: `bg-surface`, `jobs.json`.

## When not to use

- When people need to edit the text. Use a Text input or the Prompt editor.
- For ordinary values in a table, such as an ID column. Use the mono table cell.
- Inline Code across several lines. Use a code block.

## Structure

1. Header (optional): file name or label
2. Actions: copy button, more if needed
3. Content: lines, with optional numbers
4. Line marks: highlighted, added (+), removed (−)
5. Footer (optional): show more, captions

## Guidelines

- Long single-line commands scroll sideways rather than wrapping, so they stay copyable as one line. Use wrap for prose-like output.
- Past about nine lines, cap the height and offer Show more in the footer.
- Without a header, the copy button floats top right and appears on hover or focus, and always on touch screens.
- Line numbers are optional, never copied and hidden from screen readers.
- Use the destructive variant for errors and failed output.
- Light border, grey fill: the block is read, not raised, so it takes no shadow.

## Content

- Label the header with the file name or what the code is: “twoux.css”, “Install”, “Run log”.
- Show code exactly as it should be typed. No ellipses inside commands.

## Accessibility

- The scrolling area is focusable (tabindex 0) so keyboard users can scroll it.
- Added and removed lines show + and − as well as colour.
- Copying announces “Copied” through a status message without moving focus; focus stays on the button.
- Wrapping is available so long output does not force two-dimensional scrolling at 320px.
- Code text keeps 4.5:1 on the grey fill; line numbers use ink-3 (5.4:1 on surface-2).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the code area, then the copy button |
| Arrow keys | Scroll the code area when it has focus |
| Enter or Space | Copy, when the copy button has focus |

## Examples

### command

```tsx
import { CodeBlock, CodeBlockActions, CodeBlockContent, CodeBlockCopyButton } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Command", description: "One line, no header. Copy appears on hover or focus. Long commands scroll instead of wrapping.", order: 2 };

const cmd = "pnpm add @twoux/ui && pnpm llm";

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<CodeBlock className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<CodeBlockActions floating>
				<CodeBlockCopyButton value={cmd} />
			</CodeBlockActions>
			<CodeBlockContent code={`$ ${cmd}`} />
		</CodeBlock>
	);
}
```

### diff

```tsx
import { CodeBlock, CodeBlockContent, CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockTitle } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Diff", description: "Added and removed lines carry + and − as well as colour, so the change is clear without colour.", order: 3 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<CodeBlock className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<CodeBlockHeader>
				<CodeBlockTitle>Suggested change · listing title</CodeBlockTitle>
			</CodeBlockHeader>
			<CodeBlockContent code={`title: "Operations Coordinator"\ntitle: "Junior Operations Coordinator"\nteam: "Operations"`} removed={[1]} added={[2]} />
		</CodeBlock>
	);
}
```

### file

```tsx
import { CodeBlock, CodeBlockActions, CodeBlockContent, CodeBlockCopyButton, CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockTitle } from "@twoux/ui";
import { FileCode2 } from "lucide-react";
// twoux-check-disable raw-colour: the colours are code sample text, not styles

export const meta = { title: "With file name", description: "The header names what the code is. Copy sits at the end of the header.", order: 1 };

const code = `@theme {
  --color-primary: var(--color-indigo-600);
  --color-line: var(--color-neutral-100);
  --shadow-card: 0 1px 2px rgb(23 23 40 / 0.04);
}`;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<CodeBlock className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<CodeBlockHeader>
				<CodeBlockTitle icon={<FileCode2 />}>twoux.css</CodeBlockTitle>
				<CodeBlockActions>
					<CodeBlockCopyButton value={code} />
				</CodeBlockActions>
			</CodeBlockHeader>
			<CodeBlockContent code={code} lineNumbers highlight={[2]} />
		</CodeBlock>
	);
}
```

### inline

```tsx
import { Code } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Inline", description: "For a token, prop or file inside a sentence. It never breaks mid-token.", order: 5 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<p className="max-w-md text-base text-ink">
			Style only with role tokens such as <Code>bg-surface</Code> and <Code>text-ink-2</Code>, defined in <Code>twoux.css</Code>.
		</p>
	);
}
```

### output

```tsx
import { CodeBlock, CodeBlockContent, CodeBlockFooter, CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockTitle } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Run output and errors", description: "Small size for agent and tool output. The destructive variant marks a failed run.", order: 4 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-3">
			<CodeBlock size="sm">
				<CodeBlockHeader>
					<CodeBlockTitle>Run log · Rename low performers</CodeBlockTitle>
				</CodeBlockHeader>
				<CodeBlockContent code={"09:00:02  Found 2 listings under 3%\n09:00:05  Drafted 2 titles\n09:00:05  Waiting for approval"} />
			</CodeBlock>
			<CodeBlock size="sm" variant="destructive">
				<CodeBlockContent code={"09:00:07  Could not reach twoux.co.uk/jobs (timeout after 10s)"} wrap />
				<CodeBlockFooter>Try again from the run, or check the careers page link.</CodeBlockFooter>
			</CodeBlock>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Text input
- Toast

# Card

A white container that groups one object or one task, such as a settings section, a sign-in form or a summary, with an optional header, actions and footer.

Kind: component · Group: Content · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To group the fields and actions of one settings section or one form, so it reads as one unit.
- To show one summary of an object, such as a listing's status and owner, on a page that holds several.

## When not to use

- For rows of a list or table. Use the List table; cards break scanning and comparison across rows.
- Inside another card. Use a Separator or a heading to divide the content instead.
- To make text stand out. Use a Banner for a condition, or plain hierarchy.

## Structure

1. Container: white, light edge, 6px corners, resting shadow
2. Header: title and optional description
3. Action (optional): one button or menu, top right
4. Content
5. Footer (optional): actions on the right, or a tinted band with one secondary line

## Guidelines

- One card is one object or one task. If the content splits into two jobs, use two cards.
- Keep the header short: a title, an optional one-line description, and at most one action on the right.
- Put primary actions in the footer, right-aligned, with the main action last.
- Use the footer band for a single secondary line, such as “Already have an account? Sign in”.
- Cards on a white page keep their edge; cards on the grey app background can drop the shadow but keep the edge.

## Content

- Title in sentence case naming the object or task: “Notifications”, “Salary bands”.
- The description says what the section controls, not how to use the card.

## Accessibility

- When a card holds a section, give the title a real heading element at the right level, so it appears in the heading list.
- Do not make the whole card clickable when it contains other controls; link the title instead, so each target has one purpose.
- The card edge is decorative; the content does not rely on it to be understood.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves through the card's own controls in reading order; the card itself is not a stop |

## Examples

### settings

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, SwitchField } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Settings section", description: "One card, one task. The title names it, the description says what it controls, and the footer holds the save action on the right.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<Card className="w-full max-w-md">
			<CardHeader>
				<CardTitle>Applicant emails</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Choose when hiring managers hear about new applicants.</CardDescription>
				<CardAction>
					<Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Reset</Button>
				</CardAction>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent className="grid gap-3">
				<SwitchField id="email-each" label="Each new applicant" defaultChecked />
				<SwitchField id="email-digest" label="Daily digest at 9:00" />
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter className="justify-end gap-2 border-t pt-4">
				<Button variant="outline" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
				<Button size="sm">Save</Button>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	);
}
```

### sign-in

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, FieldSeparator, TextField } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Sign in, with a footer band", description: "The band holds one secondary line, apart from the main action. The labelled separator divides the two ways in.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<Card className="w-full max-w-sm">
			<CardHeader className="text-center">
				<CardTitle>Sign in to TwoUX Hiring</CardTitle>
				<CardDescription>Welcome back. Sign in to continue.</CardDescription>
			</CardHeader>
			<CardContent className="grid gap-4">
				<Button variant="outline" className="w-full">Continue with Google</Button>
				<FieldSeparator>or</FieldSeparator>
				<TextField id="signin-email" label="Work email" type="email" placeholder="name@company.co.uk" />
				<Button className="w-full">Continue</Button>
			</CardContent>
			<CardFooter band>
				Don't have an account?&nbsp;<a href="#signup" className="font-medium text-primary-ink hover:underline">Sign up</a>
			</CardFooter>
		</Card>
	);
}
```

# Separator

A thin line that divides groups of content or menu items. With a label, it separates two ways of doing the same thing, such as “or”.

Kind: component · Group: Content · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To divide groups inside a card, panel or menu when spacing alone is not enough.
- With a label, between two routes to the same result: “or” between sign in with Google and the email form.

## When not to use

- Between every row or field. Use spacing; lines everywhere add noise.
- To separate sections of a page. Use headings and space.

## Structure

1. Line: 1px, light edge colour
2. Label (optional): short word centred on the line, on the surface colour

## Guidelines

- Prefer space first. Add a line only where groups would otherwise run together.
- Keep the label to one or two words in lower case: “or”, “or continue with”.
- Lines run the full width of their container, or align with the content inset in menus.

## Content

- Label in lower case with no full stop: “or”.

## Accessibility

- A purely visual line is decorative, so screen readers skip it. Mark it as a separator only when it divides a menu or a toolbar.
- The label is real text, so it is read in order between the two groups.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| None | Not focusable |

## Examples

### plain-and-labelled

```tsx
import { FieldSeparator, Separator } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Plain and labelled", description: "A plain line divides groups when space alone is not enough. A labelled one sits between two routes to the same result.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-6">
			<div className="grid gap-3 rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-4">
				<div className="grid gap-0.5">
					<span className="text-base font-medium text-ink">Senior Product Designer</span>
					<span className="text-sm text-ink-3">Leeds · Hybrid</span>
				</div>
				<Separator />
				<div className="flex justify-between text-base text-ink-2">
					<span>Applicants</span>
					<span className="tabular text-ink">38</span>
				</div>
			</div>
			<FieldSeparator>or</FieldSeparator>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Card
- Dropdown menu

# Timestamp

One component for every date and time in the product: relative or absolute display, the exact value on hover and focus, and an optional "by" source.

Kind: component · Group: Content · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Every time a date or time appears: table columns, side panel details, activity, Inbox items, "Last updated" after a refresh.
- format="relative" for recent past events in lists; format="absolute" for details and deadlines; format="iso" for code and exports.
- source="Priya Shah" when it matters who made the change, such as Last edited on a listing.

## When not to use

- For date entry. Use a date input.
- For durations, such as "Time to hire: 18 days"; that is a number with a unit, not a timestamp.
- For a date with no time that is a property of the record, such as a start date. Show it as an absolute date.

## Structure

1. Optional label, when not given by a column header or key: "Last edited"
2. Value: relative ("3 hours ago") or absolute ("6 November 2026, 14:32 GMT")
3. Optional source: "by Priya Shah", linked to the profile, with "via Assistant" when applied from a proposal
4. Tooltip with the absolute value on hover and focus

## Guidelines

- Renders a <time> element with the ISO 8601 value in datetime.
- Relative values tick over once a minute; they never animate or announce.
- Time zone is the viewer's own and is always shown on absolute values.
- In compact table cells, `short` shows "3h ago" or "20 Nov"; the tooltip and accessible name keep the full form.
- Future deadlines use absolute dates, optionally followed by relative time in muted text.
- Give deadlines, start dates and due dates as a date with no time (2026-12-07). They show as 7 December 2026, with no time or zone, and fall on the same day in every time zone.

## Content

- Relative: "Just now", "5 minutes ago", "3 hours ago", "2 days ago", "In 3 days".
- Absolute: day, month in full, year, 24-hour time, zone: "6 November 2026, 14:32 GMT".
- Source: "Edited 6 hours ago by Priya Shah".

## Accessibility

- The accessible description carries the absolute value, so screen reader users don't need the tooltip.
- The tooltip appears on focus of the cell or link that contains the timestamp, without adding a separate tab stop.
- Never put a ticking relative time in a live region.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab or arrows (to the containing cell or link) | Show the absolute time tooltip |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |
| Tab (to a source link) | Move to the person's profile link |

## Examples

### times

```tsx
import { Timestamp } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Relative, short and absolute", description: "Relative in lists, with the full date and time zone on hover or focus. Short units in compact cells. Deadlines are always absolute.", order: 1 };

const ago = (m: number) => new Date(Date.now() - m * 60000);

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<dl className="grid grid-cols-[160px_1fr] gap-x-4 gap-y-2 text-base">
			<dt className="text-ink-2">Last edited</dt><dd><Timestamp value={ago(180)} by={<a href="#priya" className="font-medium text-primary-ink hover:underline">Priya Shah</a>} /></dd>
			<dt className="text-ink-2">In a table cell</dt><dd><Timestamp value={ago(60 * 26)} short /></dd>
			<dt className="text-ink-2">Closing date</dt><dd><Timestamp value="2026-12-04T17:00:00Z" format="absolute" /></dd>
			<dt className="text-ink-2">Applied via Assistant</dt><dd><Timestamp value={ago(12)} by={<span>Tom Becker via Assistant</span>} /></dd>
		</dl>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Timestamps
- List table
- Side panel (drawer)
- Tooltip
- Unsaved changes

# Provider logo

The official mark of a service people sign in with or connect, shown unaltered on a white tile beside the service's name.

Kind: component · Group: Content · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Identifying a service someone signs in with, such as Google or Microsoft.
- Identifying a service someone connects, such as Slack or Google Drive, in a list or a connection dialog.

## When not to use

- Marking a competitor or a product we studied as a reference. Those get a text name only.
- Decoration, avatars or a stand-in for our own brand. Use Avatar (avatar) for people and the product mark for us.
- Logos of services that are not connectable. A mark implies the connection exists.

## Structure

1. Tile (white in both themes, hairline border)
2. Official mark (unaltered)
3. Name or label beside it

## Guidelines

- Use the official mark only for third-party services people sign in with or connect. Never for competitors or reference products.
- Show the mark unaltered: no recolouring, no cropping, no effects, no new background shapes.
- Put the mark beside the service's name. When it stands alone, give it a label so the service is still named.
- Keep the tile white in light and dark themes so dark marks, such as GitHub and Notion, stay visible.
- To add a provider, add a line to the list in scripts/provider-logos.mjs and run node scripts/provider-logos.mjs. Check the brand's own page for permitted use first.
- The icon sources are licensed for reuse: Iconify's logos set is CC0, vscode-icons and thesvg-color are MIT. Trademarks stay with their owners, so show a mark only to identify that service.

## Content

- "Continue with Google" and "Connect Slack": the name is always in words, never only in the mark.
- When alone, label it with the service name only, for example "Google Drive".

## Accessibility

- Beside a visible name the mark is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Alone, it has role="img" and an aria-label with the service name (SC 1.1.1).
- The tile keeps the mark's edges distinct from either theme (SC 1.4.11).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| None | Not focusable. The button or row that contains it is the focus stop. |

## Examples

### alone-and-sizes

```tsx
import { ProviderLogo } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Alone, with a label", description: "When the mark has no name beside it, give it a label. Three sizes; the mark inside is never changed.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
			<ProviderLogo provider="slack" size="sm" label="Slack" />
			<ProviderLogo provider="slack" size="md" label="Slack" />
			<ProviderLogo provider="slack" size="lg" label="Slack" />
		</div>
	);
}
```

### beside-name

```tsx
import { PROVIDERS, ProviderLogo, type ProviderId } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Beside the name", description: "The mark identifies the service and the name says it. On a white tile in both themes, so dark marks stay visible.", order: 1 };

const SHOWN: ProviderId[] = ["google", "microsoft", "github", "slack", "notion", "google-drive"];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ul className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-1">
			{SHOWN.map((p) => (
				<li key={p} className="flex items-center gap-3 rounded-xs px-1 py-1.5">
					<ProviderLogo provider={p} />
					<span className="text-base text-ink">{PROVIDERS[p].label}</span>
				</li>
			))}
		</ul>
	);
}
```

- Connector picker
- Sign in
- Connected tools
- Avatar and avatar stack

# Toast

A short, non-blocking confirmation of something the person just did, with Undo when the action can be reversed.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Confirm an action the person just took in the current view, such as publishing, extending or closing a listing.
- Offer Undo right after a reversible change, so the change can go ahead without a confirmation dialog.
- Confirm accelerated actions done by keyboard (T, D, E, ⇧C), where the person has no other visual cue that the key worked.

## When not to use

- Errors and anything the person must act on. Use an Error state in place, or a Banner on the page.
- Events the person did not cause, such as an agent finishing or a listing about to close. Send them to the Inbox.
- When the result is already visible on screen and there is nothing else to know, show nothing.
- Irreversible, high-impact actions. Ask first with a Confirmation dialog.

## Structure

1. Status icon (check for success)
2. Title: what happened, past tense
3. Optional body: which record, one line
4. Undo button (ghost, small)
5. Live region container (role="status")

## Guidelines

- Place the toast at the bottom right, 16px from the edges, at most 340px wide, on a solid white surface. It rises above the focused element and anything marked data-toast-avoid, such as a sticky footer, so it never covers them.
- Show one toast at a time. A new toast replaces the one on screen rather than stacking.
- Hide it after 6 seconds. Pause the timer while the pointer is over the toast or focus is inside it.
- Allow one action only, and only Undo. Never put a Close or Cancel button next to it.
- Undo must also be reachable without the toast: ⌘Z undoes the last action for as long as the record allows.
- Never move focus to the toast. The person keeps working where they were.

## Content

- Title in past tense saying what happened: "Listing published", "Snoozed until Mon 9:00".
- Name the record in the body when the title alone is ambiguous: "Junior Product Designer is now live."
- Sentence case, UK spelling, one short sentence, no exclamation marks and no "successfully".
- Do not apologise or thank. Say the outcome and stop.

## Accessibility

- Render toasts into a role="status" live region that already exists in the DOM, so screen readers announce them without moving focus (4.1.3).
- Because Undo disappears with the toast, the same undo is available through ⌘Z and the record's activity, which meets the intent of 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable.
- The toast must not hide the focused element: TwoUX's Toaster measures the focused element and any data-toast-avoid element in its corner and moves up above them (2.4.11).
- Do not rely on the green check alone: the title says the outcome in words (1.4.1).
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion: the toast appears without sliding when motion is reduced (2.3.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘Z | Undo the last action, whether or not the toast is still visible |
| Tab | Reaches the Undo button while the toast is shown; the timer pauses while focus is inside |

## Examples

### undo

```tsx
import { Button, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Confirm with Undo", description: "Close a listing. The toast says what happened, offers Undo, and leaves in 6 seconds. ⌘Z undoes it too, even after the toast has gone.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);

	const reopen = () => {
		setOpen(true);
		toast.success("Listing reopened", { description: "Senior Product Designer, Leeds" });
	};

	const close = () => {
		setOpen(false);
		toast.success("Listing closed", {
			description: "Senior Product Designer, Leeds",
			action: { label: "Undo", onClick: reopen },
		});
	};

	// Undo stays reachable without the toast
	useEffect(() => {
		const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
			if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "z" && !open) {
				e.preventDefault();
				reopen();
			}
		};
		window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
		return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
	});

	return (
		<div className="flex w-full max-w-md items-center justify-between rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface px-3 py-2.5">
			<div className="grid">
				<span className="text-base font-medium text-ink">Senior Product Designer</span>
				<span className="text-sm text-ink-3">Leeds · {open ? "Open" : "Closed"}</span>
			</div>
			<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={open ? close : reopen}>
				{open ? "Close listing" : "Reopen"}
			</Button>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Banner (inline alert)
- Confirmation dialog
- Inbox (triage)
- Notifications vs inbox vs toast
- Error state (failed to load)

# Banner (inline alert)

A persistent message inside the page about a condition that affects what the person is looking at, with at most one action.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A condition on the current page that stays true until it is resolved, such as "Two listings expire this week."
- Something blocks a task until fixed, such as form errors before Publish.
- Data-loss or connection problems that affect the whole page. These may sit above the page header.

## When not to use

- Confirming an action the person just took. Use a Toast.
- Background events that need someone to act later. Use the Inbox.
- A whole region failed to load. Use the Error state in place of that region.
- Feature announcements or tips. Leave them out, or put them in the setup checklist in the sidebar.

## Structure

1. Icon (info, warning or error)
2. Message: one sentence
3. Dismiss (ghost), only when nothing is blocked
4. One action (secondary button), such as Review
5. Form variant: error strip with count and "Go to first" link

## Guidelines

- Place the banner in context: above the table it refers to, or above the submit button for form problems.
- Show one banner per region. If several apply, order them from most to least severe.
- Offer Dismiss only when nothing is blocked and no action is required. Condition banners clear themselves when the condition ends.
- At most one action, as a secondary button on the right. Dismiss sits before it as a ghost button.
- Use neutral styling for information and keep red for errors that stop the task.
- The form error strip counts the problems and links to the first one: "2 fields need fixing before you can publish. Go to first".

## Content

- Say what is true and what to do: the condition, then a verb on the button ("Review").
- One or two short sentences, sentence case, no title when one sentence is enough.
- For errors, say what went wrong and how to recover, without blaming the person.
- No apologies, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Information banners that appear after load sit in a polite live region; the form error strip uses role="alert" because it reports a blocking problem (4.1.3).
- The icon is never the only cue: the sentence states severity in words, and the icon has an accessible label (1.4.1).
- Errors name the field and describe the problem in text, and "Go to first" moves focus to it (3.3.1).
- A banner must not be sticky over content in a way that hides the focused element (2.4.11).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Reaches Dismiss, then the action |
| Enter | Activates the focused button or the "Go to first" link |

## Examples

### states

```tsx
import { Alert, AlertAction, AlertDescription, AlertTitle, Button } from "@twoux/ui";
import { CircleAlert, Info, TriangleAlert } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Information, warning and error", description: "Information is neutral and can be dismissed. A warning names one next step. An error that blocks publishing counts the problems and links to the first.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [showInfo, setShowInfo] = useState(true);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-3">
			{showInfo && (
				<Alert>
					<Info />
					<AlertTitle>Salary bands were updated on 3 November.</AlertTitle>
					<AlertAction>
						<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setShowInfo(false)}>Dismiss</Button>
					</AlertAction>
				</Alert>
			)}
			<Alert variant="warning">
				<TriangleAlert />
				<AlertTitle>4 listings close this week with no applicants.</AlertTitle>
				<AlertAction>
					<Button variant="outline" size="sm">Review</Button>
				</AlertAction>
			</Alert>
			<Alert variant="destructive">
				<CircleAlert />
				<AlertTitle>2 fields need fixing before you can publish.</AlertTitle>
				<AlertDescription>
					<a href="#salary" className="font-medium text-ink underline decoration-bad-line underline-offset-2 hover:decoration-bad">Go to first</a>
				</AlertDescription>
			</Alert>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Toast
- Error state (failed to load)
- Notifications vs inbox vs toast
- Page header

# Confirmation dialog

A modal question before an irreversible or high-impact action, stating the consequence and offering the safe option first.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Before actions that cannot be undone or that affect other people, such as closing listings that stop taking applications.
- Bulk actions on many records where a mistake is costly to repair.
- When the person must read a consequence they could not otherwise see, such as what happens to existing applicants.

## When not to use

- Reversible actions. Do them at once and offer Undo in a Toast.
- Collecting lots of input or showing a record. Use the Side panel.
- Reporting an error. Use a Banner or the Error state in place.
- Low-risk actions that are easy to redo, which need no confirmation at all.

## Structure

1. Title: a question naming the action and count ("Close 2 listings?")
2. Body: the consequence, and what is kept
3. Footer: safe secondary button ("Keep open")
4. Footer: destructive button named after the action ("Close listings")

## Guidelines

- Width up to 420px, centred, with the page dimmed behind it. One dialog at a time; never open a dialog from a dialog.
- Footer buttons sit on the right: the safe option first, the destructive action last in the destructive colour.
- On open, focus goes to the safe button, so Enter cannot destroy anything by accident.
- Esc and the safe button both close it with no change. On close, focus returns to the control that opened it.
- For the most dangerous, rare actions, require an unusual step such as typing the listing name.
- After confirming, report the result with a Toast.

## Content

- Title as a specific question with the verb and the object: "Close 2 listings?", never "Are you sure?".
- Body states the consequence and what stays: "They stop taking applications now. The 140 people who already applied stay in your pipeline."
- Buttons name the outcome ("Keep open", "Close listings"), never Yes, No or OK.
- The confirm label matches the title's verb.

## Accessibility

- Use role="alertdialog" with aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby on the title and aria-describedby on the consequence.
- Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the dialog; Esc closes it, so focus is contained but never trapped (2.1.2).
- Focus returns to the opener on close, or to the next logical row if the opener was removed (2.4.3).
- Confirming before data changes is one of the three ways to meet 3.3.4 Error Prevention.
- The destructive button is identified by its label, not only its red colour (1.4.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / ⇧Tab | Move between the two buttons, wrapping inside the dialog |
| Enter | Activates the focused button (the safe one on open) |
| Esc | Closes without changing anything |

## Examples

### close-listings

```tsx
import { AlertDialog, AlertDialogAction, AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogTrigger, Button, toast } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Close listings", description: "Closing removes listings from job boards and cannot be undone. Focus starts on the safe button, so Enter keeps them open. Esc does the same.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<AlertDialog>
			<AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
				<Button variant="outline">Close 2 listings</Button>
			</AlertDialogTrigger>
			<AlertDialogContent>
				<AlertDialogHeader>
					<AlertDialogTitle>Close 2 listings?</AlertDialogTitle>
					<AlertDialogDescription>They come off every job board today. Applicants and notes are kept, but the listings cannot be reopened.</AlertDialogDescription>
				</AlertDialogHeader>
				<AlertDialogFooter>
					<AlertDialogCancel>Keep open</AlertDialogCancel>
					<AlertDialogAction variant="destructive" onClick={() => toast.success("2 listings closed")}>Close listings</AlertDialogAction>
				</AlertDialogFooter>
			</AlertDialogContent>
		</AlertDialog>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Toast
- Side panel (drawer)
- Shortcut sheet (?)

# Empty state

What a list, table or panel shows when it loaded correctly but has nothing to show, with the next step.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Filters or search match nothing: "No listings match these filters".
- Nothing has been created yet, such as a team with no listings.
- A queue is cleared, such as the Inbox: "All caught up".

## When not to use

- Data is still loading. Use the Loading skeleton.
- Loading failed. Use the Error state, never an empty message.
- Only part of a record is missing, such as one field. Show "Add" in the field itself.

## Structure

1. Icon tile (32px, neutral)
2. Title: the state, sentence case, no full stop
3. Description: why, and what to try (max 36 characters wide per line block)
4. One action (secondary button), or none for a finished state
5. Dashed container sized to the region it replaces

## Guidelines

- Replace the region that would hold the data, inside the same container, so filters and the result count stay in place.
- Distinguish no data (nothing created) from no results (filters too narrow); they need different actions.
- Give one next step: Clear filters for no results, the create action for no data. Never leave a dead end.
- Keep the result count visible ("0 of 24") so the person sees the filters, not the data, caused the empty view.
- Show the empty state only after loading finishes; never as placeholder text that is later replaced.

## Content

- Title names the state plainly and briefly: "No listings match these filters".
- Description says why and what to try, without repeating the title: "Try a wider date range, or clear the location filter."
- Button label starts with a verb and matches the next step: "Clear filters", "New listing".
- Neutral tone for no results; a short positive line for a finished queue. No jokes, no apologies.

## Accessibility

- Replace the whole table, headers included, so screen readers do not read an empty structure first (1.3.1).
- When filtering produces zero results, announce the new count through a polite live region (4.1.3).
- The icon is decorative and has empty alt text.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Reaches the single action |
| F | Opens the filter picker to change filters instead of clearing them |

## Examples

### no-data

```tsx
import { Button, Empty, EmptyContent, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle } from "@twoux/ui";
import { BriefcaseBusiness, Plus } from "lucide-react";

export const meta = { title: "No data yet", description: "Nothing has been created. The one action is the create action, not Clear filters.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<Empty className="w-full max-w-xl">
			<EmptyHeader>
				<EmptyMedia variant="icon"><BriefcaseBusiness /></EmptyMedia>
				<EmptyTitle>No listings yet</EmptyTitle>
				<EmptyDescription>Listings you publish appear here, with their applicants.</EmptyDescription>
			</EmptyHeader>
			<EmptyContent>
				<Button variant="outline" size="sm"><Plus />New listing</Button>
			</EmptyContent>
		</Empty>
	);
}
```

### no-results

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, Empty, EmptyContent, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle } from "@twoux/ui";
import { SearchX, X } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "No results", description: "Filters are too narrow. The empty state replaces the table only; the filters and the count stay, so it is clear the filters caused it. One action: Clear filters.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [filtered, setFiltered] = useState(true);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-2">
			<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
				<span className="text-base font-medium text-ink">Listings</span>
				{filtered && (
					<Badge variant="secondary" className="gap-1">
						Location: Inverness
						<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-xs" aria-label="Remove filter Location: Inverness" onClick={() => setFiltered(false)} className="-mr-1 size-4"><X className="size-3" /></Button>
					</Badge>
				)}
				<span className="ml-auto text-sm text-ink-3 tabular">{filtered ? "0 of 24" : "24 of 24"}</span>
			</div>
			{filtered ? (
				<Empty className="min-h-56">
					<EmptyHeader>
						<EmptyMedia variant="icon"><SearchX /></EmptyMedia>
						<EmptyTitle>No listings match these filters</EmptyTitle>
						<EmptyDescription>Try another location, or clear the filters to see all 24.</EmptyDescription>
					</EmptyHeader>
					<EmptyContent>
						<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setFiltered(false)}>Clear filters</Button>
					</EmptyContent>
				</Empty>
			) : (
				<div className="grid min-h-56 place-items-center rounded-sm border border-line text-base text-ink-2">24 listings</div>
			)}
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Loading skeleton
- Error state (failed to load)
- Inbox (triage)
- Setup checklist

# Loading skeleton

Grey placeholder rows that keep the table or panel's shape while data loads.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- First load of a table, list or panel whose layout is known.
- Loads that take roughly 1 to 10 seconds.
- Several parts of a view load at once and each can fill in as it arrives.

## When not to use

- Loads under 1 second. Show nothing and render the data.
- A single action in progress, such as Apply or Run. Use the button's inline spinner.
- Work over 10 seconds or with known progress, such as an agent run. Use a progress indicator with a count ("2 / 5").
- Popovers, menus, toasts or dialogs, whose content should already be loaded.

## Structure

1. Region header kept ("Loading listings…")
2. Skeleton rows at the real row height (36px)
3. Bars per column: checkbox, title, secondary, right-aligned figure
4. Shimmer animation (off with reduced motion)

## Guidelines

- Match the real layout: same row height, same column positions, varied bar widths so it reads as text, numbers on the right.
- Keep the header, filters and page actions live; only the data region shows the skeleton.
- Replace the skeleton as soon as data arrives, section by section where possible.
- Never combine a skeleton with a spinner in the same region.
- Shimmer runs at 1.4 s per cycle and stops when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
- If loading fails, swap to the Error state in the same space.

## Content

- The region header says what is loading, short, without articles: "Loading listings…".
- No other text inside the skeleton; it holds space, it does not explain.
- Never rely on a bare "Loading…" message alone for longer waits; the skeleton shows where the data will appear, and long runs show a count.

## Accessibility

- Mark the region aria-busy while loading and give it a label ("Loading listings"); skeleton bars are hidden from assistive technology.
- Do not announce every load; announce only the result, such as the row count, through a polite live region (4.1.3).
- Shimmer shown next to usable content must stop within 5 seconds or be pausable; TwoUX's reduced-motion setting stops it (2.2.2, 2.3.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| None | No keyboard interaction; filters and page actions stay usable while it loads |

## Examples

### table

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Table rows", description: "Rows keep the real 36px height and column positions. Bars vary in width so they read as text; the figure sits on the right. The header stays live.", order: 1 };

const WIDTHS = ["w-40", "w-52", "w-36", "w-48", "w-44"];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-xl overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface" aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading listings">
			<div className="grid h-9 grid-cols-[16px_1fr_96px_64px] items-center gap-3 border-b border-line bg-surface-2 px-3 text-sm font-medium text-ink-2">
				<span />
				<span>Listing</span>
				<span>Location</span>
				<span className="text-right">Applicants</span>
			</div>
			{WIDTHS.map((w, i) => (
				<div key={w + i} className="grid h-9 grid-cols-[16px_1fr_96px_64px] items-center gap-3 border-b border-line px-3 last:border-b-0">
					<Skeleton className="size-3.5" />
					<Skeleton className={`h-2.5 ${w}`} />
					<Skeleton className="h-2.5 w-16" />
					<Skeleton className="ml-auto h-2.5 w-6" />
				</div>
			))}
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Empty state
- Error state (failed to load)
- Side panel (drawer)

# Error state (failed to load)

Shown in place of a region that failed to load: what failed, that nothing was lost, and Try again.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A table, list, chart or panel could not fetch its data.
- Only one region fails while the rest of the page works; the error stays inside that region.
- The person lacks permission to see a region's data.

## When not to use

- An action failed (save, extend, close). Show a Banner near the action and keep the person's input.
- Field validation. Use the inline field error and the form error strip (Banner).
- Nothing matched the filters. That is an Empty state, not an error.

## Structure

1. Region header kept ("Listings")
2. Icon tile in the error colour
3. Title: what failed ("Couldn't load listings")
4. Description: why if known, and what is kept
5. Try again button (secondary) with its shortcut R
6. Optional: expandable technical details

## Guidelines

- Replace only the failed region, at the same size, so the header, filters and other regions stay usable.
- Keep the person's filters, sort and selection; say so in the message.
- Offer one action, Try again, which re-runs the same request.
- Retrying swaps back to the Loading skeleton, then to data or the error again.
- Put raw error codes in an expandable details section, never in the main message.

## Content

- Title says what failed in plain words: "Couldn't load listings".
- Description says why if known and what is safe: "The server didn't respond. Your filters are kept."
- Take ownership; never imply the person caused it.
- No apologies, jokes or exclamation marks. Do not promise that a team has been told unless that is true.

## Accessibility

- The error is identified in text, not only by the red icon (3.3.1, 1.4.1).
- Announce the failure once through a live region; do not move focus unless the person triggered the load (4.1.3).
- After Try again succeeds, keep focus on a stable element such as the region header, not on the removed button (2.4.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| R | Try again (single-key shortcut, can be turned off) |
| Tab / Enter | Reach and activate Try again |

## Examples

### table

```tsx
import { Button, Empty, EmptyContent, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle, Skeleton } from "@twoux/ui";
import { CircleAlert } from "lucide-react";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Table failed to load", description: "Only the table is replaced; the header stays. Try again (or R) swaps back to the skeleton, then to the data or the error. Technical details stay folded away.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
	const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
	const retry = useCallback(() => {
		setLoading(true);
		setTimeout(() => setLoading(false), 1200);
	}, []);

	// R retries while focus is inside this region and not in a text field
	useEffect(() => {
		const el = ref.current;
		const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
			if (e.key.toLowerCase() === "r" && !e.metaKey && !e.ctrlKey && !loading && !(e.target as HTMLElement).closest("input, textarea")) retry();
		};
		el?.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
		return () => el?.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
	}, [loading, retry]);

	return (
		<div ref={ref} className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-2">
			<span className="text-base font-medium text-ink">Listings</span>
			{loading ? (
				<div className="grid min-h-56 content-start gap-0 overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line" aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading listings">
					{["w-40", "w-52", "w-36", "w-48", "w-44", "w-32"].map((w) => (
						<div key={w} className="flex h-9 items-center gap-3 border-b border-line px-3 last:border-b-0">
							<Skeleton className={`h-2.5 ${w}`} />
							<Skeleton className="ml-auto h-2.5 w-6" />
						</div>
					))}
				</div>
			) : (
				<Empty className="min-h-56 border-solid border-line">
					<EmptyHeader>
						<EmptyMedia variant="error"><CircleAlert /></EmptyMedia>
						<EmptyTitle>Couldn't load listings</EmptyTitle>
						<EmptyDescription>The server took too long to reply. Your filters are kept.</EmptyDescription>
					</EmptyHeader>
					<EmptyContent>
						<Button variant="outline" size="sm" shortcut="R" onClick={retry}>Try again</Button>
						<details className="text-sm text-ink-3">
							<summary className="cursor-pointer rounded-xs hover:text-ink-2">Technical details</summary>
							<code className="mt-1 block font-mono">504 Gateway Timeout · GET /listings · req 7f3a91</code>
						</details>
					</EmptyContent>
				</Empty>
			)}
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Loading skeleton
- Empty state
- Banner (inline alert)
- Toast

# Side panel (drawer)

A panel on the right that shows the selected row's detail beside the table, in push (default) or overlay mode; 440px by default and resizable from 360px to half the canvas in push mode.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Viewing or editing one record while the list stays in view, such as a listing's figures beside the listings table.
- Working down a list one record at a time: J and K move the selection and the panel follows.
- Secondary tasks that should not take the person off the page, such as the Assistant's quick questions.

## When not to use

- The full picture of one record, with history and long sections. Open the full page (⇧↵).
- A decision that must interrupt the task. Use a Confirmation dialog.
- Confirming an action. Use a Toast.
- Comparing many records side by side. Use the table with the chosen columns.

## Structure

1. Control bar without a title: previous, next, position ("3 of 9"), open full page, close
2. Record ID, title and status line
3. Tabs (Overview, Candidates, Activity)
4. Sections split by full-width rules, each with a 13px heading and one action on the right
5. Empty fields show "Add"
6. Pinned footer: destructive action left, primary right

## Guidelines

- Push mode (default) on list pages: the table narrows so filters, page actions and the first columns stay usable and nothing is hidden behind the panel.
- Overlay mode when the page is narrower than about 1100px, or for wide content (dashboards, wide tables) that pushing would crush. The first columns stay visible.
- One component with mode="push" | "overlay"; the person can switch with ⇧P and the choice is remembered.
- Opens only from a person's action (Enter or a click on a row), never on its own.
- Esc closes it and focus returns to the row it came from.
- Do not repeat table header actions inside the panel; the footer holds actions for this record only.
- Below 860px the panel takes the full width of the canvas.
- A panel for one thing, such as settings or a form, has its title in the 44px header bar, with the object it belongs to beside it in muted text (Table settings · People) and Close on the right. A record panel that steps through a list keeps previous, next and the position in the bar, and shows the record's name and status under it.

## Content

- The control bar has no title; the record's own title sits below it, matching the row the person picked.
- Section headings are short nouns ("Performance", "Funnel", "Details") with one action each.
- Empty fields say "Add" and the field name rather than a dash, so the gap is an invitation, not an error.
- Figures sit next to a comparison ("vs board median") so a number can be judged without leaving.

## Accessibility

- The panel is a non-modal complementary region with a label; it does not trap focus, so J/K keep driving the table (2.1.2).
- In overlay mode the panel must not cover the focused row; the table scrolls the active row into the visible part (2.4.11).
- Tabs inside the panel follow the APG tabs pattern with arrow keys between tabs.
- Push and overlay both reflow to a single column at 320px wide without horizontal scrolling of text (1.4.10).
- Focus order inside the panel follows reading order: control bar, title, tabs, sections, footer (2.4.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | Open the panel for the focused row |
| J / K | Next or previous row; the panel follows |
| ⇧↵ | Open the record as a full page |
| ⇧P | Switch between push and overlay |
| Esc | Close the panel and return focus to the row |

## Examples

### record

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, PanelMode, SegmentedControl, Segment, SidePanel, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableRow, Timestamp } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
import { LISTINGS, STATUS_VARIANT } from "../list-table/data";

export const meta = { title: "Record beside the list", description: "Push mode narrows the table so the first columns stay usable; overlay floats over it. J and K move through records with the panel following; Esc closes and focus returns to the row.", order: 1 };

const ROWS = LISTINGS.slice(0, 6);

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState<number | null>(1);
	const [mode, setMode] = useState<PanelMode>("push");
	const rec = open === null ? null : ROWS[open];
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full gap-2">
			<SegmentedControl value={mode} onValueChange={(v) => setMode(v as PanelMode)} size="sm" aria-label="Panel mode" className="justify-self-start">
				<Segment value="push">Push</Segment><Segment value="overlay">Overlay</Segment>
			</SegmentedControl>
			<div className="flex h-96 overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
				<div className="min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-auto">
					<Table aria-label="Listings">
						<TableBody>
							{ROWS.map((l, i) => (
								<TableRow key={l.id} data-state={open === i ? "selected" : undefined} tabIndex={0} onClick={() => setOpen(i)} onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === "Enter") setOpen(i); }} className="cursor-default">
									<TableCell className="font-medium text-ink">{l.role}</TableCell>
									<TableCell className="text-ink-2">{l.location}</TableCell>
									<TableCell><Badge variant={STATUS_VARIANT[l.status]} dot>{l.status}</Badge></TableCell>
								</TableRow>
							))}
						</TableBody>
					</Table>
				</div>
				{rec && (
					<SidePanel
						open={open !== null}
						onOpenChange={(o) => !o && setOpen(null)}
						mode={mode}
						label="Listing details"
						title={rec.role}
						meta={<span className="flex items-center gap-2"><span className="font-mono">{rec.id}</span><Badge variant={STATUS_VARIANT[rec.status]} dot>{rec.status}</Badge></span>}
						position={{ index: open ?? 0, total: ROWS.length }}
						onPrevious={() => setOpen((o) => Math.max(0, (o ?? 0) - 1))}
						onNext={() => setOpen((o) => Math.min(ROWS.length - 1, (o ?? 0) + 1))}
						onOpenFull={() => {}}
						footer={<Button size="sm">Edit listing</Button>}
					>
						<dl className="grid grid-cols-[120px_1fr] gap-x-3 gap-y-2 text-base">
							<dt className="text-ink-2">Location</dt><dd className="text-ink">{rec.location}</dd>
							<dt className="text-ink-2">Applicants</dt><dd className="tabular text-ink">{rec.applicants}</dd>
							<dt className="text-ink-2">Closes</dt><dd><Timestamp value={`${rec.closes}T17:00:00Z`} format="absolute" /></dd>
							<dt className="text-ink-2">Hiring manager</dt><dd><Button variant="link" size="xs">Add</Button></dd>
						</dl>
					</SidePanel>
				)}
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- App shell and sidebar navigation
- Command palette (⌘K)
- Confirmation dialog
- Loading skeleton

# Command palette (⌘K)

A searchable list of actions and destinations, scoped to the current selection, opened with ⌘K from anywhere.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Run any action by name without hunting through menus, especially on a selection of rows.
- Jump to a record or page by typing part of its name.
- Learn shortcuts: every action shows its key, so the palette teaches the faster path.

## When not to use

- As the only way to reach an action. Every command also exists as a visible button or menu item.
- Filtering the table. Use Filter (F) and its type-ahead field list.
- Confirming irreversible actions. A destructive command picked in the palette still opens the Confirmation dialog.

## Structure

1. Search input with a scope chip ("2 listings") and Esc hint
2. Group: Actions on selection, each with its shortcut
3. Group: Go to (records and pages)
4. Footer hints: ↑ ↓ navigate, ↵ run, Tab change scope

## Guidelines

- Opens centred near the top, up to 560px wide, with focus in the search input.
- Scope defaults to the current selection and shows it as a chip; Tab switches to the whole workspace.
- Order results with actions on the selection first, then Go to; show the most used actions before typing.
- Results update with each keystroke, within 400 ms.
- Enter runs the highlighted item and closes the palette; reversible results offer Undo in a toast.
- Esc closes it and focus returns to where it was.

## Content

- Commands start with a verb and name the object: "Extend end by 30 days", "Export 2 rows as CSV".
- Commands that need more input end with an ellipsis: "Extend end to a date…".
- Use the same command names as the buttons and menus they mirror.
- Placeholder text says what can be typed: "Search or run a command".

## Accessibility

- Built as a modal dialog containing a combobox with a listbox popup; DOM focus stays in the input and aria-activedescendant points to the highlighted item.
- Group headings are exposed as group labels and each option's shortcut is part of its accessible description (1.3.1).
- ⌘K uses a modifier, so it stays on when single-key shortcuts are turned off (2.1.4).
- Announce the number of results through a polite live region as the person types (4.1.3).
- Esc always exits; there is no keyboard trap (2.1.2).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘K / Ctrl+K | Open or close the palette |
| ↑ / ↓ | Move through results |
| Enter | Run the highlighted command |
| Tab | Switch scope between selection and workspace |
| Esc | Close and return focus |

## Examples

### dialog

```tsx
import { Button, CommandDialog, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandShortcut, Kbd } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Search, Settings, Users } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "As a dialog (⌘K)", description: "Opens over the page, traps focus, and returns it to where it came from on close (Radix Dialog). Press the button to try.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
	return (
		<>
			<Button shortcut="⌘K" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} variant="outline"><Search />Search</Button>
			<CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
					<CommandInput placeholder="Search or run a command…" />
					<CommandList>
						<CommandGroup heading="Go to">
							<CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}><Users />Members</CommandItem>
							<CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}><Settings />Settings<CommandShortcut><Kbd>G</Kbd><Kbd>S</Kbd></CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
						</CommandGroup>
					</CommandList>
			</CommandDialog>
		</>
	);
}
```

### inline

```tsx
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandFooter, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandSeparator, CommandShortcut, Kbd } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Briefcase, Clock, Copy, Plus, Users } from "lucide-react";

export const meta = { title: "Commands and pages", description: "One line per item: icon, label, shortcut on the right. Groups have quiet sentence-case labels. Type to filter; arrows and Enter to run.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<Command className="w-full max-w-md rounded-sm border border-line shadow-card">
			<CommandInput placeholder="Search or run a command…" />
			<CommandList>
				<CommandEmpty>No results. Try “extend” or “listings”.</CommandEmpty>
				<CommandGroup heading="Actions on 2 listings">
					<CommandItem><Clock />Extend by 30 days<CommandShortcut><Kbd>T</Kbd></CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
					<CommandItem><Copy />Duplicate<CommandShortcut><Kbd>D</Kbd></CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
				</CommandGroup>
				<CommandSeparator />
				<CommandGroup heading="Go to">
					<CommandItem><Briefcase />Listings<CommandShortcut><Kbd>G</Kbd><Kbd>L</Kbd></CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
					<CommandItem><Users />Pipeline<CommandShortcut><Kbd>G</Kbd><Kbd>P</Kbd></CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
					<CommandItem><Plus />New listing<CommandShortcut><Kbd>C</Kbd></CommandShortcut></CommandItem>
				</CommandGroup>
			</CommandList>
			<CommandFooter><span className="flex items-center gap-1"><Kbd>↵</Kbd> run</span><span className="flex items-center gap-1"><Kbd>esc</Kbd> close</span></CommandFooter>
		</Command>
	);
}
```

# Shortcut sheet (?)

A panel listing every shortcut by task, opened with ?, which also holds the switch to turn single-key shortcuts off.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Reference for people who want to learn the faster path after using the visible controls.
- The single place to turn single-key shortcuts off.
- Supporting expert users who already rely on shortcuts and want the full list in one view.

## When not to use

- As the main way to discover shortcuts. Show each key on its button, menu item and palette row.
- Searching for an action to run. Use the Command palette.

## Structure

1. Toggle: Single-key shortcuts, with the note "Turn off if you use a screen reader or voice control. ⌘ shortcuts stay on."
2. Group: Navigate (⌘K, G L, G P, /)
3. Group: Table (J K, X, ⇧J, ↵)
4. Group: Act (C, E, F, ⌘Z)
5. Each row: action name left, key caps right

## Guidelines

- Opens with ? from anywhere outside a text field, and from the Help menu.
- Group shortcuts by task, a handful per group, so the sheet can be scanned.
- Single-key shortcuts (C, E, F, J, K, X, R, G sequences) can be turned off; ⌘ shortcuts stay on.
- Single-key shortcuts never fire while focus is in a text input.
- Avoid keys that clash with the browser, the operating system or screen readers, and never override copy, paste or save.
- Prefer one or two letters with a mnemonic (C create, E edit, F filter) over stacked modifiers.

## Content

- Action names match the button labels they belong to.
- Show keys as the symbols printed on the keyboard (⌘, ⇧, ↵) and give the Windows equivalent.
- The off switch says who it is for in plain words.

## Accessibility

- Meets 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts by letting people turn single-key shortcuts off.
- Every shortcut is an extra route; the same action is reachable by Tab and Enter (2.1.1).
- Shown as a modal dialog with a heading; Esc closes it and focus returns (2.4.3).
- The toggle is a real switch with its state exposed (4.1.2).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ? | Open the shortcut sheet |
| Esc | Close it |
| Tab | Reach the single-key shortcut switch |

## Examples

### sheet

```tsx
import { Button, ShortcutSheet } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Every shortcut, by task", description: "Press ? anywhere outside a text field. The switch at the top turns single-key shortcuts off for screen reader and voice control users; ⌘ shortcuts stay on.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [single, setSingle] = useState(true);
	return (
		<div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
			<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "?" }))}>Show shortcuts (?)</Button>
			<span className="text-sm text-ink-2">Single-key shortcuts are {single ? "on" : "off"}.</span>
			<ShortcutSheet
				singleKeys={single}
				onSingleKeysChange={setSingle}
				groups={[
					{ title: "Navigate", items: [{ keys: ["⌘", "K"], action: "Search or run a command" }, { keys: ["G", "L"], action: "Go to Listings" }, { keys: ["G", "I"], action: "Go to Inbox" }, { keys: ["/"], action: "Search this list" }] },
					{ title: "Table", items: [{ keys: ["J"], action: "Next row" }, { keys: ["K"], action: "Previous row" }, { keys: ["X"], action: "Select row" }, { keys: ["↵"], action: "Open in side panel" }] },
					{ title: "Act", items: [{ keys: ["C"], action: "New listing" }, { keys: ["F"], action: "Add a filter" }, { keys: ["⌘", "Z"], action: "Undo" }] },
				]}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

# Inbox (triage)

The one place for things that need the person, shown as a list beside the selected item's detail, cleared by doing, marking done or snoozing.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Agent approvals and questions that block a run.
- Things about to need action, such as listings closing soon, mentions and new assignments.
- Anything the person may need to come back to later, so it must persist rather than flash past.

## When not to use

- Confirming the person's own action. Use a Toast.
- Events that need nothing from anyone. Record them in the record's Activity tab.
- A condition on the page being viewed. Use a Banner.

## Structure

1. Header with key hints (J K, E done, ⇧H snooze)
2. Tabs: Inbox, Snoozed, Done, each with a count
3. List (listbox): items that block an agent first, marked "Needs you", then by time
4. Detail: the item with its actions in place (approve, extend, reply, answer 1 to 3)
5. Snooze menu: quick times plus a typed time
6. Empty state per tab

## Guidelines

- List and detail side by side; acting in the detail never leaves the Inbox, and the next item opens after Done.
- Items that block an agent sort first and carry a "Needs you" badge with a word, not only a colour.
- Items stay until done or snoozed; snoozed items return at the chosen time.
- Snooze offers four quick times (an hour from now, tomorrow, next week, a month from now) and a typed time such as "4 pm" or "2 days"; an unparseable time shows an error and keeps the menu open.
- Every action (done, snooze, approve, reply) shows a toast with Undo.
- Only things that matter reach the Inbox; filter for significance so the count stays trustworthy.
- The unread count shows on the sidebar item; below 860px, when the sidebar hides, an inbox button with the same count appears in the top bar.

## Content

- Item titles say what needs doing and to what: "Approve 3 rejections for Graduate Data Analyst".
- Empty tabs say the state and what happens next: "All caught up. New items appear here when something needs you."
- Snooze placeholder shows examples: "Try 4 pm, tomorrow, 2 days or in 5 weeks."
- Snoozed items show when they come back: "Until Mon 9:00".

## Accessibility

- The list is a listbox with aria-selected on the current item; arrow keys and J/K move through it.
- Tabs follow the APG tabs pattern and expose their counts in the accessible name.
- The detail region is a polite live region, so the newly opened item is announced (4.1.3).
- The compact inbox button's label includes the count: "Inbox, 3 unread" (4.1.2).
- Single-key triage keys (E, ⇧H, 1 to 3) follow the global single-key switch (2.1.4).
- New items never interrupt; they appear in the list and count, and the person reads them when ready (2.2.4).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| G I | Go to Inbox |
| J / K | Next or previous item |
| E | Mark done |
| ⇧H | Snooze (quick times or type a time, Enter to apply) |
| 1 to 3 | Answer an agent's question |
| ⌘↵ | Send a reply from the detail |
| Esc | Close the snooze menu |

## Examples

### inbox

```tsx
import { Button, Inbox, type InboxItem, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Things that need you", description: "Items that block an agent come first, marked Needs you in words. Focus the list: J and K move, E marks done and the next item opens, ⇧H snoozes. Every action offers Undo.", order: 1 };

const START: InboxItem[] = [
	{ id: "1", title: "Approve: extend 3 listings by 30 days", source: "Agent · Weekly listing check", time: "09:12", needsYou: true, state: "inbox" },
	{ id: "2", title: "Priya Shah mentioned you on Frontend Engineer", source: "Comment", time: "Yesterday", state: "inbox" },
	{ id: "3", title: "Data Analyst closes in 2 days with 4 applicants", source: "Listing alert", time: "Mon", state: "inbox" },
	{ id: "4", title: "Export of 1,262 listings is ready", source: "Export", time: "Sun", state: "done" },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [items, setItems] = useState(START);
	const set = (id: string, patch: Partial<InboxItem>) => setItems((x) => x.map((i) => (i.id === id ? { ...i, ...patch } : i)));
	return (
		<Inbox
			className="h-96 w-full"
			items={items}
			onDone={(id) => { set(id, { state: "done" }); toast.success("Marked done", { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => set(id, { state: "inbox" }) } }); }}
			onSnooze={(id, until) => { set(id, { state: "snoozed", snoozedUntil: until }); toast.success(`Snoozed until ${until.toLowerCase()}`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => set(id, { state: "inbox" }) } }); }}
			renderDetail={(it) => (
				<div className="grid gap-3 text-base text-ink-2">
					<p>{it.source} · {it.time}</p>
					{it.needsYou && <div className="flex gap-2"><Button size="sm">Review changes</Button><Button size="sm" variant="outline">Reject</Button></div>}
				</div>
			)}
		/>
	);
}
```

- Toast
- App shell and sidebar navigation

# Notifications vs inbox vs toast

The rule for where a message goes: toast for your own action, banner for a condition on this page, inbox for anything that needs you later, activity for the rest.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Designing any new message, to choose its component before writing it.
- Reviewing a screen that shows several messages at once, to remove the ones that belong elsewhere.

## When not to use

- Field-level validation, which always sits next to the field. Use inline field errors and the Banner strip.
- Loading feedback. Use the Loading skeleton or an inline spinner.

## Structure

1. Question 1: did the person just do this, here? Toast
2. Question 2: is it a condition on the page in view? Banner
3. Question 3: does it need someone to act, now or later? Inbox
4. Question 4: must it stop the task before it continues? Confirmation dialog
5. Otherwise: the record's Activity tab, no message

## Guidelines

- Toast: passive confirmation of the person's own action in the current view; disappears; may carry Undo.
- Banner: a condition in context that persists until resolved; may carry one action.
- Inbox: events the person did not trigger, or that complete later, that need a response; persists until done or snoozed.
- Confirmation dialog: only when the task must stop for a decision that cannot be undone.
- Activity: events that need nothing. Logging them instead of notifying prevents alert fatigue.
- Errors never go in a toast.
- Keep event notifications people didn't trigger (reminders, assignments) apart from toasts. Notifications get their own component, which comes in at the top right and can stack, separate from toasts.

## Content

- Whatever the component, say what happened and what to do next, in sentence case, without apologies.
- Use the same name for the same record across toast, inbox and activity.

## Accessibility

- Toasts use role="status"; blocking errors use role="alert"; the dialog uses role="alertdialog" (4.1.3).
- Only dialogs take focus; everything else is announced without moving focus.
- Nothing important is only in a timed message (2.2.1); the Inbox and Activity keep a permanent record.
- Non-urgent updates can be postponed by the person (snooze), which supports 2.2.4 Interruptions.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘Z | Undo after a toast |
| G I | Open the Inbox |

## Examples

### choose

```tsx
import { Badge, RadioField, RadioGroup } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Where should this message go?", description: "Answer in order. The first yes decides: toast, banner, Inbox or confirmation dialog. If none apply, log it in the record's Activity and send nothing.", order: 1 };

const Q = [
	{ id: "own", q: "Did the person just do this, here?", yes: "Toast", why: "Confirms their own action and disappears; can carry Undo." },
	{ id: "cond", q: "Is it a condition on the page in view?", yes: "Banner", why: "Stays in context until resolved; at most one action." },
	{ id: "act", q: "Does it need someone to act, now or later?", yes: "Inbox", why: "Persists until done or snoozed, even if they weren't here." },
	{ id: "stop", q: "Must it stop the task before it continues?", yes: "Confirmation dialog", why: "Only when the decision can't be undone." },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [answers, setAnswers] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
	const first = Q.find((q) => answers[q.id] === "yes");
	const allNo = Q.every((q) => answers[q.id] === "no");
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-3">
			{Q.map((q, i) => (
				<fieldset key={q.id} className="grid gap-1.5 rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-3" disabled={i > 0 && answers[Q[i - 1].id] !== "no"}>
					<legend className="sr-only">{q.q}</legend>
					<span className="text-base font-medium text-ink">{i + 1}. {q.q}</span>
					<RadioGroup value={answers[q.id] ?? ""} onValueChange={(v) => setAnswers((a) => ({ ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(a).filter(([k]) => Q.findIndex((x) => x.id === k) < i)), [q.id]: v }))} className="flex gap-4">
						<RadioField id={`${q.id}-y`} value="yes" label="Yes" />
						<RadioField id={`${q.id}-n`} value="no" label="No" />
					</RadioGroup>
				</fieldset>
			))}
			<p role="status" className="flex items-center gap-2 text-base text-ink-2">
				{first ? <><Badge>{first.yes}</Badge>{first.why}</> : allNo ? <><Badge variant="secondary">Activity only</Badge>Log it on the record; don't notify anyone.</> : "Answer the questions in order."}
			</p>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Toast
- Banner (inline alert)
- Inbox (triage)
- Confirmation dialog

# App shell and sidebar navigation

The frame of every screen: a tinted left sidebar for navigation and an inset white canvas with a top bar for breadcrumb, Ask and search.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Every signed-in screen uses the same shell, with navigation in the same place and order.
- Products with more than a handful of sections, where a vertical list scales better than a top bar.

## When not to use

- Switching views of the same data, such as Live or Drafts. Use tabs in the page header.
- Moving between records in a list. Use J/K with the Side panel.
- Showing location deeper than two levels. Use the Breadcrumb.

## Structure

1. Sidebar: workspace switcher
2. Sidebar: personal items (Inbox with count, My candidates, Assistant)
3. Sidebar: group headings with items (Hiring: Listings, Pipeline, Reports; Workspace: Settings, Members, Billing)
4. Sidebar footer: setup checklist ("Get set up 3 / 5")
5. Canvas top bar: breadcrumb, Ask ⌘J, Search or run a command ⌘K
6. Canvas: page header and content; side panel docks on the right
7. Optional rail: 48px of icons with names in tooltips and a Collapse sidebar button at the foot

## Guidelines

- Keep the sidebar visible on desktop with text labels on every item. Collapse it to a rail of icons only on workspaces where the content needs the width (trading, editors), with each name in a tooltip, the Collapse sidebar button and ⌘B, and the choice saved per person.
- Two levels at most: group headings and items. Deeper structure becomes tabs on the page.
- Mark the current item with aria-current="page" and a filled background, not colour alone.
- Most used items first, settings last.
- Below 860px the sidebar hides; the top bar gains an inbox button with the same count, so nothing that needs the person disappears.
- The top bar holds global tools only (Ask, search); page actions live in the page header.
- Nav items are at least 24px tall with full-width hit areas, to meet the target size minimum.
- Use frame="flush" for workspaces whose regions sit edge to edge, divided by hairlines instead of gaps and cards; keep the inset canvas everywhere else.

## Content

- Item labels are short nouns that match the page title they open ("Listings" opens "Listings").
- Group headings are short and never include the word "navigation".
- Counts are numbers only and show only when above zero.

## Accessibility

- The sidebar is a nav landmark with a unique label ("Main"); the canvas is main; the side panel is complementary (2.4.1).
- Navigation order and labels are the same on every page (3.2.3).
- Search and the command palette provide a second way to reach pages (2.4.5).
- Each page has a title that names the page and the product (2.4.2).
- Focus is always visible on nav items, including inside the tinted sidebar (2.4.7).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| G L / G P / G I | Go to Listings, Pipeline or Inbox |
| ⌘K | Search or run a command |
| ⌘J | Open the Assistant |
| Tab | Move through sidebar items in order |
| ⌘B / Ctrl+B | Collapse or expand the sidebar, when the app offers the rail |

## Examples

### workspace

```tsx
import type React from "react";
import { AppShell, Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbList, BreadcrumbPage, BreadcrumbSeparator, Button, PageHeader, SidebarItem, SidebarSection } from "@twoux/ui";
import { BarChart3, Briefcase, Inbox, Plus, Settings, MessageSquare, Users } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Hiring workspace", description: "Tinted sidebar with a text label on every item, two levels at most, and the current page marked by fill and aria-current. Below 860px the sidebar moves behind the menu button.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [page, setPage] = useState("Listings");
	const item = (label: string, icon: React.ReactNode, count?: number) => <SidebarItem key={label} label={label} icon={icon} count={count} current={page === label} onClick={() => setPage(label)} />;
	return (
		<div className="h-120 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line">
			<AppShell
				sidebar={
					<>
						<div className="px-2 pt-1 text-base font-semibold text-ink">TwoUX Hiring</div>
						<SidebarSection>{[item("Inbox", <Inbox />, 4), item("Assistant", <MessageSquare />)]}</SidebarSection>
						<SidebarSection title="Hiring">{[item("Listings", <Briefcase />), item("Candidates", <Users />), item("Reports", <BarChart3 />)]}</SidebarSection>
						<SidebarSection title="Workspace">{[item("Settings", <Settings />)]}</SidebarSection>
					</>
				}
				topBar={
					<Breadcrumb>
						<BreadcrumbList>
							<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#hiring">Hiring</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
							<BreadcrumbSeparator />
							<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>{page}</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
						</BreadcrumbList>
					</Breadcrumb>
				}
			>
				<PageHeader title={page} description="24 listings across 6 teams" actions={<><Button variant="outline">Export</Button><Button shortcut="C"><Plus />New listing</Button></>} />
			</AppShell>
		</div>
	);
}
```
