# Pane layout

A workspace that fills the screen with columns of panes people resize with splitters and rearrange by dragging, for tool pages such as trading screens and editors where everything has to stay in view.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Tool pages where people watch and act on several regions at once and need them all in view, such as a trading screen.
- Letting people give more room to the region they work in and put regions where they expect them.

## When not to use

- List, record and dashboard pages. Use the app shell with one side panel, or a Configurable dashboard for movable items.
- Content people read top to bottom. Let the page scroll instead.

## Structure

1. Columns of panes, edge to edge, divided by 1px splitters
2. Pane header: grip, title or a view switch, one action, ⋯ menu
3. Pane body that scrolls on its own
4. Splitter: 1px line with an 8px grab area, primary on hover and focus
5. Drop line in primary where a dragged pane will land
6. Collapsed: header only, or a 36px strip with the name when the whole column is collapsed

## Guidelines

- Fit the viewport: panes scroll inside, and charts and lists size themselves to their pane with usePaneSize.
- Every drag has a keyboard path and a menu path: Move up, down, left, right and Wider, Narrower, Taller, Shorter.
- Splitters follow the window splitter pattern: role separator, a value from 0 to 100, arrow keys, Home and End.
- Save the layout per person, and offer Reset layout with Undo, never a confirmation.
- One action at most in a pane header; switch views with a segmented control in place of the title.
- Below the stack width, panes stack in one column and the page scrolls.
- Let people collapse a pane they don't need right now; it keeps its header so it is one click from coming back.
- Put a pane's own options, such as Show as table, at the top of its ⋯ menu rather than as more header buttons.
- Put a strip of at most six key figures above the panes, the ones people check first, and keep the panes for detail.
- Keep secondary detail behind a request: an expandable row, a tooltip or the pane's ⋯ menu (Show as table, View all), so the panes show what people watch.
- Keep panes people use all the time, such as filters, as panes rather than drawers, so they never hide the controls they hold.

## Content

- Name every pane with a noun people use for that region: Markets, Order book, Place order.

## Accessibility

- 2.5.7 Dragging movements: moving and resizing work from the pane's menu with single clicks.
- Each pane is a section named by its title; each move and resize is announced.
- 1.4.10 Reflow: below the stack width the panes stack and nothing scrolls sideways.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ← → (column splitter), ↑ ↓ (pane splitter) | Resize by 16px; with Shift, 64px |
| Home End | Smallest or largest size |
| Space or Enter on a grip | Pick up or drop the pane |
| ← → ↑ ↓ while picked up | Move the pane to another column or position |
| Esc while picked up | Put the pane back |

## Examples

### workspace

```tsx
import { PaneLayout, type PaneLayoutValue, toast, usePaneSize } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Resize and rearrange panes", description: "Three panes in two columns. Drag a splitter or use its arrow keys to resize; drag a pane's grip, or press Space on it and use the arrow keys, to move it; or use Move, Wider and Taller in the pane's menu. Each pane reports its own size.", order: 1 };

const DEFAULT: PaneLayoutValue = [
	{ id: "left", size: 2, panes: [{ id: "list", size: 1 }] },
	{ id: "right", size: 3, panes: [{ id: "detail", size: 2 }, { id: "log", size: 1 }] },
];

function Size() {
	const { width, height } = usePaneSize();
	return <p className="p-3 text-sm text-ink-2 tabular">{width} × {height} px</p>;
}

export default function Example() {
	const [layout, setLayout] = useState(DEFAULT);
	return (
		<div className="h-96 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line">
			<PaneLayout
				aria-label="Example workspace"
				stackBelow={480}
				value={layout}
				onValueChange={setLayout}
				onReset={() => { const before = layout; setLayout(DEFAULT); toast.success("Layout reset", { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setLayout(before) } }); }}
				panes={{
					list: { title: "Requests", children: <Size /> },
					detail: { title: "Request detail", children: <Size /> },
					log: { title: "Activity", children: <Size /> },
				}}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- App shell and sidebar navigation
- Side panel (drawer)
- Board and board item

# Breadcrumb

A short trail in the top bar showing where the page sits in the hierarchy, ending with the current page.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- On pages below the top level, to show the section they belong to ("Hiring > Listings").
- On a record's full page, so the person can go back up to the list ("Hiring > Listings > Junior Product Designer").

## When not to use

- As main navigation. The sidebar is the main navigation; the breadcrumb supplements it.
- Linking to sibling or related pages. Use tabs or the sidebar.
- Showing the path the person took. Breadcrumbs show hierarchy, not history; use the browser's Back.

## Structure

1. Section name (link when it has its own page)
2. Chevron separator (decorative)
3. Current page (not a link, darker text)

## Guidelines

- Sits at the left of the top bar on every page; top-level pages (Inbox, Assistant) show their name only.
- The last item is the current page, styled darker and not a link.
- Names match page titles exactly.
- When space runs out, collapse middle items behind an ellipsis button; the current page always stays visible.
- Keep it on one line; never wrap.

## Content

- Use the page and section names exactly as shown in the sidebar.
- For a record, end with its title; add the ID only when titles can repeat.

## Accessibility

- Wrap it in a nav landmark labelled "Breadcrumb" containing an ordered list (1.3.1).
- The current item has aria-current="page"; when it is not a link this is optional but still set for clarity.
- Separators are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- Breadcrumbs help meet 2.4.8 Location by showing where the page sits.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through the links in the trail |
| Enter | Follow the focused link |

## Examples

### trail

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbEllipsis, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbLink, BreadcrumbList, BreadcrumbPage, BreadcrumbSeparator } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Where the page sits", description: "Names match page titles. The current page is the last item, darker and not a link. On narrow screens middle items collapse behind the ellipsis; the trail never wraps.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-4">
			<Breadcrumb>
				<BreadcrumbList>
					<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#listings">Listings</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
					<BreadcrumbSeparator />
					<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#l1040">Junior Product Designer</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
					<BreadcrumbSeparator />
					<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Screening questions</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
				</BreadcrumbList>
			</Breadcrumb>
			<Breadcrumb>
				<BreadcrumbList>
					<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbLink href="#settings">Settings</BreadcrumbLink></BreadcrumbItem>
					<BreadcrumbSeparator />
					<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbEllipsis /></BreadcrumbItem>
					<BreadcrumbSeparator />
					<BreadcrumbItem><BreadcrumbPage>Email templates</BreadcrumbPage></BreadcrumbItem>
				</BreadcrumbList>
			</Breadcrumb>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- App shell and sidebar navigation
- Page header

# Page header

The page title on the left and its actions on the right, with exactly one primary action per view.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- At the top of every page in the canvas, to name the page and hold actions that affect the whole page.
- When a page has a main next step, such as creating a listing.

## When not to use

- Actions on selected rows. Use the bulk action bar.
- Actions on one record shown in the side panel. Use the panel's footer.
- Global tools such as search or Ask. Those live in the top bar of the App shell.

## Structure

1. Title (h1)
2. Actions, right-aligned: secondary actions ("Export ⇧E") then the one primary action ("New listing C")
3. Optional: view tabs below (All 24, Live 14, Drafts 3, Closed 7)

## Guidelines

- One primary button per view; every other action is secondary or in a menu.
- The primary action sits rightmost, nearest the content edge, with secondary actions to its left.
- Each button shows its shortcut (C, ⇧E) so people learn it by using it.
- Three actions at most in the header; more go into a menu.
- Title and actions wrap to two lines on narrow widths rather than truncating.
- View tabs (segmented counts) sit under the title and filter the same data; they are not navigation.

## Content

- Title is a short noun in sentence case that matches the sidebar item: "Listings".
- Action labels start with a verb and name the object: "New listing", "Export".
- Tab labels are one or two words with a count.

## Accessibility

- The title is the page's only h1 and matches the document title (2.4.2, 2.4.6).
- Shortcut hints are part of the button's accessible description, not its name, so voice users can say the label (4.1.2).
- Buttons are at least 24px tall (28 to 32px in TwoUX) (2.5.8).
- After navigation, focus can be moved to the title so screen reader users start at the page (2.4.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| C | Primary create action (New listing) |
| ⇧E | Export |
| Tab | Move from title area to actions, left to right |

## Examples

### listings

```tsx
import { Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger, PageHeader, Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Download, Ellipsis, Plus } from "lucide-react";

export const meta = { title: "Title, actions and view tabs", description: "The one primary action sits rightmost with its shortcut; secondary actions to its left; anything beyond three goes in a menu. Title and actions wrap rather than truncate.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<PageHeader
				title="Listings"
				description="24 listings across 6 teams"
				actions={
					<>
						<DropdownMenu>
							<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="More actions"><Ellipsis /></Button></DropdownMenuTrigger>
							<DropdownMenuContent align="end"><DropdownMenuItem>Import from CSV</DropdownMenuItem><DropdownMenuItem>Archive closed listings</DropdownMenuItem></DropdownMenuContent>
						</DropdownMenu>
						<Button variant="outline" shortcut="⇧E"><Download />Export</Button>
						<Button shortcut="C"><Plus />New listing</Button>
					</>
				}
				tabs={
					<Tabs defaultValue="all">
						<TabsList aria-label="Views"><TabsTrigger value="all" count={24}>All</TabsTrigger><TabsTrigger value="live" count={14}>Live</TabsTrigger><TabsTrigger value="drafts" count={3}>Drafts</TabsTrigger><TabsTrigger value="closed" count={7}>Closed</TabsTrigger></TabsList>
					</Tabs>
				}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- App shell and sidebar navigation
- Breadcrumb
- Command palette (⌘K)
- Shortcut sheet (?)

# Stepper

A vertical list of numbered steps for a task done in order, such as setting up a workspace or publishing a listing, showing what is done, what is current and what is left.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For a task of 3 to 6 steps that must happen in order, where knowing what is left helps people finish.
- For a setup checklist on an empty workspace, where each step unlocks the next.

## When not to use

- For sections people can visit in any order. Use Tabs.
- For one long form. Split it with headings; steps add clicks without reducing work.
- For background progress, such as an upload. Use a progress bar or status.

## Structure

1. Marker: number, or a check when done
2. Line joining the markers, primary up to the current step
3. Title, and an optional one-line description
4. Current step: primary marker, aria-current="step"
5. Later steps: faded

## Guidelines

- Keep it to 3 to 6 steps. More than that, group steps or simplify the task.
- Let people go back to any done step; never skip ahead to a step that depends on an unfinished one.
- Keep entered data when people go back and forward.
- Check each step when people press Next and keep them on it until it passes, with errors at the field. A final Review step checks everything again and links each problem to its step.
- Mark a done step with a check and the line in primary up to the current step, so progress reads at a glance.
- Place it beside the step's content on wide screens, and above it on narrow ones.

## Content

- Step titles are short verb phrases in sentence case: “Add the role”, “Set salary”, “Review and publish”.
- The description says what the step needs, in a few words: “Title, team and location”.

## Accessibility

- Use an ordered list, so screen readers announce the count and position.
- The current step has aria-current="step"; done and current states are also given in text, not by colour alone.
- Done steps that can be revisited are buttons with a visible focus ring.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Reaches each done step that can be revisited |
| Enter / Space | Goes back to that step |

## Examples

### publish

```tsx
import { Button, Stepper } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Publish a listing", description: "Done steps show a check and can be revisited. Later steps stay faded and locked until the one before is finished.", order: 1 };

const STEPS = [
	{ title: "Add the role", description: "Title, team and location" },
	{ title: "Set salary", description: "Band and benefits" },
	{ title: "Screening questions", description: "Up to 5 questions" },
	{ title: "Review and publish" },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [current, setCurrent] = useState(1);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-lg grid-cols-[200px_1fr] gap-8 max-sm:grid-cols-1">
			<Stepper steps={STEPS} current={current} onStepSelect={setCurrent} aria-label="Publish a listing" />
			<div className="grid content-start gap-3">
				<span className="text-md font-semibold text-ink">{STEPS[Math.min(current, STEPS.length - 1)].title}</span>
				<span className="text-base text-ink-2">Step {Math.min(current + 1, STEPS.length)} of {STEPS.length}</span>
				<div className="flex gap-2">
					<Button variant="outline" size="sm" disabled={current === 0} onClick={() => setCurrent((c) => c - 1)}>Back</Button>
					<Button size="sm" disabled={current >= STEPS.length} onClick={() => setCurrent((c) => c + 1)}>{current >= STEPS.length - 1 ? "Publish" : "Continue"}</Button>
				</div>
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Tabs (underline)
- Card
- Onboarding step

# Setup checklist

A short list in the sidebar of the few things that make the product useful, with progress shown as "2 of 4".

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing the next few things that make an empty workspace useful.
- Setup that people can do in any order and return to later.

## When not to use

- A fixed sequence. Use Stepper (stepper) or Onboarding step (onboarding-step).
- Teaching the interface. Use contextual help, not a modal tour.

## Structure

1. Heading ("Get set up")
2. Progress text ("2 of 4") and bar
3. Tasks (status, label, Start)
4. Dismiss button

## Guidelines

- Keep it to three to five tasks that make the product useful.
- Put it in the sidebar and let people dismiss it.
- Show progress as text, "2 of 4", with the bar as extra.
- Start opens the task in place. Never a modal tour or a full-page takeover.
- When everything is done, collapse it or let it disappear.

## Content

- Tasks begin with a verb: "Connect Slack", "Invite a teammate".
- Start button text stays "Start"; the task name is read out with it.

## Accessibility

- The checklist is a labelled section with a list; done tasks say "done" for assistive technology (SC 1.3.1, 1.4.1).
- Start and Dismiss have names that include what they act on (SC 2.4.6).
- The progress bar is decorative; the count is text (SC 1.4.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through Start buttons and Dismiss |
| Enter or Space | Start a task or hide the checklist |

## Examples

### sidebar

```tsx
import { Button, SetupChecklist, type SetupItem } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Get set up in the sidebar", description: "Start does the task in place. Finish all four and the checklist goes away; Hide closes it sooner.", order: 1 };

const TASKS = [
	{ id: "slack", label: "Connect Slack" },
	{ id: "invite", label: "Invite a teammate" },
	{ id: "import", label: "Import your candidates" },
	{ id: "agent", label: "Turn on the daily summary" },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [done, setDone] = useState<string[]>(["slack"]);
	const [hidden, setHidden] = useState(false);
	const items: SetupItem[] = TASKS.map((t) => ({ ...t, done: done.includes(t.id), onStart: () => setDone((d) => [...d, t.id]) }));
	const finished = done.length === TASKS.length;
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-64 gap-3">
			{!hidden && !finished && <SetupChecklist items={items} onDismiss={() => setHidden(true)} />}
			{(hidden || finished) && (
				<div className="grid gap-2 text-sm text-ink-2">
					<p>{finished ? "Setup is complete." : "The setup checklist is hidden."}</p>
					<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => { setDone(["slack"]); setHidden(false); }}>Start again</Button>
				</div>
			)}
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Onboarding to an empty workspace
- Empty state
- Onboarding step
- App shell and sidebar navigation
- Stepper

# Onboarding step

One step of first-run setup on a plain page: why we ask, the fields, which step this is, and Back, Skip and Continue.

Kind: component · Group: Navigation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A few setup steps that the product cannot guess, such as workspace name and who to invite.
- Steps that depend on each other, where each answer shapes the next.

## When not to use

- Teaching the product with a tour or video. Show it in the product and use contextual help (workspace-onboarding).
- A long form. Ask only what is needed to start and let people finish the rest later in Settings.

## Structure

1. "Step n of N" text (with Optional when it is)
2. Heading (receives focus)
3. Why we ask, in one line
4. Fields
5. Back, Skip (optional steps), Continue
6. Progress dots (decoration only)
7. Aside panel (optional, wide screens)

## Guidelines

- Keep it to a few steps. Each step says why it asks.
- Optional steps say Optional and offer Skip. Required steps do not offer it.
- Never disable Continue. Validate when it is pressed and put the error under the field.
- Say "Step 2 of 5" in text. Dots alone do not tell people how much is left.
- Move focus to the heading when the step changes, so a screen reader says where the person is.
- Use a plain background. No gradients, no illustration, no auto-playing video.
- Keep what was entered when going Back. Never ask for the same thing twice.

## Content

- Heading: a short question or task, such as "Name your workspace".
- Why line: "Teammates see this name when you invite them."
- Skip, not "Do this later" or "Not now", on optional steps.

## Accessibility

- The "Step n of N" text is real text; the dots are hidden from assistive technology (SC 1.4.1).
- The heading has tabindex -1 and receives focus on each step; the section is labelled by it (SC 2.4.3, 2.4.6).
- Errors are shown under the field and linked to it (SC 3.3.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through the fields, Back, Skip and Continue in order |
| Enter | In a text field, press Continue |
| Shift+Tab | Move back, starting from the heading on a new step |

## Examples

### workspace-setup

```tsx
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldLabel, Input, OnboardingStep } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Set up a workspace", description: "Three steps. The name is required, inviting is optional. What was typed stays when you go Back.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [step, setStep] = useState(1);
	const [name, setName] = useState("");
	const [invites, setInvites] = useState("");
	const [error, setError] = useState("");
	const next = () => {
		if (step === 1 && !name.trim()) { setError("Enter a name for your workspace, for example TwoUX."); return; }
		setError("");
		setStep((s) => Math.min(3, s + 1));
	};
	return (
		<div className="flex w-full justify-center">
			{step === 1 && (
				<OnboardingStep step={1} total={3} title="Name your workspace" description="Teammates see this name when you invite them." onContinue={next}>
					<Field data-invalid={!!error || undefined}>
						<FieldLabel htmlFor="ws-name">Workspace name</FieldLabel>
						<Input id="ws-name" value={name} aria-invalid={!!error || undefined} autoComplete="organization" onChange={(e) => { setName(e.target.value); setError(""); }} />
						{error && <FieldError>{error}</FieldError>}
					</Field>
				</OnboardingStep>
			)}
			{step === 2 && (
				<OnboardingStep step={2} total={3} title="Invite your team" description="They get an email with a link. You can also do this later in Settings." optional onBack={() => setStep(1)} onSkip={() => setStep(3)} onContinue={next}>
					<Field>
						<FieldLabel htmlFor="ws-invites">Email addresses</FieldLabel>
						<Input id="ws-invites" type="email" value={invites} placeholder="sam@twoux.example" onChange={(e) => setInvites(e.target.value)} />
						<FieldDescription>Separate several addresses with commas.</FieldDescription>
					</Field>
				</OnboardingStep>
			)}
			{step === 3 && (
				<OnboardingStep step={3} total={3} title="You are ready" description={`${name || "Your workspace"} is set up.`} continueLabel="Open workspace" onBack={() => setStep(2)} onContinue={() => setStep(1)}>
					<p className="text-base text-ink-2">{invites ? `An invitation will go to ${invites}.` : "You have not invited anyone yet."}</p>
				</OnboardingStep>
			)}
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Onboarding to an empty workspace
- Stepper
- Text input
- Form validation
- Setup checklist
- Sign in

# Help panel

Read-only help in the right-hand panel slot, opened from an Info link next to a heading or label, with the topic heading, short guidance and Learn more links.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To explain a page, section or field whose meaning or consequences aren't obvious from its label, opened from an Info link.
- On each step of a multi-step create flow, such as Create listing.
- As the page-level help for any page with decisions, opened from the Help button when no Info link was used.

## When not to use

- To name an icon or show a shortcut. Use a tooltip.
- For forms or actions. Use the side panel or the page.
- For questions about the person's data. Use the assistant panel (⌘J).

## Structure

1. Header: topic heading (matches the heading or label it opened from) and close button
2. Body: two to five short paragraphs or lists answering what this is, why it matters and how to choose
3. Optional: a short example, such as a well-written job title
4. Learn more: up to three help centre links, each opening in a new tab
5. Feedback prompt: "Was this helpful?" at the foot

## Guidelines

- Opens in TwoUX's single right-hand slot at 440px, or the width the person last chose, replacing any open panel, and restores it on close.
- Without an Info link pressed, shows the page topic. After an Info link, shows that topic until another is chosen or the page changes.
- Reopening on the same page shows the last topic, not the page default.
- Never opens empty: pages with no help content don't show the Help trigger.
- Below 860px it takes the full width of the canvas.

## Content

- Heading matches the on-screen heading or label exactly: "Visa sponsorship".
- Plain UK English, short paragraphs, no marketing. Explain consequences: "Candidates who need sponsorship can apply only if this is on."
- Learn more links say what the reader will learn: "How closing dates affect applications".

## Accessibility

- A complementary landmark labelled "Help"; it does not trap focus.
- Opening from an Info link moves focus to the topic heading; Esc or close returns focus to that Info link.
- New-tab links say so in their accessible name.
- Content reflows to 320px wide without horizontal scrolling.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter / Space (Info link) | Open the help panel at that topic |
| Tab | Move through links in the panel, then back to the page |
| Esc | Close the panel and return focus to the Info link |

## Examples

### salary

```tsx
import { FeedbackPrompt, HelpPanel, type HelpTopic, InfoLink, TextField } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Help for one field", description: "The Info link opens written help for that topic in the right-hand slot. Esc closes it and focus returns to the link. It ends with up to three Learn more links and a feedback prompt.", order: 1 };

const TOPICS: Record<string, HelpTopic> = {
	salary: {
		id: "salary",
		title: "Salary range",
		body: (
			<>
				<p>Listings with a salary range get more applicants, and UK job boards rank them higher.</p>
				<p><strong>Show a real range.</strong> Use the band you would actually pay, not a range so wide it says nothing. For example £30,000 to £36,000.</p>
				<p><strong>Check the minimum.</strong> Full-time roles must pay at least the National Living Wage for the hours worked.</p>
			</>
		),
		links: [{ label: "National Minimum Wage and Living Wage rates (GOV.UK)", href: "https://www.gov.uk/national-minimum-wage-rates" }],
	},
};

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
	const [topic, setTopic] = useState<HelpTopic | null>(null);
	return (
		<div className="flex h-96 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<div className="grid min-w-0 flex-1 content-start gap-1.5 p-5">
				<div className="flex items-center gap-2"><span className="text-base font-medium text-ink">Salary</span><InfoLink topic="salary" onOpen={(t) => { setTopic(TOPICS[t]); setOpen(true); }} /></div>
				<TextField id="help-salary" label="Salary from" prefix="£" placeholder="30,000" />
			</div>
			<HelpPanel open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} topic={topic} footer={<FeedbackPrompt onVote={() => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))} />} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Contextual help
- Secondary panels: which right-hand panel
- Side panel (drawer)
- Assistant side panel
- Feedback prompt
- Tooltip

# Feedback prompt

A small "Was this helpful?" block with Yes and No buttons, a thank you once voted, and an optional short follow-up form.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- At the end of help topics, help centre articles and beta feature pages.
- At the end of a report people have just read, to learn if it was useful.
- On a beta feature's page, to learn whether it is worth keeping.

## When not to use

- Under assistant answers; they use the good and bad controls by the origin label.
- As a modal or toast, or before people have read the content.
- For surveys of more than three questions; link to a survey page instead.

## Structure

1. Question as a small heading: "Was this helpful?"
2. Optional one-line description
3. Yes and No buttons (text, with an optional thumb icon)
4. States: default, sending (button spinner), sent (chosen answer selected and thank you text), failed (message and Try again)
5. Optional follow-up revealed after the vote: one to three fields, a privacy line and Send

## Guidelines

- Send the vote on click; send the follow-up separately with its own Send button.
- Once voted, the buttons are replaced by the chosen answer and the thank you; the vote can't be sent twice.
- One feedback prompt per page or panel.
- Free-text fields carry the privacy line and a 500 character limit with a count.
- On failure, show the message inline with Try again; keep any typed text.

## Content

- Question names the thing: "Was this help topic helpful?" or simply "Was this helpful?" when the context is clear.
- Sent: "Thanks, your feedback is recorded."
- Follow-up label: "What was missing? (optional)". Privacy line: "Don't include candidate names or other personal details."

## Accessibility

- Yes and No are real buttons with visible text; an icon alone is not enough.
- After a successful vote, focus moves to the thank you text.
- The failed state is announced in a live region.
- The follow-up fields have visible labels and follow the form validation rules.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to Yes, then No |
| Enter / Space | Send the vote |
| Tab (after voting) | Reach the optional follow-up fields and Send |

## Examples

### helpful

```tsx
import { CheckboxField, FeedbackPrompt } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Was this helpful?", description: "One vote, sent on click and never twice. After voting, an optional comment with the privacy line and a 500 character limit. Failures keep what was typed and offer Try again.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [fail, setFail] = useState(false);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
			<CheckboxField id="fb-fail" label="Simulate a failed send" checked={fail} onCheckedChange={(v) => setFail(v === true)} />
			<div className="rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-4">
				<FeedbackPrompt
					description="About the screening questions guide"
					onVote={() => new Promise((res, rej) => setTimeout(() => (fail ? rej(new Error("offline")) : res()), 600))}
					onFollowUp={() => new Promise((res) => setTimeout(res, 600))}
				/>
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Collecting product feedback
- Help panel
- Button
- Text input

# Usage meter

Credits or seats used against a limit, when it resets, and what used them. An upgrade link appears only near the limit.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing consumption against a plan limit, such as credits or seats.
- A measured value within a known range.

## When not to use

- Progress of a task. Use a progress indicator (nng-progress).
- A permanent plan promotion. Upgrade is not an always-visible bright button.

## Structure

1. Name of the unit and "used of limit"
2. Meter bar
3. Warning from 80% (what stops at the limit)
4. Resets date
5. What used them link
6. Add more link (only near the limit)

## Guidelines

- Say "13.2k of 20k credits": used, limit and unit.
- Say when it resets, for example "Resets 1 Dec".
- Link "What used them" to a breakdown, so people can reduce usage.
- From 80% used, warn and say what stops at the limit: "Agents pause until 1 Dec".
- Show the upgrade link only near the limit. Never a permanent bright button.
- Use role="meter" with min, max and now values, and a name.
- Never use colour alone: the warning has an icon and words as well as the amber bar.

## Content

- "86% used. Agents pause until 1 Dec."
- Link: "Add more", not "Upgrade now".

## Accessibility

- role="meter" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and an accessible name (APG meter, SC 4.1.2).
- Warning is text with an icon, so it does not depend on colour (SC 1.4.1).
- The bar meets 3:1 against its track (SC 1.4.11).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to What used them and Add more |
| Enter | Open the breakdown or the upgrade options |

## Examples

### states

```tsx
import { toast, UsageMeter } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Plenty, close, and at the limit", description: "The upgrade link appears from 80% used, and the warning says what stops. Colour is never the only signal.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const common = { unit: "credits", limit: 20000, resets: "1 Dec", atLimit: "Agents pause until 1 Dec", onDetails: () => toast("Opens the usage breakdown"), onUpgrade: () => toast("Opens the plans") };
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xs gap-6">
			<UsageMeter {...common} used={8400} />
			<UsageMeter {...common} used={17200} />
			<UsageMeter {...common} used={20000} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Stat card with comparison
- Banner (inline alert)
- Empty state
- Status badge

# Guide cue

A short guide of one to three popovers that point at the real controls for a task, opened only when the person asks to be shown.

Kind: component · Group: Feedback and overlays · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing where the parts of a task live after the person chose it, from a setup checklist Start, a Help menu entry, a help panel link or a feature label's Show me.
- A task spread over two or three controls in a dense toolbar, such as filter, change the layout, then save a view.

## When not to use

- On page load, first login, a timer or hover. TwoUX has no push tours; use a setup checklist (setup-checklist) and let people start the guide.
- Announcing a feature. Use a feature label (feature-label) and its popover; offer Show me inside it only if the feature spans several controls.
- Explaining a field or concept. Use contextual help (help-system) and the help panel (help-panel).
- More than three steps, or steps that depend on what was entered. Use a help article, or a stepper (stepper) for the task itself.
- Explaining an icon-only button. Use a tooltip (tooltip).

## Structure

1. Target highlight (the focus ring round the real control)
2. Popover anchored to the target
3. Heading (what the person does here)
4. Body (one or two sentences)
5. Step count as text ("Step 2 of 3")
6. Back, then Next or Done (the one primary in the cue)
7. Close ("Close guide", Esc)

## Guidelines

- Open the guide only from something the person pressed, and return focus there when it closes.
- Keep it to one to three steps, each on a real control people will use for the task.
- Point at elements by ref or a data attribute. A step whose target is missing or hidden is skipped, and the count counts only the steps shown; with no targets the guide does not open.
- Leave the page usable: no dimmed overlay or spotlight. Clicking the page keeps the cue open so people can try the control.
- Show one guide cue at a time, and close any other popover first.
- Offer Show me only where the guide can point at something; check with isGuideTargetAvailable.

## Content

- Heading names what the person does, sentence case: "Filter the list", "Save it as a view". Not "Step 1" or "Welcome".
- Body is one or two sentences on what the control does for them.
- Progress is text: "Step 2 of 3". Buttons are Back, Next and Done; the close button is named "Close guide".

## Accessibility

- The cue is a non-modal dialog: role="dialog", aria-modal="false", named by its heading and described by its body (SC 4.1.2).
- Focus moves to the heading on open and returns to the control that started the guide on close (SC 2.4.3).
- Each step change is announced in a polite live region: "Saved views guide, step 2 of 3: Choose a layout" (SC 4.1.3).
- It never opens unrequested (SC 2.2.4). Nothing pulses; the popover's entrance stops under reduced motion (SC 2.3.3).
- The highlight uses the focus colour, 3:1 or more against the page, and the cue sits beside the target so it never covers it (SC 1.4.11, 2.4.11).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter or Space | Press Next, Back, Done or Close |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Move between the cue's buttons and on to the page; focus is not trapped |
| Esc | Close the guide and return focus to what started it |

## Examples

### saved-view-guide

```tsx
import { FilterBar, FilterPill, GuideCue, SavedViews, Segment, SegmentedControl, SetupChecklist, toast, useGuide, type GuideStep, type SetupItem } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useMemo, useRef, useState } from "react";

export const meta = {
	title: "Show me from the setup checklist",
	description: "A three-step guide over the real toolbar, shown open here as a preview. In a product it opens only from Start on “Create your first saved view”; Esc or Close ends it and Start brings it back.",
	order: 1,
};

const LISTINGS = [
	{ status: "Open", location: "London" },
	{ status: "Open", location: "Leeds" },
	{ status: "Open", location: "Remote" },
	{ status: "Closing soon", location: "London" },
	{ status: "Closing soon", location: "Manchester" },
	{ status: "Draft", location: "Leeds" },
	{ status: "Closed", location: "London" },
	{ status: "Closed", location: "Remote" },
];
const STATUS = ["Open", "Closing soon", "Draft", "Closed"].map((v) => ({ value: v, label: v, count: LISTINGS.filter((l) => l.status === v).length }));
const LOCATION = ["London", "Leeds", "Manchester", "Remote"].map((v) => ({ value: v, label: v, count: LISTINGS.filter((l) => l.location === v).length }));

export default function Example() {
	const root = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
	const filtersRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
	const layoutRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
	const [views, setViews] = useState([{ id: "all", name: "All listings", count: LISTINGS.length }]);
	const [view, setView] = useState("all");
	const [status, setStatus] = useState<string[]>([]);
	const [location, setLocation] = useState<string[]>([]);
	const [layout, setLayout] = useState("table");
	const [savedOne, setSavedOne] = useState(false);

	const shown = LISTINGS.filter((l) => (status.length === 0 || status.includes(l.status)) && (location.length === 0 || location.includes(l.location))).length;

	const steps: GuideStep[] = useMemo(() => [
		{ target: filtersRef, title: "Filter the list", body: "Pick a status or a location. The count updates as you tick, and the filters stay when you save." },
		{ target: layoutRef, title: "Choose a layout", body: "Table suits scanning many listings; Board groups them by status. The view remembers which you chose.", align: "end" },
		{
			// A function target: the Save view button inside SavedViews. If it isn't on screen, this step is skipped.
			target: () => root.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[data-slot='saved-views'] [aria-haspopup='dialog']"),
			title: "Save it as a view",
			body: "Save view keeps these filters and the layout under a name, so you and your team return to them in one click.",
			align: "end",
		},
	], []);

	// Shown open here so you can see the cue straight away. In a product, never pass `preview`: the guide opens only from Start.
	const guide = useGuide(steps, { label: "Saved views guide", preview: true });

	const items: SetupItem[] = [
		{ id: "slack", label: "Connect Slack", done: true },
		{ id: "view", label: "Create your first saved view", done: savedOne, onStart: guide.start },
		{ id: "invite", label: "Invite a teammate", done: false },
	];

	return (
		<div className="flex w-full flex-wrap items-start gap-4">
			<SetupChecklist items={items} className="w-full max-w-64" />
			<section ref={root} aria-label="Listings" className="grid min-w-0 flex-1 basis-80 gap-3 rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-3">
				<SavedViews
					views={views}
					value={view}
					onValueChange={setView}
					dirty={status.length + location.length > 0 && view === "all"}
					onSaveAs={(name) => {
						const id = name.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g, "-");
						setViews((v) => [...v, { id, name, count: shown }]);
						setView(id);
						setSavedOne(true);
						toast.success(`Saved “${name}”`);
					}}
				/>
				<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
					<div ref={filtersRef} className="min-w-0 rounded-sm">
						<FilterBar>
							<FilterPill field="Status" options={STATUS} selected={status} onChange={setStatus} />
							<FilterPill field="Location" options={LOCATION} selected={location} onChange={setLocation} />
						</FilterBar>
					</div>
					<span className="flex-1" />
					<div ref={layoutRef} className="rounded-sm">
						<SegmentedControl value={layout} onValueChange={setLayout} size="sm" aria-label="Layout">
							<Segment value="table">Table</Segment>
							<Segment value="board">Board</Segment>
						</SegmentedControl>
					</div>
				</div>
				<p className="tabular text-sm text-ink-2" aria-live="polite">{shown} of {LISTINGS.length} listings</p>
			</section>
			<GuideCue {...guide.cueProps} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

# List table

A read-mostly table for scanning and triaging records such as listings or candidates, with a sticky header, sortable columns, J and K row focus and checkbox selection.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- People need to find records that match criteria, compare them, and act on one or several. These are the core table tasks.
- Every record has the same attributes and the set will keep growing, such as all live listings or an applicant inbox.
- People will scan, sort and analyse large volumes of rows rather than read each one.

## When not to use

- To edit cells, enrich with AI or total columns. Use the TwoUX Data grid, because a table is not an interactive widget and its cells are not focusable.
- For a short list of items under shared headings, such as candidates by stage. Use the TwoUX Grouped list.
- For page layout. Tables are only for structured data.
- For one figure that matters. Use the TwoUX Stat card with comparison instead of a one-row table.

## Structure

1. Table header (title, item count, actions)
2. Filter bar
3. Sticky column header row
4. Selection checkbox column
5. Identifying column (Role)
6. Data columns
7. Row focus indicator
8. Footer (count, selection count, pagination)

## Guidelines

- Keep the column header row visible on scroll when a table has more than 30 items per page, more than five columns or sortable columns.
- Put a human-readable identifier (the Role) first and order the remaining columns by importance.
- Only the sorted column shows its arrow; the others reveal it on hover. Expose the current sort with aria-sort on that header only.
- J and K (or the arrow keys) move row focus, X toggles selection, Enter opens the row in the side panel, Esc clears. Show each shortcut on its button so experts learn it.
- The header checkbox selects only the rows on the current page, and the footer reads "2 of 24 selected".
- Open a row in a non-modal side panel so the table stays visible; modals hide neighbouring rows.
- Never add cell editing or a totals row to a list table; that is the Data grid's job.
- For spreadsheet-like data people scan many rows of, such as an inventory, a ledger, an import or a mapping, use size="dense" (28px rows) and the Dense table parts. Keep the default 36px rows for everything else. Dense is a variant for that data, never a setting people switch.

## Content

- Left-align text and right-align numbers with a consistent number of decimals, in tabular figures.
- Write column labels as short, plain nouns.
- Show the total next to the title, and the selected count before the total when rows are selected. Hide the count while loading.
- Show a dash for an empty value and give it hidden text for screen readers, never a blank cell.
- Status is a bordered pill with a word, never colour alone.

## Accessibility

- 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: mark up header cells with scope="col" (and scope="row" for the Role cell) so each value is tied to its column.
- APG table pattern: use table semantics with an accessible name from a caption or aria-label, and aria-sort on the sorted header only.
- 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts: J, K, X, E and / are single-key shortcuts, so TwoUX lets people turn them off in settings.
- 2.4.7 Focus Visible: the focused row shows a visible indicator, and highlighted rows are never the only signal of selection or focus.
- 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: the sticky header must not fully cover the focused row; use scroll padding.
- Give repeated row actions unique names, for example "Open Junior Product Designer" rather than "Open".

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| J / ↓ | Move row focus down |
| K / ↑ | Move row focus up |
| ⇧J / ⇧K | Extend selection down or up |
| X | Select or deselect the focused row |
| Enter | Open the focused row in the side panel |
| Esc | Close the side panel, or clear the selection |
| / | Focus search |
| F | Open the filter field list |
| ⇧P | Switch the side panel between push and overlay |

## Examples

### listings

```tsx
import {
	AlertDialog,
	AlertDialogAction,
	AlertDialogCancel,
	AlertDialogContent,
	AlertDialogDescription,
	AlertDialogFooter,
	AlertDialogHeader,
	AlertDialogTitle,
	Badge,
	BulkActionBar,
	Button,
	Checkbox,
	DropdownMenu,
	DropdownMenuContent,
	DropdownMenuItem,
	DropdownMenuSeparator,
	DropdownMenuTrigger,
	Table,
	TableBody,
	TableCell,
	TableHead,
	TableHeader,
	TablePagination,
	TableRow,
	TableSortHead,
	toast,
	useRowKeyboard,
} from "@twoux/ui";
import { type ColumnDef, type RowSelectionState, type SortingState, flexRender, getCoreRowModel, getPaginationRowModel, getSortedRowModel, useReactTable } from "@tanstack/react-table";
import { CalendarPlus, CircleX, Copy, Ellipsis, Pencil, Trash2 } from "lucide-react";
import { useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { LISTINGS, type Listing, STATUS_VARIANT, formatDate } from "./data";

export const meta = { title: "Listings", description: "Click a header to sort; only the sorted column shows its arrow. Select rows to bring up the bulk bar. Focus the table and use J/K to move, X to select, Esc to clear.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [sorting, setSorting] = useState<SortingState>([{ id: "closes", desc: false }]);
	const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({});
	const [pagination, setPagination] = useState({ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 8 });
	const [confirm, setConfirm] = useState(false);

	const columns = useMemo<ColumnDef<Listing>[]>(
		() => [
			{
				id: "select",
				header: ({ table }) => (
					<Checkbox
						aria-label="Select all on this page"
						checked={table.getIsAllPageRowsSelected() || (table.getIsSomePageRowsSelected() && "indeterminate")}
						onCheckedChange={(v) => table.toggleAllPageRowsSelected(!!v)}
					/>
				),
				cell: ({ row }) => <Checkbox aria-label={`Select ${row.original.role}`} checked={row.getIsSelected()} onCheckedChange={(v) => row.toggleSelected(!!v)} />,
				enableSorting: false,
			},
			{ accessorKey: "role", header: "Role", cell: ({ row }) => <span className="font-medium text-ink">{row.original.role}</span> },
			{ accessorKey: "location", header: "Location", cell: ({ getValue }) => <span className="text-ink-2">{getValue<string>()}</span> },
			{ accessorKey: "status", header: "Status", cell: ({ row }) => <Badge variant={STATUS_VARIANT[row.original.status]} dot>{row.original.status}</Badge> },
			{ accessorKey: "applicants", header: "Applicants", meta: { align: "right" }, cell: ({ getValue }) => <span className="tabular block text-right">{getValue<number>()}</span> },
			{ accessorKey: "closes", header: "Closes", cell: ({ getValue }) => <span className="tabular text-ink-2">{formatDate(getValue<string>())}</span> },
			{ id: "actions", header: () => <span className="sr-only">Actions</span>, enableSorting: false, cell: ({ row, table }) => <RowMenu listing={row.original} disabled={table.getSelectedRowModel().rows.length > 0} /> },
		],
		[],
	);

	const table = useReactTable({
		data: LISTINGS,
		columns,
		state: { sorting, rowSelection, pagination },
		onSortingChange: setSorting,
		onRowSelectionChange: setRowSelection,
		onPaginationChange: (u) => {
			setPagination(u);
			setRowSelection({}); // changing page clears the selection
		},
		getRowId: (r) => r.id,
		getCoreRowModel: getCoreRowModel(),
		getSortedRowModel: getSortedRowModel(),
		getPaginationRowModel: getPaginationRowModel(),
	});

	const rows = table.getRowModel().rows;
	const selected = table.getSelectedRowModel().rows.length;
	const clear = () => setRowSelection({});
	const keys = useRowKeyboard({ count: rows.length, onToggle: (i, v) => rows[i]?.toggleSelected(v), onOpen: (i) => toast(`Opened ${rows[i].original.role}`), onClear: clear, selected });

	return (
		<div className="w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<BulkActionBar
				count={selected}
				noun={selected === 1 ? "listing" : "listings"}
				onClear={clear}
				actions={[
					{ label: "Extend 30 days", icon: <CalendarPlus />, shortcut: "T", onSelect: () => { toast.success(`Extended ${selected} listing${selected === 1 ? "" : "s"} by 30 days`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => {} } }); clear(); } },
					{ label: "Duplicate", icon: <Copy />, shortcut: "D", onSelect: () => { toast.success(`Duplicated ${selected} listing${selected === 1 ? "" : "s"}`); clear(); } },
					{ label: "Close listings", icon: <CircleX />, destructive: true, onSelect: () => setConfirm(true) },
				]}
			/>
			<Table aria-label="Listings">
				<TableHeader>
					{table.getHeaderGroups().map((hg) => (
						<TableRow key={hg.id} className="hover:bg-transparent">
							{hg.headers.map((h) => {
								const right = (h.column.columnDef.meta as { align?: string } | undefined)?.align === "right";
								if (!h.column.getCanSort()) return <TableHead key={h.id} className={h.id === "select" ? "w-9" : "w-10"}>{flexRender(h.column.columnDef.header, h.getContext())}</TableHead>;
								return (
									<TableSortHead key={h.id} sorted={h.column.getIsSorted()} onSort={() => h.column.toggleSorting(h.column.getIsSorted() === "asc")} align={right ? "right" : "left"}>
										{flexRender(h.column.columnDef.header, h.getContext())}
									</TableSortHead>
								);
							})}
						</TableRow>
					))}
				</TableHeader>
				<TableBody {...keys.bodyProps} aria-label="Listings, use J and K to move, X to select">
					{rows.map((row, i) => (
						<TableRow key={row.id} data-state={row.getIsSelected() ? "selected" : undefined} {...keys.rowProps(i)}>
							{row.getVisibleCells().map((cell) => (
								<TableCell key={cell.id}>{flexRender(cell.column.columnDef.cell, cell.getContext())}</TableCell>
							))}
						</TableRow>
					))}
				</TableBody>
			</Table>
			<TablePagination
				page={pagination.pageIndex}
				pageCount={table.getPageCount()}
				pageSize={pagination.pageSize}
				total={LISTINGS.length}
				selected={selected}
				noun="listings"
				onPageChange={(p) => table.setPageIndex(p)}
			/>
			<AlertDialog open={confirm} onOpenChange={setConfirm}>
				<AlertDialogContent>
					<AlertDialogHeader>
						<AlertDialogTitle>Close {selected} listings?</AlertDialogTitle>
						<AlertDialogDescription>They come off every job board today. Applicants and notes are kept.</AlertDialogDescription>
					</AlertDialogHeader>
					<AlertDialogFooter>
						<AlertDialogCancel>Keep open</AlertDialogCancel>
						<AlertDialogAction variant="destructive" onClick={() => { toast.success(`${selected} listing${selected === 1 ? "" : "s"} closed`); clear(); }}>Close listings</AlertDialogAction>
					</AlertDialogFooter>
				</AlertDialogContent>
			</AlertDialog>
		</div>
	);
}

function RowMenu({ listing, disabled }: { listing: Listing; disabled: boolean }) {
	return (
		<DropdownMenu>
			<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
				<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label={`Actions for ${listing.role}`} disabled={disabled}><Ellipsis /></Button>
			</DropdownMenuTrigger>
			<DropdownMenuContent align="end">
				<DropdownMenuItem><Pencil />Edit</DropdownMenuItem>
				<DropdownMenuItem><Copy />Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
				<DropdownMenuSeparator />
				<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive"><Trash2 />Close listing</DropdownMenuItem>
			</DropdownMenuContent>
		</DropdownMenu>
	);
}
```

# Dense table

The List table at 28px rows for spreadsheet-like data, such as a life-cycle inventory or a product library, with group rows, row numbers with a row menu, a filter row, in-cell buttons and frozen first columns.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- The data is spreadsheet-like and people scan many rows at once to compare values: inventories, ledgers, bills of materials, imports and field mappings.
- Rows fall into a few sections people read separately, such as Inputs, Wastes and emissions and Products.
- Every row has the same attributes and people need to find, compare and act on several rows.

## When not to use

- As a density setting, a comfortable mode or a user preference. TwoUX has one density for the app; dense is only for this kind of data.
- For a list people triage one record at a time (an inbox, candidates). Use the List table at its default 36px rows.
- To type, paste from Excel, fill or undo cell edits. Use the Sheet grid with size="dense": a table's cells are not focusable.

## Structure

1. Table size="dense": 28px header and rows, 8px cell padding, 13px text
2. Frozen first columns (data-pinned): selection, row number with ⋮ row menu, the identifying column
3. Filter row: a search field under each filterable header
4. Group rows: label, info tooltip, count, optionally collapsible
5. Cells: Tag with a value, Switch with its word, two linked items with an arrow, n/a, in-cell button on hover and focus
6. Footer: pagination; the Bulk action bar while rows are selected

## Guidelines

- Use Table size="dense". Rows and the header are 28px, cells have 8px padding and text stays 13px, so dense never means smaller type.
- Freeze the selection column, the row number and the identifying column with data-pinned, and set each one's --pin offset. Wide tables scroll sideways inside their own box.
- Group rows split the table into sections. Put each group in its own TableBody with a TableGroupRow first: label, count, and an info tooltip saying what belongs there. Make it collapsible when the sections are long.
- The row number cell holds the ⋮ row menu, named “Actions for <row>”. Every row action lives there.
- An in-cell button (Open, Share) shows on row hover and keyboard focus, and always on touch screens. It is a shortcut: the same action is always in the row menu.
- A filter row puts one search field under each filterable header, named “Filter <column>”. Filtering goes back to page 1 and Esc clears a field.
- Keep at most one in-cell button per row, and no more than two quick actions plus the row menu, so rows stay scannable.

## Content

- Tag with a value: the category as a Tag, then the value in tabular figures, such as Allocate 90.3 %. The Tag never carries the number.
- Switch with its word: the word says the current state (Published, Draft), never only the switch.
- Linked items: “Magnet preparation → NdFeB magnet powder”, read as “Magnet preparation to NdFeB magnet powder”.
- Use n/a (read as “not applicable”) when a value can't exist for the row, and a dash with hidden text when it exists but is empty.
- Right-align numbers in tabular figures with the same decimals; put units in their own column or the header, and region codes in monospace.
- Header labels in sentence case, short nouns: Amount, In reference unit.

## Accessibility

- APG table pattern: a dense table is still a table, with an accessible name, header cells and scope="rowgroup" on group rows.
- The collapsible group label is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming its TableBody.
- 2.5.8 Target size: row menu buttons and checkboxes keep a 24px hit area inside 28px rows.
- In-cell buttons stay in the tab order when hidden, appear on focus, and are named for their row (“Open Electricity, medium voltage”).
- Filter fields have their own labels, not only a placeholder.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through checkboxes, row menus, in-cell buttons and filter fields |
| Enter / Space | Open the row menu, press an in-cell button, collapse or expand a group |
| Esc (filter field) | Clear the filter |
| J / K, X, Enter | Row focus, selection and open, with useRowKeyboard as on the List table |

## Examples

### inventory

```tsx
import {
	DropdownMenuItem,
	DropdownMenuSeparator,
	Table,
	TableBody,
	TableCell,
	TableCellAction,
	TableGroupRow,
	TableHead,
	TableHeader,
	TableLinkedItems,
	TableNotApplicable,
	TableRow,
	TableRowNumber,
	Tag,
	toast,
} from "@twoux/ui";
import { Copy, PanelRight, Pencil, Trash2 } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, useState } from "react";

export const meta = {
	title: "Life-cycle inventory",
	description: "size=\"dense\" for 28px rows. Group rows with an info tooltip and count collapse their section. Hover or tab into a row to reveal Open; the ⋮ menu on the row number has Open too. Scroll sideways: the row number and Flow stay in view.",
	order: 1,
};

type Exchange = { id: string; flow: string; from?: [string, string]; kind: "Unit process" | "System process" | "Elementary flow"; allocation?: number; region: string; amount: number; unit: string; reference?: string; note?: string };
type Group = { id: string; label: string; info: string; rows: Exchange[] };

const GROUPS: Group[] = [
	{
		id: "intermediary",
		label: "Intermediary inputs",
		info: "Products made by other processes in this model and fed into this one.",
		rows: [
			{ id: "e1", flow: "NdFeB magnet powder", from: ["Magnet preparation", "NdFeB magnet powder"], kind: "Unit process", allocation: 90.3, region: "CN", amount: 1.042, unit: "kg", reference: "1.042 kg" },
			{ id: "e2", flow: "Dysprosium oxide", from: ["Rare earth separation", "Dysprosium oxide"], kind: "System process", allocation: 6.1, region: "CN", amount: 0.031, unit: "kg", reference: "31 g" },
			{ id: "e3", flow: "Nickel plating", from: ["Surface treatment", "Plated part"], kind: "Unit process", region: "GB", amount: 0.18, unit: "m²", reference: "1,800 cm²" },
			{ id: "e4", flow: "Sintering, vacuum furnace", from: ["Heat treatment", "Sintered block"], kind: "Unit process", allocation: 100, region: "GB", amount: 1, unit: "item", reference: "1 item" },
		],
	},
	{
		id: "inputs",
		label: "Inputs",
		info: "Energy, water and resources taken in directly, not made by another process in this model.",
		rows: [
			{ id: "e5", flow: "Electricity, medium voltage", kind: "System process", region: "GB", amount: 14.6, unit: "kWh", reference: "52.56 MJ" },
			{ id: "e6", flow: "Natural gas, burned in furnace", kind: "System process", region: "RER", amount: 21.4, unit: "MJ", reference: "5.94 kWh" },
			{ id: "e7", flow: "Argon, liquid", kind: "System process", region: "RER", amount: 0.42, unit: "kg", reference: "420 g" },
			{ id: "e8", flow: "Water, deionised", kind: "Elementary flow", region: "GB", amount: 0.012, unit: "m³", reference: "12 l" },
			{ id: "e9", flow: "Transport, lorry 16 to 32 t", kind: "System process", region: "RER", amount: 312, unit: "t·km", reference: "312,000 kg·km" },
		],
	},
	{
		id: "wastes",
		label: "Wastes and emissions",
		info: "What leaves the process without value: waste for treatment and emissions to air, water and soil.",
		rows: [
			{ id: "e10", flow: "Grinding sludge", from: ["Hazardous waste treatment", "Treated sludge"], kind: "Unit process", region: "GB", amount: 0.064, unit: "kg", reference: "64 g" },
			{ id: "e11", flow: "Carbon dioxide, fossil", kind: "Elementary flow", region: "GLO", amount: 1.21, unit: "kg", note: "Air, urban" },
			{ id: "e12", flow: "Particulates, < 2.5 µm", kind: "Elementary flow", region: "GLO", amount: 0.0004, unit: "kg", reference: "0.4 g" },
		],
	},
	{
		id: "products",
		label: "Products",
		info: "What the process makes. The reference product carries the result; co-products take a share by allocation.",
		rows: [
			{ id: "e13", flow: "NdFeB magnet, sintered", kind: "Unit process", allocation: 94.5, region: "GB", amount: 1, unit: "kg", reference: "1 kg" },
			{ id: "e14", flow: "Magnet offcuts, for recycling", kind: "Unit process", allocation: 5.5, region: "GB", amount: 0.058, unit: "kg", reference: "58 g" },
		],
	},
];

const COLS = 9;
const fmt = (n: number) => n.toLocaleString("en-GB", { maximumFractionDigits: 4 });

export default function Example() {
	const [collapsed, setCollapsed] = useState<string[]>([]);
	const open = (e: Exchange) => toast(`Opened ${e.flow}`, { description: "In a product it opens in the side panel." });
	let n = 0;
	return (
		<div className="w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<div className="flex items-center gap-2 border-b border-line px-3 py-2">
				<h3 className="text-md font-semibold text-ink">NdFeB magnet, per kg</h3>
				<span className="text-sm text-ink-3">Corvane Magnetics · Sheffield plant · 2025</span>
			</div>
			<Table size="dense" aria-label="Inventory for NdFeB magnet, per kg" className="min-w-328 table-fixed" containerClassName="max-h-120">
				<TableHeader>
					<TableRow className="hover:bg-transparent">
						<TableHead data-pinned="" className="w-16"><span aria-hidden="true">#</span><span className="sr-only">Row number</span></TableHead>
						<TableHead data-pinned="last" style={{ "--pin": "64px" } as CSSProperties} className="w-64">Flow</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-80">Provider</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-44">Allocation</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-20">Region</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-24 text-right">Amount</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-16">Unit</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-36 text-right">In reference unit</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-28">Compartment</TableHead>
					</TableRow>
				</TableHeader>
				{GROUPS.map((g) => {
					const isOpen = !collapsed.includes(g.id);
					return (
						<TableBody key={g.id} id={`inv-${g.id}`}>
							<TableGroupRow
								label={g.label}
								info={g.info}
								count={g.rows.length}
								colSpan={COLS}
								expanded={isOpen}
								controls={`inv-${g.id}`}
								onExpandedChange={(o) => setCollapsed((c) => (o ? c.filter((x) => x !== g.id) : [...c, g.id]))}
							/>
							{isOpen &&
								g.rows.map((e) => {
									n += 1;
									return (
										<TableRow key={e.id}>
											<TableRowNumber n={n} label={e.flow} data-pinned="">
												<DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => open(e)}><PanelRight />Open</DropdownMenuItem>
												<DropdownMenuItem><Pencil />Edit amount</DropdownMenuItem>
												<DropdownMenuItem><Copy />Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
												<DropdownMenuSeparator />
												<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive"><Trash2 />Remove from inventory</DropdownMenuItem>
											</TableRowNumber>
											<TableCell data-pinned="last" style={{ "--pin": "64px" } as CSSProperties}>
												<span className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2">
													<span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate font-medium text-ink">{e.flow}</span>
													<TableCellAction aria-label={`Open ${e.flow}`} onClick={() => open(e)}>Open</TableCellAction>
												</span>
											</TableCell>
											<TableCell className="max-w-80">{e.from ? <TableLinkedItems from={e.from[0]} to={e.from[1]} /> : <TableNotApplicable />}</TableCell>
											<TableCell>
												<span className="flex items-center gap-2">
													<Tag>{e.kind === "Elementary flow" ? "Elementary" : e.allocation !== undefined ? "Allocate" : e.kind}</Tag>
													{e.allocation !== undefined ? <span className="tabular text-ink">{e.allocation.toLocaleString("en-GB", { minimumFractionDigits: 1 })} %</span> : null}
												</span>
											</TableCell>
											<TableCell className="font-mono text-sm text-ink-2">{e.region}</TableCell>
											<TableCell className="tabular text-right text-ink">{fmt(e.amount)}</TableCell>
											<TableCell className="text-ink-2">{e.unit}</TableCell>
											<TableCell className="tabular text-right text-ink-2">{e.reference ?? <TableNotApplicable />}</TableCell>
											<TableCell className="text-ink-2">{e.note ?? <TableNotApplicable />}</TableCell>
										</TableRow>
									);
								})}
						</TableBody>
					);
				})}
			</Table>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### product-library

```tsx
import {
	BulkActionBar,
	Button,
	Checkbox,
	DropdownMenuItem,
	DropdownMenuSeparator,
	SplitButton,
	Switch,
	Table,
	TableBody,
	TableCell,
	TableCellAction,
	TableFilterRow,
	TableHead,
	TableHeader,
	TablePagination,
	TableRow,
	TableRowNumber,
	Tag,
	toast,
} from "@twoux/ui";
import { Copy, Globe, Share2, Trash2, Upload } from "lucide-react";
import { type CSSProperties, useMemo, useState } from "react";

export const meta = {
	title: "Product library",
	description: "A dense table with a selection column, a search field under each header, Published switches with their word, a Share button revealed on hover or focus (also in the ⋮ menu), pagination and an Import data split button.",
	order: 2,
};

type Product = { id: string; name: string; category: string; unit: string; gwp: number; version: string; published: boolean; updated: string };

const NAMES = [
	["NdFeB magnet, sintered", "Magnets", "1 kg"],
	["Ferrite magnet, ring", "Magnets", "1 kg"],
	["Copper winding wire", "Metals", "1 kg"],
	["Aluminium housing, die cast", "Metals", "1 item"],
	["Steel shaft, machined", "Metals", "1 item"],
	["Motor controller board", "Electronics", "1 item"],
	["Hall sensor", "Electronics", "1 item"],
	["Ball bearing, 6204", "Components", "1 item"],
	["Epoxy potting compound", "Chemicals", "1 kg"],
	["Varnish, insulating", "Chemicals", "1 l"],
	["Cardboard box, double wall", "Packaging", "1 item"],
	["Polyethylene foam insert", "Packaging", "1 item"],
	["Hub motor, 250 W", "Assemblies", "1 item"],
	["Stator assembly", "Assemblies", "1 item"],
	["Rotor assembly", "Assemblies", "1 item"],
	["Cable harness, 1.2 m", "Electronics", "1 item"],
	["Silicon steel lamination", "Metals", "1 kg"],
	["Nickel plating bath", "Chemicals", "1 l"],
	["Pallet, softwood", "Packaging", "1 item"],
	["Shrink wrap film", "Packaging", "1 kg"],
	["Thermal paste", "Chemicals", "1 kg"],
	["Encoder disc", "Components", "1 item"],
	["Brushless fan, 80 mm", "Assemblies", "1 item"],
] as const;

const PRODUCTS: Product[] = NAMES.map(([name, category, unit], i) => ({
	id: `p${i + 1}`,
	name,
	category,
	unit,
	gwp: Math.round(((i * 7.31) % 38) * 100 + 42) / 100,
	version: `${1 + (i % 3)}.${i % 4}`,
	published: i % 3 !== 1,
	updated: new Date(Date.UTC(2025, 9, 28 - i)).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
}));

const PAGE = 8;
const date = (v: string) => new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short" }).format(new Date(v));
const pin = (px: number) => ({ "--pin": `${px}px` }) as CSSProperties;

export default function Example() {
	const [products, setProducts] = useState(PRODUCTS);
	const [filters, setFilters] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
	const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([]);
	const [page, setPage] = useState(0);

	const shown = useMemo(
		() =>
			products.filter((p) =>
				Object.entries(filters).every(([k, q]) => !q.trim() || String(k === "published" ? (p.published ? "Published" : "Draft") : p[k as keyof Product]).toLowerCase().includes(q.trim().toLowerCase())),
			),
		[products, filters],
	);
	const pageRows = shown.slice(page * PAGE, (page + 1) * PAGE);
	const allOnPage = pageRows.length > 0 && pageRows.every((p) => selected.includes(p.id));
	const someOnPage = pageRows.some((p) => selected.includes(p.id));
	const toggle = (id: string) => setSelected((s) => (s.includes(id) ? s.filter((x) => x !== id) : [...s, id]));
	const share = (p: Product) => toast.success(`Link to ${p.name} copied`, { description: "Anyone in Corvane Magnetics can open it." });
	const publish = (p: Product, on: boolean) => {
		setProducts((ps) => ps.map((x) => (x.id === p.id ? { ...x, published: on } : x)));
		toast(on ? `Published ${p.name}` : `${p.name} is a draft again`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setProducts((ps) => ps.map((x) => (x.id === p.id ? { ...x, published: !on } : x))) } });
	};

	return (
		<div className="w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2 border-b border-line px-3 py-2">
				<h3 className="text-md font-semibold text-ink">Product library</h3>
				<span className="tabular text-sm text-ink-3">{products.length} products</span>
				<span className="flex-1" />
				<SplitButton
					variant="outline"
					onClick={() => toast("Choose a CSV or Excel file to import")}
					menuLabel="More import options"
					menu={
						<>
							<DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => toast("Importing all products from the file")}>Import all</DropdownMenuItem>
							<DropdownMenuItem disabled={!selected.length} onSelect={() => toast(`Updating ${selected.length} selected products from the file`)}>Import selection{selected.length ? ` (${selected.length})` : ""}</DropdownMenuItem>
						</>
					}
				>
					<Upload />Import data
				</SplitButton>
			</div>
			<BulkActionBar size="dense" count={selected.length} noun={selected.length === 1 ? "product" : "products"} onClear={() => setSelected([])} actions={[
					{ label: "Publish", icon: <Globe />, onSelect: () => { setProducts((ps) => ps.map((p) => (selected.includes(p.id) ? { ...p, published: true } : p))); toast.success(`Published ${selected.length} products`); setSelected([]); } },
					{ label: "Share", icon: <Share2 />, onSelect: () => toast.success(`Links to ${selected.length} products copied`) },
				]} />
			<Table size="dense" aria-label="Product library" className="min-w-260 table-fixed">
				<TableHeader>
					<TableRow className="hover:bg-transparent">
						<TableHead data-pinned="" className="w-9">
							<Checkbox aria-label="Select all on this page" checked={allOnPage ? true : someOnPage ? "indeterminate" : false} onCheckedChange={(v) => setSelected((s) => (v ? [...new Set([...s, ...pageRows.map((p) => p.id)])] : s.filter((id) => !pageRows.some((p) => p.id === id))))} />
						</TableHead>
						<TableHead data-pinned="" style={pin(36)} className="w-14"><span aria-hidden="true">#</span><span className="sr-only">Row number</span></TableHead>
						<TableHead data-pinned="last" style={pin(92)} className="w-64">Product</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-32">Category</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-24">Declared unit</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-32 text-right">GWP, kg CO₂e</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-20">Version</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-36">Status</TableHead>
						<TableHead className="w-24">Updated</TableHead>
					</TableRow>
					<TableFilterRow
						columns={[null, null, { id: "name", label: "Product" }, { id: "category", label: "Category" }, { id: "unit", label: "Declared unit" }, { id: "gwp", label: "GWP", align: "right" }, { id: "version", label: "Version" }, { id: "published", label: "Status" }, null]}
						values={filters}
						onChange={(id, v) => { setFilters((f) => ({ ...f, [id]: v })); setPage(0); }}
					/>
				</TableHeader>
				<TableBody>
					{pageRows.map((p, i) => {
						const on = selected.includes(p.id);
						return (
							<TableRow key={p.id} data-state={on ? "selected" : undefined}>
								<TableCell data-pinned=""><Checkbox aria-label={`Select ${p.name}`} checked={on} onCheckedChange={() => toggle(p.id)} /></TableCell>
								<TableRowNumber n={page * PAGE + i + 1} label={p.name} data-pinned="" style={pin(36)}>
									<DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => share(p)}><Share2 />Share</DropdownMenuItem>
									<DropdownMenuItem><Copy />Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
									<DropdownMenuSeparator />
									<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive"><Trash2 />Delete product</DropdownMenuItem>
								</TableRowNumber>
								<TableCell data-pinned="last" style={pin(92)}>
									<span className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2">
										<span className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate font-medium text-ink">{p.name}</span>
										<TableCellAction aria-label={`Share ${p.name}`} onClick={() => share(p)}>Share</TableCellAction>
									</span>
								</TableCell>
								<TableCell><Tag>{p.category}</Tag></TableCell>
								<TableCell className="text-ink-2">{p.unit}</TableCell>
								<TableCell className="tabular text-right text-ink">{p.gwp.toLocaleString("en-GB", { minimumFractionDigits: 2 })}</TableCell>
								<TableCell className="tabular text-ink-2">{p.version}</TableCell>
								<TableCell>
									<span className="flex items-center gap-2">
										<Switch size="sm" checked={p.published} onCheckedChange={(v) => publish(p, v)} aria-label={`Publish ${p.name}`} />
										<span className={p.published ? "text-ink" : "text-ink-3"}>{p.published ? "Published" : "Draft"}</span>
									</span>
								</TableCell>
								<TableCell className="tabular text-ink-2">{date(p.updated)}</TableCell>
							</TableRow>
						);
					})}
				</TableBody>
			</Table>
			{shown.length === 0 && <p className="px-3 py-4 text-base text-ink-2">No products match these filters.</p>}
			<TablePagination page={page} pageCount={Math.ceil(shown.length / PAGE)} pageSize={PAGE} total={shown.length} selected={selected.length} noun="products" onPageChange={setPage} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

### prospects

```tsx
import { BulkActionBar, Button, DropdownMenuItem, type SheetCellChange, SheetGrid, type SheetRow, type SheetSort, ShortcutList, sheetGridShortcuts, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Copy, Trash2 } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { PROSPECT_COLUMNS, prospectRows } from "./prospects-data";

export const meta = {
	title: "TwoUX prospects: every cell editable",
	description:
		"When every cell is editable, use Sheet grid with size=\"dense\". Stage and Seniority are selectors: click the active cell or its chevron, or press Enter. Hover shows the row, the cell under the pointer and the active cell in three tones. Drag a header edge to resize, double-click it to fit; pin or unpin from the column menu. Add row scrolls to the new row. Every key is listed under the grid.",
	order: 0,
};

export default function Example() {
	const [columns, setColumns] = useState(PROSPECT_COLUMNS);
	const [rows, setRows] = useState<SheetRow[]>(() => prospectRows());
	const [sort, setSort] = useState<SheetSort>(null);
	const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([]);
	// A paste or fill arrives as one batch, so one state update covers every cell.
	const onCellsChange = (changes: SheetCellChange[]) =>
		setRows((rs) => rs.map((r) => {
			const mine = changes.filter((c) => c.rowId === r.id);
			return mine.length ? { ...r, values: { ...r.values, ...Object.fromEntries(mine.map((c) => [c.columnId, c.value])) } } : r;
		}));
	const remove = (ids: string[]) => {
		const before = rows;
		setRows((rs) => rs.filter((r) => !ids.includes(r.id)));
		setSelected((s) => s.filter((id) => !ids.includes(id)));
		toast(`Deleted ${ids.length} ${ids.length === 1 ? "person" : "people"}`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setRows(before) } });
	};
	const duplicate = (ids: string[]) =>
		setRows((rs) => [...rs, ...rs.filter((r) => ids.includes(r.id)).map((r, i) => ({ id: `${r.id}-copy-${rs.length + i}`, values: { ...r.values, name: `${r.values.name} (copy)` } }))]);
	const n = selected.length;
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full gap-6">
			<BulkActionBar
				size="dense"
				count={n}
				noun={n === 1 ? "person" : "people"}
				onClear={() => setSelected([])}
				className="-mb-6 rounded-sm border border-line"
				actions={[
					{ label: "Duplicate", icon: <Copy />, onSelect: () => { duplicate(selected); toast.success(`Duplicated ${n} ${n === 1 ? "person" : "people"}`); setSelected([]); } },
					{ label: "Delete", icon: <Trash2 />, destructive: true, onSelect: () => remove(selected) },
				]}
			/>
			<SheetGrid
				aria-label="TwoUX prospects"
				size="dense"
				filterRow
				className="h-112 w-full"
				columns={columns}
				onColumnsChange={setColumns}
				rows={rows}
				onCellChange={(id, col, v) => setRows((rs) => rs.map((r) => (r.id === id ? { ...r, values: { ...r.values, [col]: v } } : r)))}
				onCellsChange={onCellsChange}
				sort={sort}
				onSortChange={setSort}
				selectedRowIds={selected}
				onSelectedRowIdsChange={setSelected}
				rowActions={(row) => (
					<>
						<DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => duplicate([row.id])}><Copy />Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
						<DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onSelect={() => remove([row.id])}><Trash2 />Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
					</>
				)}
				onAddRows={(n) => setRows((rs) => [...rs, ...Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({ id: `new-${rs.length + i}`, values: { subscribed: false } }))])}
			/>
			{/* The keys work as in Google Sheets; list them under the grid so nobody has to guess. */}
			<ShortcutList groups={sheetGridShortcuts()} />
		</div>
	);
}
```
