# Data grid

An editable, spreadsheet-like grid for enriching and exporting many columns, with pinned columns, cell-by-cell keyboard navigation, a totals row and AI-generated columns.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- People edit, enrich or export many columns of data, and cells contain interactive or editable content.
- The table is wider than the screen and people compare values across columns, so the identifying column must stay in view.
- People need summary content such as totals kept in view while they scroll, for example total salary or average apply rate.

## When not to use

- For scanning and triage of records. Use the TwoUX List table; a static table keeps reading simpler.
- For deep edits of one record. Use the side panel or full record page; in-place editing only works for narrow edits.
- For a handful of records. Use the TwoUX List table without pagination or totals.
- For spreadsheet work: selecting ranges, copying to and pasting from Excel or Google Sheets, fill down and undo. Use the Sheet grid, with size="dense" for 28px rows.

## Structure

1. Toolbar (view name, Columns, Group, Export)
2. Pinned header row with column type icons
3. Pinned checkbox and identifying columns
4. Scrollable data cells
5. AI column (tinted, with run state per cell)
6. Pinned totals row
7. Status line for save and validation messages

## Guidelines

- The grid has one tab stop. Arrow keys move between cells, Home and End go to the first and last cell in the row.
- Enter or F2 starts editing, Escape cancels, Enter or Tab commits. Validation is per field.
- Pin the checkbox and Role columns while scrolling sideways, and the header and totals row while scrolling down.
- Mark editable columns in the header and show the edit affordance on hover.
- The totals row is chosen per column (sum, average, empty percentage) and counts only rows on screen; say so in the label.
- The AI column runs on demand with progress, Stop and per-cell state, and never overwrites real data.
- The Data grid keeps 36px rows. For spreadsheet-like data where people need many rows in view, use the Sheet grid with size="dense" instead of changing the Data grid's height.

## Content

- Each column shows its type icon so people recognise number, money, person, link, date and AI columns at a glance.
- Right-align numbers and money with consistent decimals.
- Keep three empty states apart: a dash when there is nothing, "Not found" when the AI looked and found nothing, and a red message with Retry when it failed.
- Validation messages name the field and the rule, for example "Enter at least £23,400, the UK minimum for a full-time role."

## Accessibility

- APG grid pattern: role="grid", roving focus on cells, aria-selected on selected rows, aria-sort on the sorted header.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: every cell action, including sort, hide, totals and AI run, works from the keyboard.
- 3.3.1 Error Identification: invalid values stay in edit with a red outline and a text message, not the outline alone.
- 4.1.3 Status Messages: save confirmations and AI progress are announced from the status line without moving focus.
- 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: pinned columns and rows must not hide the focused cell; scroll it into view.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move one cell |
| Home / End | First or last cell in the row |
| Enter / F2 | Edit the focused cell |
| Enter (editing) | Save and stay |
| Tab (editing) | Save and move to the next cell |
| Esc (editing) | Cancel the edit |
| ⇧Space | Select or deselect the active row; the bulk action bar shows above the header |

## Examples

### enrich

```tsx
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn, type GridRow, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Copy, Trash2 } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Enrich listings in place", description: "Focus the grid, move with the arrow keys and press Enter, F2 or just type to edit. Esc cancels; Enter saves and stays; Tab saves and moves on. Salary must be a whole number above the minimum.", order: 1 };

const COLUMNS: GridColumn[] = [
	{ id: "role", label: "Role", width: 220, pin: true },
	{ id: "team", label: "Team", width: 130, editable: true },
	{ id: "location", label: "Location", width: 140, editable: true },
	{ id: "salary", label: "Salary from (£)", width: 150, editable: true, type: "number", total: "average", validate: (v) => (!/^[0-9]+$/.test(v.replace(/,/g, "")) ? "Enter a whole number, such as 32000." : Number(v.replace(/,/g, "")) < 23400 ? "Enter at least £23,400, the full-time minimum." : undefined) },
	{ id: "applicants", label: "Applicants", width: 120, type: "number", total: "sum" },
	{ id: "manager", label: "Hiring manager", width: 160, editable: true },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [rows, setRows] = useState<GridRow[]>([
		{ id: "1", role: "Junior Product Designer", team: "Design", location: "Leeds", salary: 30000, applicants: 38, manager: "Priya Shah" },
		{ id: "2", role: "Frontend Engineer", team: "Engineering", location: "Manchester", salary: 52000, applicants: 112, manager: "Tom Becker" },
		{ id: "3", role: "Data Analyst", team: "Data", location: "Remote (UK)", salary: 41000, applicants: 64, manager: "" },
		{ id: "4", role: "Recruitment Coordinator", team: "People", location: "London", salary: 29000, applicants: 0, manager: "Amara Okafor" },
		{ id: "5", role: "Customer Success Lead", team: "Customer", location: "Bristol", salary: 45000, applicants: 21, manager: "" },
	]);
	const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([]);
	const n = selected.length;
	const noun = n === 1 ? "listing" : "listings";
	const duplicate = () => {
		setRows((rs) => [...rs, ...rs.filter((r) => selected.includes(r.id)).map((r, i) => ({ ...r, id: `${r.id}-copy-${rs.length + i}`, role: `${r.role} (copy)` }))]);
		toast.success(`Duplicated ${n} ${noun}`);
		setSelected([]);
	};
	const remove = () => {
		const before = rows;
		setRows((rs) => rs.filter((r) => !selected.includes(r.id)));
		toast(`Deleted ${n} ${noun}`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setRows(before) } });
		setSelected([]);
	};
	return (
		<DataGrid
			className="w-full"
			aria-label="Listings"
			columns={COLUMNS}
			rows={rows}
			onCellChange={(id, col, v) => setRows((r) => r.map((x) => (x.id === id ? { ...x, [col]: v } : x)))}
			selectedRowIds={selected}
			onSelectedRowIdsChange={setSelected}
			noun={noun}
			bulkActions={[
				{ label: "Duplicate", icon: <Copy />, onSelect: duplicate },
				{ label: "Delete", icon: <Trash2 />, destructive: true, onSelect: remove },
			]}
		/>
	);
}
```

# Filter pills and filter bar

Filters applied from one button in the toolbar and shown as segmented chips on their own row: each reads as a sentence, values apply as soon as they are ticked, and the row appears only while something is filtered.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- People filter a table by a few properties and need to see every active filter without opening anything.
- People combine several properties, values and operators on a large collection.
- Results load quickly enough for each change to apply live.

## When not to use

- When there are many fields to filter by, as in candidate search. Use the TwoUX Filter panel.
- For collections under about five items. Do not filter at all.
- For settings that always have a value, such as a chart's date range or Daily and Weekly. Use a rectangle control or the TwoUX segmented control.

## Structure

1. Filter button in the toolbar (F): fields, then the chosen field’s values beside them
2. Filter row, shown only once a filter is applied
3. Applied filter chip: field, operator, value, remove
4. Add another filter (+)
5. Result count
6. Clear

## Guidelines

- Shape says what a control does. A filter is a segmented chip (field, operator, value, remove) on the filter row; actions and view settings are buttons in the toolbar.
- Each chip reads field, operator, value, for example "Status is any of Live, Expiring". Three or more values are counted: "3 statuses".
- Put the filter button in the toolbar. Picking a field opens its values beside the field list, and the chip appears on the filter row only once a value is ticked, never as an empty suggestion.
- List values apply as soon as they are ticked and show how many rows each matches. Typed values (numbers, dates) apply on Enter.
- Put the result count and Clear at the end of the filter row, and filter the full collection, not only the loaded rows.
- Each chip can be removed on its own with the remove button at its end; + after the chips adds another field.

## Content

- Use "is", "is not" and "is any of" as operators, matching the field, operator, value token model.
- Dates offer quick picks first, then "in the last N days", then a calendar.
- Write the result count as a full phrase, "24 listings", not a bare number.
- Show the field name before the value so values like "2" or "London" are never ambiguous.

## Accessibility

- 4.1.3 Status Messages: announce the updated result count without moving focus.
- 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: each remove button is named "Remove Status filter"; ticked values expose their checked state.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: the chip border must reach 3:1 against the filter row, since it is the chip’s only boundary.
- 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts: F can be turned off with the other single-key shortcuts.
- Moving focus or scroll back to the top after each change is avoided so people keep their place.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| F | Open the field list |
| ↑ ↓, Enter | Move through and choose fields or values |
| Space | Tick or untick a list value (applies at once) |
| Enter | Apply a typed number or date |
| Esc | Close the values, then the field list, and return focus to the filter button |

## Examples

### listings

```tsx
import { Badge, FilterButton, type FilterFieldDef, FilterRow, type FilterValue, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableRow, Timestamp, dateFilterFromValues, resolveDateRange } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
import { LISTINGS, type Listing, STATUS_VARIANT } from "../list-table/data";

export const meta = {
	title: "Filter listings",
	description: "The filter button sits in the toolbar. Pick a field, then tick its values beside the list: each tick applies at once, and the filter shows as a chip on its own row only once it has a value. A date field (Closing date) opens typed dates and a calendar instead. + adds another field; Clear removes them all.",
	order: 1,
};

const FIELDS = [
	{ id: "status", label: "Status", noun: { one: "status", many: "statuses" } },
	{ id: "location", label: "Location", noun: { one: "location", many: "locations" } },
	{ id: "role", label: "Role", noun: { one: "role", many: "roles" } },
] as const;

export default function Example() {
	const [filters, setFilters] = useState<FilterValue>({ status: ["Open", "Closing soon"] });
	const matches = (l: Listing, skip?: string) =>
		Object.entries(filters).every(([f, vals]) => {
			if (f === skip) return true;
			if (f !== "closes") return vals.includes(String(l[f as keyof Listing]));
			// A date field holds dateFilterToValues; resolveDateRange turns it into the dates to compare.
			const { from, to } = resolveDateRange(dateFilterFromValues(vals, []));
			return (!from || l.closes >= from) && (!to || l.closes <= to);
		});
	const rows = LISTINGS.filter((l) => matches(l));
	// Counts reflect the other filters, so people see what a tick will give them.
	const fields: FilterFieldDef[] = [
		...FIELDS.map((f) => ({
			id: f.id,
			label: f.label,
			valueNoun: f.noun,
			options: [...new Set(LISTINGS.map((l) => String(l[f.id])))].sort().map((v) => ({ value: v, label: v, count: LISTINGS.filter((l) => matches(l, f.id) && String(l[f.id]) === v).length })),
		})),
		// Closing dates are in the future, so "last 30 days" presets mean nothing here: typed dates and the calendar only.
		{ id: "closes", label: "Closing date", kind: "date", presets: [], group: "All fields" },
	];

	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<div className="flex items-center gap-2 border-b border-line px-3 py-2">
				<span className="text-base font-medium text-ink">Listings</span>
				<span className="flex-1" />
				<FilterButton fields={fields} value={filters} onChange={setFilters} />
			</div>
			<FilterRow fields={fields} value={filters} onChange={setFilters} shown={rows.length} total={LISTINGS.length} noun="listings" className="border-b border-line bg-surface-2 px-3 py-2" />
			<div className="max-h-56 overflow-y-auto">
				<Table aria-label="Filtered listings">
					<TableBody>
						{rows.map((l) => (
							<TableRow key={l.id}>
								<TableCell className="font-medium text-ink">{l.role}</TableCell>
								<TableCell className="text-ink-2">{l.location}</TableCell>
								<TableCell className="text-ink-2"><Timestamp value={l.closes} format="date" short /></TableCell>
								<TableCell><Badge variant={STATUS_VARIANT[l.status]} dot>{l.status}</Badge></TableCell>
							</TableRow>
						))}
					</TableBody>
				</Table>
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Filter panel
- Saved views
- List table
- Data grid

# Filter panel

A side panel of collapsible filter sections for searches with many fields, with live counts per option and a main action that says how many rows it will act on.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Search across many dimensions at once, such as candidates by location, team, experience and salary. That is faceted navigation.
- People set filters across several categories, which work best placed vertically on the left.
- People need counts per option to avoid zero-result combinations.

## When not to use

- For two or three filters on a table. Use the TwoUX Filter bar so filters stay inline.
- Inside a dropdown or menu when there are several categories; multiple categories should never go in a menu.
- For saved combinations people reuse. Use TwoUX Saved views.

## Structure

1. Header (Filters, count of active filters, Clear all)
2. Collapsible sections with set-value count
3. Options with result counts
4. Results table
5. Footer ("Showing 5 of 412 candidates", Save search, main action with count)

## Guidelines

- Sections collapse, and each closed section shows how many values are set.
- Show the most used sections open and the rest collapsed.
- Each option shows how many results it matches.
- The result count updates live and the main action states its scope, "Add 412 to pipeline".
- Offer Clear all for the panel and a clear per section.

## Content

- Section titles are the field names people use, not database names.
- Write "Any team" or "Any time" when a section has no value, so the default is explicit.
- Keep counts in the same place on every option so they scan down the column.

## Accessibility

- APG disclosure pattern: each section header is a button with aria-expanded; Enter or Space toggles it.
- 4.1.3 Status Messages: the live result count is announced as a full phrase, "412 candidates".
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: every section, option and Clear all can be reached and used from the keyboard.
- 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: options are grouped under their section with a group label.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / ⇧Tab | Move between sections and controls |
| Enter / Space (section) | Expand or collapse the section |
| Space (option) | Tick or untick an option |

## Examples

### candidates

```tsx
import { Button, FilterPanel, type FilterSection, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableRow, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Search candidates by many fields", description: "Sections collapse and show how many values are set. Each option shows its count. The footer says what the main action will affect.", order: 1 };

const PEOPLE = [
	{ name: "Amara Okafor", stage: "Screen", source: "Referral", location: "Leeds" },
	{ name: "Tom Becker", stage: "Applied", source: "Job board", location: "Manchester" },
	{ name: "Priya Shah", stage: "Interview", source: "Careers page", location: "London" },
	{ name: "Liam Walsh", stage: "Applied", source: "Job board", location: "Leeds" },
	{ name: "Sofia Romano", stage: "Offer", source: "Agency", location: "Remote (UK)" },
	{ name: "Hana Kim", stage: "Screen", source: "Job board", location: "Glasgow" },
];
type K = "stage" | "source" | "location";

export default function Example() {
	const [value, setValue] = useState<Record<string, string[]>>({ stage: ["Applied", "Screen"] });
	const match = (p: (typeof PEOPLE)[number], skip?: K) => (Object.entries(value) as [K, string[]][]).every(([k, v]) => k === skip || !v.length || v.includes(p[k]));
	const rows = PEOPLE.filter((p) => match(p));
	const section = (id: K, title: string, open?: boolean): FilterSection => ({ id, title, defaultOpen: open, options: [...new Set(PEOPLE.map((p) => p[id]))].sort().map((v) => ({ value: v, label: v, count: PEOPLE.filter((p) => match(p, id) && p[id] === v).length })) });
	return (
		<div className="grid h-96 w-full grid-cols-[240px_1fr] overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface max-md:grid-cols-1">
			<FilterPanel className="border-r border-line" value={value} onChange={setValue} sections={[section("stage", "Stage", true), section("source", "Source", true), section("location", "Location")]} />
			<div className="flex min-h-0 flex-col">
				<div className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto">
					<Table aria-label="Candidates"><TableBody>{rows.map((p) => <TableRow key={p.name}><TableCell className="font-medium text-ink">{p.name}</TableCell><TableCell className="text-ink-2">{p.stage}</TableCell><TableCell className="text-ink-2">{p.location}</TableCell></TableRow>)}</TableBody></Table>
				</div>
				<div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-t border-line px-3 py-2">
					<span className="tabular text-sm text-ink-2" aria-live="polite">Showing {rows.length} of {PEOPLE.length} candidates</span>
					<Button size="sm" disabled={!rows.length} onClick={() => toast.success(`Added ${rows.length} to the pipeline`)}>Add {rows.length} to pipeline</Button>
				</div>
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Saved views
- List table
- Bulk action bar

# Saved views

Named, reusable combinations of filters, sort order and column choices, also kept in the URL so a link reproduces the view.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- People apply the same filter configuration on every visit; saving it reduces memory load and repeat work.
- A team needs shared starting points, such as "Expiring this week".
- Expert users want to customise the interface to their own needs.

## When not to use

- For one-off filtering. Use the TwoUX Filter bar; a URL already preserves the state.
- For display choices only. Use the TwoUX Columns menu, which is saved per person per table.

## Structure

1. View switcher (tabs or select) with live counts
2. Save view (rectangle button, shown when filters are on)
3. Unsaved changes indicator
4. Manage: rename, update, set default, delete

## Guidelines

- A view stores filters, sort order and column choices together.
- Keep filter state in the URL. On arrival, apply the default view unless the URL carries filter parameters.
- Show unsaved changes and let people return to the saved state in one step.
- Confirm before deleting or overwriting a view, naming the view in the dialog.
- Show only the metadata people need to tell views apart, such as name and live count.

## Content

- Name views after what they show, "Expiring this week", not "View 3".
- Use fixed action labels for the lifecycle: "Save view", "Update view", "Delete view", "Set as default".
- Confirmation text says what will change, for example that deleting removes the saved filters and columns.
- Most people will not customise, so ship sensible default views.

## Accessibility

- 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: the view switcher exposes the current view as selected.
- APG dialog pattern: the delete confirmation traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to the trigger.
- 4.1.3 Status Messages: "View saved" is announced without moving focus.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab, ← → | Move between views |
| Enter | Apply the view |
| Esc | Close the save or manage dialog |

## Examples

### views

```tsx
import { FilterBar, FilterPill, SavedViews, type SavedView, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Views with live counts", description: "A view stores filters, sort and columns together. Change a filter and the view shows Unsaved changes, with Reset and Update one click away. The ⋮ menu renames, sets the default or deletes the current view; deleting offers Undo.", order: 1 };

const OPTIONS = ["Open", "Closing soon", "Draft", "Closed"].map((v) => ({ value: v, label: v }));

export default function Example() {
	const [views, setViews] = useState<SavedView[]>([
		{ id: "all", name: "All listings", count: 24 },
		{ id: "open", name: "Open", count: 14 },
		{ id: "closing", name: "Closing soon", count: 4 },
	]);
	const [saved, setSaved] = useState<Record<string, string[]>>({ all: [], open: ["Open", "Closing soon"], closing: ["Closing soon"] });
	const [defaultId, setDefaultId] = useState("all");
	const [view, setView] = useState("open");
	const [status, setStatus] = useState(saved.open);
	const current = saved[view] ?? [];
	const dirty = status.length !== current.length || status.some((s) => !current.includes(s));
	const open = (id: string) => { setView(id); setStatus(saved[id] ?? []); };
	const nameOf = (id: string) => views.find((v) => v.id === id)?.name ?? "";

	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl gap-3">
			<SavedViews
				views={views}
				value={view}
				onValueChange={open}
				dirty={dirty}
				defaultId={defaultId}
				onReset={() => setStatus(current)}
				onSave={() => {
					const before = current;
					setSaved((s) => ({ ...s, [view]: status }));
					toast.success(`Updated “${nameOf(view)}”`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setSaved((s) => ({ ...s, [view]: before })) } });
				}}
				onSaveAs={(name) => {
					const id = `${name.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g, "-")}-${views.length}`;
					setSaved((s) => ({ ...s, [id]: status }));
					setViews((v) => [...v, { id, name, count: 6 }]);
					setView(id);
					toast.success(`Saved “${name}”`);
				}}
				onRename={(id, name) => {
					const before = nameOf(id);
					const rename = (to: string) => setViews((v) => v.map((x) => (x.id === id ? { ...x, name: to } : x)));
					rename(name);
					toast.success(`Renamed “${before}” to “${name}”`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => rename(before) } });
				}}
				onSetDefault={(id) => {
					const before = defaultId;
					setDefaultId(id);
					toast.success(`“${nameOf(id)}” opens by default`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setDefaultId(before) } });
				}}
				onDelete={(id) => {
					const index = views.findIndex((v) => v.id === id);
					const removed = views[index];
					const next = views.filter((v) => v.id !== id);
					const wasDefault = id === defaultId;
					setViews(next);
					// Deleting the default hands it to the first view left; the open view moves to the default.
					const fallback = wasDefault ? next[0].id : defaultId;
					if (wasDefault) setDefaultId(fallback);
					open(fallback);
					toast.success(`Deleted “${removed.name}”`, {
						action: {
							label: "Undo",
							onClick: () => {
								setViews((v) => [...v.slice(0, index), removed, ...v.slice(index)]);
								if (wasDefault) setDefaultId(id);
								open(id);
							},
						},
					});
				}}
			/>
			<FilterBar>
				<FilterPill field="Status" options={OPTIONS} selected={status} onChange={setStatus} />
			</FilterBar>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Filter pills and filter bar
- Filter panel
- Columns menu
- List table
- Data grid

# Bulk action bar

A grey band directly above the table while rows are selected: the actions that apply to every selected row, the count and Clear selection.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- People act on several records at once; checkboxes plus batch actions is the standard pattern.
- An action applies to all selected items, such as extending or closing listings.
- People select rows from the keyboard with X or Shift with J and K, then act without reaching for the mouse.

## When not to use

- For one or two actions on a single row. Use inline row actions or the side panel.
- For actions on the whole table regardless of selection, such as Export. Put them in the table toolbar.

## Structure

1. Band directly above the table, below any filters; the header row stays visible
2. Actions with icons and shortcuts, up to four (Ask, Extend 30 days, Duplicate); the rest in More
3. Destructive action (Close listings)
4. Count ("2 listings selected") and Clear selection (Esc)

## Guidelines

- Show the bar only while rows are selected, and always show how many.
- Place the bar directly above the table, below the filters, so the filters and the column headers stay in view.
- Show up to four actions as buttons. The rest, and any that don't fit the width, move into a More menu that keeps their shortcuts; never shrink actions to icons only.
- Exit by clearing the selection or pressing Esc.
- Disable row-level actions while the bulk bar is showing so the two do not compete.
- Confirm destructive bulk actions in a dialog that states the count and consequence, and offer Undo when the action can be reversed.
- Selection on the header checkbox covers the visible page only, and actions affect only selected rows.

## Content

- Label actions verb plus noun, "Close listings", and put the count in confirmations, "Close 2 listings?".
- Show each action's shortcut on the button.
- Put destructive actions last.

## Accessibility

- APG toolbar pattern: role="toolbar" with aria-label "Bulk actions", one tab stop, arrow keys between buttons.
- 4.1.3 Status Messages: announce "2 listings selected" when the count changes.
- 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: the bar sits in the page flow above the table, so it never covers a focused row.
- 2.5.8 Target Size: every button is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ← → | Move between actions |
| T | Extend 30 days |
| D | Duplicate |
| ⇧C | Close listings (asks to confirm) |
| ⌘J | Ask the assistant about the selection |
| Esc | Clear the selection |

## Examples

### selection

```tsx
import { BulkActionBar, Button, Checkbox, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { CalendarPlus, Copy } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { LISTINGS } from "../list-table/data";

export const meta = { title: "Act on selected listings", description: "While rows are selected, a band appears directly above the table with the actions, then the count and Clear selection. The header row and any filters stay in view. Arrow keys move between its buttons; Esc clears.", order: 1 };

const ROWS = LISTINGS.slice(0, 4);

export default function Example() {
	const [sel, setSel] = useState<string[]>([ROWS[0].id, ROWS[2].id]);
	const toggle = (id: string) => setSel((s) => (s.includes(id) ? s.filter((x) => x !== id) : [...s, id]));
	const all = sel.length === ROWS.length ? true : sel.length ? "indeterminate" : false;
	const setAll = (v: boolean) => setSel(v ? ROWS.map((r) => r.id) : []);
	const n = sel.length;
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-xl overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<BulkActionBar count={n} noun={n === 1 ? "listing" : "listings"} onClear={() => setSel([])} actions={[
					{ label: "Extend 30 days", icon: <CalendarPlus />, shortcut: "T", onSelect: () => toast.success(`Extended ${n} listing${n === 1 ? "" : "s"} by 30 days`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => {} } }) },
					{ label: "Duplicate", icon: <Copy />, shortcut: "D", onSelect: () => toast.success(`Duplicated ${n} listing${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}`) },
				]} />
			<Table aria-label="Listings">
				<TableHeader>
					<TableRow className="hover:bg-transparent">
						<TableHead className="w-9"><Checkbox aria-label="Select all on this page" checked={all} onCheckedChange={(v) => setAll(!!v)} /></TableHead>
						<TableHead>Role</TableHead>
						<TableHead>Location</TableHead>
					</TableRow>
				</TableHeader>
				<TableBody>
					{ROWS.map((r) => (
						<TableRow key={r.id} data-state={sel.includes(r.id) ? "selected" : undefined}>
							<TableCell><Checkbox checked={sel.includes(r.id)} onCheckedChange={() => toggle(r.id)} aria-label={`Select ${r.role}`} /></TableCell>
							<TableCell className="font-medium text-ink">{r.role}</TableCell>
							<TableCell className="text-ink-2">{r.location}</TableCell>
						</TableRow>
					))}
				</TableBody>
			</Table>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- List table
- Data grid
- Export menu

# Pagination and counts

The footer that says which rows are showing and how many exist ("1–100 of 1,262"), with previous and next controls and the selection count.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A collection is too large for one page or one view.
- Lists over 20 items, with pagination at the bottom.
- People need to know where they are and return to a section, which pagination supports better than endless scroll.

## When not to use

- Collections under five items.
- Steps in a flow. Use buttons or a progress control.
- When the total cannot be known, do not invent one; use an open-ended count such as "100+".

## Structure

1. Range and total ("Showing 1–9 of 24")
2. Selection count when rows are selected
3. Previous page
4. Page numbers or compact "1 of 3"
5. Next page

## Guidelines

- Show the range and the total. When rows are selected, put the selected count first.
- Use the compact "1 of 3" form where a row of page numbers does not fit, and offer jump to page past about 9 pages.
- Previous is inactive on the first page and Next on the last.
- Show pagination even when everything fits on one page, so the layout does not shift.
- Changing page clears the selection; say so in the selection count.

## Content

- Show the current range and the total together, for example "1–100 of 1,262", with an en dash and thousands separators.
- Name controls by destination, "Previous page", "Page 6", not "left".
- Do not show a count while the table is loading.

## Accessibility

- Wrap page links in a nav landmark with an aria-label, and mark the current page with aria-current="page".
- Give previous, next and page buttons labels; set them explicitly for non-English interfaces.
- 4.1.3 Status Messages: the range and selection count update as status text, "2 of 24 selected".
- After a page change, move focus and scroll to the top of the new content.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Reach the pagination controls |
| Enter / Space | Go to the previous, next or chosen page |

## Examples

### footer

```tsx
import { Checkbox, TablePagination } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Table footer", description: "Range and total always show, even on one page. With rows selected, the count comes first. Previous is off on the first page, Next on the last.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [page, setPage] = useState(0);
	const [selectSome, setSelectSome] = useState(true);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-3">
			<label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-base text-ink-2">
				<Checkbox checked={selectSome} onCheckedChange={(v) => setSelectSome(v === true)} />
				Show with 2 rows selected
			</label>
			<div className="overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
				<div className="grid h-24 place-items-center text-base text-ink-3">Page {page + 1} of the listings table</div>
				<TablePagination page={page} pageCount={14} pageSize={100} total={1262} selected={selectSome ? 2 : 0} noun="listings" onPageChange={setPage} />
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Data grid
- Columns menu
- Bulk action bar

# Grouped list

A compact list of records split under group headers (such as candidates by stage), each header showing its count.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Records fall into a small number of meaningful groups that people scan one at a time, such as pipeline stages.
- A short list where a full table would be heavy; simple vertical content reads better as a simple list.

## When not to use

- When people sort or compare many attributes across all records. Use the TwoUX List table.
- For nested hierarchies more than one level deep. Use a tree.
- For more than about seven groups at once; split with a filter or Saved view instead.

## Structure

1. Group header (name, count, optional action)
2. Rows: ID, title, secondary text, owner avatar, date
3. Divider between rows

## Guidelines

- Each group header has a tinted background so rows read as belonging to it.
- Show the count beside every group name.
- Keep the same row layout in every group so columns line up down the list.
- Allow groups to collapse when lists are long.

## Content

- Group names are the states people use, "Interviewing", "Screening", "Offer accepted".
- Order groups by workflow, not alphabetically.
- Keep row text to the ID, name, role, owner and date; open the row for more.

## Accessibility

- 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: each group is a list with a heading, so the grouping is available to assistive technology.
- APG disclosure pattern: collapsible headers are buttons with aria-expanded.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: J and K move through rows across groups, as in the List table.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| J / K | Move to the next or previous row |
| Enter | Open the row |
| Enter / Space (header) | Collapse or expand the group |

## Examples

### by-stage

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, GroupedList, ListGroup } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Candidates by stage", description: "Each tinted header names the group and counts it. Every row keeps the same layout so columns line up. Headers collapse with Enter or Space.", order: 1 };

const STAGES = [
	{ stage: "Interview", people: [["Priya Shah", "Frontend Engineer", "28 Oct"], ["Sofia Romano", "Junior Product Designer", "20 Oct"]] },
	{ stage: "Screen", people: [["Amara Okafor", "Junior Product Designer", "2 Nov"]] },
	{ stage: "Applied", people: [["Tom Becker", "Frontend Engineer", "4 Nov"], ["Liam Walsh", "Data Analyst", "5 Nov"], ["Hana Kim", "QA Engineer", "5 Nov"]] },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<GroupedList className="w-full max-w-xl" aria-label="Candidates by stage">
			{STAGES.map((g) => (
				<ListGroup key={g.stage} title={g.stage} count={g.people.length} defaultOpen={g.stage !== "Applied"} action={g.stage === "Applied" ? <Button variant="ghost" size="xs">Screen all</Button> : undefined}>
					{g.people.map(([name, role, date]) => (
						<li key={name} className="grid h-9 grid-cols-[1fr_auto_auto] items-center gap-3 px-3 text-base hover:bg-hover">
							<span className="min-w-0 truncate"><span className="font-medium text-ink">{name}</span> <span className="text-ink-3">· {role}</span></span>
							<Badge variant="secondary">{g.stage}</Badge>
							<span className="tabular w-14 text-right text-sm text-ink-3">{date}</span>
						</li>
					))}
				</ListGroup>
			))}
		</GroupedList>
	);
}
```

# Export menu

One Export menu per table: options first (only visible columns, include AI columns), then file formats, then copy to clipboard.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- People take table data to another tool. Export is a table-level toolbar action.
- Several related export actions start one action each; a menu suits 5 to 15 such items.

## When not to use

- For a single format. Use a plain button, "Export CSV", as on chart cards.
- To choose a value that changes the view. Use a select.

## Structure

1. Export button with a download icon
2. Menu heading with the shortcut (⇧E)
3. Options: Only visible columns, Include AI columns (checkable, the menu stays open)
4. Download CSV, Download JSON
5. Copy as CSV, Copy as JSON

## Guidelines

- Group items with labelled sections: options, download, copy.
- Options are checkbox items that toggle without closing the menu.
- Order by frequency: the most used format first.
- Confirm a copy or a finished download with a short status message.

## Content

- Use verb plus format, "Download CSV", "Copy as JSON".
- Checkbox labels state the choice so its opposite is clear, "Only visible columns".
- Write labels in sentence case on a single line.

## Accessibility

- APG menu button pattern: Enter, Space or Down Arrow opens the menu and focuses the first item.
- APG menu pattern: options use role="menuitemcheckbox" with aria-checked; Escape closes and returns focus to Export.
- 4.1.3 Status Messages: "Copied 24 rows as CSV" is announced without moving focus.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⇧E | Open the Export menu |
| ↑ ↓ | Move between items |
| Space | Toggle an option without closing |
| Enter | Run the export and close |
| Esc | Close and return focus to Export |

## Examples

### menu

```tsx
import { ExportMenu, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Export a table", description: "Options toggle without closing the menu. Downloads and copies run and close, then confirm with a toast. Opens with ⇧E.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [onlyVisible, setOnlyVisible] = useState(true);
	const [includeAi, setIncludeAi] = useState(false);
	const scope = `${onlyVisible ? "visible" : "all"} columns${includeAi ? ", with AI columns" : ""}`;
	return (
		<ExportMenu
			onlyVisible={onlyVisible}
			onOnlyVisibleChange={setOnlyVisible}
			includeAi={includeAi}
			onIncludeAiChange={setIncludeAi}
			onDownload={(f) => toast.success(`listings.${f.toLowerCase()} downloaded`, { description: `24 rows, ${scope}` })}
			onCopy={(f) => toast.success(`Copied 24 rows as ${f}`)}
		/>
	);
}
```

- Data grid
- List table
- Breakdown table
- Line chart card

# Board and board item

A dashboard grid of self-contained items, such as charts, stats and lists, that people can reorder, resize and remove to build the overview they need.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For an overview page people tailor to their own job, such as a hiring lead choosing which pipeline charts to watch.
- When each item stands alone and can be read without the others.

## When not to use

- For a fixed report everyone reads the same way. Lay it out with a plain grid; rearranging adds work without benefit.
- For a list of records. Use the List table.

## Structure

1. Board: a grid of up to 4 columns that stacks on narrow screens
2. Board item: drag handle, title and optional description, settings menu
3. Item content (padded by default)
4. Item footer (optional), such as a link to the full report
5. Empty slot: what shows when no items are on the board

## Guidelines

- Each item does one job: one chart, one stat, one short list. Its title names what it shows.
- Put the most important item first: the first row is what people see before they scroll.
- Every drag has two alternatives: the keyboard (pick up with Enter or Space, move with arrows, drop with Enter, Esc to cancel) and the item menu (Move earlier, Move later, Wider, Narrower).
- Announce every pick-up, move, resize, drop and removal to screen readers.
- Show an empty state with a way to add the first item when the board has none.
- Save the layout per person, so a change on one screen doesn't move someone else's dashboard.
- Add items opens the items palette in the side panel. Removed items return to the palette, so Remove and Add undo each other.
- Offer Reset to default layout in the page's more menu, applied at once with Undo in a toast.
- Save the layout on the server as each change happens, per person and per column count (4, 2 and 1), and restore it on reload and on other devices.
- The board has 4 columns on wide screens, 2 on tablet widths and 1 on phones; items span 1 to 4 columns and keep their order when stacking.
- When the board has no items, its empty state offers Add items and Reset to default layout.
- While dragging, show a drop preview of the item's size. Items swap where there is room and push others along where there is not; dropping outside the board returns the item to where it was.
- Moving an item keeps its size and its own settings. Heights snap to fixed row steps; the default height fits the default content.
- Show every stage of a drag. Ready: the grip darkens on hover and focus, with a grab cursor and a tooltip saying how to move it. Dragging: a lifted copy follows the pointer, the board tints to show where drops are allowed, and a dashed slot shows exactly where the item will land.
- Other items glide to make room (180ms, off with reduced motion) instead of jumping. On drop, a short highlight settles on the moved item and the new position is announced. Esc cancels and puts it back.
- Work out the landing slot against where items were when the drag started, so the slot doesn't jump as items move aside.

## Content

- Item titles are nouns for what is shown: “Applications this month”, not “Chart 1”.
- The menu says what will happen to the item: “Move earlier”, “Wider”, “Remove from dashboard”.

## Accessibility

- The drag handle is a button named “Move <title>”, with a description of the keys.
- Dragging is never the only way to move or resize (2.5.7 Dragging Movements).
- Moves and resizes are announced in a live region (4.1.3 Status Messages).
- Each item is an article labelled by its title, so screen reader users can jump between items.
- Every board item region has an accessible name, and the board offers a keyboard way to jump between items.
- Use a grab cursor on handles and a grabbing cursor while dragging, in addition to the handle icon.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter / Space (handle) | Pick up the item, or drop it |
| Arrow keys | Move the picked-up item one place |
| Esc | Cancel and put the item back |
| Tab | Reach the handle, the item's controls and its settings menu |

## Examples

### hiring-overview

```tsx
import { Board, BoardItem, type BoardItemData, Button, DropdownMenuItem, Empty, EmptyContent, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyMedia, EmptyTitle, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { LayoutDashboard } from "lucide-react";
import type React from "react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Hiring overview", description: "Drag an item by its handle, or focus the handle and press Enter, then the arrow keys. The ⋯ menu moves and resizes without dragging. Every change is announced.", order: 1 };

const DEFAULT: BoardItemData[] = [
	{ id: "apps", title: "Applications this month", columnSpan: 1 },
	{ id: "open", title: "Open listings", columnSpan: 1 },
	{ id: "tth", title: "Median time to hire", columnSpan: 2 },
	{ id: "stages", title: "Pipeline by stage", columnSpan: 2 },
	{ id: "closing", title: "Closing this week", columnSpan: 2 },
];

const STAGES = [["Applied", 412], ["Screen", 126], ["Interview", 48], ["Offer", 9]] as const;

// Colour says whether a change is good, not which way it went.
function Stat({ value, change, note, tone = "neutral" }: { value: string; change: string; note: string; tone?: "good" | "neutral" }) {
	return (
		<div className="grid gap-0.5">
			<span className="tabular text-2xl font-semibold text-ink">{value}</span>
			<span className="text-sm text-ink-2"><span className={tone === "good" ? "font-medium text-ok" : "font-medium text-ink"}>{change}</span> {note}</span>
		</div>
	);
}

function content(id: string) {
	if (id === "apps") return <Stat value="595" change="↑ 12%" note="vs October" tone="good" />;
	if (id === "open") return <Stat value="14" change="↓ 2" note="vs last week" />;
	if (id === "tth") return <Stat value="23 days" change="↓ 4 days" note="vs last quarter" tone="good" />;
	if (id === "stages")
		return (
			<ul className="grid gap-1.5">
				{STAGES.map(([s, n]) => (
					<li key={s} className="grid grid-cols-[72px_1fr_40px] items-center gap-2 text-sm">
						<span className="text-ink-2">{s}</span>
						<span className="h-2 overflow-hidden rounded-xs bg-hover" aria-hidden="true">
							<span className="block h-full w-(--w) rounded-xs bg-primary" style={{ "--w": `${(n / 412) * 100}%` } as React.CSSProperties} />
						</span>
						<span className="tabular text-right text-ink">{n}</span>
					</li>
				))}
			</ul>
		);
	return (
		<ul className="grid gap-1 text-sm">
			{[["Frontend Engineer", "Fri 21 Nov"], ["Customer Success Lead", "Sun 23 Nov"]].map(([r, d]) => (
				<li key={r} className="flex justify-between gap-2"><span className="truncate text-ink">{r}</span><span className="tabular shrink-0 text-ink-3">{d}</span></li>
			))}
		</ul>
	);
}

export default function Example() {
	const [items, setItems] = useState(DEFAULT);
	return (
		<Board
			className="w-full"
			aria-label="Hiring overview"
			items={items}
			onItemsChange={setItems}
			empty={
				<Empty className="min-h-48">
					<EmptyHeader>
						<EmptyMedia variant="icon"><LayoutDashboard /></EmptyMedia>
						<EmptyTitle>No items on this dashboard</EmptyTitle>
						<EmptyDescription>Add the charts and lists you want to watch.</EmptyDescription>
					</EmptyHeader>
					<EmptyContent><Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setItems(DEFAULT)}>Restore default items</Button></EmptyContent>
				</Empty>
			}
			renderItem={(it) => (
				<BoardItem
					id={it.id}
					header={it.title}
					footer={it.id === "stages" ? <a href="#pipeline" className="font-medium text-primary-ink hover:underline">Open pipeline report</a> : undefined}
					settings={<DropdownMenuItem onSelect={() => toast(`Opened ${it.title}`)}>View details</DropdownMenuItem>}
				>
					{content(it.id)}
				</BoardItem>
			)}
		/>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Line chart card
- Stat card with comparison
- Empty state

# Stat card with comparison

One number that matters, with its change against a named previous period shown by arrow, sign and colour, and an optional faint previous-period line.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A quick view of how one metric is doing, alone or beside related stats.
- The number is the answer; a chart would add reading time without insight.

## When not to use

- For one metric over time. Use the TwoUX Line chart card.
- For plain text or labels.

## Structure

1. Label with period ("Applications · last 30 days")
2. Value
3. Change: arrow, signed percentage, comparison text
4. Optional mini chart: current solid, previous dashed grey
5. Legend (This period, Previous period)

## Guidelines

- The number leads; label and change are secondary.
- Show change with an arrow, a sign and colour together, never colour alone.
- Say what the change compares against, "vs 264 the 30 days before".
- Draw the previous period as a dashed grey line behind the current one.
- Loading shows a skeleton of the number and change; an error shows "Couldn't load" with Try again in the card; no data shows a dash and "No data for this period", never 0.
- When the stat has a target, say it in text ("18 of 25 roles filled") rather than a ring or donut.

## Content

- Label with the metric and the period, and include units.
- Round the value for reading, keep the exact value in the tooltip.
- Keep any description to two lines; longer text is truncated with the full text in a tooltip.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: good or bad change is also shown by arrow and sign.
- 1.1.1 Non-text Content: the mini chart has a text alternative or is hidden because the figures are in text.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: the arrow and line reach 3:1 unless the text carries the same information.
- A missing value reads "No data for this period" to screen readers, not "dash".

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the card when it links to a report |

## Examples

### kpis

```tsx
import { StatCompare } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Key numbers", description: "One number, its change against a named period, and whether that change is good, said in colour and in words. Time to hire going down is good; applications going down is not.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full grid-cols-3 gap-3 max-md:grid-cols-1">
			{[
				{ label: "Applications this month", value: "595", change: "+12%", period: "October", good: true, spark: [42, 48, 51, 47, 55, 60, 58, 66] },
				{ label: "Median time to hire", value: "23 days", change: "-4 days", period: "last quarter", good: true, spark: [31, 30, 29, 27, 27, 25, 24, 23] },
				{ label: "Offer acceptance", value: "71%", change: "-6 pts", period: "last quarter", good: false, spark: [80, 79, 77, 78, 75, 74, 72, 71] },
			].map((s) => (
				<div key={s.label} className="rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-4 shadow-card"><StatCompare {...s} /></div>
			))}
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Line chart card

- Data visualisation colours
- Usage meter

# Line chart card

A card that shows how one or more series change over time, with a title, period controls, a Chart or Table switch, direct labels, a shared crosshair tooltip and a source footer.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing how a value changes over time.
- Comparing trends across a few series, such as applies per day by team.

## When not to use

- Comparing amounts between categories. Use the TwoUX Bar chart.
- Two measures with different units. Use two charts side by side, never two y-axes.
- One number that matters. Use the TwoUX Stat card with comparison.
- More than 8 series. Fold extras into "Other" or filter.

## Structure

1. Title (what is measured)
2. Subtitle (period)
3. Controls row: time range (7d, 30d, 90d), Chart or Table
4. Plot: 2px lines, faint grid, one y-axis
5. Direct labels at line ends
6. Legend (2 or more series)
7. Crosshair tooltip
8. Footer: source, updated time, Export CSV, Add to dashboard

## Guidelines

- Title says what is measured; the subtitle gives the period.
- Label line ends directly, and add a legend only for two or more series.
- One tooltip lists every series at the hovered day, sorted by value, with both axis values.
- Keep the grid faint and lines 2px; remove anything that does not carry data.
- A line chart may start above zero, unlike a bar chart.
- Every chart can switch to a table, which is also its accessible version.
- Every line chart has four states in the plot area, never blank: Loading: skeleton of the plot (axes and faint grid) with "Loading applications" as the region label. Empty: "No applications in this period" with one next step. No match: "No data matches these filters" with Clear filters. Error: "Couldn't load applications. Your filters are kept." with Try again.
- Missing days show as a break in the line, not a drop to zero.
- Legend items are toggles that show or hide a series; hidden series keep their colour slot. With three or more series, add a Series filter (all selected by default); with one, no filter and no legend.
- Selecting a point or pressing Enter pins the tooltip as a popover. A pinned popover can hold a breakdown of up to seven items and up to two footer buttons; see Chart drill-down.
- A target or limit is a threshold: a dashed line at a fixed value with a text label ("Target 40 a day"), not an extra series.
- Skip x-axis date labels at a regular interval rather than crowding or rotating them. The y-axis never shows time units.
- A forecast after today continues in the same colour but dashed, with a vertical "Today" marker, so the split is not shown by colour alone. Keep grey dashed for the previous period only.

## Content

- Use nouns in titles and keep axis titles to one to three words with units.
- Labels, values and legends use text colours; the series colour sits beside them as a swatch.
- The footer names the data source and when it updated.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: a short alternative names the chart type, data and period; the table view is the long description.
- 1.4.1 Use of Color: direct labels identify series, so colour is not the only cue.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: lines needed to read the data reach 3:1 against the background.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the plot is focusable and arrow keys move the crosshair day by day.
- The accessible name matches the visible title; the description reads "Line chart showing applications per day by team, last 30 days."
- Legend toggles are buttons with aria-pressed, and hiding a series is announced politely.
- Enter pins the tooltip, Tab moves into its content, Esc closes it and returns focus to the same day.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the plot |
| ← → | Move the crosshair to the previous or next day |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### applications

```tsx
import { CartesianChart, ChartFrame, ChartLegend, type ChartStatus, SegmentedControl, Segment, chartTable, seriesColor } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
import { APPLICATIONS, WEEKS } from "./data";

export const meta = { title: "Applications by team", description: "Hover, or focus the chart and use the arrow keys, to read every value. Click a legend key to hide a series. The table button shows the same numbers as a table.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [hidden, setHidden] = useState<string[]>([]);
	const [state, setState] = useState<ChartStatus>("ready");
	const [period, setPeriod] = useState("8w");
	const n = period === "4w" ? 4 : 8;
	const x = WEEKS.slice(-n);
	const series = APPLICATIONS.map((s) => ({ ...s, data: s.data.slice(-n) }));
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full gap-3">
			<ChartFrame
				title="Applications per week"
				description={`All open listings, last ${n} weeks`}
				status={state}
				onRetry={() => setState("ready")}
				table={chartTable("Week", x, series)}
				actions={
					<SegmentedControl value={period} onValueChange={setPeriod} size="sm" aria-label="Period">
						<Segment value="4w">4 weeks</Segment>
						<Segment value="8w">8 weeks</Segment>
					</SegmentedControl>
				}
				legend={<ChartLegend items={APPLICATIONS.map((s, i) => ({ id: s.id, label: s.label, color: seriesColor(i), shape: "line" }))} hidden={hidden} onToggle={(id) => setHidden((h) => (h.includes(id) ? h.filter((x) => x !== id) : [...h, id]))} />}
			>
				<CartesianChart kind="line" x={x} series={series} hidden={hidden} aria-label="Applications per week by team" />
			</ChartFrame>
			<SegmentedControl value={state} onValueChange={(v) => setState(v as ChartStatus)} size="sm" aria-label="Preview state" className="justify-self-start">
				{(["ready", "loading", "empty", "error"] as const).map((s) => <Segment key={s} value={s}>{s[0].toUpperCase() + s.slice(1)}</Segment>)}
			</SegmentedControl>
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Bar chart
- Stat card with comparison
- Breakdown table
- Data visualisation colours
- Export menu

# Bar chart

Vertical bars from a zero baseline for comparing amounts per period or category, with the latest bar labelled and an incomplete period shown lighter.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Comparing amounts across items or periods; simple bars are quickly processed and understood.
- Emphasising the total of each data point.

## When not to use

- Showing a trend over time where shape matters more than totals. Use the TwoUX Line chart card.
- Two dimensions at once. Use the TwoUX Heatmap.
- Breaking down task outcomes as stacks; stacked bars are hard to read. Use separate simple bars.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Zero baseline
3. Bars (4px rounded top, gap between)
4. Latest-bar label
5. Incomplete period bar (lighter, labelled)
6. Hover tooltip

## Guidelines

- Bars always start at zero.
- Use horizontal bars when category names are long.
- Label only the latest bar; hover shows the rest.
- The current, incomplete period is lighter and says so in a label.
- A single series uses colour 1 and no legend.
- Bar charts have the same four states as line charts: skeleton plot while loading, empty, no match with Clear filters, and error with Try again.
- Use horizontal bars when there are many categories or long names, such as applications by listing title; vertical bars for periods.
- With several series, group bars to compare the parts. Stack only when the total is the main reading and there are four parts or fewer, with a 2px surface-colour gap between segments.
- A single series uses one colour for every bar. Never colour bars by month or by category for variety.
- A goal or limit is a dashed threshold line with a text label, such as "Target 120".
- The pinned popover can break a bar down into up to seven parts, with a link on the name or the value, not both.

## Content

- Title names the measure; subtitle gives the period and scope.
- Keep tick increments fixed and match time labels to the data's period.
- Label the incomplete period plainly, "This week so far".

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: provide a short alternative and a table with the values.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: bars reach 3:1 against the background.
- 1.4.1 Use of Color: the incomplete period is marked in text, not lightness alone.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: arrow keys move between bars and show each value.
- Description: "Bar chart showing applications per week, last 12 weeks." It matches the visible title and period.
- Grouped and stacked bars name each part in the tooltip and table, so colour is not the only cue.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → | Move to the previous or next bar |

## Examples

### hires

```tsx
import { CartesianChart, ChartFrame, ChartLegend, SegmentedControl, Segment, chartTable, seriesColor } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
import { HIRES, WEEKS } from "../chart-card-line/data";

export const meta = { title: "Hires per week", description: "Grouped bars compare teams week by week; stacked shows the total. Bars start at zero with 4px rounded ends and 2px gaps.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [mode, setMode] = useState("grouped");
	return (
		<ChartFrame
			className="w-full"
			title="Hires per week"
			description="Offers accepted, by team"
			table={chartTable("Week", WEEKS, HIRES)}
			actions={
				<SegmentedControl value={mode} onValueChange={setMode} size="sm" aria-label="Bar layout">
					<Segment value="grouped">Grouped</Segment>
					<Segment value="stacked">Stacked</Segment>
				</SegmentedControl>
			}
			legend={<ChartLegend items={HIRES.map((s, i) => ({ id: s.id, label: s.label, color: seriesColor(i) }))} />}
		>
			<CartesianChart kind="bar" stacked={mode === "stacked"} x={WEEKS} series={HIRES} aria-label="Hires per week by team" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

# Heatmap

A grid of two dimensions (such as team by weekday) shaded in one hue from light to dark, with every cell showing its number and a legend under the grid.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing a quantity across two dimensions at once, such as when people apply by team and weekday.
- Spotting patterns and hot spots matters more than reading exact values; the printed numbers cover exact reading.

## When not to use

- When people must compare exact amounts; colour is a poor encoding of magnitude. Use the TwoUX Bar chart or Breakdown table.
- For one dimension over time. Use the TwoUX Line chart card.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Row labels (team)
3. Column labels (weekday)
4. Cells with value text
5. Legend: Fewer to More ramp, under the grid

## Guidelines

- One hue, light for low and dark for high, never a rainbow.
- Every cell shows its number, so colour is never the only cue.
- Avoid red and green together; for diverging values use blue against orange or red.
- Separate neighbouring cells with a gap in the surface colour.
- Put the legend under the grid.
- While loading, show the grid with empty cells and labels; on error replace the grid with the error state and Try again; with no data, an empty state.
- Missing cells show a dash and "No data" in the tooltip, never the lightest step, which would read as low.
- Selecting a cell can drill down to the list behind it, such as candidates who applied to Design on Mondays, as a filtered List table.

## Content

- Legend ends say "Fewer" and "More", not colour names.
- Title says what is counted; subtitle gives the period, "Applies by team and weekday, last 30 days".
- Choose text colour per cell so numbers stay readable on dark steps.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: values are printed in the cells, which is the sufficient technique of adding text.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: heat maps can fall under the essential exception, but because the cells show values TwoUX does not depend on it.
- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: give a short alternative and a table of the values.
- The grid is keyboard reachable: Tab to the grid, arrow keys move cell to cell, and each cell is announced with row, column and value.
- Accessible description: "Heatmap showing applies by team and weekday, last 30 days."

## Examples

### weekday

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, Heatmap } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "When candidates apply", description: "One hue from light to dark, a legend from fewer to more, and every value in the cell's accessible name. Zero is grey, not the lightest step.", order: 1 };

const DAYS = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"];
const TEAMS = ["Design", "Engineering", "Data", "People"];
const V = [[12, 18, 15, 14, 9, 2, 4], [31, 36, 33, 29, 21, 6, 9], [7, 9, 11, 8, 6, 0, 1], [4, 6, 5, 7, 3, 0, 0]];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full max-w-2xl" title="Applications by weekday" description="Last 4 weeks, by team">
			<Heatmap rows={TEAMS} columns={DAYS} values={V} aria-label="Applications by team and weekday" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Data visualisation colours
- Breakdown table
- Bar chart

# Funnel

Horizontal bars for ordered stages (views, applies, interviews, offers) that show each stage's count and its rate from the stage before, darkest to lightest.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing ordered stages where people care how many make it from one step to the next.
- Comparing amounts at each stage, which simple bars make quick to read.

## When not to use

- For unordered categories. Use the TwoUX Bar chart.
- For change over time. Use the TwoUX Line chart card.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle (scope, starting count)
2. Stage label
3. Bar (length by count)
4. Count
5. Rate from the previous stage

## Guidelines

- Encode counts as bar length from a shared left edge; length is judged accurately.
- Show each stage's rate from the stage before; that is the number people act on.
- Stages go darkest to lightest in one hue, following order.
- Write counts beside bars so colour and length are not the only cues.
- Show the four states: skeleton bars while loading, empty, no match with Clear filters, error with Try again.
- A stage's count links to the List table filtered to that stage, so people go from "Interviewed 42" to those 42 candidates.
- Do not use a donut for stages; order is the point and a ring loses it.

## Content

- Stage names are the steps people use, "Viewed", "Applied", "Interviewed".
- The subtitle states the base, "from 6,840 views".
- Write rates as percentages with the same decimals on every stage.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 Non-text Content: the accessible name lists each stage with its count.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: the lightest stage bar still reaches 3:1, or the printed count carries the value.
- 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: stages are in reading order in the markup.
- Stage links are named by stage and count: "View 42 interviewed candidates".
- Arrow keys move between stages when the funnel is focused.

## Examples

### pipeline

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, Funnel } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Hiring funnel", description: "Ordered stages as horizontal bars. Each stage shows its count and the share that moved on from the stage before.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full max-w-2xl" title="Pipeline, this quarter" description="All listings">
			<Funnel aria-label="Hiring funnel this quarter" stages={[{ label: "Viewed", value: 8420 }, { label: "Applied", value: 595 }, { label: "Screened", value: 126 }, { label: "Interviewed", value: 48 }, { label: "Offered", value: 9 }]} />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Bar chart
- Stat card with comparison
- Data visualisation colours


---

# Breakdown table

A table under a chart that splits its figure by team, location or owner, with current and previous periods side by side and change in both units.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A chart needs its exact values and a split by dimension; the table doubles as the chart's long description.
- People compare values across rows.

## When not to use

- For many columns people edit. Use the TwoUX Data grid.
- For record lists. Use the TwoUX List table.

## Structure

1. Breakdown switch (By team, By location, By owner)
2. Export CSV
3. Columns: dimension, This period, Previous period, Change, Change %

## Guidelines

- Sit directly under the chart it explains.
- Show change with sign and arrow, not colour alone.
- Show a dash when there is nothing to compare, with hidden text for screen readers.
- Sort by the current period by default and allow sorting by any column.
- When a chart offers drill-down, the breakdown table is where the same split lives in full; a popover breakdown never holds data that is not also here.
- Each row's count can link to the filtered List table behind it; link the count or the name, not both.
- Rows follow the chart's filters and series toggles, so the table and chart never disagree.

## Content

- Right-align numbers with consistent decimals.
- Column headers state the period, "This period", "Previous period".
- Write change with its sign, "+12" and "−8%", so direction reads without colour.

## Accessibility

- 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: real table markup with scoped headers.
- APG sortable table: aria-sort on the sorted header only.
- The By team, By location, By owner switch exposes the pressed state.
- When the chart filters change, announce the new row count politely without moving focus.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the switch, Export and sortable headers |
| Enter / Space | Change breakdown or sort |

## Examples

### by-team

```tsx
import type React from "react";
import { CartesianChart, ChartFrame, ChartLegend, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, seriesColor } from "@twoux/ui";
import { APPLICATIONS, WEEKS } from "../chart-card-line/data";

export const meta = { title: "Chart with its breakdown", description: "The table under the chart splits the same figure by team, with current, previous and change. The colour key in each row ties it to the chart.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Applications per week" description="Last 8 weeks" legend={<ChartLegend items={APPLICATIONS.map((s, i) => ({ id: s.id, label: s.label, color: seriesColor(i), shape: "line" }))} />}>
			<CartesianChart kind="line" x={WEEKS} series={APPLICATIONS} height={180} aria-label="Applications per week by team" />
			<div className="overflow-hidden rounded-xs border border-line">
				<Table aria-label="Applications by team">
					<TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Team</TableHead><TableHead className="text-right">This week</TableHead><TableHead className="text-right">Last week</TableHead><TableHead className="text-right">Change</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
					<TableBody>
						{APPLICATIONS.map((s, i) => {
							const [now, prev] = [s.data[s.data.length - 1] ?? 0, s.data[s.data.length - 2] ?? 0];
							const pct = Math.round(((now - prev) / (prev || 1)) * 100);
							return (
								<TableRow key={s.id}>
									<TableCell><span className="inline-flex items-center gap-2"><span aria-hidden="true" className="h-0.5 w-3 rounded-full bg-(--c)" style={{ "--c": seriesColor(i) } as React.CSSProperties} />{s.label}</span></TableCell>
									<TableCell className="tabular text-right font-medium">{now}</TableCell>
									<TableCell className="tabular text-right text-ink-2">{prev}</TableCell>
									<TableCell className="tabular text-right">{pct >= 0 ? "↑" : "↓"} {Math.abs(pct)}%</TableCell>
								</TableRow>
							);
						})}
					</TableBody>
				</Table>
			</div>
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Line chart card
- Bar chart
- Stat card with comparison
- Export menu

# Stacked area chart

Two or more series stacked over time, so the top edge is the total and each band is one part of it, such as applications per week split by source.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When the total over time matters and so does how it splits, such as weekly applications by source (LinkedIn, Indeed, Careers page, Referral).
- When the parts always add up to a meaningful whole, such as candidates in the pipeline by stage at the end of each week.

## When not to use

- For one series. Use the Line chart card; a single filled area only adds ink.
- For values that can go negative, such as net change in open roles. Use the Line chart card or Bar chart.
- For series that do not add up to a whole, such as applications for two unrelated listings. Overlapping areas hide each other; use lines.
- When people need to compare the middle bands exactly. Only the bottom band sits on a flat baseline; use the Line chart card or a Breakdown table.

## Structure

1. Title (what is measured) and subtitle (period)
2. Controls row: time range, Chart or Table
3. Plot: stacked bands from a zero baseline, a thin surface-colour line between bands, one y-axis
4. Legend: one item per band, in stack order, each a toggle
5. Crosshair tooltip: every band's value and the total at the hovered date
6. Optional threshold: dashed line with a text label
7. Footer: source and updated time

## Guidelines

- Always stack, always from zero. The top edge must read as the true total.
- Use two to five bands. Fold the smallest sources into "Other" at the top of the stack rather than adding a sixth colour.
- Put the largest or steadiest band at the bottom so the most important part has a flat baseline, and keep the stack order the same on every chart.
- Use categorical colours in fixed order from colour 1, separated by a thin line in the surface colour so neighbouring bands stay distinct.
- The tooltip lists bands in the same order as the stack, top to bottom, then the total.
- Show missing weeks as a gap, never as a drop to zero.
- Hiding a band from the legend restacks the rest and updates the total in the tooltip. Colours do not move.

## Content

- Title names the total and the split: "Applications by source". Subtitle gives the period: "Last 12 weeks".
- Legend items use the names people use in the product: "Careers page", not "careers_site". Never truncate a name if the end is what tells two apart.
- Skip x-axis labels at a regular interval (every other week) instead of crowding them, and abbreviate months: "3 Nov".

## Accessibility

- The chart has an accessible name matching its title and a description such as "Stacked area chart showing applications by source, last 12 weeks."
- The Table view lists every band per week plus the total, and is the long description.
- Bands are named in the tooltip and legend, so colour is never the only way to tell them apart.
- Legend items are toggle buttons with a pressed state; hiding one is announced politely: "Referral hidden".

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the plot, then each legend item |
| ← → | Move the crosshair to the previous or next week |
| Enter | Pin the tooltip so its links can be reached with Tab |
| Esc | Close the tooltip and return focus to the plot |
| Space (legend item) | Show or hide that band |

## Examples

### pipeline

```tsx
import { CartesianChart, ChartFrame, ChartLegend, chartTable, seriesColor } from "@twoux/ui";
import { APPLICATIONS, WEEKS } from "../chart-card-line/data";

export const meta = { title: "Applications, stacked by team", description: "Stacked from zero, so the top edge is the total and each band is one team. Use it when the total matters as much as the parts; for comparing teams, use lines.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Applications per week" description="Stacked by team" table={chartTable("Week", WEEKS, APPLICATIONS)} legend={<ChartLegend items={APPLICATIONS.map((s, i) => ({ id: s.id, label: s.label, color: seriesColor(i) }))} />}>
			<CartesianChart kind="area" stacked x={WEEKS} series={APPLICATIONS} aria-label="Applications per week, stacked by team" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Line chart card
- Bar chart
- Data visualisation colours
- Breakdown table
- Data visualisation

# Bar and line chart

One bar series with one to three lines on the same y-axis and unit, such as weekly applications as bars and their four-week average as a line.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When a count and a reference for that count share a unit: hires per month as bars, planned hires per month as a line.
- When volume per period is the main reading and the line adds the trend, such as applications per week with the four-week average.

## When not to use

- When the two measures have different units or scales, such as applications (count) and conversion to interview (%). Use two charts side by side; never a second y-axis.
- When every series is the same kind of measure, such as applications for three listings. Use the Line chart card or grouped bars.
- For a fixed target that does not change by period. Use a threshold line on the Bar chart instead.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Plot: one y-axis, zero baseline, bars for the main measure
3. Line or lines (2px) for a related measure in the same unit: average, plan or previous period
4. Legend: bar swatch and line swatch with names
5. Crosshair tooltip with each series at the hovered period
6. Optional threshold: dashed line with a text label

## Guidelines

- Only one series is drawn as bars. Lines carry up to three related series, so the chart stays within four series in all.
- Bars start at zero, so the shared axis starts at zero too.
- Bars use categorical colour 1; lines use the next colours in order. A previous-period line stays the dashed grey from the Period comparison pattern.
- Draw lines on top of bars and put a marker on each line point so it stays visible where it crosses a bar.
- Show missing periods as gaps in the line and no bar, not as zero.
- If the line and the bars stop sharing a unit after a change in the data, split the chart. Do not add a right-hand axis.

## Content

- Name each series by role: "Hires", "Plan", "4-week average". The legend says which is the bar and which is the line through its swatch.
- Axis title states the shared unit once: "Applications". No unit on the y-axis for time.
- Title is a noun phrase naming the main measure: "Hires against plan".

## Accessibility

- Description names both marks: "Bar and line chart showing hires per month against plan, last 12 months."
- Bars and lines differ by shape, not only by colour, and the tooltip names every series.
- Bars and lines reach 3:1 against the background; the line marker keeps 3:1 where it sits on a bar.
- The Table view has one column per series with the same names as the legend.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the plot, then each legend item |
| ← → | Move to the previous or next period |
| Enter | Pin the tooltip |
| Esc | Close the tooltip |

## Examples

### applications-target

```tsx
import { CartesianChart, ChartFrame, ChartLegend, type ChartSeries, chartTable, seriesColor } from "@twoux/ui";
import { WEEKS } from "../chart-card-line/data";

export const meta = { title: "Applications against the average", description: "Bars for this period, a line for the 8-week average, and a dashed target. All three share one axis and one unit; different units would need two charts.", order: 1 };

const SERIES: ChartSeries[] = [
	{ id: "apps", label: "Applications", type: "bar", data: [151, 170, 168, 188, 204, 219, 218, 250] },
	{ id: "avg", label: "8-week average", type: "line", data: [160, 163, 165, 171, 178, 186, 192, 196] },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Applications per week" description="Against the rolling average and the target" table={chartTable("Week", WEEKS, SERIES)} legend={<ChartLegend items={SERIES.map((s, i) => ({ id: s.id, label: s.label, color: seriesColor(i), shape: s.type === "line" ? "line" : "box" }))} />}>
			<CartesianChart kind="mixed" x={WEEKS} series={SERIES} threshold={{ value: 220, label: "Target 220" }} aria-label="Applications per week with average and target" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Bar chart
- Line chart card
- Stat card with comparison
- Data visualisation colours
- Data visualisation
