# Donut chart

Two to five parts of one total at a single moment, with the total in the centre and every segment labelled with its count and share. Most of the time a bar chart is better.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When the question is how one total splits at one moment, and there are two to five parts: open roles by work pattern (On site, Hybrid, Remote (UK)).
- When the total itself is worth showing, which the centre of the donut holds.

## When not to use

- For change over time. Use the Line chart card, or the Stacked area chart for parts over time.
- For more than five parts. Use a horizontal Bar chart sorted by size.
- When parts are close in size and the difference matters, such as 31% against 34%. Angles are hard to compare; use a Bar chart.
- For one value against a goal, such as 18 of 25 roles filled. Use the Stat card with comparison.
- For ordered stages such as Applied to Offer. Use the Funnel.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle (the moment or period)
2. Ring of segments starting at 12 o'clock, clockwise, with a 2px surface-colour gap between segments
3. Centre: total value and a one or two word unit ("412 candidates")
4. Segment labels: name, count, share
5. Legend, required when any part is zero
6. Details popover on hover or select

## Guidelines

- Order segments clockwise from 12 o'clock, largest first, unless the parts have their own order (Junior, Mid, Senior), in which case keep that order.
- Colour segments with categorical colours in fixed order from colour 1. Never give each slice a colour chosen by meaning.
- Label every segment with its count and share, so the chart reads without hovering.
- A part with a value of zero has no segment but stays in the legend, so people can see it was counted.
- Keep a minimum segment size so a small part stays visible and selectable, and show its true share in the label.
- When people filter parts out, recalculate the centre total and every share.

## Content

- Segment labels read count, unit, share: "124 candidates, 30%".
- Centre text is the total and a short unit: "412" over "candidates". One or two words only.
- Title is a noun phrase that names the whole: "Open roles by work pattern".
- If a name must be cut, keep the part that tells it apart: "…Designer, Leeds" rather than "Junior Product…".

## Accessibility

- Description: "Donut chart showing open roles by work pattern, today." The Table view lists each part with count and share.
- Segments are identified by their printed labels and the legend, never by colour alone.
- Segments reach 3:1 against the background, and the 2px gap keeps neighbours apart.
- Arrow keys move between segments and show each one's details in the popover.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart, then the legend items |
| ← → | Move to the previous or next segment |
| Enter | Pin the details popover |
| Esc | Close the popover |

## Examples

### sources

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, DonutChart } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Where applicants come from", description: "Two to five parts of one whole, each labelled with its count and share. For more parts, or to compare sizes closely, use a bar chart.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full max-w-xl" title="Applications by source" description="This month">
			<DonutChart totalLabel="applications" aria-label="Applications by source" segments={[
				{ id: "board", label: "Job boards", value: 312 },
				{ id: "site", label: "Careers page", value: 164 },
				{ id: "ref", label: "Referrals", value: 71 },
				{ id: "agency", label: "Agencies", value: 48 },
			]} />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Bar chart
- Stat card with comparison
- Stacked area chart
- Data visualisation colours
- Data visualisation

# Scatter chart

One dot per record placed by two measures, such as each live listing by advertised salary and applications, for spotting relationships and outliers.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When the question is whether two measures move together across records: salary and applications per listing, or days open and applications.
- When outliers matter: a listing with a high salary and few applications is worth opening.

## When not to use

- For change over time. Use the Line chart card.
- For fewer than about ten records. Use a Breakdown table; a scatter of five dots shows no pattern.
- To compare candidates. Plotting people by scores invites ranking them; candidate decisions stay with the hiring team and are never made from a chart.
- To encode a third measure as dot size. Use a second scatter or a table instead.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Plot: x-axis and y-axis, each with a title and unit
3. Dots, one per record (up to three groups by colour and shape)
4. Optional threshold lines with text labels
5. Legend when there are two or more groups
6. Details popover: the record's name and both values, with a link to it

## Guidelines

- Each axis has a title with its unit; axes may start above zero if the axis says so, because position, not length, carries the value.
- Use at most three groups, coloured with categorical colours 1 to 3 and each with its own marker shape (circle, square, triangle), since any dot can touch any other.
- Keep dots small (6px) with a 1px surface-colour outline so overlapping dots stay visible.
- Selecting a dot opens the details popover with the listing's name, both values and a link to the record.
- Do not draw a trend line unless the team asked for one and its method is named in the footer.

## Content

- Title names both measures: "Salary and applications by listing". Subtitle gives the scope: "Live listings, last 30 days".
- Axis titles are short with units: "Salary (£k)", "Applications".
- Popover reads as key and value pairs: "Junior Product Designer, Leeds", "Salary £32k", "Applications 46".

## Accessibility

- Description: "Scatter chart showing salary and applications for 38 live listings, last 30 days." The Table view lists every record with both values.
- Groups differ by marker shape as well as colour.
- Arrow keys move from dot to dot in x order and open each popover; a pinned popover stays until Esc.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the plot, then the legend |
| ← → | Move to the previous or next dot along the x-axis |
| Enter | Pin the popover and reach its link |
| Esc | Close the popover |

## Examples

### salary-applicants

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, ScatterChart } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Salary against applicants", description: "One dot per listing, up to three teams, each with its own colour and shape. Arrow keys move along the x axis; Enter pins the details with a link to the listing.", order: 1 };

const P = [
	["Junior Product Designer", 30, 38, "Design"], ["Senior Product Designer", 58, 37, "Design"], ["Content Designer", 42, 21, "Design"],
	["Frontend Engineer", 52, 112, "Engineering"], ["Backend Engineer", 60, 64, "Engineering"], ["QA Engineer", 40, 47, "Engineering"], ["Platform Engineer", 68, 29, "Engineering"],
	["Data Analyst", 41, 64, "Data"], ["Analytics Engineer", 55, 33, "Data"], ["Data Scientist", 62, 41, "Data"],
] as const;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Salary and applicants" description="Open listings, salary from in £000s">
			<ScatterChart aria-label="Salary against applicants by team" xTitle="Salary from (£000s)" yTitle="Applicants" points={P.map(([label, x, y, group], i) => ({ id: String(i), label, x, y, group, href: "#listing" }))} />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Line chart card
- Breakdown table
- Data visualisation colours
- Chart drill-down
- Data visualisation

# Items palette

A searchable list, in a side panel beside a configurable dashboard, of the items a person can add, each with a title, a short description, its type and an Add to dashboard button.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- With a configurable dashboard, to add items that are not on the board yet.
- As the place removed items return to, so people can add them back.
- When new item types ship, so people find them without a layout being changed for them.

## When not to use

- On a static dashboard. There is nothing to add.
- To pick records or templates. Use the command palette or the templates gallery.
- To change what an item on the board shows. Use Preferences in that item's menu.

## Structure

1. Panel header: "Add items", item count and close
2. Search field that filters by title and description
3. Palette item: drag handle, title, one-line description, type tag (Chart, List, Key metrics), Add to dashboard button
4. Zero results: message with Clear search
5. Empty palette: "All items are on your dashboard"

## Guidelines

- List only items that are not on the board. When one is added it leaves the palette; when it is removed it comes back.
- Palette items describe; they do not preview. No live numbers, charts or menus, only title, description and type.
- Every palette item has an Add to dashboard button as well as its drag handle. The button adds the item at the end of the board in its default size. Keyboard users add with the button, then place the item with the board's own keyboard move; there is no separate keyboard drag from the palette.
- While dragging, the palette item takes the shape of its default size on the board and shows a drop preview.
- Add search once there are more than about ten items, and show a zero results message with Clear search.
- The panel pushes the board, stays open while people add several items, and closes with Esc or Add items again.

## Content

- Descriptions say what the item answers: "Applications per week for the last 12 weeks, compared with the previous period."
- Type tags use one word or two: Chart, List, Key metrics, Links, Alerts.
- Zero results: "No items match \"cost\"." with Clear search.

## Accessibility

- The panel is a complementary region labelled "Add items"; focus moves to its search field when it opens and returns to Add items when it closes.
- Add to dashboard is named with the item: "Add Applications this week to dashboard".
- After an add, announce "Applications this week added to the end of the dashboard" and keep focus in the palette on the next item.
- Dragging from the palette is never required; the button covers the same result with a single action.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move between search, palette items and their Add buttons |
| Enter (Add button) | Add the item to the end of the board |
| Esc | Cancel a pick-up, or close the panel |
| Then, on the board | Use the new item's handle (Enter, arrows, Enter) or its menu to move it |

## Examples

### add-items

```tsx
import { Board, BoardItem, type BoardItemData, Button, ItemsPalette, type PaletteItem, SidePanel, StatCompare, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Plus } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Add items to a dashboard", description: "The palette lists only what isn't on the board. Add puts an item at the end in its default size; drag drops it where you let go. Removing an item returns it to the palette.", order: 1 };

const CATALOGUE: PaletteItem[] = [
	{ id: "apps", title: "Applications this month", description: "Total applications and change against last month", type: "Key metrics" },
	{ id: "tth", title: "Median time to hire", description: "Days from opening a listing to an accepted offer", type: "Key metrics" },
	{ id: "accept", title: "Offer acceptance", description: "Share of offers accepted this quarter", type: "Key metrics" },
	{ id: "closing", title: "Closing this week", description: "Listings that close in the next 7 days", type: "List" },
];
const VALUES: Record<string, [string, string, string, boolean]> = { apps: ["595", "+12%", "October", true], tth: ["23 days", "-4 days", "last quarter", true], accept: ["71%", "-6 pts", "last quarter", false] };

export default function Example() {
	const [items, setItems] = useState<BoardItemData[]>([{ id: "apps", title: "Applications this month" }]);
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);
	const palette = CATALOGUE.filter((c) => !items.some((i) => i.id === c.id));
	const add = (id: string, at = items.length) => {
		const c = CATALOGUE.find((x) => x.id === id);
		if (!c) return;
		setItems((x) => { const n = [...x]; n.splice(at, 0, { id, title: c.title }); return n; });
		toast.success(`Added ${c.title}`);
	};
	return (
		<div className="flex h-104 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-bg">
			<div className="min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-auto p-3">
				<div className="mb-2 flex justify-end"><Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}><Plus />Add items</Button></div>
				<Board
					items={items}
					onItemsChange={setItems}
					onAddFromPalette={add}
					empty={<p className="rounded-sm border border-dashed border-line-strong p-8 text-center text-base text-ink-2">Drag an item here, or use Add.</p>}
					renderItem={(it) => (
						<BoardItem id={it.id} header={it.title}>
							{VALUES[it.id] ? <StatCompare label="" value={VALUES[it.id][0]} change={VALUES[it.id][1]} period={VALUES[it.id][2]} good={VALUES[it.id][3]} /> : <p className="text-sm text-ink-2">Frontend Engineer · Fri 21 Nov</p>}
						</BoardItem>
					)}
				/>
			</div>
			<SidePanel open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} label="Add items" title="Add items" meta={`${palette.length} available`}>
				<ItemsPalette items={palette} onAdd={(id) => add(id)} />
			</SidePanel>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Board and board item
- Configurable dashboard
- Dashboard items
- Side panel (drawer)

# Share bar

One whole split into up to six parts in a single horizontal bar, with each part's name and share in a legend above. Smaller parts fold into a grey Other.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing how one total splits at one moment, read at a glance, such as recurring revenue by plan.
- A card or table header has room for a line, not a chart: a thin bar takes 8px and the legend carries the numbers.

## When not to use

- To compare parts precisely or rank more than six of them. Use the TwoUX Bar chart, because bars on one baseline compare more exactly than segments end to end.
- To show the split changing over time. Use the TwoUX Area chart.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Legend above the bar: swatch, name and share for each part
3. Bar: one block per part with a 2px surface gap
4. Other: the folded tail, in grey
5. Tooltip: name, share and amount

## Guidelines

- Keep to six parts; the smallest fold into Other, which is always grey and always last.
- Separate parts with a 2px gap in the surface colour, never a border.
- Colours follow the order you pass, c1 first. Pass parts in a stable order so a part keeps its colour from one period to the next.
- Thin bar: shares go in the legend above, not on the bar. Tall bar: the share prints inside each block only when it fits, and the legend gives names.
- Use a share bar instead of a donut when space is a line, not a square.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Shares to one decimal place in the legend, whole percentages inside a tall bar.
- Name the part people know (Business, Team), not an internal code.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: every part is named in the legend and in the generated summary, so colour is not the only way to tell parts apart.
- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### plan-revenue

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, ShareBar, shareTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Recurring revenue by plan", description: "A thin bar under a legend that already gives each share. Eight plans arrive; the two smallest fold into Other so the bar keeps six parts.", order: 1 };

const PLANS = [
	{ id: "business", label: "Business", value: 1_284_000 },
	{ id: "team", label: "Team", value: 612_000 },
	{ id: "enterprise", label: "Enterprise", value: 498_000 },
	{ id: "starter", label: "Starter", value: 231_000 },
	{ id: "agency", label: "Agency", value: 104_000 },
	{ id: "education", label: "Education", value: 46_000 },
	{ id: "charity", label: "Charity", value: 21_000 },
	{ id: "legacy", label: "Legacy", value: 9_000 },
];
const gbp = (n: number) => `£${(n / 1000).toLocaleString("en-GB", { maximumFractionDigits: 0 })}k`;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Recurring revenue by plan" description="Annual run rate, 5 November 2026" table={shareTable(PLANS, gbp, "Plan")} height={60}>
			<ShareBar parts={PLANS} format={gbp} aria-label="Recurring revenue by plan" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

# Ranked list

Ranked rows with a series dot or icon, name, value and change, optionally a sparkline. Beside a stacked chart it is the chart's legend; each row links to the record.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- As the legend of a stacked chart when people also need the ranking and values for the latest period.
- A dashboard list of the top items by one measure, each opening its record.

## When not to use

- To compare many attributes per row or sort by them. Use the TwoUX List table.
- For a price or index list where the code and unit matter. Use the TwoUX Change list.

## Structure

1. Heading that names the moment, such as Top models on 28 Apr
2. Rank
3. Series dot (or icon)
4. Name
5. Optional sparkline
6. Value, tabular
7. Change: arrow, sign and percentage

## Guidelines

- Rank by the value shown, highest first, and say which period ranks it in the heading.
- When the list is a legend, each dot keeps its series colour from the chart; never recolour by rank.
- Show change with an arrow and a sign; colour it green or red only when the direction means good or bad, otherwise grey.
- Hovering or focusing a row highlights that series in the chart, and the chart's crosshair can highlight the row.
- Each row is one link or one button for the whole row, never several actions.

## Content

- Values carry their unit (bn tokens, £); changes say the comparison in the heading or subtitle.
- Keep names short enough to fit; the full name goes in the record.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: change is an arrow, a sign and a word read out (up or down), not colour.
- 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: the list is an ordered list, so rank is announced.
- 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: each row is a single link or button whose name includes the label, value and change.
- 2.4.7 Focus Visible: rows show the focus ring inside their edge.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the next row |
| Enter | Open the row's record |

## Examples

### top-models

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { CartesianChart, ChartFrame, type ChartSeries, chartTable, RankedList } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Top models beside a stacked chart", description: "The ranked list is the legend: each row's dot matches its series, ranked by the last day, with the change since the week before.", order: 1 };

const DAYS = ["22 Apr", "23 Apr", "24 Apr", "25 Apr", "26 Apr", "27 Apr", "28 Apr"];
const SERIES: ChartSeries[] = [
	{ id: "atlas", label: "Atlas 3", data: [3.1, 3.4, 3.3, 3.8, 2.9, 2.6, 4.2] },
	{ id: "nimbus", label: "Nimbus Pro", data: [2.4, 2.5, 2.7, 2.6, 2.1, 1.9, 2.8] },
	{ id: "kestrel", label: "Kestrel 2", data: [1.2, 1.4, 1.5, 1.7, 1.3, 1.2, 1.9] },
	{ id: "orbit", label: "Orbit Mini", data: [1.6, 1.5, 1.4, 1.4, 1.1, 1.0, 1.3] },
	{ id: "other", label: "Others", data: [0.9, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 0.8, 0.7, 1.0] },
];
const CHANGE = [12.4, 6.1, 31.0, -9.7, 4.2];
const tokens = (n: number) => `${n.toFixed(1)}bn`;

export default function Example() {
	const [active, setActive] = useState<string | null>(null);
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Tokens by model" description="Daily tokens, last 7 days" table={chartTable("Day", DAYS, SERIES)}>
			<div className="grid grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,18rem)] gap-6 max-lg:grid-cols-1">
				<CartesianChart kind="bar" stacked x={DAYS} series={SERIES} format={(n) => `${n}bn`} aria-label="Tokens by model, stacked by day" />
				<div className="grid content-start gap-1">
					<h4 className="px-2 text-sm font-medium text-ink-2">Top models on 28 Apr</h4>
					<RankedList
						aria-label="Top models on 28 April, by tokens"
						items={SERIES.map((s, i) => ({ id: s.id, label: s.label, value: s.data[6] ?? 0, change: CHANGE[i], colorIndex: i, href: `#${s.id}` }))}
						format={tokens}
						upIs="neutral"
						activeId={active}
						onActiveChange={setActive}
					/>
				</div>
			</div>
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

# Change list

Ticker rows for indices, prices or rates: name and code, value with unit, change by arrow, sign and colour, an optional sparkline, and a See all link.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A short dashboard list of instruments or metrics where today's level and change matter most.
- Several numbers that move together, each too small for its own stat tile.

## When not to use

- For one headline number. Use the TwoUX Stat compare.
- To rank items by a share of a total. Use the TwoUX Ranked list.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle (period, delay)
2. Row: name and code
3. Optional sparkline of the period
4. Value with unit, tabular
5. Change: arrow, sign and percentage
6. Footer: See all link

## Guidelines

- Keep to about five to seven rows and link to the full list with See all.
- Change shows an arrow, a sign and a colour; colour alone is never the signal.
- Values align in tabular figures with their unit after the number.
- Sparklines use one colour and no axis; they show shape, the number gives the level.
- Say how fresh the data is in the subtitle, such as 15 minutes delayed.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Name first, code second in smaller text: people scan names, specialists scan codes.
- Use a real minus sign for falls and two decimals for percentage change.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: arrow and sign carry direction; screen readers hear up or down with the value.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: arrows use the status text colours, which meet 4.5:1.
- 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: each row is one link named by its whole content.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the next row, then See all |
| Enter | Open the row |

## Examples

### indices

```tsx
import { ChangeList } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Market indices", description: "Name and code, value with unit, change by arrow, sign and colour, and today's line. The footer links to the full list.", order: 1 };

// Intraday path: 48 five-minute points from a seeded walk that ends at today's change, so each line has real ups and downs.
function intraday(value: number, changePct: number, volatility: number, seed: number) {
	const rand = () => ((seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647);
	const open = value / (1 + changePct / 100);
	const n = 48;
	const walk = [0];
	for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) walk.push(walk[i - 1] + (rand() - 0.5) * 2);
	const end = walk[n - 1];
	return walk.map((w, i) => open + (w - (end * i) / (n - 1)) * open * volatility + ((value - open) * i) / (n - 1));
}

const ROWS = [
	{ id: "uk100", name: "UK 100", symbol: "UKX", value: 8412.36, unit: "pts", change: 0.42, spark: intraday(8412.36, 0.42, 0.0011, 11) },
	{ id: "uk250", name: "UK 250", symbol: "MCX", value: 20184.9, unit: "pts", change: -0.31, spark: intraday(20184.9, -0.31, 0.001, 23) },
	{ id: "eu600", name: "Europe 600", symbol: "SXXP", value: 512.07, unit: "pts", change: 0.18, spark: intraday(512.07, 0.18, 0.0009, 37) },
	{ id: "gilt10", name: "UK gilt, 10 year", symbol: "GUKG10", value: 4.12, unit: "%", change: 0.0, spark: intraday(4.12, 0.0, 0.0016, 53) },
	{ id: "gbpusd", name: "Pound to dollar", symbol: "GBP/USD", value: 1.2846, unit: "USD", change: -0.12, spark: intraday(1.2846, -0.12, 0.0004, 71) },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChangeList
			className="w-full max-w-md"
			title="Major indices"
			description="Today, 15 minutes delayed"
			items={ROWS.map((r) => ({ ...r, href: `#${r.id}` }))}
			format={(n) => n.toLocaleString("en-GB", { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: n < 10 ? 4 : 2 })}
			seeAll={{ href: "#markets", label: "See all markets" }}
		/>
	);
}
```

- Price chart

# Price chart

One price over a session: a line with a light wash, the last value tagged on the right axis, the previous close as a dashed reference, a live dot, and an axis that says when it does not start at zero.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A price or rate that moves within a narrow band, where the movement is the point, such as a share price today.
- A live value where people need the latest level and where it stands against a reference.

## When not to use

- For amounts that should be compared from zero, such as revenue. Use the TwoUX Line chart card, which always starts at zero.
- For open, high, low and close per day. Use the TwoUX Candlestick chart.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle (unit, delay)
2. Plot: line with a 10% wash down to the axis floor
3. Right axis with ticks and the last-value tag
4. Dashed reference line with label (previous close)
5. Live dot at the last point
6. Time axis across the whole session
7. Note under the axis when it does not start at zero
8. Crosshair tooltip: time, price, change against the reference

## Guidelines

- Start the axis at zero unless the range is narrow; when it does not, say so under the axis.
- Lay out the whole session on the time axis so the empty part of the day stays visible.
- Tag the last value on the right axis and hide ticks that would collide with it.
- Draw the reference as a dashed grey line with a text label, never a series.
- Fill under the line with a light wash of the series colour, not a solid block.
- The live dot pulses only while the market is open, and never under reduced motion.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Put the unit and delay in the subtitle, such as In pence, 15 minutes delayed.
- Label the reference by what it is (Previous close), with its value.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.
- Accessible description: "Line chart showing Ashdown plc share price today in pence."
- 2.2.2 and 2.3.3: the pulsing dot is under five seconds per cycle and stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### intraday

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, PriceChart } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Share price today", description: "Ten-minute prices from the open, the session's remaining slots left empty, the last price tagged on the right axis and the previous close as a dashed reference. The axis starts above zero and says so.", order: 1 };

const TIMES = ["08:00", "08:10", "08:20", "08:30", "08:40", "08:50", "09:00", "09:10", "09:20", "09:30", "09:40", "09:50", "10:00", "10:10", "10:20", "10:30", "10:40", "10:50", "11:00", "11:10", "11:20", "11:30", "11:40", "11:50", "12:00", "12:10", "12:20", "12:30", "12:40", "12:50", "13:00", "13:10", "13:20", "13:30", "13:40", "13:50", "14:00", "14:10", "14:20", "14:30", "14:40", "14:50", "15:00", "15:10", "15:20", "15:30", "15:40", "15:50", "16:00", "16:10", "16:20", "16:30"];
const TRADED = [741.8, 742.7, 742.5, 742.2, 741.0, 740.9, 742.6, 743.3, 745.0, 745.5, 746.2, 746.6, 744.4, 745.7, 746.6, 747.4, 745.2, 742.9, 741.8, 741.3, 741.9, 742.0, 742.9, 742.1, 742.7, 743.4, 742.6, 745.2, 746.1, 747.9, 747.2, 746.3, 746.0, 746.0, 747.0, 747.5, 747.1, 745.9, 745.3];
const PRICES = TIMES.map((_, i) => TRADED[i] ?? null);
const pence = (n: number) => `${n.toLocaleString("en-GB", { minimumFractionDigits: 1, maximumFractionDigits: 1 })}p`;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame
			className="w-full"
			title="Ashdown plc share price"
			description="Today, in pence, 15 minutes delayed"
			table={{ columns: ["Time", "Price"], rows: TIMES.slice(0, TRADED.length).map((t, i) => [t, pence(TRADED[i])]) }}
		>
			<PriceChart x={TIMES} data={PRICES} format={pence} reference={{ value: 741.2, label: "Previous close" }} live aria-label="Ashdown plc share price today" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

- Candlestick chart
- Change list

# Waterfall chart

How an opening amount becomes a closing amount: each increase and decrease floats from the running total, joined by connectors, with totals in grey from zero.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Explaining how a balance or profit moved from one figure to another, such as cash flow for a month.
- A bridge between two totals where each step matters, such as budget to actual.

## When not to use

- To show a series over time. Use the TwoUX Line chart card.
- For parts of one total with no order. Use the TwoUX Share bar or Bar chart.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Y axis from zero (or below, when totals go negative)
3. Total bars in grey from zero
4. Increase and decrease bars floating from the running total
5. Connector lines between bars
6. Value labels with + or − where they fit
7. Legend: increase, decrease, total
8. Tooltip: change and running total

## Guidelines

- Increases and decreases take two categorical colours (c1 and c2), never green and red; the + or − on each label carries direction.
- Totals are grey and start from zero, so they read as levels, not changes.
- Join bars with thin connectors at the running total.
- Print a value only where it fits; the tooltip and table always have it.
- Order steps as the money moved: opening, money in, money out, closing.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Use a real minus sign and a plus sign on every change; totals have no sign.
- Name the legend by meaning (Money in, Money out, Balance), not by colour.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: direction is carried by the sign on each label, in the tooltip and in the table, not by colour.
- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.
- Accessible description: "Waterfall chart showing cash flow for October 2026."

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### cash-flow

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, Waterfall, type WaterfallStep, waterfallTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Cash flow for the month", description: "Opening balance, money in and money out, then the closing balance as a total. Grey totals, two categorical colours for in and out, a + or − on every change that fits.", order: 1 };

const STEPS: WaterfallStep[] = [
	{ id: "open", label: "Opening", value: 1_240_000, total: true },
	{ id: "subs", label: "Subscriptions", value: 486_000 },
	{ id: "services", label: "Services", value: 92_000 },
	{ id: "payroll", label: "Payroll", value: -412_000 },
	{ id: "hosting", label: "Hosting", value: -88_000 },
	{ id: "rent", label: "Rent", value: -46_000 },
	{ id: "vat", label: "VAT", value: -131_000 },
	{ id: "close", label: "Closing", total: true },
];
const gbp = (n: number) => (Math.abs(n) >= 1_000_000 ? `£${(n / 1_000_000).toFixed(2)}m` : n === 0 ? "£0" : `£${Math.round(n / 1000)}k`);

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Cash flow" description="October 2026, all accounts" table={waterfallTable(STEPS, gbp)}>
			<Waterfall steps={STEPS} format={gbp} labels={{ increase: "Money in", decrease: "Money out", total: "Balance" }} aria-label="Cash flow, October 2026" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Bar chart
- Bullet chart
- Stat card with comparison

# Bullet chart

Actual against target for a few measures: a thin bar over grey qualitative bands with the target as a dark tick, in a fraction of a gauge's space.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing progress against a target for several measures in one card, such as bookings this quarter.
- Where a gauge or dial was asked for: a bullet chart says the same in a line.

## When not to use

- For a single number with no target. Use the TwoUX Stat compare.
- For usage against a hard limit. Use the TwoUX Usage meter.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Row: measure name, actual and target as text
3. Qualitative bands in neutral grey steps, darkest for the worst
4. Actual: thin bar in c1
5. Target: dark tick
6. Scale under each bar
7. Legend: actual, target, bands

## Guidelines

- Use a bullet chart, never a gauge or dial.
- Bands are neutral grey steps, darkest for the worst range; they never use status colours.
- The actual is a thin bar in the first series colour, the target a dark tick across it.
- Print actual and target as text on each row, so the bar is never the only way to read them.
- Each row has its own scale; never compare bar lengths between rows with different scales.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Name the bands by meaning (Poor, Satisfactory, Good), worst first.
- Write actual of target, such as £412k of £450k.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: values are printed; bands are named in the legend and in each row's name.
- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: each row's accessible name gives the actual, target, percentage of target and band.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: each row is focusable and shows the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: the actual bar and target tick meet 3:1 against every band.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the next measure |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### quarter-targets

```tsx
import { BulletChart, ChartFrame } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Quarter to date against target", description: "Each measure is a thin bar over grey bands, with the target as a dark tick. It replaces a row of gauges in a third of the space.", order: 1 };

const ROWS = [
	{ id: "new", label: "New business", value: 412_000, target: 450_000, bands: [300_000, 400_000, 500_000] },
	{ id: "expansion", label: "Expansion", value: 188_000, target: 160_000, bands: [100_000, 150_000, 220_000] },
	{ id: "renewals", label: "Renewals", value: 731_000, target: 820_000, bands: [700_000, 800_000, 900_000] },
];
const gbp = (n: number) => (n === 0 ? "£0" : `£${Math.round(n / 1000)}k`);

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame
			className="w-full"
			title="Bookings against target"
			description="Quarter to date, Q4 2026"
			table={{ columns: ["Measure", "Actual", "Target", "Of target"], rows: ROWS.map((r) => [r.label, gbp(r.value), gbp(r.target), `${Math.round((r.value / r.target) * 100)}%`]) }}
		>
			<BulletChart rows={ROWS} format={gbp} aria-label="Bookings against target, quarter to date" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

# Treemap

Parts of a total as nested rectangles sized by value: squarified so tiles stay readable, names only where they fit, and the tail folded into Other after 12 tiles.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing which of many items make up most of a total, such as cloud spend by service.
- A total with one level of grouping, where the groups matter as well as the items.

## When not to use

- To compare items precisely. Use the TwoUX Bar chart, because areas are read less exactly than lengths.
- For five parts or fewer. Use the TwoUX Share bar.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Tiles sized by value, with 2px surface gaps
3. Name and share inside tiles that can hold them
4. Other tile in grey
5. Legend of groups when there are two or more
6. Tooltip: name, value, share, group

## Guidelines

- Keep to 12 tiles; the rest fold into a grey Other.
- Use the squarified layout so tiles stay close to square and readable.
- Without groups every tile is one colour; with groups each group takes its series colour and a legend. Never colour tiles by value.
- Print a name only where it fits and a share only where there is room; never clip text.
- Values go in the tooltip and the Table view.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Short tile names; the full name is in the tooltip and table.
- Subtitle gives the period and scope, such as October 2026, all projects.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: groups are named in the legend and the tooltip; every value is in the table.
- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.
- Accessible description: "Treemap showing cloud spend by service, October 2026."

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### cloud-spend

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, shareTable, Treemap } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Cloud spend by service", description: "Fifteen services in three groups: the twelfth tile onwards fold into Other. Names show only on tiles big enough to hold them.", order: 1 };

const ITEMS = [
	{ id: "vm", label: "Virtual machines", value: 48_200, group: "Compute" },
	{ id: "k8s", label: "Kubernetes", value: 31_400, group: "Compute" },
	{ id: "fn", label: "Functions", value: 6_900, group: "Compute" },
	{ id: "gpu", label: "GPU instances", value: 22_800, group: "Compute" },
	{ id: "obj", label: "Object storage", value: 18_600, group: "Storage" },
	{ id: "block", label: "Block storage", value: 12_100, group: "Storage" },
	{ id: "backup", label: "Backups", value: 5_400, group: "Storage" },
	{ id: "pg", label: "Postgres", value: 19_700, group: "Data" },
	{ id: "wh", label: "Warehouse", value: 15_300, group: "Data" },
	{ id: "cache", label: "Cache", value: 4_200, group: "Data" },
	{ id: "stream", label: "Streaming", value: 3_900, group: "Data" },
	{ id: "search", label: "Search", value: 2_800, group: "Data" },
	{ id: "dns", label: "DNS", value: 600, group: "Compute" },
	{ id: "logs", label: "Log archive", value: 1_100, group: "Storage" },
	{ id: "etl", label: "ETL jobs", value: 900, group: "Data" },
];
const gbp = (n: number) => `£${n.toLocaleString("en-GB")}`;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Cloud spend by service" description="October 2026, all projects" table={shareTable(ITEMS, gbp, "Service")} height={260}>
			<Treemap items={ITEMS} format={gbp} aria-label="Cloud spend by service, October 2026" />
		</ChartFrame>

}
```

# Sankey chart

Flows from left to right across two or three columns, such as traffic sources to pages to outcomes. Link width shows value; hover or focus highlights a path.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing how a quantity splits and recombines across stages, such as visits from sources to pages to outcomes.
- Finding the largest flows into a loss, such as where people leave.

## When not to use

- For ordered stages where each is a subset of the last. Use the TwoUX Funnel.
- For more than three columns or about 12 nodes; split it or use a table.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Columns of nodes
3. Links, width by value
4. Labels: name, value and share of column
5. Highlighted path on hover or focus
6. Tooltip: from, to, value, share of source

## Guidelines

- Keep to two or three columns and about 12 nodes.
- Link width is proportional to value; links use one hue at low opacity so overlaps stay readable.
- Hovering a node lights every flow through it; hovering a link lights that link.
- Labels give name, value and share of the column when there is room; on narrow screens names only.
- The Table view lists every flow as from, to and value.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Name the last column by outcome (Started trial, Left), not by page.
- Shares are of the column, so each column adds to 100%.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.
- Accessible description: "Sankey chart showing visits from source to page to outcome, last 30 days."
- 1.4.1 Use of Color: links are one hue; their values are in labels, tooltips and the table.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### pricing-traffic

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, SankeyChart, sankeyTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Visits to the pricing page", description: "Where visits came from, which page they reached, and what they did next. Hover a node to light every flow through it.", order: 1 };

const NODES = [
	{ id: "organic", label: "Organic search" },
	{ id: "paid", label: "Paid search" },
	{ id: "direct", label: "Direct" },
	{ id: "referral", label: "Referral" },
	{ id: "pricing", label: "Pricing page" },
	{ id: "docs", label: "Docs" },
	{ id: "trial", label: "Started trial" },
	{ id: "demo", label: "Booked demo" },
	{ id: "left", label: "Left" },
];
const LINKS = [
	{ source: "organic", target: "pricing", value: 8_200 },
	{ source: "organic", target: "docs", value: 4_100 },
	{ source: "paid", target: "pricing", value: 5_600 },
	{ source: "direct", target: "pricing", value: 3_900 },
	{ source: "direct", target: "docs", value: 2_300 },
	{ source: "referral", target: "pricing", value: 1_800 },
	{ source: "pricing", target: "trial", value: 2_900 },
	{ source: "pricing", target: "demo", value: 1_100 },
	{ source: "pricing", target: "left", value: 15_500 },
	{ source: "docs", target: "trial", value: 1_200 },
	{ source: "docs", target: "left", value: 5_200 },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Visits to pricing and docs" description="Last 30 days" table={sankeyTable(NODES, LINKS)} height={280}>
			<SankeyChart nodes={NODES} links={LINKS} aria-label="Visits from source to page to outcome, last 30 days" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

# Histogram

How values spread: touching columns, one per equal bin, counted on one axis, with an optional dashed marker such as the median.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Seeing the shape of a distribution, such as salary offers, where an average hides the tail.
- Checking whether most values sit in a range before setting a threshold.

## When not to use

- To compare distributions of several groups. Use the TwoUX Box plot.
- For counts by named category. Use the TwoUX Bar chart.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Y axis: count
3. Columns, one per bin, 2px gaps
4. X axis: bin edges and title with unit
5. Optional dashed marker with label
6. Tooltip: range, count, share

## Guidelines

- Use equal, round bin widths and say the width in the subtitle or table.
- Columns touch with a 2px surface gap, because bins are continuous.
- The y axis starts at zero and counts; there is one axis only.
- Mark the median or a threshold with a dashed grey line and a text label.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- X axis title names the measure and unit, such as Annual salary offered.
- Count label is the plural noun of what is counted (offers).

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.
- Accessible description: "Histogram showing salary offers in £5k bins, last 12 months."

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### salary-offers

```tsx
import { binValues, ChartFrame, Histogram, histogramTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Salary offers", description: "140 offers in £5k bins with the median marked. The shape shows the long tail a single average hides.", order: 1 };

const OFFERS = [23000, 27000, 28500, 29500, 30000, 30000, 30000, 30000, 31500, 32500, 33000, 33500, 33500, 34000, 34000, 35500, 36000, 36000, 36500, 37000, 37500, 38000, 38000, 38000, 38000, 38500, 38500, 39000, 39500, 40000, 40000, 40500, 40500, 40500, 40500, 41000, 41000, 41000, 41500, 41500, 42000, 42500, 42500, 43000, 43000, 43000, 43500, 43500, 43500, 44000, 44000, 45000, 45000, 45500, 45500, 46500, 46500, 46500, 47000, 49500, 50000, 50500, 50500, 50500, 50500, 51000, 51000, 51000, 51500, 51500, 52000, 52500, 53000, 53500, 53500, 53500, 54000, 54000, 54500, 55000, 55000, 55000, 55000, 55500, 56000, 56500, 57000, 57500, 57500, 57500, 57500, 57500, 58000, 58000, 58500, 59000, 60000, 62000, 62000, 62000, 62500, 62500, 63000, 63000, 63000, 63000, 63500, 64000, 64500, 65000, 65000, 65500, 66000, 67000, 67500, 68000, 68000, 68000, 70000, 70500, 75500, 75500, 76000, 76500, 76500, 77500, 78500, 79500, 79500, 79500, 82500, 83000, 83500, 83500, 88000, 91000, 92000, 93500, 101500, 104000];
const BINS = binValues(OFFERS, { binWidth: 5000, start: 20000 });
const gbp = (n: number) => `£${n / 1000}k`;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Salary offers" description="Offers made, last 12 months" table={histogramTable(BINS, gbp, "Salary")}>
			<Histogram bins={BINS} format={gbp} xTitle="Annual salary offered" countLabel="offers" marker={{ value: 52000, label: "Median £52k" }} aria-label="Salary offers, last 12 months" />
		</ChartFrame>
```

# Box plot

Distributions of several groups on one axis: a box for the middle half, a line for the median, whiskers to 1.5 times the IQR and dots for outliers.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Comparing how spread out several groups are, such as response times by team.
- Finding outliers worth opening, such as the slowest tickets.

## When not to use

- For one group's shape. Use the TwoUX Histogram.
- For audiences new to statistics; show median and range in a table or a range plot instead.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Group labels
3. Shared value axis with title and unit
4. Box from Q1 to Q3
5. Median line
6. Whiskers with caps
7. Outlier dots
8. Legend explaining the parts
9. Tooltip: median, middle half, whiskers, outliers

## Guidelines

- Put every group on one shared axis.
- Whiskers reach the furthest value within 1.5 times the IQR; values beyond are outlier dots.
- Always show the legend explaining box, median, whiskers and outliers.
- Order groups by meaning or by median, not alphabetically by default.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Say Middle half (Q1 to Q3) rather than only IQR.
- Axis title gives the measure and unit, such as Hours to first response.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.
- Accessible description: "Box plot showing first response time by team, last 40 tickets."

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### response-times

```tsx

const TEAMS = [
	{ id: "billing", label: "Billing", values: [4.7, 1.3, 2.9, 3.3, 4.0, 4.2, 3.4, 2.1, 3.4, 5.1, 2.6, 1.9, 2.4, 5.4, 2.1, 3.7, 2.2, 0.9, 2.4, 3.3, 1.7, 10.8, 3.2, 2.4, 2.7, 5.0, 2.8, 1.3, 4.3, 5.4, 1.6, 2.1, 6.8, 2.9, 2.9, 2.7, 3.0, 1.8, 1.6, 7.0] },
	{ id: "onboarding", label: "Onboarding", values: [9.5, 3.2, 3.3, 11.4, 7.0, 2.4, 4.1, 9.9, 3.3, 18.5, 2.0, 15.3, 5.2, 11.0, 9.5, 6.5, 9.4, 6.5, 8.4, 7.9, 4.3, 2.1, 5.7, 4.8, 4.1, 4.7, 6.5, 2.3, 3.5, 4.4, 5.6, 5.3, 31.2, 8.4, 11.4, 4.3, 6.2, 5.9, 2.1, 5.7] },
	{ id: "integrations", label: "Integrations", values: [27.7, 7.3, 6.3, 18.5, 10.2, 22.2, 8.0, 22.1, 6.1, 3.5, 8.3, 12.8, 6.9, 10.9, 12.7, 11.7, 12.8, 9.4, 6.0, 8.5, 15.8, 5.0, 5.4, 20.1, 7.7, 15.4, 7.4, 7.5, 13.6, 2.9, 12.4, 3.6, 8.6, 9.0, 4.1, 2.2, 20.4, 11.0, 13.6, 11.3] },
```

# Candlestick chart

Open, high, low and close per period for a price. Up candles are hollow and down candles filled, in two categorical colours, or green and red on trading screens; volume is its own chart below.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing how a traded price moved each day, including its range, for people who read markets.
- Spotting days with wide ranges or large volume.

## When not to use

- For a general audience or one price over time. Use the TwoUX Price chart or Line chart card.
- For anything that is not open, high, low and close.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Price axis on the right, not from zero, with a note
3. Candles: wick for high and low, body for open and close
4. Optional last-price tag on the axis, with a dashed line
5. Up: hollow c1; down: filled c2 (green and red with colors="market")
6. Volume chart below with its own axis, sharing the crosshair
7. Legend: up and down
8. Tooltip: change, open, high, low, close, volume

## Guidelines

- Up and down take two categorical colours and differ in fill too: up hollow, down filled.
- Use two categorical colours by default. On trading screens, where people expect it, use green for up and red for down (colors="market"); the hollow and filled bodies stay, so colour is never the only cue.
- Put volume in its own chart below with its own axis; never a second y axis.
- The price axis need not start at zero, and says so.
- One crosshair for both charts, so a day's price and volume read together.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.
- On a live market, tag the last price on the axis (showLast) and move only the forming candle as prices arrive.

## Content

- Dates as day and short month (5 Nov); the unit in the subtitle.
- Legend says what up means: Up (close above open).

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: direction is carried by hollow or filled bodies, the tooltip and the table.
- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart has a short generated summary as its accessible name and a Table view with every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the chart is one tab stop; arrow keys move between marks and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip never covers the mark it describes, stays while the pointer is over the chart and closes with Esc.
- Accessible description: "Candlestick chart showing Ashdown plc daily prices, last 30 trading days."

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next mark and show its values |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last mark |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### daily

```tsx
import { type Candle, CandlestickChart, candleTable, ChartFrame } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Daily prices with volume", description: "Ninety trading days. Up days are hollow, down days filled, and volume sits in its own panel under the prices with the same crosshair.", order: 1 };

// 90 trading days from a seeded random walk, so the example looks like a real price series and stays the same on every load.
function tradingDays(count: number, endDate: Date) {
	const days: Date[] = [];
	const d = new Date(endDate);
	while (days.length < count) {
		if (d.getDay() !== 0 && d.getDay() !== 6) days.unshift(new Date(d));
		d.setDate(d.getDate() - 1);
	}
	return days;
}
function makeCandles(): Candle[] {
	let seed = 7;
	const rand = () => ((seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647);
	let close = 742;
	return tradingDays(90, new Date(2026, 10, 5)).map((day) => {
		const open = close + (rand() - 0.5) * 4;
		const pull = (742 - open) * 0.06; // drifts back towards a middle price, like a stock trading in a range
		close = open + pull + (rand() - 0.5) * 22 + (rand() > 0.93 ? (rand() - 0.5) * 34 : 0);
		const high = Math.max(open, close) + rand() * 9;
		const low = Math.min(open, close) - rand() * 9;
		const big = Math.abs(close - open) > 12;
		const v = Math.round((1.4 + rand() * 1.4 + (big ? 1.2 : 0)) * 1_000_000);
		const r = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 10) / 10;
		return { t: day.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "short" }), o: r(open), h: r(high), l: r(low), c: r(close), v };
	});
}
const DAYS: Candle[] = makeCandles();
const pence = (n: number) => `${n.toLocaleString("en-GB", { minimumFractionDigits: 1, maximumFractionDigits: 1 })}p`;

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Ashdown plc, daily" description="Last 90 trading days, in pence" table={candleTable(DAYS, pence)} height={320}>
			<CandlestickChart candles={DAYS} format={pence} aria-label="Ashdown plc daily prices, last 90 trading days" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Price chart
- Line chart card
- Bar chart
- Order book

# Order book

Resting sell and buy orders either side of the spread, each with a bar for the running total, so people see where the price is likely to meet resistance and can pick a price to trade at.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- A trading screen where people place limit orders and need the prices other people are offering.
- Showing how much can be bought or sold before the price moves, through the running totals.

## When not to use

- For a price over time. Use the TwoUX Candlestick chart or Price chart.
- For a short list of prices with today's change. Use the TwoUX Change list.

## Structure

1. Group by: − and + to widen or narrow price groups
2. Column headings with units: Price, Amount, Total
3. Sell orders above, best (lowest) price next to the spread
4. Middle line: last price with its direction, and the spread
5. Buy orders below, best (highest) price next to the spread
6. Depth bar behind each row: running total against the deeper side

## Guidelines

- Sells above, buys below, best prices next to the spread; side is carried by position, the row's name and colour together.
- Sell prices are red and buy prices green, the way depth charts draw asks and bids.
- Bars show the running total against the deeper side, so walls stand out.
- Choosing a row puts its price in the order form; it never places an order.
- Rows keep their place as prices update and never flash; only the values change.
- Group sell prices up and buy prices down, so a group never shows a better price than its orders.

## Content

- Put the unit in each heading: Price (USDC), Amount (BTC).
- Say Spread, not a symbol, and give it in the price's unit.

## Accessibility

- 1.4.1 Use of Color: each row is named Sell or Buy with its amount, price and total, and the two sides are separate lists.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the book is one tab stop; arrow keys move between rows and Enter uses the price.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the book |
| ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next price |
| Page Up Page Down | Move five prices |
| Home End | Jump to the first or last price |
| Enter Space | Use the price in the order form |

## Examples

### live

```tsx
import { OrderBook, type OrderLevel, TextField } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useMemo, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Pick a price for the order form", description: "Sells above and buys below the spread, each row's bar showing the running total. Choose a row, by click or with the arrow keys and Enter, to put its price in the limit price field. The − and + buttons group prices.", order: 1 };

// Levels from a seeded random sequence, so the book looks real and stays the same on every load.
function levels(mid: number, dir: 1 | -1, seed: number): OrderLevel[] {
	const rand = () => ((seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647);
	return Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => ({ price: mid + dir * 0.4 * (i + 1) * (1 + rand()), amount: Number((rand() ** 3 * 0.9 + 0.0002).toFixed(5)) }));
}
const money = (n: number) => n.toLocaleString("en-GB", { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });
const coin = (n: number) => n.toLocaleString("en-GB", { minimumFractionDigits: 5, maximumFractionDigits: 5 });
const STEPS = [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10];

export default function Example() {
	const asks = useMemo(() => levels(70_237.17, 1, 11), []);
	const bids = useMemo(() => levels(70_237.17, -1, 29), []);
	const [step, setStep] = useState(0.01);
	const [limit, setLimit] = useState("");
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-3xl gap-6 sm:grid-cols-[18rem_1fr]">
			<OrderBook
				aria-label="BTC-USDC order book"
				asks={asks}
				bids={bids}
				rows={8}
				format={money}
				formatAmount={coin}
				priceLabel="Price (USDC)"
				amountLabel="Amount (BTC)"
				step={step}
				steps={STEPS}
				onStepChange={setStep}
				last={{ price: 70_237.17, direction: "up" }}
				onSelectPrice={(p) => setLimit(p.toFixed(2))}
			/>
			<div className="grid content-start">
				<TextField label="Limit price" suffix="USDC" inputMode="decimal" value={limit} onChange={(e) => setLimit(e.target.value)} hint="Choose a row in the order book to use its price." />
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Candlestick chart
- Change list
- Price chart

# Map chart

Regions shaded by a rate in five steps of one hue, or circles sized by an amount at places. For questions where location itself matters; missing regions are hatched and labelled No data.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When where something happens is the question: clusters, neighbours, regions with nothing, such as trial conversion by country.
- Placing amounts at locations, such as ARR by customer head office city, with circles sized by value.

## When not to use

- To compare amounts or rank countries. Use a Bar chart or a Ranked list: lengths are read more exactly than shades, and small countries don't disappear.
- For raw counts across regions of very different size or population, as shading. Normalise to a rate or per head, or use markers.
- For change over time. Use a Line chart card; a map shows one moment.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle
2. Regions from your TopoJSON, thin borders
3. Shading in five classed steps, or circles sized by value
4. Hatched fill for regions with no data
5. Legend: bin ranges and No data
6. Details: name, value, share of total, rank
7. Pinned details with a drill-down button
8. Note listing values with no shape on the map

## Guidelines

- Shade by a rate, a share or a per-head figure; put raw counts and amounts on markers, where circle area grows with value.
- One measure per map: values or markers, never both.
- Colour is five classed steps of one hue (q1 to q5), darkest for the highest in light, lightest in dark. The legend shows the range of each step.
- Regions with no value are hatched and labelled No data in the legend. Never draw them as zero or in the lowest step.
- Join values by feature id (ISO 3166-1 numeric in world-atlas), not by name; names differ between sources.
- Values with no shape on the map, such as Singapore at 1:110m, are listed under the map and stay in the table.
- Use Equal Earth for the world so areas are not inflated towards the poles; leave Antarctica out unless it matters.
- For drill-down, a pinned region offers one button that says where the filter lands (Filter page) and adds a pill to the filter bar.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states and the Table view (mapTable).

## Content

- Title names the measure and period: "Trial conversion by country", subtitle "Paid accounts per 100 trials, July to September".
- Legend ranges read "Under 5%", "5% to 10%", "20% and over". Missing regions read "No data".
- Turn off share of total for rates and averages; a share of a sum of rates means nothing.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the map's accessible name is a generated summary (label, number of regions, top three, how many have no data), and the Table view lists every value.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the map is one tab stop; arrow keys move between regions with data, highest value first, and show the same details as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: details sit beside the region, stay while the pointer is over the map and close with Esc.
- 1.4.1 Use of Color: values are in the details, legend ranges and table; No data has a pattern as well as a colour.
- Accessible description: "Map showing trial conversion by country, July to September."

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the map |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the next or previous region with data, highest value first, and show its details |
| Home End | Jump to the highest or lowest value |
| Enter | Pin the details; focus moves to the drill-down button when there is one |
| Esc | Close the details and return focus to the map |

## Examples

### arr-by-city

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, MapChart, mapTable } from "@twoux/ui";
import world from "world-atlas/countries-110m.json";

export const meta = { title: "ARR by customer location", description: "Raw amounts go on markers, never as shading: circle area grows with ARR, so London and New York stand out without painting all of the UK or the US.", order: 2 };

const gbp = (n: number) => `£${(n / 1_000_000).toFixed(1)}m`;
// Annual recurring revenue by the city of the customer's head office.
const ARR = [
	{ id: "lon", label: "London", lon: -0.13, lat: 51.51, value: 4_820_000 },
	{ id: "man", label: "Manchester", lon: -2.24, lat: 53.48, value: 910_000 },
	{ id: "dub", label: "Dublin", lon: -6.26, lat: 53.35, value: 1_340_000 },
	{ id: "ber", label: "Berlin", lon: 13.4, lat: 52.52, value: 2_150_000 },
	{ id: "ams", label: "Amsterdam", lon: 4.9, lat: 52.37, value: 1_620_000 },
	{ id: "par", label: "Paris", lon: 2.35, lat: 48.86, value: 1_280_000 },
	{ id: "sto", label: "Stockholm", lon: 18.07, lat: 59.33, value: 740_000 },
	{ id: "nyc", label: "New York", lon: -74.0, lat: 40.71, value: 3_960_000 },
	{ id: "sfo", label: "San Francisco", lon: -122.42, lat: 37.77, value: 2_480_000 },
	{ id: "tor", label: "Toronto", lon: -79.38, lat: 43.65, value: 860_000 },
	{ id: "syd", label: "Sydney", lon: 151.21, lat: -33.87, value: 1_050_000 },
	{ id: "sin", label: "Singapore", lon: 103.82, lat: 1.35, value: 690_000 },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="ARR by customer location" description="Head office city, as of 30 September" table={mapTable(ARR, { format: gbp, first: "City", valueLabel: "ARR" })} height={260}>
			<MapChart topology={world} object="countries" exclude={["010"]} markers={ARR} format={gbp} valueLabel="ARR" aria-label="Map showing ARR by customer head office city, as of 30 September" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

### trial-conversion

```tsx
import * as React from "react";
import { ChartFrame, FilterBar, FilterPill, MapChart, mapTable } from "@twoux/ui";
import world from "world-atlas/countries-110m.json";

export const meta = { title: "Trial conversion by country", description: "A rate, so countries of different size compare fairly. Arrow keys move from highest to lowest; Enter pins the details and offers Filter page.", order: 1 };

// Trials that became paid accounts, per 100 trials, last quarter. ISO 3166-1 numeric ids.
const RATES = [
	{ id: "826", label: "United Kingdom", value: 18.4 },
	{ id: "372", label: "Ireland", value: 21.2 },
	{ id: "276", label: "Germany", value: 14.9 },
	{ id: "250", label: "France", value: 11.3 },
	{ id: "528", label: "Netherlands", value: 19.7 },
	{ id: "752", label: "Sweden", value: 16.1 },
	{ id: "724", label: "Spain", value: 8.2 },
	{ id: "616", label: "Poland", value: 9.6 },
	{ id: "840", label: "United States", value: 15.8 },
	{ id: "124", label: "Canada", value: 13.4 },
	{ id: "484", label: "Mexico", value: 5.1 },
	{ id: "076", label: "Brazil", value: 6.7 },
	{ id: "356", label: "India", value: 4.3 },
	{ id: "392", label: "Japan", value: 7.9 },
	{ id: "036", label: "Australia", value: 17.2 },
	{ id: "710", label: "South Africa", value: 6.0 },
	{ id: "702", label: "Singapore", value: 22.5 },
];
const pctFmt = (n: number) => `${n.toFixed(1)}%`;

export default function Example() {
	const [country, setCountry] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
	const options = RATES.map((r) => ({ value: r.id, label: r.label }));
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full gap-3">
			<FilterBar>
				<FilterPill field="Country" options={options} selected={country} onChange={setCountry} />
			</FilterBar>
			<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Trial conversion by country" description="Paid accounts per 100 trials, July to September" table={mapTable(RATES, { format: pctFmt, share: false, first: "Country", valueLabel: "Conversion" })} height={260}>
				<MapChart
					topology={world}
					object="countries"
					exclude={["010"]}
					values={RATES}
					format={pctFmt}
					share={false}
					valueLabel="Conversion"
					filterField="Country"
					onSelect={(r) => setCountry([r.id])}
					aria-label="Map showing trial conversion by country, July to September"
				/>
			</ChartFrame>
		</div>
	);
}
```

# Timeline

Scheduled work across a few tracks on one time ruler, such as releases and maintenance per service or hiring campaigns per team. Spans and instants, a labelled Now line, four zoom levels; selecting an event opens it in the side panel.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Seeing what runs in parallel across services, teams or resources, such as release and maintenance windows, and where it overlaps.
- Planning or reviewing phases with a start and an end, such as hiring campaigns per team, with deadlines as instants.

## When not to use

- For what happened, one item after another, in one stream. Use the Agent activity log or a Grouped list.
- For amounts over time. Use the Line chart card or a Bar chart.
- For editing dates by dragging. The Timeline is read-only; change dates in the record's side panel.
- For more than about 12 tracks or when people compare exact dates. Use a List table with start and end columns.

## Structure

1. Toolbar: period, Go to now, zoom
2. Ruler with UK date ticks
3. Sticky track label column
4. Spans (start to end) and instants (diamond)
5. Lanes for overlapping events in a track
6. Now line labelled with the time
7. Tooltip: track, status word, start, end, length

## Guidelines

- Keep to about 12 tracks and one period people plan in, such as two weeks or a quarter.
- Give every event a status word with statusLabel (Done, At risk, Blocked); the tint repeats it, never replaces it.
- Selecting an event opens its record in the SidePanel; pass its id back as selectedId so the timeline marks it.
- Pass now for current and future periods; leave it out for past ones. Go to now appears only when Now is in the period.
- Offer the zoom levels that fit the period with zooms: hour and day for a week, week and month for a quarter.
- Wrap it in ChartFrame for the title, the Table view (timelineTable) and the loading, error and no match states.

## Content

- Dates are UK format, "Wed 11 Nov, 09:00"; the tooltip and table give the full date with zone, as Timestamp does.
- Name tracks with nouns (Payments API, Engineering) and events by what happens (Release 4.13, Database upgrade).

## Accessibility

- 2.1.1 Keyboard and the APG grid: one tab stop, arrow keys move between events, Enter or Space opens one.
- Each event is a gridcell named "Label, track, start to end, status"; each track is a row with a row header.
- 1.4.1 Use of Color: status is a word in the tooltip, accessible name and table view, not the tint alone.
- 1.4.10 Reflow: only the time area scrolls, inside its own box, with the track column sticky.
- 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts: + and − zoom only while the timeline has focus.
- 1.1.1 and complex images: a description gives tracks, events, period and current time, and the Table view lists every event.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip follows hover and focus and closes with Esc.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the timeline |
| ← → | Previous or next event in the track |
| ↑ ↓ | Nearest event in time on the track above or below |
| Home End | First or last event in the track (with Ctrl, overall) |
| Enter Space | Open the event in the side panel |
| + − | Zoom in or out (off when single-key shortcuts are turned off) |
| Esc | Clear the focused event and hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### hiring-campaigns

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, ChartStatus, Segment, SegmentedControl, Timeline, TimelineTrack, timelineTable } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Hiring campaign phases by team", description: "A quarter of hiring campaigns at month and week zoom, with closing dates as instants. The state control shows the frame's loading, empty and error states.", order: 2 };

const TRACKS: TimelineTrack[] = [
	{ id: "eng", label: "Engineering", events: [
		{ id: "c1", label: "Sourcing: backend", start: "2026-10-05", end: "2026-10-30", status: "ok", statusLabel: "Done" },
		{ id: "c2", label: "Interviews: backend", start: "2026-10-26", end: "2026-11-27", status: "warn", statusLabel: "Behind plan" },
		{ id: "c3", label: "Offers close", start: "2026-12-04", status: "neutral", statusLabel: "Planned" },
	] },
	{ id: "sales", label: "Sales", events: [
		{ id: "c4", label: "Account executives, London", start: "2026-10-12", end: "2026-12-11", status: "ok", statusLabel: "On track" },
		{ id: "c5", label: "SDR graduate intake", start: "2026-11-16", end: "2026-12-18", status: "neutral", statusLabel: "Planned" },
	] },
	{ id: "support", label: "Customer support", events: [
		{ id: "c6", label: "Weekend cover", start: "2026-10-19", end: "2026-11-13", status: "bad", statusLabel: "Paused" },
		{ id: "c7", label: "Listing closes", start: "2026-11-13", status: "bad", statusLabel: "Paused" },
	] },
	{ id: "finance", label: "Finance", events: [
		{ id: "c8", label: "Financial controller", start: "2026-11-02", end: "2026-12-23", status: "ok", statusLabel: "On track" },
	] },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [state, setState] = useState<ChartStatus>("ready");
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full gap-2">
			<SegmentedControl size="sm" value={state} onValueChange={(v) => setState(v as ChartStatus)} aria-label="Example state" className="justify-self-start">
				<Segment value="ready">Data</Segment><Segment value="loading">Loading</Segment><Segment value="error">Error</Segment>
			</SegmentedControl>
			<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Hiring campaigns" description="Q4 2026, all teams" status={state} onRetry={() => setState("ready")} table={timelineTable(TRACKS)} height={200}>
				<Timeline tracks={TRACKS} start="2026-10-01" end="2027-01-01" now="2026-11-11T09:00" defaultZoom="week" zooms={["week", "month"]} aria-label="Hiring campaigns" />
			</ChartFrame>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### release-schedule

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, ChartFrame, SidePanel, Timeline, TimelineEvent, TimelineTrack, timelineDate, timelineTable } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Releases and maintenance by service", description: "Two weeks of releases, maintenance windows and freezes across five services. Select an event, or press Enter on it, to open it in the side panel; + and − zoom.", order: 1 };

const TRACKS: TimelineTrack[] = [
	{ id: "payments", label: "Payments API", events: [
		{ id: "REL-412", label: "Release 4.12", start: "2026-11-10T09:00", end: "2026-11-10T11:00", status: "ok", statusLabel: "Done" },
		{ id: "MNT-88", label: "Database upgrade", start: "2026-11-12T22:00", end: "2026-11-13T02:00", status: "warn", statusLabel: "At risk" },
		{ id: "REL-413", label: "Release 4.13", start: "2026-11-17T09:00", end: "2026-11-17T10:30", status: "neutral" },
	] },
	{ id: "billing", label: "Billing", events: [
		{ id: "FRZ-11", label: "Month-end freeze", start: "2026-11-16T00:00", end: "2026-11-19T00:00", status: "neutral", statusLabel: "Scheduled" },
		{ id: "REL-207", label: "Invoice PDF fix", start: "2026-11-11T13:00", status: "ok", statusLabel: "Deployed" },
	] },
	{ id: "auth", label: "Identity", events: [
		{ id: "MNT-91", label: "Certificate rotation", start: "2026-11-11T06:00", end: "2026-11-11T08:00", status: "ok", statusLabel: "Done" },
		{ id: "REL-330", label: "SSO for Okta", start: "2026-11-11T12:00", end: "2026-11-12T18:00", status: "bad", statusLabel: "Blocked" },
	] },
	{ id: "search", label: "Search", events: [
		{ id: "MNT-93", label: "Index rebuild", start: "2026-11-14T01:00", end: "2026-11-14T07:00", status: "neutral" },
		{ id: "REL-119", label: "Ranking change", start: "2026-11-18T10:00", status: "warn", statusLabel: "Needs review" },
	] },
	{ id: "web", label: "Web app", events: [
		{ id: "REL-905", label: "Weekly release", start: "2026-11-12T10:00", end: "2026-11-12T12:00", status: "ok", statusLabel: "On track" },
		{ id: "REL-906", label: "Weekly release", start: "2026-11-19T10:00", end: "2026-11-19T12:00", status: "neutral" },
	] },
];
const VARIANT = { ok: "success", warn: "warning", bad: "destructive", neutral: "secondary" } as const;

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState<{ e: TimelineEvent; track: string } | null>(null);
	return (
		<div className="flex w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<div className="min-w-0 flex-1 p-3">
				<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Releases and maintenance" description="All services, 9 to 22 November" table={timelineTable(TRACKS)} height={260}>
					<Timeline
						tracks={TRACKS}
						start="2026-11-09T00:00"
						end="2026-11-23T00:00"
						now="2026-11-11T14:30"
						defaultZoom="day"
						zooms={["hour", "day", "week"]}
						selectedId={open?.e.id ?? null}
						onSelect={(e, t) => setOpen({ e, track: t.label })}
						aria-label="Releases and maintenance"
					/>
				</ChartFrame>
			</div>
			{open && (
				<SidePanel
					open
					onOpenChange={(o) => !o && setOpen(null)}
					label="Change details"
					title={open.e.label}
					meta={<span className="flex items-center gap-2"><span className="font-mono">{open.e.id}</span><Badge variant={VARIANT[open.e.status ?? "neutral"]}>{open.e.statusLabel ?? "Planned"}</Badge></span>}
					footer={<Button size="sm">Edit change</Button>}
				>
					<dl className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-3 gap-y-2 text-base">
						<dt className="text-ink-2">Service</dt><dd className="text-ink">{open.track}</dd>
						<dt className="text-ink-2">Starts</dt><dd className="text-ink">{timelineDate(new Date(open.e.start))}</dd>
						<dt className="text-ink-2">Ends</dt><dd className="text-ink">{open.e.end ? timelineDate(new Date(open.e.end)) : "Same time"}</dd>
					</dl>
				</SidePanel>
			)}
		</div>
	);
}
```
