# Radial bars

One to four small concentric rings, each the share of a fixed limit such as seats, credits or storage, with used of limit always written beside them. Never actual against target: that stays the bullet chart.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing two to four limits of a plan together in the space of a stat card, such as seats, assistant credits and storage this month.
- One budget that resets, such as an SLA error budget, where a ring with the share in the centre fits a small tile.

## When not to use

- For actual against a target, such as bookings against plan. Use the TwoUX Bullet chart: angles are read less exactly than lengths.
- For a single limit with a reset date and what stops at the limit. Use the TwoUX Usage meter.
- To compare amounts across categories around a circle. Use a Bar chart: outer rings look longer than inner ones for the same value.
- For parts of one total. Use a Donut chart or Share bar.
- For a value with no fixed maximum, or for the progress of a task. A ring needs a real limit.

## Structure

1. Rings, outermost first: grey track and an arc from 12 o'clock clockwise
2. Zero tick at 12 o'clock
3. Share in the centre when there is one ring
4. List: colour key, measure name, used of limit and share
5. Status badge when a ring is at or over its limit
6. Tooltip under the rings on hover or focus

## Guidelines

- Use radial bars only for share of a fixed limit, 0 to 100% of capacity, quota or budget.
- Show at most four rings, at 96 to 160px. Extra items are not drawn.
- Write used of limit and the share as text beside the rings; the ring only repeats it.
- Start every ring at 12 o'clock and run clockwise from zero. A value over the limit fills the ring; it never wraps round twice.
- Colour rings in series order. A ring at or over its limit adds At limit or Over limit as a badge; never recolour a ring as the only cue.
- No needle, no half-circle dial and no thresholds on the ring.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Name each ring by what it measures, as a noun: Seats, Assistant credits, Storage.
- Write used of limit with the unit, then the share: 38 of 50 seats · 76%.
- Put the plan and reset date in the chart description: Growth plan · resets 1 Dec.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the chart's accessible name lists each measure as used of limit, share and status.
- 1.4.1 Use of Color: every value and status is printed in the list; colour only links a ring to its row.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: arcs meet 3:1 against the grey track.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: one tab stop, arrow keys move between rings and show the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.10 Reflow: the list moves under the rings on narrow screens.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move to the previous or next ring |
| Home End | Go to the outer or inner ring |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### error-budget

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, RadialBars, radialBarsTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "One ring: SLA error budget", description: "A single ring shows its share in the centre. The budget is a fixed limit for the month, so the ring fits; progress against a target would be a bullet chart.", order: 2 };

const ITEMS = [{ id: "budget", label: "Error budget used", value: 26, limit: 43, unit: "min" }];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full max-w-sm" title="Checkout API error budget" description="99.9% availability · November" table={radialBarsTable(ITEMS)} height={120}>
			<RadialBars items={ITEMS} size={104} aria-label="Checkout API error budget used in November" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

### workspace-usage

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, RadialBars, radialBarsTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Workspace usage this month", description: "Seats, assistant credits and storage, each as a share of the plan's limit. The list says every value in words; the rings only repeat it. Seats at the limit add a status badge.", order: 1 };

const ITEMS = [
	{ id: "seats", label: "Seats", value: 50, limit: 50, unit: "seats" },
	{ id: "credits", label: "Assistant credits", value: 13_200, limit: 20_000, unit: "credits" },
	{ id: "storage", label: "Storage", value: 38, limit: 100, unit: "GB" },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full max-w-md" title="Plan usage" description="Growth plan · resets 1 Dec" table={radialBarsTable(ITEMS)} height={140}>
			<RadialBars items={ITEMS} aria-label="Plan usage this month" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

# Radial lines

A line chart wrapped round a circle for cyclical periods (hour of day, day of week, month), so the last period runs into the first. One to three series, values from zero, gaps for missing data.

Kind: component · Group: Data visualisation · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Showing how a measure rises and falls through a repeating cycle where the wrap-around matters, such as support tickets by hour of day across two queues.
- Daily or weekly rhythms, such as sign-ins by day of week, where Sunday into Monday should read as one stretch.

## When not to use

- For time that does not repeat, such as revenue by month over two years. Use the TwoUX Line chart card.
- For exact comparisons between periods. Use a Bar chart: values near the centre are hard to compare.
- For a cycle against a second dimension, such as hour by weekday. Use the TwoUX Heatmap.
- For more than three series. Split them into small charts side by side.

## Structure

1. Title and subtitle with the period averaged and time zone
2. Value rings from zero, three or four, labelled along the top spoke
3. One spoke per period, labels round the outside
4. Lines in series colours, joined from the last period to the first
5. Gaps for missing data
6. Legend for two or more series
7. Tooltip for the nearest period on hover or focus

## Guidelines

- Use radial lines only for cyclical periods: hour of day, day of week, month of year.
- Start the first period at 12 o'clock and run clockwise.
- Start the value axis at zero with three or four labelled rings; never crop the centre.
- Draw missing data as a gap, never as zero. Join the last period to the first only when both have values.
- Show one to three series as lines; no area fill.
- Show a legend only for two or more series; legend keys hide series without changing colours.
- Use ChartFrame for the four states: loading keeps the frame, an error says what failed with Try again, an empty period says so, and no match offers Clear filters.

## Content

- Name the measure and the cycle in the title: Tickets opened by hour.
- Say what was averaged and the time zone in the description: Average per day, last 30 days, UK time.
- Write periods as people read them: 00:00 to 23:00, Mon to Sun, Jan to Dec.

## Accessibility

- 1.1.1 and WAI complex images: the accessible name gives the cycle, where it starts, and each series' highest and lowest period and gaps.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: one tab stop; arrow keys move round the cycle and wrap, showing the same tooltip as hover.
- 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: the tooltip stays while the period is active and Esc hides it.
- 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: lines meet 3:1 against the surface.
- 1.4.10 Reflow: the chart shrinks to its container and the table view lists every value.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus the chart |
| → ↓ | Next period, clockwise; wraps from the last to the first |
| ← ↑ | Previous period, anticlockwise |
| Home End | Go to the first or last period |
| Esc | Hide the tooltip |

## Examples

### logins-by-weekday

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, RadialLines, radialLinesTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "One series: sign-ins by day of week", description: "One series needs no legend. Sunday meets Monday, so the weekend dip reads as one shape.", order: 2 };

const DAYS = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"];
const SERIES = [{ id: "signins", label: "Sign-ins", data: [4_820, 5_130, 5_060, 4_910, 3_980, 820, 640] }];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full max-w-md" title="Sign-ins by day of week" description="Average per day, last 12 weeks" table={radialLinesTable(DAYS, SERIES, undefined, "Day")} height={260}>
			<RadialLines periods={DAYS} series={SERIES} periodLabel="Day" maxSize={260} aria-label="Sign-ins by day of week, last 12 weeks" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

### tickets-by-hour

```tsx
import { ChartFrame, RadialLines, radialLinesTable } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Support tickets by hour of day", description: "Two queues over 24 hours. Midnight sits at the top, so the overnight hours read as one stretch. 04:00 has no data after a logging outage and shows as a gap.", order: 1 };

const HOURS = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => `${String(h).padStart(2, "0")}:00`);
const SERIES = [
	{ id: "billing", label: "Billing", data: [6, 4, 3, 2, null, 3, 8, 18, 34, 52, 61, 58, 49, 55, 60, 54, 44, 31, 22, 17, 14, 12, 10, 8] },
	{ id: "technical", label: "Technical", data: [14, 12, 10, 9, null, 11, 16, 24, 31, 38, 42, 40, 36, 39, 43, 41, 37, 33, 29, 27, 24, 21, 18, 16] },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<ChartFrame className="w-full" title="Tickets opened by hour" description="Average per day, last 30 days, UK time" table={radialLinesTable(HOURS, SERIES, undefined, "Hour")} height={320}>
			<RadialLines periods={HOURS} series={SERIES} periodLabel="Hour" aria-label="Support tickets opened by hour of day, last 30 days" />
		</ChartFrame>
	);
}
```

- Line chart card
- Heatmap
- Bar chart
- Data visualisation

# Scheduler

Interviews, shifts or bookings on a day, week or month grid, with people or rooms as resources. Click a free time to add, click an event to open it, and drag, use the keyboard or the event menu to move it. Below 768px it becomes an agenda list.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Booking and arranging time-bound records where free time matters, such as interviews across several interviewers, shifts or room bookings.
- Seeing who is busy when, side by side, before choosing a time.

## When not to use

- For a list of upcoming items with no need to see free time; use a Grouped list or List table with Timestamps.
- For a record's history of changes; use Timeline.
- For picking one date in a form; use a date field.
- For editing recurring series; the Scheduler shows events the app has already expanded and has no recurrence editor.

## Structure

1. Toolbar: Today, Previous, Next, period heading, time zone, Day / Week / Month
2. Resource legend: stripe and name
3. Time gutter, 24-hour, with a labelled now line
4. Column headers: days, or resources in day view
5. All-day row
6. 30-minute slots
7. Event: resource stripe, title, detail, time, resource, status badge, ⋮ menu
8. Month cells with up to three events and +N more
9. Agenda list grouped by day, below 768px

## Guidelines

- Switch Day, Week and Month with the segmented control; they are views of the same data.
- Open an event in the side panel with onSelectEvent, so people keep their place in the schedule.
- Create from a free time with onCreate and a dialog of up to three fields; the time comes from the slot.
- Apply every move at once with a toast offering Undo. Confirm first only if the move contacts someone outside the workspace, such as re-sending a candidate invite.
- Every drag has a keyboard path (Space, arrows, Enter, Esc) and a menu path (the event's ⋮: earlier, later, other day, longer, shorter, another resource).
- Resource colour is a left stripe from the series colours; text stays ink and the resource is always named.
- Keep day and week views to working hours (dayStart, dayEnd) and use workWeek when weekends are never booked.
- Below 768px the grid becomes an agenda grouped by day, so the schedule reflows to 320px without sideways scrolling.
- Loading shows skeleton rows inside the frame; an error says what failed with Try again; an empty period says so and stays clickable.

## Content

- Times are 24-hour with an en dash: 09:30–10:15. Weeks start on Monday. Day headings read Thursday 12 November.
- Write the time zone once in the toolbar: Times in GMT. Details in the side panel use Timestamp in absolute format.
- Name the noun in the empty message: No interviews this week. Choose a free time to add one.
- Status is a word in a Badge (Confirmed, Tentative), never a colour alone.

## Accessibility

- 2.1.1 Keyboard: the grid is one tab stop with roving focus; arrows walk free times and events in time order, and Enter opens or adds.
- 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: moving and resizing also work with Space and arrows, and from the event menu with single clicks.
- 4.1.3 Status Messages: pick-up, each step, drop and cancel are announced in a polite live region.
- Month view follows the APG calendar grid: arrows by day and week, Enter lists the day's events.
- 1.4.1 Use of Color: resources and status are written in words; colour repeats them.
- 1.4.10 Reflow: the agenda replaces the grid below 768px.
- 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts: T, J, K, D, W and M stop when single-key shortcuts are turned off; keys inside the focused grid are not affected.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| T | Go to today |
| J K | Next or previous day, week or month |
| D W M | Day, week or month view |
| ↑ ↓ | Previous or next free time or event in the column |
| ← → | Same time in the previous or next column |
| Home End | First or last time in the column |
| Page up Page down | Previous or next period |
| Enter | Open the event, or add one at the free time |
| Space | Pick up the event to move it |
| ↑ ↓ ← → (moving) | Move by one slot, or to the next day or interviewer |
| ⇧↑ ⇧↓ (moving) | Make it shorter or longer |
| Enter Space (moving) | Drop it here |
| Esc | Cancel the move and put it back |
| ⇧F10 | Open the event menu |

## Examples

### interviews

```tsx
import {
	Badge, Button, Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, RadioField, RadioGroup,
	Scheduler, SidePanel, TextField, Timestamp, formatTimeRange, toast, type SchedulerEvent, type SchedulerSlot, type SchedulerView,
} from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
import { INTERVIEWERS, INTERVIEWS, NOW, STATUS_VARIANT } from "./data";

export const meta = {
	title: "Interview week",
	description: "Three interviewers, one week. Click an interview to open it beside the schedule; click a free time to add one. Drag to move or the bottom edge to change the length; Space, arrows and Enter do the same from the keyboard, and the ⋮ menu offers the same moves. Every move has Undo.",
	order: 1,
};

const TYPES = ["Phone screen", "Technical interview", "Final interview"];
const name = (id?: string) => INTERVIEWERS.find((r) => r.id === id)?.label;

export default function Example() {
	const [events, setEvents] = useState(INTERVIEWS);
	const [view, setView] = useState<SchedulerView>("week");
	const [date, setDate] = useState(NOW);
	const [openId, setOpenId] = useState<string | null>(null);
	const [draft, setDraft] = useState<SchedulerSlot | null>(null);
	const [candidate, setCandidate] = useState("");
	const [type, setType] = useState(TYPES[0]);
	const [interviewer, setInterviewer] = useState("tom");
	const [error, setError] = useState<string | undefined>();
	const open = events.find((e) => e.id === openId) ?? null;

	const move = (ev: SchedulerEvent, to: SchedulerSlot) => {
		const before = events;
		setEvents((list) => list.map((e) => (e.id === ev.id ? { ...e, start: to.start.toISOString(), end: to.end.toISOString(), resourceId: to.resourceId } : e)));
		toast.success(`${ev.title} moved to ${to.start.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { weekday: "long" })} ${formatTimeRange(to.start, to.end)}`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setEvents(before) } });
	};
	const startCreate = (slot: SchedulerSlot) => {
		setDraft(slot); setCandidate(""); setType(TYPES[0]); setInterviewer(slot.resourceId ?? "tom"); setError(undefined);
	};
	const create = (e: React.FormEvent) => {
		e.preventDefault();
		if (!draft) return;
		if (!candidate.trim()) { setError("Enter the candidate's name."); return; }
		const id = `INT-${300 + events.length}`;
		setEvents((list) => [...list, { id, title: type, detail: candidate.trim(), start: draft.start.toISOString(), end: draft.end.toISOString(), resourceId: interviewer, status: "Tentative" }]);
		setDraft(null);
		toast.success(`${type} added for ${candidate.trim()}`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setEvents((list) => list.filter((x) => x.id !== id)) } });
	};

	return (
		<div className="flex w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm">
			<div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
				<Scheduler
					aria-label="Interviews"
					noun="interviews"
					resourceTitle="Interviewer"
					events={events}
					resources={INTERVIEWERS}
					view={view}
					onViewChange={setView}
					date={date}
					onDateChange={setDate}
					now={NOW}
					workWeek
					height={460}
					selectedId={openId ?? undefined}
					statusVariant={STATUS_VARIANT}
					onSelectEvent={(e) => setOpenId(e.id)}
					onCreate={startCreate}
					onMove={move}
				/>
			</div>
			{open && (
				<SidePanel
					open
					onOpenChange={(o) => !o && setOpenId(null)}
					mode="overlay"
					label="Interview details"
					title={open.detail ? `${open.title}, ${open.detail}` : open.title}
					meta={<span className="flex items-center gap-2"><span className="font-mono">{open.id}</span>{open.status && <Badge variant={STATUS_VARIANT(open.status)}>{open.status}</Badge>}</span>}
					footer={<Button size="sm" variant="outline">Edit interview</Button>}
				>
					<dl className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-3 gap-y-2 text-base">
						<dt className="text-ink-2">Starts</dt><dd><Timestamp value={open.start} format="absolute" /></dd>
						<dt className="text-ink-2">Ends</dt><dd><Timestamp value={open.end} format="absolute" /></dd>
						<dt className="text-ink-2">Interviewer</dt><dd className="text-ink">{name(open.resourceId) ?? "Not assigned"}</dd>
						<dt className="text-ink-2">Role</dt><dd className="text-ink">Senior Backend Engineer</dd>
					</dl>
				</SidePanel>
			)}
			<Dialog open={!!draft} onOpenChange={(o) => !o && setDraft(null)}>
				<DialogContent>
					<form onSubmit={create} className="grid gap-4" noValidate>
						<DialogHeader>
							<DialogTitle>Add interview</DialogTitle>
							<DialogDescription>{draft && <Timestamp value={draft.start} format="absolute" />}{draft && `, until ${formatTimeRange(draft.start, draft.end).split("–")[1]}`}</DialogDescription>
						</DialogHeader>
						<TextField label="Candidate" required value={candidate} onChange={(e) => { setCandidate(e.target.value); setError(undefined); }} error={error} autoFocus />
						<fieldset className="grid gap-2">
							<legend className="mb-2 text-base font-medium text-ink">Interview type</legend>
							<RadioGroup value={type} onValueChange={setType}>
								{TYPES.map((t) => <RadioField key={t} id={`type-${t}`} value={t} label={t} />)}
							</RadioGroup>
						</fieldset>
						<fieldset className="grid gap-2">
							<legend className="mb-2 text-base font-medium text-ink">Interviewer</legend>
							<RadioGroup value={interviewer} onValueChange={setInterviewer}>
								{INTERVIEWERS.map((r) => <RadioField key={r.id} id={`who-${r.id}`} value={r.id} label={r.label} />)}
							</RadioGroup>
						</fieldset>
						<DialogFooter>
							<Button type="button" variant="outline" onClick={() => setDraft(null)}>Cancel</Button>
							<Button type="submit">Add interview</Button>
						</DialogFooter>
					</form>
				</DialogContent>
			</Dialog>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### states

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl, Segment, Scheduler, type SchedulerView } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
import { INTERVIEWERS, INTERVIEWS, NOW, STATUS_VARIANT } from "./data";

export const meta = {
	title: "Agenda, loading, empty and error",
	description: "Below 768px the grid becomes this agenda, grouped by day, so the schedule reflows to 320px; it is also the list view for screen reader users who prefer one. Loading keeps the frame with skeleton rows, an error says what failed with Try again, and an empty week says so.",
	order: 2,
};

type Demo = "agenda" | "loading" | "error" | "empty";

export default function Example() {
	const [demo, setDemo] = useState<Demo>("agenda");
	const [view, setView] = useState<SchedulerView>("week");
	const [date, setDate] = useState(NOW);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-3">
			<SegmentedControl value={demo} onValueChange={(v) => setDemo(v as Demo)} size="sm" aria-label="State" className="justify-self-start">
				<Segment value="agenda">Agenda</Segment><Segment value="loading">Loading</Segment><Segment value="error">Error</Segment><Segment value="empty">Empty</Segment>
			</SegmentedControl>
			<Scheduler
				aria-label="Interviews"
				noun="interviews"
				resourceTitle="Interviewer"
				events={demo === "empty" ? [] : INTERVIEWS}
				resources={INTERVIEWERS}
				view={view}
				onViewChange={setView}
				date={date}
				onDateChange={setDate}
				now={NOW}
				workWeek
				layout="agenda"
				status={demo === "loading" ? "loading" : demo === "error" ? "error" : "ready"}
				onRetry={() => setDemo("agenda")}
				statusVariant={STATUS_VARIANT}
				onSelectEvent={() => {}}
				onMove={() => {}}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Side panel (drawer)
- Segmented control
- Grouped list
- List table
- Dropdown menu
- Confirmation dialog

# Sheet grid

A spreadsheet of records with typed columns, a menu per column, row numbers and a status row for computed columns, and Excel and Google Sheets keys: select ranges, copy and paste to and from either, fill, clear and undo. size="dense" gives 28px rows for spreadsheet-like data.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- People build a table of records and add columns that are typed, calculated or filled in per row, such as a work email looked up for every person.
- The table is wider than the screen and people compare values across columns, so the name column must stay in view.
- People work as they would in Excel or Google Sheets: they paste blocks of values in, fill down, copy ranges out and undo mistakes.
- Spreadsheet-like data, such as inventories, ledgers and imports, where people need many rows in view: use size="dense".

## When not to use

- For scanning and triage of records. Use the List table; a static table is simpler to read.
- For editing a few columns of known data without computed columns. Use the Data grid.
- For deep edits of one record. Use the side panel.

## Structure

1. Header row: type icon (or the service's logo), column name, sort arrow, menu
2. Filter row (optional): a search field under each header
3. Status row for computed columns: Up to date, 62%, 3 errors
4. Pinned row numbers (with checkbox and ⋮ row menu when set) and frozen first columns
5. Group rows (optional): label, count and each total column's sum, collapsible
6. Cells: values, Tag for select, Switch with its word, n/a, or Waiting, Writing, Looking up, Failed with the reason, Not found; the selected range in indigo
7. Totals row (optional), then Add row, Add 10 rows, the status line and the sum and count of the selection

## Guidelines

- Every column shows its type in the header: an icon for text, number, date and select, the formula mark, the AI origin mark, or the logo of the service an enrichment uses.
- The grid has one tab stop. Arrow keys move between cells; Up from the first row reaches the column headers, where Enter opens the column menu.
- The column menu holds rename, change type, sort, filter, wrap text, pin or unpin, column width, hide, insert left or right and delete. Delete happens at once with Undo.
- Columns resize from the header: drag its right edge (60 to 640px) or double-click the edge to fit the widest value. From the keyboard, ⌥⇧ with an arrow on a header, or Column width in the column menu (Wider, Narrower, Fit to content).
- Pin any column from its menu to keep it in view when scrolling sideways; pinned columns move to the left edge and show a pin in the header. Pinned columns never take more than 60% of the grid's width.
- You always see where you are and which record changes: the row being edited is tinted (--color-active-row), and its row number and column header turn primary, as in Google Sheets. The active cell has a 2px primary outline on the surface. Under the pointer, the row takes --color-hover and the cell --color-selected. A select's list opens below the cell, never over it.
- Select columns read as selectors: the value with a chevron, shown on row hover and focus. A second click on the active cell, a click on the chevron, Enter or any letter opens the list. Don't show select values as badges in an editable grid; badges read as status, not as something to change.
- The row header is one compact slot: the row number, replaced by a checkbox on hover, on focus and while any row is checked, then the ⋮ menu, shown on hover. On touch screens both stay visible.
- Computed columns show their progress in the status row and their state in each cell, in words. A run never overwrites a typed value.
- Pressing Enter on a failed cell runs it again; the status line states the cost first.
- Keys follow Excel and Google Sheets: Shift with an arrow extends the selection, ⌘ or Ctrl with an arrow jumps to the edge of the data, ⌘C and ⌘V copy and paste, ⌘D and ⌘R fill, ⌘Z undoes. Ctrl replaces ⌘ on Windows and Linux.
- Copy puts tab-separated values on the clipboard, so a range pastes straight into Excel or Google Sheets, and numbers stay numbers.
- Paste reads tab-separated values from Excel or Sheets into the range starting at the active cell, and checks each value against its column's type. Cells that don't fit keep their value, are outlined in red with the reason, and the status line says how many were left and why. Nothing is dropped without saying so.
- Paste, fill, clear and edits can all be undone (⌘Z) and redone (⌘⇧Z or Ctrl+Y), and each one is announced: “Pasted 12 cells”, “Undid paste of 12 cells”.
- Use size="dense" (28px rows) for spreadsheet-like data. It is a variant for that data, never a row height setting; offer Wrap text per column for long values.
- Tab moves out of the grid unless a cell is being edited, where it saves and moves right, so the grid stays one tab stop.
- With onOpenRow, the name cell shows Open on hover and focus and the row menu has Open too; ⇧F10 opens the row menu from the keyboard.
- Pair the grid with a ShortcutSheet group from sheetGridShortcuts(), which writes ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere, and list the same groups on the page with ShortcutList, so the keys are visible without pressing ? or ⌘/.
- Add row and Add 10 rows put the new rows at the bottom, scroll there and make the first new cell active, so people can type straight away.

## Content

- Keep the three empty-looking states apart: a dash when there is nothing, Not found when the service looked and found nothing, and Failed with the reason.
- Status row words: Up to date, 62%, 3 errors, Out of date. Never a bare spinner.
- Right-align numbers; show dates as 14 Mar 2026.
- Status line messages say what happened and to how many cells: Copied 6 cells, Pasted 12 cells. 2 cells left as they were, Filled down 4 cells, Cleared 3 cells.
- Rejection reasons say what to enter: “Enter a number, such as 1200.”, “Choose one of Lead, Qualified, Proposal.”

## Accessibility

- APG grid pattern: role grid, roving focus on cells, aria-sort on the sorted header, row numbers as row headers.
- 2.1.1 Keyboard: every column action is in a menu reached from the header by keyboard.
- 1.4.1 Use of colour: failed cells carry an icon and the reason, not only red.
- 4.1.3 Status messages: saves, clears and retries are announced from the status line.
- 2.4.11 Focus not obscured: cells scroll clear of the sticky header and frozen columns.
- APG grid: aria-multiselectable on the grid and aria-selected on cells in the range; selections are announced as “6 cells selected: Job title to Seniority, rows 1 to 3.”
- 4.1.3 Status messages: copy, paste, fill, clear, undo and redo are announced from the status line, including the reason any cell was rejected.
- 3.3.1 Error identification: a rejected paste cell has aria-invalid, a red dashed outline and its reason in text, not colour alone.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ← → ↑ ↓ | Move one cell; up from row 1 to the filter row and the headers |
| ⌘ / Ctrl + arrow | Jump to the edge of the data in that direction |
| Home / End | First or last cell in the row |
| ⌘ Home / ⌘ End (Ctrl on Windows) | First or last cell in the sheet |
| Page Up / Page Down | Move 10 rows |
| ⇧ + arrow, ⇧ Home / End | Extend the selection |
| ⌘ ⇧ + arrow | Extend the selection to the edge of the data |
| ⇧ click, click and drag | Select a range with the mouse |
| ⌘ A | Select all cells |
| Ctrl Space | Select the column |
| ⇧ Space | Select or deselect the rows of the selected cells (with row selection) |
| ⌘ C | Copy the range as tab-separated values, for here, Excel or Google Sheets |
| ⌘ X | Copy the range and clear it |
| ⌘ V | Paste from here, Excel or Google Sheets into the range from the active cell; each value is checked |
| Delete / Backspace | Clear the editable cells in the range |
| ⌘ D | Fill down: the top row of the range into the rows below (one row: from the row above) |
| ⌘ R | Fill right: the left column of the range into the columns to its right |
| ⌘ Z | Undo the last edit, paste, clear or fill |
| ⌘ ⇧ Z / Ctrl Y | Redo |
| Enter / F2 | Edit; on a header, open the column menu; on a failed cell, run it again; on a group row, collapse or expand |
| Any character | Start editing and replace the value; on a select cell, open the list |
| Space (yes or no cell) | Turn it on or off |
| Enter (editing) | Save and move down |
| ⇧ Enter (editing) | Save and move up |
| Tab (editing) | Save and move right |
| ⇧ Tab (editing) | Save and move left |
| ⌘ Enter (editing) | Save the value into every selected cell |
| Esc (editing) | Cancel the edit |
| Esc | Clear the selection back to the active cell |
| ⇧ F10 / Menu key, right click | Open the row's actions |
| Alt ↓ | Open the column menu from a header |
| ⌥ ⇧ ← / → (Alt Shift on Windows) | On a header: make the column narrower or wider by 16px |
| ⌘ ; (Ctrl ; on Windows) | Put today's date in a date cell |
| ⌘ / (Ctrl / on Windows), ? | Show every shortcut |
| Tab | Leave the grid (one tab stop) |

## Examples

### dense

```tsx
import { Button, type SheetCellChange, SheetGrid, type SheetRow, ShortcutSheet, sheetGridShortcuts } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Keyboard } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";
import { PROSPECT_COLUMNS, prospectRows } from "../dense-table/prospects-data";

export const meta = {
	title: "Dense, with spreadsheet keys",
	description: "The TwoUX prospects table at size=\"dense\" for 28px rows. Shift+arrows or drag to select, ⌘C to copy as tab-separated values, ⌘V to paste from here, Excel or Google Sheets (each value is checked against its column), ⌘D and ⌘R to fill, Delete to clear, ⌘Z to undo. Press ? for every key.",
	order: 2,
};

export default function Example() {
	const [columns, setColumns] = useState(PROSPECT_COLUMNS);
	const [single, setSingle] = useState(true);
	const [rows, setRows] = useState<SheetRow[]>(() => prospectRows(30));
	const onCellsChange = (changes: SheetCellChange[]) =>
		setRows((rs) => rs.map((r) => {
			const mine = changes.filter((c) => c.rowId === r.id);
			return mine.length ? { ...r, values: { ...r.values, ...Object.fromEntries(mine.map((c) => [c.columnId, c.value])) } } : r;
		}));
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full gap-2">
			<div className="flex items-center gap-2">
				<span className="text-sm text-ink-2">TwoUX prospects · {rows.length} people</span>
				<span className="flex-1" />
				<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "?" }))}><Keyboard />Keys (?)</Button>
			</div>
			<SheetGrid
				size="dense"
				aria-label="TwoUX prospects"
				className="h-96 w-full"
				columns={columns}
				onColumnsChange={setColumns}
				rows={rows}
				onCellChange={(id, col, v) => setRows((rs) => rs.map((r) => (r.id === id ? { ...r, values: { ...r.values, [col]: v } } : r)))}
				onCellsChange={onCellsChange}
				onAddRows={(n) => setRows((rs) => [...rs, ...Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({ id: `new-${rs.length + i}`, values: { subscribed: false } }))])}
			/>
			<ShortcutSheet singleKeys={single} onSingleKeysChange={setSingle} groups={sheetGridShortcuts()} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

### prospects

```tsx
import { SheetGrid, type SheetColumn, type SheetRow, type SheetSort } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Prospects with computed columns", description: "Focus a cell and use the arrow keys. Enter edits, Esc cancels, Tab saves and moves on. Press Up from the first row to reach the headers, then Enter for the column menu. Enter on a failed cell runs it again.", order: 1 };

const COLUMNS: SheetColumn[] = [
	{ id: "name", label: "Name", type: "text", width: 160, pinned: true, locked: true },
	{ id: "title", label: "Job title", type: "text", width: 200 },
	{ id: "seniority", label: "Seniority", type: "select", width: 120, options: ["Mid", "Senior", "Director", "VP"] },
	{ id: "size", label: "Company size", type: "number", width: 130 },
	{ id: "summary", label: "Summarise role", type: "ai", width: 260, costPerRow: 1, status: { done: 3, total: 5, running: true } },
	{ id: "email", label: "Work email", type: "enrichment", provider: "hubspot", width: 230, costPerRow: 0.5, status: { done: 5, total: 5, errors: 1 } },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [columns, setColumns] = useState(COLUMNS);
	const [sort, setSort] = useState<SheetSort>(null);
	const [rows, setRows] = useState<SheetRow[]>([
		{ id: "1", values: { name: "Ana Silva", title: "Head of Revenue Operations", seniority: "Senior", size: 240 }, computed: { summary: { state: "done", value: "Leads a function; shortlists tools." }, email: { state: "done", value: "ana.silva@harbourvale.co.uk" } } },
		{ id: "2", values: { name: "Ben Hughes", title: "Chief Operating Officer", seniority: "VP", size: 160 }, computed: { summary: { state: "done", value: "Runs the business; owns the budget." }, email: { state: "not-found" } } },
		{ id: "3", values: { name: "Chloe Patel", title: "", seniority: "Mid", size: 410 }, computed: { summary: { state: "failed", reason: "Job title is empty." }, email: { state: "done", value: "chloe.patel@mosaiclending.co.uk" } } },
		{ id: "4", values: { name: "Daniel Murray", title: "IT Director", seniority: "Director", size: 1200 }, computed: { summary: { state: "writing" }, email: { state: "failed", reason: "No company domain." } } },
		{ id: "5", values: { name: "Ella Brennan", title: "Operations Manager", seniority: "Mid", size: 130 }, computed: { summary: { state: "queued" }, email: { state: "done", value: "ella.brennan@orrin.dev" } } },
	]);
	return (
		<SheetGrid
			aria-label="Prospects"
			className="h-96 w-full"
			columns={columns}
			onColumnsChange={setColumns}
			rows={rows}
			onCellChange={(id, col, v) => setRows((rs) => rs.map((r) => (r.id === id ? { ...r, values: { ...r.values, [col]: v } } : r)))}
			sort={sort}
			onSortChange={setSort}
			onRetryCell={(id, col) => setRows((rs) => rs.map((r) => (r.id === id ? { ...r, computed: { ...r.computed, [col]: { state: "queued" } } } : r)))}
			onAddRows={(n) => setRows((rs) => [...rs, ...Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({ id: `n${rs.length + i}`, values: {} }))])}
		/>
	);
}
```

# Columns menu

A menu that shows, hides and reorders the columns of a sheet or list table, with search, Show all and Hide all, type icons and eye toggles, plus wrapping and rows per page on list tables. Changes apply at once.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- On a sheet or list table where people change which columns they see while they work and expect the change at once.
- A table has more columns than most people need at once; let each person show, hide and reorder them.
- People choose page size or line wrapping for their own work on a list table.

## When not to use

- To change what a column holds. Use the column menu in the sheet.
- For filtering rows. Use the TwoUX Filter bar.
- For saving a full working setup with filters. Use TwoUX Saved views.
- As the main way to make a table usable; most people never customise, so defaults must already work.

## Structure

1. Button: Columns
2. Search field
3. Count with Show all and Hide all
4. Row per column: drag handle, type icon, name, Move up, Move down, eye toggle or lock
5. List tables: Wrap long text and Rows per page (25, 50, 100)
6. Where the choice is kept ("Saved for you on this table") and the help line for keyboard reordering

## Guidelines

- Apply each change at once; there is nothing to confirm. Changing it back is the undo.
- Every drag has a keyboard path (Space to pick up, arrows, Space to drop, Esc to cancel) and Move up and Move down buttons.
- The column that names the record is locked: always shown, marked with a lock and the words Always shown.
- Show the type icon of each column so people recognise it among similar names.
- List columns in the same order they appear in the table.
- Store the choice per person and per table, restore it on return, and say so in the menu: "Saved for you on this table".
- Rows per page is a radio group, not a select, so the menu never opens a second popover.

## Content

- Use sentence case and plain labels, for example "Wrap long text".
- Zero results: No columns match "cost".

## Accessibility

- Eye toggles are buttons with aria-pressed and a name that says what they do: Hide Email.
- Moves are announced: Email moved to position 3 of 10.
- 2.5.7 Dragging movements: the Move buttons do the same as dragging.
- Wrap long text is a labelled switch; Rows per page is a radio group named by its label.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Space / Enter on a handle | Pick up or drop |
| ↑ ↓ (picked up) | Move the column |
| Esc (picked up) | Cancel the move |
| Esc | Close the menu; focus returns to Columns |

## Examples

### list-table

```tsx
import { ColumnsMenu, type ColumnsMenuItem, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";
import { LISTINGS, type Listing, formatDate } from "../list-table/data";

export const meta = { title: "On a list table", description: "The same menu on a list table, with Wrap long text and Rows per page. Role is locked so every row stays recognisable. Every change applies at once.", order: 2 };

const CELL: Record<string, (l: Listing) => string | number> = { role: (l) => l.role, location: (l) => l.location, status: (l) => l.status, applicants: (l) => l.applicants, closes: (l) => formatDate(l.closes) };

export default function Example() {
	const [columns, setColumns] = useState<ColumnsMenuItem[]>([
		{ id: "role", label: "Role", locked: true },
		{ id: "location", label: "Location" },
		{ id: "status", label: "Status" },
		{ id: "applicants", label: "Applicants", hidden: true },
		{ id: "closes", label: "Closes" },
	]);
	const [wrap, setWrap] = useState(false);
	const [pageSize, setPageSize] = useState(25);
	const cols = columns.filter((c) => !c.hidden);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl gap-2">
			<div className="flex justify-end">
				<ColumnsMenu columns={columns} onChange={setColumns} wrap={wrap} onWrapChange={setWrap} pageSize={pageSize} onPageSizeChange={setPageSize} note="Saved for you on this table" />
			</div>
			<div className="overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
				<Table aria-label="Listings">
					<TableHeader>
						<TableRow className="hover:bg-transparent">{cols.map((c) => <TableHead key={c.id}>{c.label}</TableHead>)}</TableRow>
					</TableHeader>
					<TableBody>
						{LISTINGS.slice(0, 4).map((l) => (
							<TableRow key={l.id}>{cols.map((c) => <TableCell key={c.id} className={wrap ? "whitespace-normal" : undefined}>{CELL[c.id](l)}</TableCell>)}</TableRow>
						))}
					</TableBody>
				</Table>
				<p className="tabular border-t border-line px-3 py-2 text-sm text-ink-2">Showing 1–4 of {LISTINGS.length} listings · {pageSize} per page</p>
			</div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### sheet

```tsx
import { ColumnsMenu, type ColumnsMenuItem } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Show, hide and reorder columns", description: "Changes apply at once. Drag a handle, use Move up and Move down, or focus a handle, press Space, move with the arrow keys and press Space to drop.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [columns, setColumns] = useState<ColumnsMenuItem[]>([
		{ id: "name", label: "Name", type: "text", locked: true },
		{ id: "title", label: "Job title", type: "text" },
		{ id: "company", label: "Company", type: "text" },
		{ id: "size", label: "Company size", type: "number" },
		{ id: "added", label: "Added", type: "date", hidden: true },
		{ id: "fit", label: "Fit score", type: "formula" },
		{ id: "summary", label: "Summarise role", type: "ai" },
		{ id: "email", label: "Work email", type: "enrichment", provider: "hubspot" },
	]);
	return (
		<div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
			<ColumnsMenu columns={columns} onChange={setColumns} align="start" />
			<p className="text-sm text-ink-2">Shown, in order: {columns.filter((c) => !c.hidden).map((c) => c.label).join(", ")}</p>
		</div>
	);
}
```

# Run status bar

The bottom bar of a sheet: Table up to date, or how far the run is with a meter, the credits spent so far and Stop; run history; and Auto-run with its cost per row.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- At the bottom of a sheet with computed columns, so people always see what is running and what it costs.

## When not to use

- For credits against a monthly limit. Use the Usage meter.
- For one agent run with steps. Use Agent run.

## Structure

1. Status: icon, words, rows done of total, percentage and meter
2. Credits so far
3. Errors link
4. Stop while running, or Run remaining with its cost
5. Auto-run switch with the cost per row
6. History popover

## Guidelines

- Stop is always available while anything runs, and stopping keeps the finished cells.
- Show progress as rows and a percentage, with a meter, never a bare spinner.
- State the credits spent so far while running, and the cost of Run remaining before it starts.
- Auto-run states its cost per row next to the switch, before anyone turns it on.
- History lists each run with rows, credits, outcome and when.

## Content

- Running: "1,240 of 2,000 rows · 62%". Stopped: "Stopped at 62%". Done: "Table up to date".
- Costs use the unit: "≈ 1.5 credits / row".

## Accessibility

- The progress is a progressbar with its value; the status line is a live region.
- Errors are words with an icon, not a red dot.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Reach Stop, Auto-run and History |

## Examples

### running

```tsx
import { RunStatusBar, Timestamp } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "A run with cost and Stop", description: "Progress, credits so far and Stop while running. Stop keeps finished rows; Run remaining states its cost first. Auto-run shows its cost per row before it is turned on.", order: 1 };

const TOTAL = 2000;

export default function Example() {
	const [done, setDone] = useState(1240);
	const [running, setRunning] = useState(true);
	const [autoRun, setAutoRun] = useState(false);
	useEffect(() => {
		if (!running) return;
		const t = window.setInterval(() => setDone((d) => { const n = Math.min(TOTAL, d + 20); if (n === TOTAL) setRunning(false); return n; }), 300);
		return () => window.clearInterval(t);
	}, [running]);
	return (
		<RunStatusBar
			className="w-full rounded-sm border border-line"
			running={running}
			label="Work email"
			done={done}
			total={TOTAL}
			errors={3}
			creditsUsed={done * 0.5}
			costPerRow={0.5}
			onStop={() => setRunning(false)}
			onRunRemaining={() => setRunning(true)}
			autoRun={autoRun}
			onAutoRunChange={setAutoRun}
			history={[{ id: "1", label: "Work email · test on 10 rows", rows: 10, credits: 5, outcome: "Done", when: <Timestamp value={new Date(Date.now() - 3600_000)} /> }]}
		/>
	);
}
```

# Field mapping

A list of target fields, each with the source column that fills it: required fields marked, type mismatches warned in words, and other source columns skipped or created as new columns. Used by imports and, later, automations.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When data from one place fills fields in another: a CSV import, a connected service, an automation step.

## When not to use

- For choosing which columns show. Use the Columns menu.

## Structure

1. Headings: Field in the table, Column in the file
2. Row: type icon, field name, Required, arrow, source select with a sample value
3. Warning under a row: 3 of 20 values aren't an email address
4. Other columns in the file: Don't import or Create column

## Guidelines

- Map by name automatically, ignoring case and punctuation, and let people change every pair.
- Mark required fields in words, and check them when people submit, not by disabling the button.
- Warn about values that don't fit the field type under that row, with how many.
- Offer Create column for source columns no field uses, defaulting to Don't import.

## Content

- Warnings name the column and the type: "3 of 20 values in E-mail aren't an email address."

## Accessibility

- Each select is labelled by its field name; warnings are linked with aria-describedby.
- Warnings carry an icon and words, not colour alone.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move between selects |
| Space / Enter | Open a select |

## Examples

### automation

```tsx
import { type ExtraColumns, type FieldMap, FieldMapping, type MappingSource, type MappingTarget, autoMapFields } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Map a form's answers to table fields", description: "Fields with matching names are paired automatically. Required fields are marked, values that don't fit the field type are warned about, and unused columns can become new columns.", order: 1 };

const TARGETS: MappingTarget[] = [
	{ id: "name", label: "Name", kind: "text", required: true },
	{ id: "email", label: "Work email", kind: "email", required: true },
	{ id: "size", label: "Company size", kind: "number" },
	{ id: "start", label: "Start date", kind: "date" },
];
const SOURCES: MappingSource[] = [
	{ id: "q1", label: "Your name", samples: ["Ana Silva", "Ben Hughes", "Chloe Patel"] },
	{ id: "q2", label: "Email", samples: ["ana@harbourvale.co.uk", "ben at brightwater", "chloe@mosaiclending.co.uk"] },
	{ id: "q3", label: "Company size", samples: ["240", "about 150", "410"] },
	{ id: "q4", label: "How did you hear about us?", samples: ["Event", "Search"] },
];

export default function Example() {
	const [map, setMap] = useState<FieldMap>(() => ({ ...autoMapFields(TARGETS, SOURCES), name: "q1" }));
	const [extra, setExtra] = useState<ExtraColumns>({});
	return <FieldMapping className="w-full max-w-2xl" targets={TARGETS} sources={SOURCES} value={map} onChange={setMap} extra={extra} onExtraChange={setExtra} sourceHeading="Answer in the form" />;
}
```

## Related

- CSV import
- Sheet grid

# CSV import

A two-step dialog: choose a CSV file, its delimiter and header row; then match columns, read the problems before importing, preview the first 20 rows with problem cells marked, and import with the count on the button.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Bringing rows from a spreadsheet into a table.

## When not to use

- For a single file attached to a record. Use File drop.
- For syncing a connected service. Use the connector and an automation.

## Structure

1. Step 1: File drop, Use the sample file, Delimiter, First row contains column names
2. Step 2: problem summary with what happens to bad rows
3. Field mapping
4. Preview of the first 20 rows, or only rows with problems, with Fix on problem cells
5. Footer: Back, Cancel, Import 1,248 rows

## Guidelines

- Show problems before importing, in a summary at the top that says what will happen to bad rows: skipped, or imported with the cells left empty.
- Mark problem cells in the preview with an icon and a word, and let people fix them in place.
- Put the number of rows on the Import button, so the result is known before pressing it.
- Accept the file by drop or by the Upload button, state the type and size limit, and explain a wrong file in words.
- Detect the delimiter and header row, and let people change both.
- Read dates day first, as in the UK (02/11/2026 is 2 November), accept ISO 8601 and written months (14 Mar 2026), and mark anything else, including impossible dates such as 31/02/2026, as Not a date. Hand dates to the app as ISO 8601 so it never re-reads them.

## Content

- Summary: "3 rows have an invalid email. They will be skipped or you can fix them."
- Wrong file: "That isn't a CSV file. Save the sheet as CSV and choose it again."

## Accessibility

- Progress is written as Step 2 of 2.
- The summary takes focus after a failed Import; problem cells have the word, not only a tint.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Esc | Close the dialog |
| Enter (fixing) | Save the fixed value |
| Esc (fixing) | Cancel the fix |

## Examples

### leads

```tsx
import { Button, CsvImport, type MappingTarget, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { FileUp } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Import event leads", description: "Use the sample file or choose your own CSV. The summary says what happens to rows with problems before anything is imported, and the button states how many rows will be added.", order: 1 };

const TARGETS: MappingTarget[] = [
	{ id: "name", label: "Name", kind: "text", required: true },
	{ id: "email", label: "Work email", kind: "email" },
	{ id: "company", label: "Company", kind: "text" },
	{ id: "size", label: "Company size", kind: "number" },
];
const SAMPLE = {
	name: "leads.csv",
	text: "Full name,E-mail,Company,Headcount,Country\nMaya Fischer,maya.fischer@larkfield.energy,Larkfield Energy,3100,UK\nRuairi Doyle,ruairi.doyle@pennine,Pennine Freight,1200,Ireland\nSana Iqbal,sana.iqbal@mosaiclending.co.uk,Mosaic Lending,410,UK\n,info@copperleaf.co.uk,Copperleaf Foods,780,UK\nTheo Clarke,theo.clarke@orrin.dev,Orrin Software,about 130,UK\nGrace Ndlovu,grace.ndlovu@harbourvale.co.uk,Harbour & Vale,240,UK",
};

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
	return (
		<>
			<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}><FileUp />Import CSV</Button>
			<CsvImport open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} targets={TARGETS} tableName="People" sample={SAMPLE} aliases={{ email: ["e-mail"], size: ["headcount"] }} onImport={(r) => toast.success(`Imported ${r.rows.length} rows${r.skipped ? `, skipped ${r.skipped}` : ""}`)} />
		</>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Field mapping
- File drop
- Sheet grid

# Action catalogue

A searchable list, in the side panel, of actions that add a column: look-ups from other services, AI, formulas and exports, each with a one-line description and its cost per row. Choosing one opens a short set-up with the estimated total.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- To add a computed column to a sheet.

## When not to use

- For adding a dashboard item. Use the Items palette.
- For templates of whole tables. Use the Templates gallery.

## Structure

1. Search
2. Tabs: Suggested, Enrichment, AI, Formulas, Exports, with counts
3. Action: logo or icon, name, description, cost per row
4. Set-up: column name, inputs, Run after adding (test, all, not yet), estimated total, Add column

## Guidelines

- State the cost per row on every action, and the total for the current rows before adding.
- Default to testing on the first 10 rows when an action costs credits.
- Show the service's logo with ProviderLogo when an action uses one; otherwise a plain icon.
- Search covers every category; tabs group the rest.

## Content

- Cost: "≈ 0.5 credits / row"; total: "About 1,000 credits for 2,000 rows".
- The button says what happens: "Add column and test on 10 rows".

## Accessibility

- Each action is a button whose name includes its cost.
- Back to the list returns focus to the action chosen.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through actions |
| Enter | Open an action's set-up |

## Examples

### add-column

```tsx
import { ActionCatalogue, type CatalogueAction, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { AtSign, PenLine, Sigma, Tags } from "lucide-react";

export const meta = { title: "Add a column to 2,000 rows", description: "Search or pick a category, choose an action, then set it up. Paid actions test on 10 rows by default; the total for every row is shown before you add.", order: 1 };

const ACTIONS: CatalogueAction[] = [
	{ id: "email", name: "Find work email", description: "Looks up the person's work email in HubSpot from their name and company domain.", category: "Enrichment", suggested: true, provider: "hubspot", costPerRow: 0.5, inputs: [{ id: "domain", label: "Company domain column", options: ["Company domain", "Company"] }] },
	{ id: "account", name: "Company details from Salesforce", description: "Industry, headcount and account owner from the matching account.", category: "Enrichment", provider: "salesforce", costPerRow: 0.5 },
	{ id: "summary", name: "Summarise role", description: "One sentence on what the person does and whether they buy tools.", category: "AI", suggested: true, icon: <PenLine />, costPerRow: 1 },
	{ id: "industry", name: "Classify industry", description: "Puts each company into one of your industries, with the reason.", category: "AI", icon: <Tags />, costPerRow: 0.5 },
	{ id: "combine", name: "Combine columns", description: "Joins two or more columns with a separator you choose.", category: "Formulas", suggested: true, icon: <Sigma />, costPerRow: 0 },
	{ id: "domain", name: "Domain from email", description: "Takes the part after @ from an email column.", category: "Formulas", icon: <AtSign />, costPerRow: 0 },
	{ id: "sheet", name: "Add to a Google Sheet", description: "Appends each row to a sheet you choose and keeps it in step.", category: "Exports", provider: "google-sheets", costPerRow: 0 },
];

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-md rounded-sm border border-line p-4">
			<ActionCatalogue actions={ACTIONS} rowCount={2000} onAdd={(c) => toast.success(`Added “${c.columnName}”`, { description: c.run === "test" ? "Testing on 10 rows." : c.run === "all" ? "Running on 2,000 rows." : "Not run yet." })} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

# Table settings

Settings for one table in the side panel: how duplicates are handled with the consequence written out, deleting empty rows, and sharing as a template with who can use it. Saved with Save; closing with changes asks first.

Kind: component · Group: Data · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For rules that apply to a whole table rather than one column.

## When not to use

- For column set-up. Use the column menu.

## Structure

1. Duplicate rows: match on, Keep the oldest, Keep the newest, Keep both, each with what happens
2. Empty rows: Delete empty rows automatically
3. Share as a template: checkbox, who can use it, link with Copy
4. Footer: Cancel, Save

## Guidelines

- Write out the consequence of each duplicate rule, including overwritten values and runs that cost credits again.
- Use checkboxes and radios in this form, saved with Save; a switch is only for changes that apply at once.
- Ask before discarding only when something changed, and warn before leaving the page while dirty.
- Say what a template shares and what it never shares.

## Content

- "Rows and looked-up values are never shared."

## Accessibility

- Radio groups are labelled by their heading; hints are linked to each option.
- The discard dialog puts focus on Keep editing.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘ Enter | Save |
| Esc | Close; asks first when there are changes |

## Examples

### settings

```tsx
import { Button, TableSettings, type TableSettingsValue } from "@twoux/ui";
import { Settings } from "lucide-react";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Settings for the People table", description: "Change a setting and close the panel: it asks before discarding. Close without changes and it doesn't ask. Each duplicate rule says what happens to existing rows and credits.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
	const [value, setValue] = useState<TableSettingsValue>({ duplicates: "keep-oldest", matchOn: "email", deleteEmptyRows: false, template: { shared: false, audience: "workspace" } });
	return (
		<>
			<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}><Settings />Table settings</Button>
			<TableSettings
				open={open}
				onOpenChange={setOpen}
				mode="overlay"
				value={value}
				onSave={async (v) => { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400)); setValue(v); }}
				columns={[{ id: "email", label: "Work email" }, { id: "name", label: "Name" }]}
				tableName="People"
				workspaceName="TwoUX"
				templateLink="https://app.example.com/t/people"
			/>
		</>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Side panel (drawer)
- Sheet grid

# Assistant side panel

A side panel, opened with ⌘J, where people ask about the records on screen and get answers grounded in the current selection and filters.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Quick questions about the listings or candidates on screen, where the answer needs the data beside it. ⌘J opens the panel with the current selection and filters already attached.
- When people need to invoke help without leaving the table they are working through. HAX G7 asks for efficient invocation and G8 for efficient dismissal, so the panel opens and closes with one shortcut.
- When an answer may lead to a change. The panel can hold a proposal next to the rows it affects, so the person can compare before applying.

## When not to use

- Long research answers that need room for sources and a records list. Use the Assistant page (assistant-page) instead, which keeps the same conversation.
- Repeated tasks with the same shape every week. Use the Task builder (task-builder) so the inputs are slots, not free text.
- Filling one value per row across a table. Use the AI column (ai-column), which writes into a generated column and cites each row.
- Do not add a floating chat bubble to every page. The panel opens from ⌘J or Ask in the bulk bar, where the context is.

## Structure

1. Panel bar (Assistant, conversation title, Open as a full page, Previous conversations, Share, New, Close)
2. Thread (questions, thinking row, answers)
3. Clarifying question card (docked above the message box when needed)
4. Message box with context chips
5. Caveat line

## Guidelines

- Open in the same side panel as row details, in push mode by default, so the table stays readable. Opening the assistant closes the row detail panel and the other way round.
- Turn the selection and active filters into context chips automatically. Removing a chip narrows what the assistant reads.
- Lead each answer with the figure, then a small table, then the reason. Every claim about a record carries its record ID as a citation.
- Changes never apply from the thread. They arrive as Suggested changes with checkboxes and one Apply button, and nothing changes until the person applies.
- While a response is running, the send button becomes Stop in the same place. Stopping keeps what was written and says it is incomplete.
- Keep the message box pinned and let only the thread scroll. Do not jump the thread to the bottom while someone is reading an older message.
- Show the caveat under the message box at all times: what data it uses and what to check.

## Content

- Call it Assistant. Do not use "AI-powered", "smart" or "magic". Say what it read and what it did.
- Empty state: say what it will use ("Ask about 2 listings. Uses what you have selected and filtered. Nothing changes until you apply it.").
- Caveat copy is specific: "Uses your workspace data only. Check figures before you act on them."
- Answers open with the answer. No greeting, no "Great question", no disclaimer about being an AI before the content.
- Name the conversation from the first question and show it in the panel bar, so it can be found later.

## Accessibility

- Render the panel as an aside with aria-label="Assistant" (complementary landmark). Label it because the row details panel is a second complementary landmark.
- The thread is a log (role="log", implicit aria-live polite) with an accessible name, so new answers are announced without moving focus (SC 4.1.3).
- Do not announce every streamed token. Announce the thinking step titles and the finished answer; Stop satisfies SC 2.2.2 for content that auto-updates in parallel with the table.
- When the panel opens, focus moves to the message box; Esc closes the innermost open layer first (menu, history, then panel) and focus returns to the trigger, as the dialog pattern does (SC 2.4.3).
- The send button changes its accessible name from "Send (Enter)" to "Stop" while running, which the button pattern allows when the label itself changes.
- The panel must not cover the focused row in push mode (SC 2.4.11).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘J / Ctrl+J | Open or close the assistant with the current selection as context |
| Enter | Send the message |
| Shift+Enter | New line |
| Esc | Close the open menu, then history, then the panel |
| ⌘↵ | Apply the suggested changes in focus |

## Examples

### flow

```tsx
import { AnswerActions, AssistantMessage, AssistantPanel, Button, Citation, FollowUps, MessageComposer, StepCard, SuggestedChanges, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableRow, ThinkingSteps, UserMessage, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Ask, propose, apply", description: "The assistant reads the selection, thinks in visible steps, answers with the figure first and record IDs, and proposes changes. Nothing changes until you apply; the step card shows progress and Undo follows.", order: 1 };

type Stage = "idle" | "thinking" | "answered" | "applying" | "applied";

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);
	const [stage, setStage] = useState<Stage>("idle");
	const [t, setT] = useState(0);
	const [steps, setSteps] = useState<("pending" | "done")[]>(["pending", "pending"]);
	useEffect(() => {
		if (stage !== "thinking") return;
		const i = setInterval(() => setT((x) => x + 0.1), 100);
		const d = setTimeout(() => setStage("answered"), 1800);
		return () => { clearInterval(i); clearTimeout(d); };
	}, [stage]);
	useEffect(() => {
		if (stage !== "applying") return;
		const a = setTimeout(() => setSteps(["done", "pending"]), 600);
		const b = setTimeout(() => { setSteps(["done", "done"]); setStage("applied"); toast.success("Extended 2 listings by 30 days", { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setStage("answered") } }); }, 1200);
		return () => { clearTimeout(a); clearTimeout(b); };
	}, [stage]);
	return (
		<div className="flex h-140 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<div className="grid min-w-0 flex-1 content-start gap-2 p-4">
				<span className="text-base text-ink-2">2 listings selected</span>
				{!open && <Button variant="outline" size="sm" shortcut="⌘J" className="justify-self-start" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Ask the assistant</Button>}
			</div>
			<AssistantPanel caveat="Reads listings and applications, not emails. Check closing dates before you extend a listing."
				open={open}
				onOpenChange={setOpen}
				title="Why are these closing with few applicants?"
				onOpenPage={() => {}}
				composer={<MessageComposer noun={{ one: "listing", many: "listings" }} chips={[{ id: "sel", label: "2 selected listings" }, { id: "f", label: "Status is Closing soon" }]} busy={stage === "thinking"} onStop={() => setStage("idle")} onSend={() => { setT(0); setStage("thinking"); }} />}
			>
				{stage === "idle" ? (
					<p className="text-base text-ink-2">Ask about the 2 selected listings, for example “Why are these closing with few applicants?”</p>
				) : (
					<>
						<UserMessage>Why are these closing with few applicants?</UserMessage>
						<ThinkingSteps done={stage !== "thinking"} seconds={stage === "thinking" ? t : 1.8} steps={[{ title: "Reading 2 listings", detail: "LST-1041, LST-1044" }, { title: "Comparing with 22 similar listings", detail: "Same teams, last 90 days" }, { title: "Checking salary and posting dates" }]} />
						{stage !== "thinking" && (
							<AssistantMessage
								from="2 listings and 22 similar ones"
								actions={<AnswerActions text="Both close in under 5 days with 9 applicants between them." onRegenerate={() => { setT(0); setStage("thinking"); }} onFeedback={() => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400))} />}
								followUps={<FollowUps items={["Which job boards are they on?", "Draft a shorter job description for LST-1044"]} onPick={() => {}} />}
							>
								<p><strong>9 applicants</strong> between them, against a median of 38 for similar listings.</p>
								<Table aria-label="Applicants"><TableBody><TableRow><TableCell>Frontend Engineer <Citation id="LST-1041" /></TableCell><TableCell className="tabular text-right">6</TableCell></TableRow><TableRow><TableCell>Customer Success Lead <Citation id="LST-1044" /></TableCell><TableCell className="tabular text-right">3</TableCell></TableRow></TableBody></Table>
								<p>Both were posted 9 days ago and close within 5 days. Similar listings stay open 30 days.</p>
							</AssistantMessage>
						)}
						{stage === "answered" && <SuggestedChanges changes={[{ id: "a", label: "Extend Frontend Engineer by 30 days", detail: "LST-1041", before: "Closes 21 Nov", after: "Closes 21 Dec" }, { id: "b", label: "Extend Customer Success Lead by 30 days", detail: "LST-1044", before: "Closes 23 Nov", after: "Closes 23 Dec" }]} onApply={() => { setSteps(["pending", "pending"]); setStage("applying"); }} onDismiss={() => setStage("idle")} />}
						{(stage === "applying" || stage === "applied") && <StepCard title="Extending 2 listings" steps={[{ label: "Frontend Engineer closes 21 Dec", state: steps[0] }, { label: "Customer Success Lead closes 23 Dec", state: steps[1] }]} />}
					</>
				)}
			</AssistantPanel>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant page
- Message composer
- Thinking and steps
- Suggested changes
- Citations and sources
- Previous conversations
- Side panel (drawer)

# Assistant page

The same conversation opened as a full page, with Answer and Records tabs and a Sources panel listing every record the answer used.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Answers that rely on many records and need checking. The Sources panel lists every record so people can verify without hunting.
- Research-style questions across the whole workspace, such as Thorough answers that also read candidates and past listings.
- When the person wants to keep the answer as the main task, not as help beside a table.

## When not to use

- A quick question about the rows on screen. Use the Assistant side panel (assistant-panel) so the table stays visible.
- Watching an agent work through steps over time. Use the Agent run timeline (agent-run).
- Browsing past conversations. Use Previous conversations (conversation-history).

## Structure

1. Top bar (Answer and Records tabs, Share, Open in side panel)
2. Centred reading column (thread)
3. Records tab (the rows the answer used, as a table)
4. Sources panel (every cited record)
5. Message box

## Guidelines

- Expand opens the same conversation; "Open in side panel" goes back without losing the thread, context or scroll position.
- Use a centred reading column and align messages user to the end, assistant to the start, on full, dedicated surfaces.
- The Sources panel lists every record the answer used. Selecting a citation highlights its source in the panel.
- The Records tab shows the rows behind the answer as a table that can open as a filtered view, so the claim and the data sit one click apart.
- Say when there are no sources rather than showing filler: empty states keep trust.
- Long task conversations get an outline: a list of key moments (question asked, values given, changes applied) that jumps to each message.
- Long drafts open here beside the conversation rather than in a second panel.

## Content

- Tabs are nouns: Answer and Records (with a count). Avoid branded names for modes or tabs.
- Source rows show the record ID, title and what was used (for example "Views and applies, last 30 days").
- Keep the same caveat and origin label as in the panel so the two surfaces read as one product.

## Accessibility

- Answer and Records use the tabs pattern: role="tablist", role="tab" with aria-selected and aria-controls, arrow keys move between tabs.
- The Sources panel is an aside labelled "Sources" so it is reachable as a landmark.
- Highlighting a source after a citation is selected must not rely on colour alone; add an outline or marker (SC 1.4.1).
- New answers are announced through the thread's log region without moving focus (SC 4.1.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Left / Right arrow | Move between Answer and Records tabs |
| Tab | Move from the tabs into the panel content |
| ⌘J / Ctrl+J | Focus the message box |
| Enter | Send |
| Esc | Close an open menu |

## Examples

### page

```tsx
import { AssistantMessage, AssistantPage, Citation, MessageComposer, SourcesList, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, UserMessage } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "The conversation as a full page", description: "A centred reading column with Answer and Records tabs, and a Sources panel listing every record the answer used. Selecting a citation highlights its source.", order: 1 };

const SOURCES = [{ id: "LST-1041", title: "Frontend Engineer", detail: "Manchester · 6 applicants" }, { id: "LST-1044", title: "Customer Success Lead", detail: "Bristol · 3 applicants" }];

export default function Example() {
	const [active, setActive] = useState<string>();
	return (
		<div className="h-120 w-full overflow-auto rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface">
			<AssistantPage
				thread={
					<>
						<UserMessage>Which listings close this week with fewer than 10 applicants?</UserMessage>
						<AssistantMessage from="24 listings">
							<p><strong>2 listings</strong>: Frontend Engineer <Citation id="LST-1041" active={active === "LST-1041"} onOpen={setActive} /> and Customer Success Lead <Citation id="LST-1044" active={active === "LST-1044"} onOpen={setActive} />.</p>
						</AssistantMessage>
					</>
				}
				records={<Table aria-label="Records used"><TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Listing</TableHead><TableHead className="text-right">Applicants</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader><TableBody>{SOURCES.map((s) => <TableRow key={s.id}><TableCell>{s.title}</TableCell><TableCell className="tabular text-right">{s.detail?.split("· ")[1]}</TableCell></TableRow>)}</TableBody></Table>}
				sources={<SourcesList sources={SOURCES} active={active} onSelect={setActive} />}
				composer={<MessageComposer noun={{ one: "listing", many: "listings" }} onSend={() => {}} placeholder="Ask a follow-up" />}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant side panel
- Citations and sources
- Message composer
- Follow-ups and starters
- Tabs (underline)

# Message composer

The message box with context chips, a + menu, @ mentions, / saved tasks, typeahead completions and the Quick or Thorough answer mode.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Any free question or instruction to the assistant, in the panel or on the full page.
- When people need to add or narrow context: @ adds a record as a chip, the + menu attaches files and tools.
- When the trade-off between speed and depth matters: Quick reads what is on screen, Thorough also reads candidates and past listings and says what it costs.

## When not to use

- A task that repeats with the same inputs. Use the Task builder (task-builder) with slots.
- A prompt that runs on every row. Use the Prompt editor (prompt-editor), which lists inputs and outputs with types.
- Searching records by name. Use the table filters (filters), not the assistant.

## Structure

1. Context chips (selection, filters, mentions)
2. Text area
3. Typeahead list
4. + menu (Mention a listing, Run a saved task, Attach a file, toggles, Writing style submenu, Connected tools submenu)
5. Answer mode button (Quick or Thorough)
6. Send or Stop button

## Guidelines

- The box stays clean. Everything that changes context or output lives in the + menu, grouped: inserts, toggles, writing style, connected tools.
- @ and / work without opening the menu. @ suggests listings and adds the chosen one as a removable chip; / suggests saved tasks.
- Typeahead suggests whole questions from your own records and saved tasks. What you typed stays regular and the completion is bold. Enter still sends what you typed unless you moved into the list.
- Answer mode is a stable contract: Quick or Thorough, each with one line on what it does and what it costs. The model name is shown but set by an admin.
- Allow attachments at any point, including follow-ups, and cite files when an answer relies on them.
- While running, Send becomes Stop in the same place. People can still draft the next message.
- One symbol per menu: / for saved tasks and actions, @ for records and files. Each also has a button in the composer bar with the same symbol.
- Only one menu is open at a time; group items under labels such as "Saved tasks" and "Actions".
- A hint under the composer says what the symbols do: "/ for tasks, @ to add a record".
- The Quick or Thorough setting stays visible as a chip and carries over to the next message until changed.

## Content

- Placeholder says what to do: "Ask, or type @ for a listing and / for a saved task".
- Menu items are verbs with the shortcut shown: "Mention a listing @", "Run a saved task /".
- Mode descriptions state the trade-off in plain words: "Answers from what's on screen, in seconds" and "Also reads candidates and past listings. About 5 credits."
- Never name controls with branded or vague words such as "Magic" or "Boost".

## Accessibility

- The text area is an editable combobox: aria-autocomplete="list", aria-controls pointing at the suggestions listbox, aria-expanded reflecting whether it is shown, and aria-activedescendant on the highlighted option.
- Down Arrow moves into suggestions, Enter or Tab accepts the highlighted one, Esc closes the list and keeps focus in the box.
- The + and mode buttons are menu buttons (aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded). Toggles are menuitemcheckbox and writing styles are menuitemradio with aria-checked.
- The text area has a programmatic label ("Message") even though the label is visually hidden (SC 3.3.2, 4.1.2).
- @ and / only trigger while the text area has focus, so they are not global character key shortcuts (SC 2.1.4).
- Each context chip's remove button names what it removes, for example "Remove 2 listings from context".
- Typing / or @ opens a combobox list; arrows move, Enter inserts, Esc closes and leaves the typed symbol.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | Send, or accept the highlighted suggestion |
| Shift+Enter | New line |
| Down / Up arrow | Move through suggestions |
| Tab | Accept the highlighted suggestion |
| Esc | Close suggestions or the open menu |
| @ | Suggest listings to add as context |
| / | Suggest saved tasks |
| Right arrow / Left arrow | Open or close a submenu in the + menu |

## Examples

### composer

```tsx
import { DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, MessageComposer, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Ask with context", description: "The selection and filters arrive as chips; removing one narrows what the assistant reads. Type @ for a listing or / for a saved task. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [chips, setChips] = useState([{ id: "sel", label: "3 selected listings" }, { id: "f", label: "Team is Engineering" }]);
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-xl">
			<MessageComposer
				noun={{ one: "listing", many: "listings" }}
				chips={chips}
				onRemoveChip={(id) => setChips((c) => c.filter((x) => x.id !== id))}
				mentions={[{ id: "1", label: "FrontendEngineer" }, { id: "2", label: "DataAnalyst" }, { id: "3", label: "QAEngineer" }]}
				tasks={["Weekly-pipeline-summary", "Draft-rejection-reasons"]}
				onSend={(t, m) => toast(`Sent (${m}): ${t}`)}
				plusMenu={<><DropdownMenuLabel>Insert</DropdownMenuLabel><DropdownMenuItem>Mention a listing</DropdownMenuItem><DropdownMenuItem>Run a saved task</DropdownMenuItem><DropdownMenuItem>Attach a file</DropdownMenuItem><DropdownMenuSeparator /><DropdownMenuLabel>Connected tools</DropdownMenuLabel><DropdownMenuItem>Calendar</DropdownMenuItem></>}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant side panel
- Assistant page
- Task builder
- Connected tools
- Team instructions and files
