# Thinking and steps

A row that shows what the assistant is doing in words with a running timer, then collapses to "Thought for 2.1s · 4 steps" and expands on request.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Any response that takes more than about a second, so people know what is happening instead of watching a bare spinner.
- When the answer depends on what was read: steps say "Read 2 listings and 3,000 views" so people can judge scope.
- Keeping the reasoning in the history after the answer arrives, so it can be checked later.

## When not to use

- Responses under a second. Stream the answer directly; short loading states flicker.
- Multi-step agent work that changes records. Use the Agent run timeline (agent-run) with states and Stop.
- Progress of applying approved changes. Use the Step card (step-card).

## Structure

1. Header (status mark, "Thinking", timer)
2. Step list (short title and one line of detail each)
3. Collapsed summary button ("Thought for Xs · N steps")

## Guidelines

- Say the current step in words ("Reading 9 listings"), never only an animation.
- Show a running timer while thinking. When the answer starts, collapse to "Thought for 2.1s · 4 steps" with a check.
- Each step has a short title and one line of detail. Keep plan, execution and evidence apart.
- If the person answered clarifying questions, add a step "Using your answers" with their choices.
- Stopping during thinking marks the header "Stopped" and removes unfinished steps; nothing is changed.

## Content

- Use present participles for running steps ("Reading listings", "Comparing with the board median") and past tense once done.
- Include counts and time: "Read 2 listings and 3,000 views · 4s".
- Do not write "Thinking deeply" or anything that implies a person or magic.

## Accessibility

- The thinking row is a polite live region; announce each step title, not the timer ticks (SC 4.1.3).
- The running timer updates in parallel with other content, so Stop must be available (SC 2.2.2); the pulse animation is decorative and stops when done.
- The collapsed summary is a disclosure button with aria-expanded; Enter or Space toggles the steps.
- Step states use an icon shape as well as colour (SC 1.4.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter / Space | Expand or collapse finished steps |
| Tab | Move to the summary button |

## Examples

### steps

```tsx
import { Button, ThinkingSteps } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Say what it is doing", description: "The current step in words with a running timer, never only an animation. When the answer starts, it collapses to a summary you can open.", order: 1 };

const STEPS = [{ title: "Reading 24 listings", detail: "Open and closing soon" }, { title: "Comparing applicants with last quarter" }, { title: "Checking salary bands", detail: "Against the 2026 bands file" }, { title: "Writing the answer" }];

export default function Example() {
	const [n, setN] = useState(1);
	const [t, setT] = useState(0);
	const done = n > STEPS.length;
	useEffect(() => {
		if (done) return;
		const i = setInterval(() => setT((x) => x + 0.1), 100);
		const s = setTimeout(() => setN((x) => x + 1), 700);
		return () => { clearInterval(i); clearTimeout(s); };
	}, [n, done]);
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-3">
			<ThinkingSteps done={done} seconds={t} steps={STEPS.slice(0, Math.min(n, STEPS.length))} />
			<Button variant="outline" size="sm" className="justify-self-start" onClick={() => { setN(1); setT(0); }}>Replay</Button>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant side panel
- Agent run timeline
- Step card
- Clarifying question card

# Clarifying question card

A card docked above the message box that asks up to three questions with recommended defaults when the answer would change the result.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When the request is ambiguous and the answer changes the result, for example which listings to rewrite.
- Before high-impact changes or when confidence is low, collect details first.

## When not to use

- Information already in context or retrievable from the data. Do not re-ask; use the context chips (message-composer).
- Suggesting what to ask next after an answer. Use Follow-ups (follow-ups-starters).
- Approving a change. Use Suggested changes (suggested-changes).

## Structure

1. Counter ("1 / 2") and question
2. Options (title and one line each, recommended first, number key)
3. Other (free text, last)
4. Footer (Previous, Skip, Next ↵)
5. Thread line "Waiting for your answer" with timer

## Guidelines

- Ask only when the answer changes the result, at most three questions, one at a time.
- Every question has a default, shown first and marked "(Recommended)". Skip uses the defaults for the rest.
- Options first, free text last. Structured choices beat free text.
- Dock the card above the message box so the thread does not fill with back and forth.
- Stop ends the questions and says "Stopped. Nothing was changed."

## Content

- Questions are short and specific: "Which titles should I rewrite?"
- Each option has a title and one line of consequence ("Leaves listings that are doing well alone").
- Use "choose" or "select", not "click".

## Accessibility

- Options are a radiogroup labelled by the question; each option is role="radio" with aria-checked.
- Arrow keys move and select within the group; Tab moves to Other and the footer buttons in order (SC 2.4.3).
- Number keys 1 to 4 are single character shortcuts, so they must be active only while the card is open and focus is not in a text field, and must respect the setting that turns single-key shortcuts off (SC 2.1.4). The mock listens while the card is open but ignores that setting, which needs fixing.
- The waiting timer must not limit time to answer (SC 2.2.1); it only shows elapsed time.
- Announce the new question when Next is pressed (SC 4.1.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| 1 to 3 | Choose an option |
| 4 | Move focus to Other |
| Arrow keys | Move between options |
| Enter | Next question, or run when it is the last |
| Esc | Close the panel (Stop ends the questions) |

## Examples

### ask

```tsx
import { ClarifyingQuestion, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Ask only what changes the result", description: "One question at a time, at most three. The recommended option comes first; number keys choose; Other is last; Skip keeps the defaults.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [k, setK] = useState(0);
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<ClarifyingQuestion
				key={k}
				questions={[
					{ question: "Which listings should I compare?", options: [{ id: "team", title: "Same team, last 90 days", detail: "22 listings" }, { id: "all", title: "All listings this year", detail: "141 listings" }] },
					{ question: "How should I show the result?", options: [{ id: "table", title: "A short table" }, { id: "chart", title: "A chart by week" }] },
				]}
				onDone={(a) => { toast(`Continuing with: ${a.join(", ")}`); setK((x) => x + 1); }}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant side panel
- Message composer
- Thinking and steps
- Agent run timeline
- Plan preview
- Confidence note

# Suggested changes

A proposal card listing each change with a checkbox and before and after, applied with one button and undoable afterwards.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Any time the assistant or an agent would change records: extend, rename, close, email.
- When several changes are proposed and people may want only some of them.

## When not to use

- Read-only answers. Show the figure and table without a proposal (assistant-panel).
- Actions set to Allow in Agent permissions; those run and appear in the Agent run timeline (agent-run) with Undo.
- Generated values that fill a new column. Use the AI column (ai-column), which never overwrites real data.

## Structure

1. Header ("Suggested changes · 2")
2. Change rows (checkbox, change, detail line, inline diff)
3. Footer (note "Nothing changes until you apply.", Dismiss, Edit, Apply N changes ⌘↵)
4. Undo toast after applying

## Guidelines

- Nothing runs until the person applies. Say so in the footer.
- Each change has a checkbox, ticked by default, and shows the before and after (strikethrough and inserted text).
- The Apply button counts what it will change ("Apply 2 changes") and updates as boxes are unticked.
- Edit opens the changes for adjustment; Dismiss removes the card without changing anything.
- After applying, show a toast with Undo (⌘Z) that restores the previous values.
- Match friction to risk: changes that reach people outside the workspace need a stronger confirmation.

## Content

- Write each change as a plain action: "Extend Operations Coordinator by 30 days", with the consequence on the next line ("New closing date 6 Dec").
- State what does not change ("Title only. Description stays the same.").
- After Undo: "Undone. Nothing was changed."

## Accessibility

- Each change is a native checkbox with its label, so the change and its detail are read together (SC 1.3.1, 4.1.2).
- Before and after use del and ins elements and text, not colour alone (SC 1.4.1).
- Applying changes records data, so it must be reversible or confirmed (SC 3.3.4): this card is the review step and Undo makes it reversible.
- The applied and undone messages are status messages in a role="status" toast (SC 4.1.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Space | Tick or untick the focused change |
| ⌘↵ / Ctrl+Enter | Apply the ticked changes |
| ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z | Undo from the toast |

## Examples

### proposal

```tsx
import { SuggestedChanges, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "A proposal you apply", description: "Each change ticked by default with before and after. Apply counts what it will change; ⌘↵ applies. Undo follows.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [k, setK] = useState(0);
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<SuggestedChanges
				key={k}
				changes={[
					{ id: "1", label: "Rename Frontend Engineer", detail: "LST-1041", before: "Frontend Engineer", after: "Frontend Engineer (React)" },
					{ id: "2", label: "Add salary range", detail: "LST-1041", after: "£48,000 to £56,000" },
					{ id: "3", label: "Extend closing date by 30 days", detail: "LST-1041", before: "21 Nov", after: "21 Dec" },
				]}
				onApply={(ids) => { toast.success(`Applied ${ids.length} changes`, { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setK((x) => x + 1) } }); setK((x) => x + 1); }}
				onDismiss={() => toast("Dismissed")}
				onEdit={() => toast("Opened for editing")}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Step card
- Agent permissions
- Assistant side panel
- Toast
- Change review

# Step card

The proposal turns into a step card while changes apply: each change shows a spinner then a check, with an "N / M" counter, and the table updates row by row.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Applying approved changes that take more than an instant, so people can see each one land.
- When the table should update as each step finishes, so the result can be checked in place.

## When not to use

- Scheduled or long agent runs with waiting steps. Use the Agent run timeline (agent-run).
- Reasoning before an answer. Use Thinking and steps (thinking-steps).

## Structure

1. Header ("Applying 2 changes" and counter)
2. Step rows (spinner or check, change label)
3. Footer note ("Working…" then "Applied 2 changes.")

## Guidelines

- Each step has a visible state: pending with spinner, then done with a check. A failed step says why and keeps the others.
- Show the counter ("1 / 2") so progress reads without counting icons.
- Finish with a summary and an Undo toast.
- Keep the step card in the thread as a record of what was done.

## Content

- Use the same label as the proposal row so people recognise each change.
- Finish in past tense with a count: "Applied 2 changes."

## Accessibility

- Announce the counter and the final summary through a status region (SC 4.1.3); do not announce every spinner.
- Spinners are aria-hidden and the state is also given in text (SC 1.3.1, 1.4.1).
- Spinner motion stops when the step ends; runs over five seconds need Stop (SC 2.2.2).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z | Undo the applied changes from the toast |

## Examples

### apply

```tsx
import { Button, StepCard } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Applying, step by step", description: "Each change shows pending, then done. A failed step says why and keeps the others. The counter reads progress without counting icons.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [n, setN] = useState(0);
	useEffect(() => { if (n < 3) { const t = setTimeout(() => setN((x) => x + 1), 700); return () => clearTimeout(t); } }, [n]);
	const state = (i: number) => (i >= n ? "pending" : i === 2 ? "failed" : "done") as "pending" | "done" | "failed";
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-2">
			<StepCard title="Extending 3 listings" steps={[{ label: "Frontend Engineer closes 21 Dec", state: state(0) }, { label: "Data Analyst closes 12 Jan", state: state(1) }, { label: "QA Engineer", state: state(2), reason: n > 2 ? "Already closed. Reopen it first." : undefined }]} />
			<Button variant="outline" size="sm" className="justify-self-start" onClick={() => setN(0)}>Replay</Button>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Suggested changes
- Agent run timeline
- Toast
- Plan preview

# Follow-ups and starters

Follow-ups continue an answer as muted rows under a "Follow-ups" label; starters appear only in the empty state as suggested tasks based on what is on screen.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- In the empty state, to show two or three tasks based on the selection, instead of a blank "How can I help?".
- After an answer, to offer one or two ways to go deeper and one to widen.
- To prompt checking, such as "Show who viewed these but didn't apply", not only moving on.

## When not to use

- Asking for missing details. Use the Clarifying question card (clarifying-question).
- Reusable workflows. Use the Templates gallery (templates-gallery) or saved tasks via / (message-composer).
- Inside an answer's body. Follow-ups sit after the answer actions, never inside the answer.

## Structure

1. Starters: "Try asking" label, bulb icon, two or three chips, Hide
2. Follow-ups: "Follow-ups" label, rows with a ↳ icon, muted text, full width

## Guidelines

- Starters are based on what is selected ("Why are these 2 doing badly?") or, with nothing selected, on common tasks.
- Show three or fewer. Too many options cause scanning fatigue.
- Anchor follow-ups in the last answer and keep them visually apart from it.
- Selecting a follow-up sends it; selecting a starter that needs editing fills the box instead.
- Starters can be hidden. Do not show them everywhere.
- Starters fill the composer for editing and show an edit icon; slots in them are dashed until filled. Follow-ups send at once.
- A prompt has no state: picking it inserts or sends once, and it doesn't stay selected.
- Follow-ups that narrow an answer offer up to five options, most likely first, each under 72 characters.

## Content

- Write them as the person would ask, specific to the data: "Which of these close this week?"
- Sentence case, no exclamation marks, no trailing arrow.
- Include at least one prompt that helps check the answer, not only extend it.

## Accessibility

- Each follow-up and starter is a button with its full text as the name (SC 4.1.2).
- Group them under a visible label ("Follow-ups", "Try asking") that is programmatically associated (SC 1.3.1).
- Rows are full width and at least 24 by 24 px targets (SC 2.5.8).
- Starters and follow-ups are buttons whose names say what happens: "Insert: Which listings close this week?" or "Ask: Compare with last month".

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the next suggestion |
| Enter / Space | Send the follow-up, or fill the box with the starter |

## Examples

### suggestions

```tsx
import { FollowUps, Starters, toast } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Starters and follow-ups", description: "Starters come from what is selected; follow-ups continue the last answer, muted and apart from it. Three at most.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-6">
			<Starters items={["Why are these 2 doing badly?", "Compare applicants with last quarter", "Draft a shorter description"]} onPick={(q) => toast(q)} onHide={() => {}} />
			<FollowUps items={["Which job boards are they on?", "Show the same for Design", "Extend both by 30 days"]} onPick={(q) => toast(q)} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant side panel
- Message composer
- Templates gallery
- Clarifying question card

# Citations and sources

Record IDs inline in answers that open the record, plus a Sources panel on the full page listing every record and file the answer used.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Every claim about a record or figure in an answer or an AI column cell.
- When an answer relies on a team file, cite the file.

## When not to use

- Generic wording with no factual claim. Do not add filler citations.
- To label content as generated. Use the AI origin label (ai-origin-label).

## Structure

1. Inline citation (record ID, for example LST-1044)
2. Sources panel (record rows, files)
3. Highlight state on the cited source

## Guidelines

- Citations are record IDs that open the record, so checking takes one click.
- In the panel, a citation focuses the row in the table; on the full page it highlights the source in the Sources panel.
- Place citations at the end of the claim they support, consistently.
- Say when a source is missing or stale rather than showing an empty state that implies success.
- Point to the exact data used where possible (views, applies, period).

## Content

- Use the record's own ID format (LST-1044), not numbers like [1], so the citation is meaningful on its own.
- Sources list title, ID and what was read.

## Accessibility

- Citations are links with an accessible name that includes the record, for example "LST-1044, Operations Coordinator" (SC 2.4.6, 4.1.2).
- Do not signal citations by colour alone; use the chip shape (SC 1.4.1).
- Moving focus to the cited row must keep that row visible (SC 2.4.11).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the next citation |
| Enter | Open or highlight the cited record |

## Examples

### cite

```tsx
import { Citation, SourcesList } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Every claim names its record", description: "Citations are record IDs at the end of the claim. Selecting one highlights the source; on a list page it would focus the row.", order: 1 };

const SRC = [{ id: "LST-1041", title: "Frontend Engineer", detail: "6 applicants · closes 21 Nov" }, { id: "LST-1044", title: "Customer Success Lead", detail: "3 applicants · closes 23 Nov" }];

export default function Example() {
	const [a, setA] = useState<string>();
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl grid-cols-[1fr_240px] gap-4 max-md:grid-cols-1">
			<p className="text-base text-ink">Two listings close this week with fewer than 10 applicants: Frontend Engineer <Citation id="LST-1041" active={a === "LST-1041"} onOpen={setA} /> and Customer Success Lead <Citation id="LST-1044" active={a === "LST-1044"} onOpen={setA} />.</p>
			<SourcesList sources={SRC} active={a} onSelect={setA} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant page
- AI column
- Team instructions and files
- AI origin label
- Confidence note

# AI origin label

One small mark and short text on generated content, such as "Assistant · from your workspace data". No sparkle on every button and no separate AI colour.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Under every assistant answer, with the feedback actions.
- On a generated column header, once for the group, not on every cell.
- Where generated and human content sit together, so people can tell them apart.

## When not to use

- On buttons that start an action. Name the action instead ("Draft titles"), and keep the mark for content.
- As decoration or branding across the product.
- To say where a value came from. Use Citations and sources (citations-sources).

## Structure

1. Assistant mark (icon)
2. Text (who and from what)
3. Optional time ("2 min ago")

## Guidelines

- Label the origin, not the feature. Say what produced it and from what.
- One mark per group of generated content: a column header, an answer.
- No separate AI colour. TwoUX uses its neutral palette plus a faint tint on generated columns, always with the mark and text.
- Do not use the sparkle as the universal AI sign; it loses meaning when it is everywhere.
- Generated output must also be machine-detectable as generated, for example a data attribute or metadata on the record.

## Content

- "Assistant · from your workspace data". Never "AI-powered", "smart" or "magic".
- When a person edits generated text, the label goes; the history keeps the original.

## Accessibility

- The mark is decorative (aria-hidden) and the text carries the meaning (SC 1.3.1, 1.4.1).
- The tint on generated columns must keep text contrast; the column header text identifies it (SC 1.4.11 for the mark).
- Use the same wording everywhere (SC 3.2.4).

## Examples

### labels

```tsx
import { AiOrigin } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Say what made it, from what", description: "One small mark and plain words, once per group of generated content. No separate AI colour, no gradients.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid gap-3">
			<AiOrigin from="your workspace data" time="2 min ago" />
			<AiOrigin from="24 listings and the 2026 salary bands" />
			<div className="rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-3"><AiOrigin from="the job description" /><p className="mt-1.5 text-base text-ink">Junior designer with a portfolio of 2 or 3 product case studies; Figma required; hybrid in Leeds.</p></div>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Assistant side panel
- AI column
- Citations and sources
- Confidence note
- Why this choice

# AI column

A generated table column that fills one row at a time, cites each row, shows when it was written and never overwrites real data.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Adding a judgement or summary per row, such as "Likely reason" for a low apply rate.
- When people need to compare many rows on the same question.

## When not to use

- Changing real fields such as title or closing date. Use Suggested changes (suggested-changes).
- One-off questions. Use the Assistant side panel (assistant-panel).
- Decisions about candidates that would filter or rank them for hiring. These are high-risk; keep them as human decisions with the assistant as a reference only.

## Structure

1. Header (assistant mark, name, "2 min ago", Refresh)
2. Cells (value and citation, writing state, failed state with Try again)
3. Add a column menu (suggested columns, Describe your own…)

## Guidelines

- Mark the header once and show when the column was written.
- Never overwrite real data; the column is separate and can be removed.
- Cells fill one by one with a visible state and a Stop. A failed cell says why ("The listing has no description") and offers Try again.
- Each cell cites its record.
- When source data changes, mark the column out of date instead of silently rewriting.
- Show the cost per row before running on the whole table, and test on a few rows first.

## Content

- Name columns by the question they answer ("Likely reason", "Risk of closing empty").
- Cell text is short and leads with the judgement: "Many views, few applies."
- Failed cells explain in plain words and say what to do.

## Accessibility

- Follow the grid pattern: arrow keys move between cells, Enter or F2 to act, Esc to return (APG grid).
- Header is a columnheader; the Refresh button has a name ("Refresh column") (SC 4.1.2).
- Announce progress and completion ("12 of 24 written") as a status message (SC 4.1.3); filling cells is auto-updating content that needs Stop (SC 2.2.2).
- Writing, failed and out-of-date states use text, not colour alone (SC 1.4.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Arrow keys | Move between cells |
| Enter / F2 | Act on the cell, for example Try again |
| Esc | Return to grid navigation |

## Examples

### summaries

```tsx
import { AiCell, type AiCellState, AiColumnHeader, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "A generated column", description: "Marked once in the header with when it was written. Cells fill one at a time, each cites its record, and a failed cell says why with Try again. Real data is never overwritten.", order: 1 };

const ROWS = [["LST-1040", "Junior Product Designer", "Portfolio, Figma, hybrid in Leeds"], ["LST-1041", "Frontend Engineer", "React and TypeScript, 3+ years"], ["LST-1043", "Recruitment Coordinator", ""], ["LST-1045", "QA Engineer", "Playwright, CI, test plans"]];

export default function Example() {
	const [n, setN] = useState(0);
	useEffect(() => { if (n < ROWS.length) { const t = setTimeout(() => setN((x) => x + 1), 600); return () => clearTimeout(t); } }, [n]);
	const cell = (i: number): AiCellState => (i > n ? { state: "queued" } : i === n ? { state: "writing" } : ROWS[i][2] ? { state: "done", value: ROWS[i][2], source: ROWS[i][0] } : { state: "failed", reason: "The listing has no description" });
	return (
		<div className="w-full overflow-hidden rounded-sm border border-line">
			<Table aria-label="Listings with requirements summary">
				<TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Listing</TableHead><TableHead className="bg-primary-soft/40"><AiColumnHeader name="Key requirements" written={n >= ROWS.length ? "just now" : "writing"} onRefresh={() => setN(0)} /></TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
				<TableBody>{ROWS.map((r, i) => <TableRow key={r[0]}><TableCell className="font-medium text-ink">{r[1]}</TableCell><TableCell className="max-w-72 bg-primary-soft/20"><AiCell cell={cell(i)} onRetry={() => setN(i)} /></TableCell></TableRow>)}</TableBody>
			</Table>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Prompt editor with fields
- Citations and sources
- AI origin label

# Task builder

Repeated tasks written as a sentence with editable slots that reuse filter values, with Run blocked until every required slot is filled.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Tasks people run often with the same shape, such as "Find Live listings under 3% and draft new titles for hiring managers".
- When the inputs map to filters already in TwoUX, so slots reuse those values.
- When an answer should be saved and rerun on a schedule.

## When not to use

- A one-off question. Use the Message composer (message-composer).
- A prompt that runs per row with typed outputs. Use the Prompt editor (prompt-editor).
- Browsing ready-made tasks. Use the Templates gallery (templates-gallery).

## Structure

1. Sentence with slots (dashed when empty, filled when set)
2. Actions (Schedule, Save as task, Run ⌘↵)
3. Inline error naming the empty slot

## Guidelines

- Make the critical slots prominent and say which can be left empty.
- An empty slot is dashed and blocks Run; the message says which slot.
- Filled slots show as regular text; empty ones as placeholders.
- Do not overload the sentence with slots.
- Scheduled runs notify before they act and land in the Inbox when they need approval.
- An empty slot shows its field name in italics in a dashed box; once filled it shows the value as normal text.
- The popover field label matches the slot name exactly, so people know which slot they are editing.
- Slots hold one value each. Status belongs in a badge and several related values in a key-value list, not in slots.

## Content

- Write the sentence as an instruction in plain words; slot placeholders match the filter field names.
- Error: "Choose who gets the titles before you run this."

## Accessibility

- Each slot is a button whose name includes the slot and value ("Status: Live") (SC 4.1.2).
- Slots open a menu or listbox following the menu button pattern.
- The disabled Run has its reason in text next to it (SC 3.3.1, 3.3.2).
- Dashed versus solid is not the only cue; empty slots show placeholder text (SC 1.4.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move between slots |
| Enter / Space | Open a slot's options |
| ⌘↵ / Ctrl+Enter | Run when all required slots are filled |

## Examples

### weekly

```tsx
import { TaskBuilder, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "A task written as a sentence", description: "Slots are dashed until set. Run (⌘↵) is blocked while a required slot is empty, and the message names it.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [v, setV] = useState<Record<string, string>>({ when: "Every Monday" });
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-xl">
			<TaskBuilder
				value={v}
				onChange={setV}
				onRun={() => toast.success("Task started")}
				onSave={() => toast("Saved as a task")}
				onSchedule={() => toast("Scheduled")}
				parts={[{ id: "when", placeholder: "When", options: ["Every Monday", "Every day at 9:00", "Once"], required: true }, ", summarise", { id: "which", placeholder: "which listings", options: ["listings closing this week", "listings with no applicants", "all open listings"], required: true }, "and send it to", { id: "who", placeholder: "who", options: ["me", "the hiring managers", "#hiring on Slack"], required: true }, "."]}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Templates gallery
- Prompt editor with fields
- Agent run timeline

# Agent permissions

Per-action access set in plain words with three levels, Off, Ask first and Allow, grouped into Read and Change.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Setting what an agent may read and change before it runs.
- Adjusting automation per action as trust grows.

## When not to use

- Approving one specific change. Use Suggested changes (suggested-changes).
- Connecting an outside account. Use Connected tools (connected-tools).

## Structure

1. Group header (Read, Change) with summary level
2. Permission rows (action, what it covers, Off / Ask first / Allow segmented control)

## Guidelines

- Three levels per action: Off, Ask first, Allow.
- Defaults: reading Allow, changes Ask first, anything that reaches people outside the workspace Off.
- Group by Read and Change and describe each in plain words ("Sends from your address").
- Ask first is just-in-time consent: the agent pauses with a proposal. Set up front only the default, not a one-off decision.
- Remind people of the setting when it blocks a step ("Email is Off in permissions") with a link to change it.
- Candidate data is personal data; keep it Ask first so a person reviews each use.
- Per-run choices ("Allow once", "Allow in this conversation") never change the saved level; only "Always allow" does, and it shows here as Allow with who set it and when.
- Allow is never preselected or focused when a level is offered for a risky action.

## Content

- Name actions, not systems: "Edit, extend or close listings", "Email candidates".
- Detail line says what it covers or what happens ("Shows a proposal before each change").

## Accessibility

- Each segmented control is a group labelled by its row, with toggle buttons using aria-pressed (APG button).
- Alternatively use a radiogroup with arrow keys; pick one and use it consistently (SC 3.2.4).
- Changing a level must not change context (SC 3.2.2).
- The selected state is shown with more than colour (SC 1.4.1, 1.4.11).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move between permission rows |
| Enter / Space | Set the focused level |

## Examples

### levels

```tsx
import { AgentPermissions, type Permission } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Off, Ask first or Allow", description: "Reading defaults to Allow, changes to Ask first, anything that reaches people outside the workspace to Off. Decisions about candidates can never be set to Allow.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [items, setItems] = useState<Permission[]>([
		{ id: "r1", group: "Read", action: "Read listings and applicants", covers: "Titles, descriptions, stages and counts", level: "allow" },
		{ id: "r2", group: "Read", action: "Read team files", covers: "Salary bands and the hiring handbook", level: "allow" },
		{ id: "c1", group: "Change", action: "Edit listings", covers: "Titles, descriptions, closing dates", level: "ask" },
		{ id: "c2", group: "Change", action: "Move candidates between stages", covers: "Screen, interview, offer, reject", level: "ask", neverAllow: true },
		{ id: "c3", group: "Change", action: "Email candidates", covers: "Sends from your address", level: "off" },
	]);
	return <div className="w-full max-w-2xl"><AgentPermissions items={items} onChange={(id, level) => setItems((x) => x.map((p) => (p.id === id ? { ...p, level } : p)))} /></div>;
}
```

- Agent run timeline
- Suggested changes
- Connected tools
- Segmented control
- Plan preview
- Change review
- Connector picker

# Agent run timeline

The steps of an agent run with state in shape and colour, the filter each step used, a highlighted waiting step and Stop always visible.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Watching or reviewing an agent run, scheduled or started from a task.
- When a run is waiting for approval, to show what it needs.

## When not to use

- A single answer. Use Thinking and steps (thinking-steps).
- Applying a proposal you just approved. Use the Step card (step-card).
- Listing everything that needs you across runs. Use the Inbox (inbox).

## Structure

1. Header (task name, status badge, Stop)
2. Step rows (state icon, title, detail, action)
3. Footer (started by, when, schedule)

## Guidelines

- Every step has a state: done, running, waiting for you, skipped, failed.
- Steps that pick rows show the filter used and open it as a view.
- A waiting step is highlighted and holds its action (Review).
- Stop is always visible and in the same place.
- Skipped steps say why and link to the setting.
- Record who started it, when and on what schedule, and keep the log.
- In parallel steps, a failed step shows its own error and Retry on its row while the rest keep running; the run isn't shown as blocked.
- Failed and stopped steps are never counted as done; the counts add up to the steps shown.

## Content

- Step titles say what happened in past tense with counts ("Found 2 live listings under 3%").
- Badge text is a state, not a mood: "Needs you", "Done", "Failed".

## Accessibility

- States combine an icon shape, colour and text (SC 1.4.1, 1.4.11).
- Use a list with each step as a list item so the order is exposed (SC 1.3.1).
- Announce new steps and a change to "Needs you" as status messages (SC 4.1.3).
- Running runs are auto-updating content in parallel with the page; Stop meets SC 2.2.2.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through step actions |
| Enter | Open the step's view or Review |
| Enter on Stop | Stop the run |

## Examples

### run

```tsx
import { AgentRun, Button } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "One run, step by step", description: "Every step has a state in shape and words. A step that picked rows names its filter; the waiting step is highlighted and holds its action.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-xl">
			<AgentRun
				task="Weekly listing check"
				status="Needs you"
				meta="Started by Priya Shah · Monday 09:00 · Every Monday"
				steps={[
					{ title: "Found listings closing within 7 days", detail: "Filter: Closes is in the next 7 days · 3 listings", state: "done", action: <Button variant="ghost" size="xs">Open as view</Button> },
					{ title: "Compared applicants with similar listings", state: "done" },
					{ title: "Proposed extending 2 listings by 30 days", detail: "Waiting for your review", state: "waiting", action: <Button size="xs">Review</Button> },
					{ title: "Post a summary to #hiring", state: "skipped", detail: "Skipped until the review is done" },
				]}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Agent permissions
- Task builder
- Step card
- Inbox (triage)
- Plan preview
- Change review

# Connected tools

Outside tools listed in the + menu and settings, each with a detail card saying what it can read and change, where data is stored and who connected it.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Connecting a tool at the moment it is needed, from the + menu.
- Reviewing what a connected tool can access.

## When not to use

- Setting what the agent may do with TwoUX data. Use Agent permissions (agent-permissions).
- Adding a single file. Use Attach a file in the Message composer (message-composer).

## Structure

1. Tools menu (tool, status, Connect, Browse tools)
2. Detail card (name, type, status badge, description, Can read, Can change, Data stored, Connected by, Privacy policy, Disconnect, Permissions)

## Guidelines

- Before and after connecting, say in plain words what it can read and change, where data is stored and who connected it.
- Let people scope a tool to what it needs.
- Give each tool a consistent icon and name across menus and answers.
- When a tool fails or is partly loaded, say so inline and offer reconnect or retry; avoid blank states that imply success.
- Show when data was last synced.

## Content

- "Brings candidates and pipeline stages into TwoUX so the assistant can compare them with your listings."
- Use "Nothing" rather than leaving Can change empty.

## Accessibility

- The tools list is a menu; each tool is a menuitemcheckbox when it toggles use, or a menuitem when it connects (APG menu).
- The detail card uses a description list for its fields (SC 1.3.1).
- Disconnect is a destructive action; confirm with the consequence and keep focus order (SC 2.4.3, 3.3.4).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Right arrow | Open the tools submenu from the + menu |
| Space | Turn a connected tool on or off for this conversation |
| Enter | Connect or open the tool |
| Esc | Close the menu |

## Examples

### tool

```tsx
import { ConnectedToolCard, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Say what a tool can do", description: "Before and after connecting: what it can read, what it can change, where data is stored and who connected it.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [on, setOn] = useState(true);
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-md">
			<ConnectedToolCard
				tool={{ id: "cal", name: "Google Calendar", kind: "Calendar", connected: on, canRead: "Free and busy times of interviewers", canChange: "Nothing. It suggests interview slots only.", stored: "Not stored; read when you ask", connectedBy: on ? "Priya Shah on 3 Nov" : undefined, privacyHref: "#privacy" }}
				onConnect={() => { setOn(true); toast.success("Connected Google Calendar"); }}
				onDisconnect={() => { setOn(false); toast.success("Disconnected Google Calendar", { action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => setOn(true) } }); }}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

# Team instructions and files

Shared instructions and files set once for the workspace, visible and editable, and named in the assistant's empty state and citations when used.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Rules the assistant should always follow for the team, such as UK English or never contacting candidates without asking.
- Reference files such as salary bands or hiring policy that answers should cite.

## When not to use

- Personal preferences for one person. Use writing style in the Message composer (message-composer).
- Rules that grant or block actions. Use Agent permissions (agent-permissions).

## Structure

1. Instructions card (text, Edit, set by and scope)
2. Files card (file list, Add a file)
3. Privacy note

## Guidelines

- Shared context is visible and editable, not hidden in a system prompt.
- Show who set it and that it applies to everyone in the workspace.
- The empty state says it is in use ("Using team instructions and 3 files").
- Answers cite the file when they rely on it.
- Keep conversations private unless shared.

## Content

- Instructions are short imperatives in plain English.
- Scope line: "Set by Rahul S. · applies to everyone in TwoUX".

## Accessibility

- Edit and Add a file are icon buttons with names (SC 4.1.2).
- Card headings label each section (SC 2.4.6, 1.3.1).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to Edit or Add a file |
| Enter | Edit instructions or add a file |

## Examples

### instructions

```tsx
import { TeamInstructions, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Shared context, visible", description: "Instructions and files the assistant reads for everyone, shown with who set them. Edit in place.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [text, setText] = useState("Write in UK English. Always state the salary range. Never comment on age, nationality or gaps in employment.");
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<TeamInstructions text={text} setBy="Priya Shah" files={[{ name: "Salary bands 2026.pdf", size: "220 KB" }, { name: "Hiring handbook.docx", size: "1.4 MB" }]} onSave={(t) => { setText(t); toast.success("Instructions saved"); }} onAddFile={() => toast("Choose a file")} />
		</div>
	);
}
```

# Previous conversations

A searchable list opened from the clock in the panel bar: scheduled tasks first, then recent conversations, with a dot for a new answer and "Needs you" for one waiting.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Returning to an earlier answer or a run waiting for you.
- Finding conversations by their title, named from the first question.

## When not to use

- Handling everything that needs you across the product. Use the Inbox (inbox).
- Auditing agent actions. Use the Agent run timeline (agent-run) log.

## Structure

1. Search field
2. Scheduled tasks
3. Recent conversations (title, status dot or Needs you badge, date)

## Guidelines

- Name conversations from the first question so they are findable.
- Mark a new answer with a dot and a waiting run with "Needs you".
- Selecting a past conversation lets people continue it or start from it.
- Offer deletion and keep history private by default.
- Title each conversation from its first question or a short summary, never "New conversation".
- Group by Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, then month; show local time with the full date and time on hover.
- Delete has Undo. Conversations are never removed automatically without notice; the retention period is stated at the top of the list.
- History is the person's record of conversations; what the assistant keeps between conversations lives in Team instructions, where it can be seen and edited.

## Content

- Dates are short and relative where recent ("Yesterday", "Mon", "2 Nov").

## Accessibility

- The search field filters the list; announce the result count (SC 4.1.3).
- The new-answer dot has a text equivalent ("New answer") (SC 1.4.1, 1.3.1).
- Esc closes the history and returns focus to the clock button (SC 2.4.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Esc | Close the list |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move through conversations |
| Enter | Open a conversation |

## Examples

### history

```tsx
import { ConversationHistory, toast } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Find past conversations", description: "Named from the first question, scheduled tasks first, a dot for a new answer and Needs you for a waiting run.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-md rounded-sm border border-line bg-surface p-3">
			<ConversationHistory
				scheduled={[{ id: "s1", title: "Weekly listing check", date: "Mon", status: "needs-you" }]}
				recent={[{ id: "r1", title: "Why are these closing with few applicants?", date: "Today", status: "new" }, { id: "r2", title: "Compare Design applicants with last quarter", date: "Tue" }, { id: "r3", title: "Draft a shorter description for LST-1044", date: "3 Nov" }]}
				onOpen={(id) => toast(`Opened ${id}`)}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

# Templates gallery

A dialog with categories on the left, search on top and cards that say what each template does and which tools it uses; picking one opens it as a draft task.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Starting a new task from a proven pattern, such as sourcing or reporting.
- Showing what agents can do to people who have not used them.

## When not to use

- Running a saved task you already use. Use / in the Message composer (message-composer).
- Quick prompts in the empty state. Use starters (follow-ups-starters).

## Structure

1. Category nav with search
2. Heading and Close
3. Template cards (name, what it does, tools used)

## Guidelines

- Picking a template opens it as a draft task, never runs it.
- Cards say what the template does and which tools it uses.
- Search and categories make browsing easy.
- Expose the inputs the template needs before running.
- Curate and retire templates so the gallery stays current.

## Content

- Names are tasks ("Find hiring managers for open roles").
- Descriptions say the outcome in one line.

## Accessibility

- The gallery is a dialog labelled "Start from a template"; focus moves in on open, Esc closes and focus returns (APG dialog).
- The category nav marks the current item with aria-current (SC 4.1.2, 1.3.1).
- Search announces the number of matching templates (SC 4.1.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move between search, categories and cards |
| Enter | Open the template as a draft |
| Esc | Close the gallery |

## Examples

### gallery

```tsx
import { Button, TemplatesGallery, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Start from a template", description: "Categories, search and cards that say what each template does and which tools it uses. Picking one opens a draft task; it never runs.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
	return (
		<>
			<Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Browse templates</Button>
			<TemplatesGallery
				open={open}
				onOpenChange={setOpen}
				onPick={(t) => { setOpen(false); toast(`Opened “${t.name}” as a draft`); }}
				templates={[
					{ id: "1", name: "Weekly pipeline summary", does: "Summarises new applicants and stage changes every Monday.", tools: ["Listings", "Slack"], category: "Reporting" },
					{ id: "2", name: "Listings at risk", does: "Finds listings closing soon with few applicants and proposes extensions.", tools: ["Listings"], category: "Listings" },
					{ id: "3", name: "Interview slots", does: "Suggests interview times from interviewers' calendars.", tools: ["Calendar"], category: "Interviews" },
					{ id: "4", name: "Job description review", does: "Checks a draft for salary, inclusive language and length.", tools: ["Listings", "Team files"], category: "Listings" },
				]}
			/>
		</>
	);
}
```

# Prompt editor with fields

An editor where row fields and team files are removable chips, inputs and outputs are listed with types, and the prompt is tested on a few rows before running on the whole table.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Defining the prompt behind an AI column or a per-row agent.
- When the output must have a type (text, person, link) to land in the table.

## When not to use

- Asking a question once. Use the Message composer (message-composer).
- Repeated tasks with filter inputs. Use the Task builder (task-builder).

## Structure

1. Hint line ({{ for a field, @ for a team file, ⌘K to rewrite)
2. Prompt text with field chips
3. Inputs list with types
4. Output (one field or several) with types
5. Suggest outputs from prompt
6. Test on 3 rows

## Guidelines

- Fields are chips you can remove, not hidden syntax.
- List inputs and outputs with their type.
- Test on a few rows before running on the whole table; show the per-row cost.
- Let the prompt return "Not found" when it is unsure, rather than forcing an answer.
- ⌘K rewrites selected text as a suggestion, not an overwrite.

## Content

- Use plain headings in the prompt ("Your task", "Rules").
- Field names match the column names people see.

## Accessibility

- Each chip's remove button is named ("Remove field listing.title") (SC 4.1.2).
- {{ and @ open a combobox list of fields or files, with arrow keys and Enter (APG combobox).
- Output type is a radiogroup with a label (APG radio).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| {{ | Add a field from the row |
| @ | Add a team file |
| ⌘K / Ctrl+K | Rewrite the selected text |
| Enter | Insert the highlighted field |
| Esc | Close the field list |

## Examples

### editor

```tsx
import { PromptEditor } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Prompt with fields as chips", description: "Fields from the row are removable chips, not hidden syntax. Inputs and outputs are listed with their type, and Test on 3 rows comes before running on the whole table.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [segs, setSegs] = useState<(string | { field: string })[]>(["List the 3 key requirements in ", { field: "description" }, " for the role ", { field: "role" }, ", in under 12 words."]);
	const [testing, setTesting] = useState(false);
	const [results, setResults] = useState<{ row: string; value: string }[]>();
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-xl">
			<PromptEditor
				segments={segs}
				onRemoveField={(i) => setSegs((s) => s.filter((_, j) => j !== i))}
				inputs={[{ name: "description", type: "Long text" }, { name: "role", type: "Text" }]}
				outputs={[{ name: "key_requirements", type: "Text" }]}
				testing={testing}
				results={results}
				onTest={() => { setTesting(true); setTimeout(() => { setTesting(false); setResults([{ row: "LST-1040", value: "Portfolio, Figma, hybrid in Leeds" }, { row: "LST-1041", value: "React, TypeScript, 3+ years" }, { row: "LST-1045", value: "Playwright, CI, test plans" }]); }, 800); }}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

- AI column
- Task builder
- Templates gallery
- Change review

# Answer actions

The row under every answer: origin label on the left, then Copy, Helpful, Not helpful, Regenerate and a More menu. Always visible, never only on hover.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Under every answer the assistant gives in the side panel or on the assistant page.
- Under a stacked group of answer parts once, after the last part, not after each one.
- Under an answer that was stopped, so Regenerate and feedback are still reachable.

## When not to use

- For actions on a generated file, such as Download. Those belong in the file's own card.
- For feedback about the page or product. Use the product feedback route, not answer feedback.
- Under approval results, notices or the clarifying question card.

## Structure

1. Origin label: "Assistant · from your workspace data" (see AI origin label)
2. Copy: copies the answer as plain text with record IDs
3. Helpful and Not helpful: feedback toggles with submitting and sent states
4. Regenerate: latest answer only
5. More (⋯): Save as task, Open as page, Copy link
6. Not helpful form (optional): a short dismissible form under the answer

## Guidelines

- Show at most four icon buttons; anything else goes in More.
- Keep the row visible at all times. Hover-only actions are invisible to keyboard and touch users.
- Feedback has three states: default, sending (spinner in the pressed button) and sent. Once sent, the chosen button stays pressed and the other is disabled with a reason.
- Not helpful opens an optional form under the answer: reasons as checkboxes (Wrong figures, Missed records, Too long, Other) and a note. It can be closed without sending.
- Same order everywhere: label, Copy, Helpful, Not helpful, Regenerate, More.

## Content

- Tooltips: "Copy", "Helpful", "Not helpful", "Regenerate answer", "More actions".
- After feedback: "Feedback sent". Disabled reason on the other button: "You marked this as helpful".
- Copy confirmation is a short tooltip, "Copied", not a toast.

## Accessibility

- Feedback buttons are toggle buttons with aria-pressed, named "Helpful" and "Not helpful".
- "Feedback sent" and "Copied" are announced as status messages without moving focus.
- Disabled buttons stay focusable so their reason can be read.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through the actions after reading the answer |
| Enter / Space | Press the focused action |
| Esc | Close the More menu or the Not helpful form |

## Examples

### actions

```tsx
import { AnswerActions, AssistantMessage, DropdownMenuItem } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Under every answer", description: "Copy, Helpful, Not helpful and Regenerate (latest answer only), with the rest under More. Always visible, not on hover. Feedback shows sending, then stays pressed.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<AssistantMessage from="24 listings" actions={<AnswerActions text="2 listings close this week with fewer than 10 applicants." onRegenerate={() => {}} onFeedback={() => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))} more={<><DropdownMenuItem>Save as task</DropdownMenuItem><DropdownMenuItem>Open as page</DropdownMenuItem><DropdownMenuItem>Copy link</DropdownMenuItem></>} />}>
				<p><strong>2 listings</strong> close this week with fewer than 10 applicants.</p>
			</AssistantMessage>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Regenerating an answer
- Labelling AI output
- AI origin label
- Assistant side panel

# Generated file card

A compact card under an answer for one thing the assistant made: name, type and size, origin label, and up to two actions with the rest in a More menu.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- For each draft or file the assistant produced in an answer.
- In agent run results when a step produced a file.
- For a short command or snippet a person will copy into another tool.

## When not to use

- For records that already exist. Cite them by ID instead.
- For files people attached. Those are context chips in the composer.
- For a figure or short table that answers the question. Keep it in the answer text.

## Structure

1. Icon for the type (document, table, chart, code)
2. Title: file name or what it is
3. Metadata: type, size in KB or MB, rows or words
4. Origin label with sources on hover
5. Actions: up to two buttons (Open, Download, Copy, Suggest for record) and More (⋯)
6. Inline preview (optional): first lines of a snippet, or the chart image

## Guidelines

- One card per output, stacked under the answer in the order they were made.
- Code and commands preview in the Code block style with Copy; long previews cut at about eight lines with Open for the rest.
- While a file is being made, the card shows a skeleton line and "Writing job description"; text around it may stream, the card does not.
- If making the file failed, the card says why and offers Try again; other cards in the answer stay.

## Content

- Sizes in KB, MB or GB with one decimal at most: "1.2 MB".
- Loading text names the thing: "Writing job description", "Loading 38 listings".
- Title is the file name or a plain description, never "Artifact" or "Output 1".

## Accessibility

- The card is a group with an accessible name from its title.
- Action names include the file: "Open job description".
- The More menu follows the menu button pattern.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Reach the card's actions in order |
| Enter | Run the focused action |
| ↓ / ↑ | Move through the More menu |
| Esc | Close the More menu |

## Examples

### draft

```tsx
import { ArtifactCard, Button, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "A draft the assistant made", description: "One card per output, with type and size, the origin label and two actions. While it is being written, the card says so; the draft reaches the record only through Suggest for record.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [writing, setWriting] = useState(true);
	useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => setWriting(false), 1400); return () => clearTimeout(t); }, []);
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-lg">
			<ArtifactCard
				title="Job description"
				meta="Document · 312 words"
				from="LST-1044 and the hiring handbook"
				writing={writing}
				actions={<><Button variant="outline" size="xs" onClick={() => toast("Proposed for LST-1044")}>Suggest for record</Button><Button variant="ghost" size="xs">Open</Button></>}
				preview={<p>Customer Success Lead, Bristol (hybrid). £45,000 to £52,000. You'll look after 40 hiring teams, help them get value from TwoUX in their first 90 days…</p>}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Generated drafts and files
- Code block
- AI origin label
- Answer actions

# Plan preview

The plan an agent shows before a multi-step or costly run: numbered steps people can remove, risky steps marked in words, and nothing running until it is approved.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- Before any run with several steps, or one that costs time or money, so people can see it first.
- When a step reaches people outside the workspace (an email, a message to a candidate) or cannot be undone (a close, a delete).
- When the agent was started by a schedule or a request people did not write step by step.

## When not to use

- A single, small change. Use Suggested changes (suggested-changes), which is the review step for one proposal.
- Questions whose answer would change the plan. Ask first with a Clarifying question (clarifying-question); show the plan once the answer is known.
- Work that has already started. Show progress in the Agent run (agent-run) and use PlanChange only if the plan itself changes.

## Structure

1. Header (plan title, origin label with what it is based on)
2. Step rows (number, step, optional detail, risk line, Remove or Put back)
3. Footer (count "3 of 4 steps", note "nothing runs until you approve", Cancel, Approve plan)
4. Plan change line (PlanChange) in the run if the plan changes later

## Guidelines

- Show the plan before any multi-step or costly run. Nothing runs until the person approves, and never on a timeout.
- Each step is a plain action with its detail underneath. People can remove a step, and put it back, before approving.
- Mark steps that reach people outside the workspace or cannot be undone, with an icon and words, not colour alone.
- The footer counts what will run ("3 of 4 steps") and updates as steps are removed. Approve is disabled when no steps are left.
- When any step is high-stakes, Approve and Cancel carry equal weight. This is the one exception to one primary action: both are outline buttons, so neither is nudged.
- If the plan changes mid-run, add a PlanChange line saying what changed and why. Never reroute silently.
- Ask clarifying questions first only if the answer changes the plan. Otherwise show the plan and let people adjust it.

## Content

- Title the plan by its outcome ("Close three expired listings and tell applicants"), not by the agent's method.
- Write steps as actions in the order they happen. Put the consequence in the detail line: "Sends an email to 14 applicants".
- Name the risk in words: "Reaches people outside the workspace" or "Can't be undone". Do not soften it.
- PlanChange reads as what changed, then why: "Plan changed: skipped the email step. The listing has no applicants."

## Accessibility

- The plan is an ordered list, so the number of steps and each position are announced (SC 1.3.1).
- Risk is shown by an icon and a line of text, not colour alone (SC 1.4.1).
- Remove and Put back are real buttons with the step number in their hidden label, and a removed step carries the hidden word "removed" (SC 4.1.2).
- Nothing starts on a timer, so there is no time limit to adjust (SC 2.2.1). Approving is the review step for work that records data (SC 3.3.4).
- PlanChange is a role="status" line, so a plan change is announced without moving focus (SC 4.1.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through Remove buttons, then Cancel and Approve plan |
| Enter / Space | Remove or put back the focused step, or press the focused button |

## Examples

### low-stakes

```tsx
import { PlanCard, PlanChange, toast } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "A plan, then a change to it", description: "With no risky step, Approve is the one primary action. If the plan changes during the run, a PlanChange line says what and why.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-3">
			<PlanCard
				title="Tidy the Operations Coordinator listing"
				from="Your request, listing LST-1041"
				steps={[
					{ id: "1", title: "Rename the listing", detail: "Operations Coordinator (hybrid)" },
					{ id: "2", title: "Add the salary range", detail: "£32,000 to £36,000" },
					{ id: "3", title: "Extend the closing date by 30 days", detail: "21 Nov to 21 Dec" },
				]}
				onApprove={(kept) => toast.success(`Approved ${kept.length} steps`)}
				onCancel={() => toast("Plan cancelled. Nothing ran.")}
			/>
			<PlanChange what="Skipped the salary step" why="The listing already shows a range." />
		</div>
	);
}
```

### plan

```tsx
import { PlanCard, toast } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "A plan with a risky step", description: "Steps can be removed. The step that emails applicants is marked, so Approve and Cancel carry equal weight. Nothing runs until you approve.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-xl">
			<PlanCard
				title="Close three expired listings and tell applicants"
				from="Weekly listing check, 3 listings past their closing date"
				steps={[
					{ id: "1", title: "Find listings past their closing date", detail: "Filter: Closes is before today · 3 listings" },
					{ id: "2", title: "Close the 3 listings", detail: "Hides them from the careers page", risk: "irreversible" },
					{ id: "3", title: "Email 14 applicants that the role has closed", detail: "Uses the template Role closed", risk: "external" },
					{ id: "4", title: "Post a summary to #hiring" },
				]}
				onApprove={(kept) => toast.success(`Approved ${kept.length} steps`)}
				onCancel={() => toast("Plan cancelled. Nothing ran.")}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

- Agent permissions
- Suggested changes
- Step card

# Change review

The review queue for changes an agent proposes to records, procedures, prompts, tools or another agent: the reason, the diff, and test results, approved or rejected by a person.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When an agent proposes to change how something works: a procedure, a prompt, a tool, a rule, or another agent's instructions.
- When a change can be tested against a set of known cases (a regression set) before it goes live.
- When many agent changes arrive together and a person has to work through them in order.

## When not to use

- Changes to a few records a person asked for. Use Suggested changes (suggested-changes).
- Plans for work that has not started. Use the Plan preview (plan-card).
- Actions set to Allow in Agent permissions (agent-permissions). Those run and appear in the Activity log with Undo.

## Structure

1. Header (title, status badge, origin label, reason in plain words)
2. Diff view (files changed, +/− counts, unified diff)
3. Simulation results ("228 of 240 pass", failures first, newly failing called out)
4. Footer (note, Reject, Approve change) or the Reject reason field
5. Resolved line (who decided and when)

## Guidelines

- Nothing goes live until a person approves. Say so in the footer.
- State the reason in plain words and what the proposal is based on (the origin label), for example "14 conversations this week".
- Show the diff and the simulation results in the same card, so the person can decide without opening anything else.
- Run the change against a regression set. Failures come first, and a case that passed before and fails now is called out in words ("Newly failing"), with a count in the footer.
- Rejecting needs a reason the agent can learn from. If the box is empty, say why it is needed, next to the field.
- Every decision leaves a resolved line with who decided and when. Changes are logged and attributable to the agent that proposed them and the person who approved.
- A change one agent proposes to another agent's procedures is reviewed in the same way, with the proposing agent named as the origin.
- Group many changes by batch, each batch with a stated rationale. Stage risky ones with a traffic split or a gradual ramp, not all at once.

## Content

- Title the change by what it does: "Reply in the applicant's language", not "Update prompt v14".
- Write the reason as cause and effect: "Applicants wrote in Welsh in 6 of 14 conversations and the assistant replied in English."
- Name failures in words: "2 conversations that passed before now fail." Do not rely on a coloured count.
- Resolved line: "Approved by Imogen Hart · 10:42" or "Rejected by Imogen Hart · 10:42", with the reason kept in the log.

## Accessibility

- Each card is an article labelled with the change title, so people can move through a queue of changes by heading (SC 1.3.1).
- Added and removed lines carry a + or − marker and a hidden word ("Added", "Removed"), not colour alone (SC 1.4.1).
- File rows are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded (SC 4.1.2).
- The Reject reason field has a visible label, and a missing reason is an error shown beside it as text (SC 3.3.1, 3.3.2).
- Approving puts a change live, so the review step, the simulation results and the logged decision satisfy error prevention (SC 3.3.4). The resolved line is a role="status" message (SC 4.1.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move through file rows, then Reject and Approve change |
| Enter / Space | Open or close a file's diff, or press the focused button |
| Enter (in Reject) | New line in the reason field; Tab to Reject change to send it |

## Examples

### agent-to-agent

```tsx
import { ChangeRequest, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "One agent changes another's procedure", description: "A reviewing agent proposes an edit to the Listing checker's steps. It is reviewed like any change, with the proposing agent named and a staged ramp.", order: 2 };

export default function Example() {
	const [state, setState] = useState<"open" | "approved" | "rejected">("open");
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-2xl">
			<ChangeRequest
				title="Listing checker: ask before closing a listing with applicants"
				from="9 listings closed with active applicants last month, found by the Quality reviewer agent"
				reason="The Listing checker closed 3 listings that still had active applicants. This adds a step to ask for approval first. It would start with 10% of runs, then ramp up over a week."
				files={[
					{
						path: "agents/listing-checker/steps.md",
						lines: [
							{ type: "ctx", text: "1. Find listings past their closing date." },
							{ type: "add", text: "2. If a listing has active applicants, ask for approval." },
							{ type: "del", text: "2. Close the listing." },
							{ type: "add", text: "3. Close the listing." },
						],
					},
				]}
				simulation={{
					suite: "Regression set, 60 listings",
					cases: [
						{ name: "Listing with 12 active applicants", status: "fixed" },
						{ name: "Listing with no applicants", status: "pass" },
						{ name: "Listing closed by a person yesterday", status: "pass" },
					],
				}}
				state={state}
				decidedBy={state === "approved" ? "Approved by Imogen Hart · 14:05 · ramping from 10%" : "Rejected by Imogen Hart · 14:05"}
				onApprove={() => { setState("approved"); toast.success("Approved. Starting with 10% of runs."); }}
				onReject={(why) => { setState("rejected"); toast("Rejected", { description: why }); }}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

### review

```tsx
import { ChangeRequest, toast } from "@twoux/ui";
import { useState } from "react";

export const meta = { title: "Review a change to a prompt", description: "The reason, the diff and the test results in one card. Two cases that passed before now fail, so the footer says so. Reject asks for a reason.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	const [state, setState] = useState<"open" | "approved" | "rejected">("open");
	const [by, setBy] = useState<string>();
	return (
		<div className="w-full max-w-2xl">
			<ChangeRequest
				title="Reply in the applicant's language"
				from="14 conversations this week"
				reason="Applicants wrote in Welsh in 6 of 14 conversations and the assistant replied in English. This adds a line telling it to reply in the language the applicant used."
				files={[
					{
						path: "prompts/applicant-reply.md",
						lines: [
							{ type: "ctx", text: "You answer applicants for Harbour Recruitment." },
							{ type: "del", text: "Always reply in English." },
							{ type: "add", text: "Reply in the language the applicant wrote in." },
							{ type: "add", text: "If you are unsure of the language, reply in English." },
							{ type: "ctx", text: "Never promise an interview date." },
						],
					},
					{ path: "prompts/shortlist-summary.md", lines: [{ type: "add", text: "Summaries stay in English for the hiring team." }] },
				]}
				simulation={{
					suite: "Golden set, 240 conversations",
					cases: [
						{ name: "Applicant asks about the closing date, in Welsh", status: "fixed" },
						{ name: "Applicant asks about visa support, in Polish", status: "fixed" },
						{ name: "Applicant mixes English and Welsh", status: "new-fail", detail: "Replied in Welsh only. Passed before this change." },
						{ name: "Applicant writes only 'hi'", status: "new-fail", detail: "Replied in Welsh. Passed before this change." },
						{ name: "Applicant asks for a call back", status: "fail", detail: "Still promises a date." },
						{ name: "Applicant withdraws", status: "pass" },
						{ name: "Applicant asks about pay", status: "pass" },
					]}}
				state={state}
				decidedBy={by}
				onApprove={() => { setState("approved"); setBy("Approved by Imogen Hart · 10:42"); toast.success("Approved. The change is live."); }}
				onReject={(why) => { setState("rejected"); setBy("Rejected by Imogen Hart · 10:42"); toast("Rejected", { description: why }); }}
			/>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Suggested changes
- Agent permissions
- Agent run timeline
- Confidence note
- Plan preview
- Prompt editor with fields

# Confidence note

A short note beside agent output that says, in words, what the agent is unsure about, why, and the safer option or the way to check.

Kind: component · Group: AI and agents · Status: built, import from @twoux/ui

## When to use

- When the output affects other people, shared records or money and the agent has a real reason to be unsure.
- When the cause is specific: missing data, out-of-date data, or an ambiguous request.
- When the agent is unsure whether a change applies to one item, all items or future items. Ask before acting.

## When not to use

- As a standing disclaimer on every answer. Use the caveat line under the message box (assistant-panel).
- To report an error. Use an error message (error-messages) with the fix.
- Low-stakes output the person can see and change in a second. A note there is noise people learn to skip.

## Structure

1. Lead line ("Not sure:" and the cause)
2. Safer option or what to check
3. Optional actions (for example Check the source, Use the safer option)

## Guidelines

- Say uncertainty in words, never as a percentage. A figure like 72% looks exact and gives people nothing to do.
- Say what caused it: missing data, out of date, or an ambiguous request.
- Offer a safer alternative or a concrete way to check, such as the record to open or the filter to apply.
- Scale to the stakes: use it when the output affects other people, shared records or money, and leave it off elsewhere.
- When unsure whether a change applies to one item, all items or future items, ask before acting. Do not pick the widest.
- Place the note next to the output it is about, not in a corner, so it is read together with it.

## Content

- Start with "Not sure:" and the cause: "Not sure: the connection is 35 minutes, and the last export was in March."
- Follow with what to do, as an instruction: "Check the rail times before sending this to applicants."
- Avoid "might", "may" and "possibly" on their own. Say which part, and why.
- Do not apologise. State the cause and the next step.

## Accessibility

- The cause is text with an icon that is hidden from assistive technology, so meaning does not rely on colour or the icon (SC 1.4.1).
- The note sits next to the output in reading order so it is read with it (SC 1.3.1).
- Any action in the note is a real button with a visible name (SC 4.1.2).
- If a note appears after the output has loaded, put it in a role="status" region so it is announced (SC 4.1.3).

## Keyboard

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Move to the note's actions, if it has any |
| Enter / Space | Press the focused action |

## Examples

### note

```tsx
import { Button, ConfidenceNote, toast } from "@twoux/ui";

export const meta = { title: "Unsure, and why", description: "The cause in words, then the safer option and a way to check. Use it when the output reaches people, shared records or money.", order: 1 };

export default function Example() {
	return (
		<div className="grid w-full max-w-xl gap-3">
			<ConfidenceNote
				cause="the venue's opening hours are from March, so they may be out of date"
				action={<><Button size="xs" variant="outline" onClick={() => toast("Opened the venue page")}>Check the venue page</Button><Button size="xs" variant="ghost" onClick={() => toast("Draft saved without a time")}>Send without a time</Button></>}
			>
				Check the hours before this goes to 14 applicants. If you cannot, send the invitation without a time and ask them to reply.
			</ConfidenceNote>
			<ConfidenceNote cause="your request does not say whether the new closing date applies to the 3 selected listings or to every listing in this view">
				I have not changed anything. Tell me which, and whether future listings should follow it too.
			</ConfidenceNote>
		</div>
	);
}
```

## Related

- Citations and sources
- Clarifying question card
- AI origin label
- Suggested changes
- Change review
